name: 5280 Watch Company
description: More than a timepiece, it's a legacy — a wearable work of art designed to be passed down. With handcrafted details celebrating Denver's Mile High identity, 5280 Watch Company creates accessible everyday timepieces that carry the spirit of Colorado craftsmanship into every wrist.

keyCollections.name: Higgins
keyCollections.description: Higgins is a flagship dress-watch family from 5280 Watch Company, associated with Denver-inspired storytelling and the brand’s artisanal, heirloom-focused approach to watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: Olde Town Arvada
keyCollections.description: Olde Town Arvada is a heritage-inspired collection within 5280 Watch Company’s lineup, evoking classic American localism while pairing the theme with the brand’s Swiss-made, artisanal watchmaking style.

timeline.event: Ira Fullerton founds 5280 Watch Company in Denver, Colorado, named after the city's mile-high elevation (5,280 feet).
First collection launches, emphasising handcrafted details and Denver heritage.
Expands distribution through direct-to-consumer online sales and local Colorado retailers.

faqItems.question: What does '5280' mean?
faqItems.answer: 5,280 is the number of feet in a mile — Denver's elevation, earning it the nickname 'Mile High City.' The brand celebrates this identity.

faqItems.question: Where are 5280 watches made?
faqItems.answer: Designed in Denver, Colorado. The watches use Swiss quartz movements assembled with quality components, positioned as affordable heirloom pieces.

name: A. Lange & Söhne
description: Founded in 1845 by Ferdinand Adolph Lange in Glashütte, Germany, A. Lange & Söhne is renowned for its hand-finished movements and quintessentially Germanic precision. The manufacture was refounded in 1990 after decades of suppression under East German rule, and quickly reclaimed its position among the world's finest watchmakers.

keyCollections.name: Lange 1
keyCollections.description: A. Lange & Söhne’s defining modern classic, the Lange 1 pairs an off-centre dial, outsize date, power-reserve display and Saxon movement finishing in a design first launched on 24 October 1994 and still central to the brand’s identity.

image.alt: A. Lange & Sohne Lange 1 reference 191.032 in pink gold
A. Lange & Sohne Lange 1 reference 191.039 in white gold
A. Lange & Sohne Lange 1 reference 191.025 in platinum

timeline.event: A. Lange & Söhne launches the original Lange 1 on 24 October 1994, establishing the family’s off-centre dial design and signature outsize date.
The Lange 1 Time Zone expands the family with a dual-time execution based on the Lange 1 layout.
The Lange 1 Moon Phase is updated with a new movement and a combined moon-phase/day-night display.
The Lange 1 Time Zone is reintroduced with manufacture calibre L141.1 and ring-shaped day/night indicators.
The Lange 1 Perpetual Calendar debuts, adapting a peripheral month ring to the collection’s asymmetrical architecture.
For the 30th anniversary, Lange unveils limited Lange 1 models in platinum with black onyx dial and pink gold with blue dial.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Lange 1 is the watch that defined modern A. Lange & Söhne after its revival, proving that a radically asymmetrical dial could feel perfectly balanced. Its outsize date, golden-ratio display layout, hand-finished Saxon movement architecture and long-running influence make it one of contemporary haute horlogerie’s most recognizable dress watches.

A. Lange & Sohne Lange 1 reference 191.039 in white gold

newsItems.title: Distinctive. In every detail.
newsItems.summary: For the Lange 1’s 30th anniversary, A. Lange & Söhne introduced limited Lange 1 editions in platinum with black onyx dial and pink gold with blue dial, alongside matching Little Lange 1 models.

newsItems.title: LANGE 1 PERPETUAL CALENDAR
newsItems.summary: Lange added a platinum-and-black-dial version to the Lange 1 Perpetual Calendar family introduced in 2021.

newsItems.title: LANGE 1 PERPETUAL CALENDAR
newsItems.summary: The brand launched the Lange 1 Perpetual Calendar with a peripheral month ring tailored to the family’s off-centre layout.

newsItems.title: LANGE 1 TIME ZONE

newsItems.title: LANGE 1 MOON PHASE
newsItems.summary: The Lange 1 Moon Phase was renewed with a new movement and an integrated moon-phase/day-night display.

faqItems.question: When was the Lange 1 introduced?
faqItems.answer: The Lange 1 was launched on 24 October 1994 as part of A. Lange & Söhne’s first modern post-revival collection.

faqItems.question: Why is the Lange 1 dial laid out asymmetrically?
faqItems.answer: Its displays are arranged off-centre but proportioned according to the golden ratio, which gives the watch its unusual yet balanced appearance.

faqItems.question: What is the signature feature of the Lange 1?
faqItems.answer: Its best-known hallmark is the Lange outsize date, paired with an off-centre time display, power-reserve indicator and subsidiary seconds.

faqItems.question: Is the Lange 1 manually wound?
faqItems.answer: The core Lange 1 models are manually wound; the family also includes related complications and variants such as Moon Phase, Time Zone and Daymatic.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: The Lange 1’s launch date is precisely documented by A. Lange & Söhne as 24 October 1994.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2
funFacts.body: The 2024 anniversary platinum Lange 1 marked the first time an onyx dial was used on a Lange 1 model.

keyCollections.description: A. Lange & Söhne’s 1815 is the Saxon manufacture’s classically styled family, named after Ferdinand Adolph Lange’s 1815 birth year and shaped by 19th-century Glashütte pocket-watch cues such as Arabic numerals, chemin-de-fer minute tracks, subsidiary seconds and manually wound movements.

referenceDetails.notes: Manual-wind 1815 variant with Lange’s historic UP/DOWN power-reserve display, whose roots trace to an 1879 A. Lange & Söhne patent.
Manual-wind flyback chronograph in the 1815 family, using calibre L951.5 and a classic pocket-chronograph-inspired dial layout with pulsometer scale on current models.
Manual-wind annual calendar with analogue date, day, month and moon phase, positioned by Lange as the second annual calendar in its history but the first in the 1815 line.

timeline.event: The 1815 family makes its first documented appearance in the revived A. Lange & Söhne era, with period and secondary sources pointing to 1995 as the best-supported launch year.
Lange expands the line with the 1815 Annual Calendar and introduces the limited 1815 “Homage to Walter Lange,” featuring a stoppable jumping seconds hand inspired by a historic Lange invention.
A. Lange & Söhne unveils a new 34 mm 1815 with newly developed calibre L152.1, a 72-hour power reserve and slimmer, more discreet proportions.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The 1815 matters because it is Lange’s purest expression of traditional German watchmaking: restrained design, historical Glashütte cues, hand-finished manual calibres and a platform that stretches from simple three-hand dress watches to some of the brand’s most admired chronographs and calendar complications.

newsItems.title: The new 1815
newsItems.summary: Lange introduced a smaller 34 mm 1815 with a newly developed L152.1 calibre, 72-hour power reserve and refined dress-watch proportions.

newsItems.title: 1815 TOURBILLON
newsItems.summary: Lange returned attention to the 1815 family with a fresh 1815 Tourbillon release, underscoring the collection’s role as a home for classical high complications.

newsItems.title: Hands-On Review - A. Lange & Söhne 1815 Rattrapante Platinum
newsItems.summary: Monochrome covered the platinum 1815 Rattrapante limited edition, highlighting the collection’s credibility in ultra-high-end split-seconds chronographs.

newsItems.title: 1815 “Homage to Walter Lange”
newsItems.summary: A commemorative 1815 with stoppable jumping seconds paid tribute to Walter Lange and revived a historical Lange-style seconds complication.

newsItems.title: 1815 Annual Calendar
newsItems.summary: The 1815 line gained a manually wound annual calendar with analogue calendar displays and moon phase, broadening the family beyond time-only and chronograph models.

faqItems.question: Why is the collection called 1815?
faqItems.answer: It is named after 1815, the birth year of Ferdinand Adolph Lange, founder of the original A. Lange & Söhne manufacture.

faqItems.question: What design cues define the 1815 family?
faqItems.answer: Typical cues include Arabic numerals, a railway-track minute scale, subsidiary seconds, lancet-style hands and styling inspired by historic Lange pocket watches.

faqItems.question: Is the 1815 a dress-watch collection only?
faqItems.answer: Mostly yes in spirit, but the family spans from restrained three-hand models to serious complications such as chronographs, annual calendars, tourbillons and rattrapantes.

faqItems.question: What are the best-known 1815 models today?
faqItems.answer: Among the most visible current or recent anchors are the 1815, 1815 Up/Down, 1815 Chronograph and 1815 Annual Calendar, with notable special pieces like the Homage to Walter Lange and 1815 Tourbillon.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: The 1815 Up/Down’s power-reserve concept references an A. Lange & Söhne patent granted on 18 May 1879 for showing whether a watch was wound or unwound.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2
funFacts.body: The 2025 34 mm 1815 runs on calibre L152.1, described by Lange as the 75th manufacture calibre developed since the brand’s modern re-establishment.

keyCollections.name: Saxonia
keyCollections.description: A. Lange & Söhne’s Saxonia collection is the brand’s broadest expression of understated elegance: a family that pairs minimalist German design with increasingly sophisticated mechanics, from slim two-hand dress watches to outsize-date models, moon phases, annual calendars and the Datograph line. Named for Saxony, it also connects the modern manufacture to its regional roots in Glashütte.

referenceDetails.summary: The pared-back manual-wind dress watch of the family and Lange’s flattest timepiece, focused purely on hours and minutes.

image.alt: A. Lange & Sohne Saxonia Thin in white gold

referenceDetails.summary: An ultra-thin self-winding Saxonia emphasizing discreet proportions and simple time-only display.

referenceDetails.summary: A balanced complication model combining Lange’s outsize date with a precise moon-phase display.

timeline.event: The first Saxonia debuts as one of the four watches in A. Lange & Söhne’s post-relaunch opening collection in Dresden.
Saxonia Thin is introduced, establishing the family’s modern extra-slim dress-watch pillar.
Saxonia Moon Phase joins the collection, combining the outsize date with a moon-phase display.
Saxonia Outsize Date is launched with a new self-winding calibre and black-dial debut references.
The Datograph’s 25th anniversary is marked by a new Datograph Up/Down white-gold limited edition within the broader Saxonia family.
Two 200-piece Saxonia Thin limited editions in honey gold and platinum add glossy black onyx dials to the line.
A refreshed Saxonia Annual Calendar with a new self-winding movement is introduced at Watches and Wonders 2026.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Saxonia matters because it shows how A. Lange & Söhne translates high horology into restrained form. It is the collection where the manufacture’s signatures—German precision, immaculate finishing, legibility, and inventive mechanics—are presented in their most elegant and versatile dress-watch language, while still spanning everything from simple thin watches to Datograph-level icons.

faqItems.question: When was the Saxonia collection introduced?
faqItems.answer: The Saxonia collection debuted in 1994 as one of the four watches in A. Lange & Söhne’s first post-relaunch collection.

faqItems.question: What does the name Saxonia mean?
faqItems.answer: Saxonia is the Latin name for Saxony, the German region tied to Glashütte and the historic roots of A. Lange & Söhne.

faqItems.question: Is Saxonia only a simple dress-watch line?
faqItems.answer: No. While Saxonia is known for restrained dress-watch design, the family also includes models with outsize date, moon phase, annual calendar, and the Datograph chronograph line.

faqItems.question: Which Saxonia models best represent the collection today?
faqItems.answer: Core modern references include the Saxonia Thin, Saxonia Automatic, Saxonia Moon Phase, and Saxonia Outsize Date, while the wider family also encompasses the Annual Calendar and Datograph models.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: The original Saxonia was one of the four watches that marked A. Lange & Söhne’s modern rebirth in 1994.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2
funFacts.body: Although many collectors think of Saxonia as a minimalist dress-watch family, A. Lange & Söhne officially places the Datograph line inside the broader Saxonia family.

keyCollections.name: Odysseus
keyCollections.description: The A. Lange & Söhne Odysseus is the manufacture’s sporty-elegant watch family, introduced in 2019 with an integrated bracelet, 120-metre water resistance, outsized day and date displays, and a dedicated self-winding Datomatic movement developed specifically for the line.

timeline.event: A. Lange & Söhne launched the Odysseus in stainless steel as its first sporty-elegant watch family with an integrated metal bracelet and dedicated calibre L155.1 Datomatic.
The collection expanded with an Odysseus in 750 white gold, broadening the family beyond the original steel debut.
Lange introduced the limited Odysseus in titanium, the manufacture’s first titanium watch, with an ice-blue dial and matching titanium bracelet.
The Odysseus Chronograph debuted as a limited 100-piece model, introducing Lange’s first self-winding chronograph movement, calibre L156.1 Datomatic.
The Odysseus Honeygold arrived with a full HONEYGOLD® case and bracelet, adding a precious-metal bracelet execution limited to 100 pieces.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Odysseus matters because it opened an entirely new chapter for A. Lange & Söhne: a modern, water-resistant, bracelet-equipped luxury sports watch that still preserves the brand’s distinctive Saxon design language, oversized calendar displays, and exceptionally finished in-house movements.

faqItems.question: When was the A. Lange & Söhne Odysseus introduced?
faqItems.answer: The Odysseus collection debuted in 2019 with the stainless-steel reference 363.179.

faqItems.question: Why is the Odysseus important for Lange?
faqItems.answer: It is Lange’s sporty-elegant family with integrated bracelet architecture, 120-metre water resistance, and a dedicated automatic movement created specifically for the collection.

faqItems.question: What movement powers the standard Odysseus models?
faqItems.answer: The three-hand Odysseus models use the in-house calibre L155.1 Datomatic, a self-winding movement with day and outsize date displays.

faqItems.question: What makes the Odysseus Chronograph special?
faqItems.answer: It introduced the calibre L156.1 Datomatic, the manufacture’s first self-winding chronograph movement, with centrally mounted chronograph hands and dual-function pushers.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: The titanium Odysseus was the first titanium watch ever introduced by A. Lange & Söhne.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2

timeline.event: Ferdinand Adolph Lange founds A. Lange & Cie in Glashütte on 7 December, employing 15 apprentices and launching the Saxon watchmaking industry.
Richard Lange joins the company; name changes to A. Lange & Söhne.
Headquarters destroyed in a Soviet air raid on the last day of World War II.
East German government nationalises Glashütte watchmakers; the Lange name disappears from dials.
Walter Lange and Günter Blümlein re-found the company on 7 December — exactly 145 years after the original founding.
Four debut models launched simultaneously: Lange 1, Saxonia, Arkade, and Tourbograph. The watch world is stunned.
Richemont Group acquires A. Lange & Söhne, ensuring long-term stability.
Debuted Odysseus in Honeygold on full gold bracelet, Minute Repeater Perpetual, and smaller 34mm 1815 at Watches & Wonders 2025.
Released limited-edition Lange 1 Daymatic Honeygold (250 pieces, boutique-only).

faqItems.question: Why is A. Lange & Söhne considered Germany's finest watchmaker?
faqItems.answer: Lange produces only around 5,000 watches per year, each hand-finished in Glashütte. The signature three-quarter plate, hand-engraved balance cock, and outsize date complication are hallmarks of uncompromising craft.

faqItems.question: What makes the Lange 1 so iconic?
faqItems.answer: Introduced in 1994 at the brand's relaunch, the Lange 1 broke every design convention: off-centre dial layout, outsize date, asymmetric subsidiary dials, and a patented twin mainspring barrel.

faqItems.question: Is A. Lange & Söhne Swiss or German?
faqItems.answer: German. Lange is based in Glashütte, Saxony. Despite being owned by the Swiss Richemont group, all watches are made in Germany.

faqItems.question: How much does a Lange watch cost?
faqItems.answer: Entry models start around CHF 15,000-20,000. Grand complications like the Datograph or Zeitwerk reach CHF 50,000-100,000+.

pronunciation.note: The German “Söhne” means sons; English collectors often say “Lange.”

description: Abingdon Watch Co. is an American watch brand founded in 2009 by Abingdon King, specifically designed for female pilots, divers, and adventurers. Named after a World War II aviation pioneer, the brand produces robust sport watches sized for women's wrists, with aviation bezels, diver ratings, and Swiss quartz movements.

keyCollections.name: Marina
keyCollections.description: A professional dive watch rated to 200 meters, built with a rotating bezel and bold indices for female divers and other users who want a straightforward underwater tool watch.

keyCollections.name: Amelia
keyCollections.description: An aviation-inspired watch named after Amelia Earhart, designed with a slide-rule bezel and aimed at women pilots and enthusiasts of practical cockpit-style tool watches.

Marina dive watch launches, establishing the brand's credibility in women's sport watches.

faqItems.question: Why was Abingdon Watch Co. founded?
faqItems.answer: Founder Abingdon Mullin, a pilot and diver, couldn't find rugged sport watches that fit women's wrists. She created the brand to fill that gap.

faqItems.question: Are Abingdon watches only for women?
faqItems.answer: The brand designs primarily for women, with case sizes and proportions tailored to smaller wrists, but anyone can wear them.

name: Accutron
description: Accutron pioneered electronic timekeeping in 1960 with the world's first tuning fork watch, a revolutionary departure from traditional mechanical movements. Revived as an independent brand by Bulova in 2020, it now produces watches powered by its proprietary electrostatic energy-harvesting movement.

hq.address: 350 Fifth Avenue, New York, NY 10118, United States

defunct_reason: Bulova discontinued the iconic tuning fork Accutron movement in 1977 as quartz technology rendered the precision electro-mechanical system commercially obsolete.
revival_attempt: Revived by Bulova in 2020 as an independent sub-brand featuring a proprietary electrostatic energy-harvesting movement — a spiritual successor to the original tuning fork technology.

keyCollections.name: Spaceview
keyCollections.description: The original Accutron Spaceview turned an electronic tuning-fork movement into the watch’s visual identity. First commercialized in the early 1960s after beginning as a dealer demonstration format, it became one of the defining open-dial designs of postwar American watchmaking and a lasting symbol of the Space Age.

referenceDetails.name: Bulova Spaceview Accutron, 1961
referenceDetails.note: Early gold-cased Spaceview noted by Christie’s as a 1961 example with exposed tuning-fork movement and chapter ring printed on the crystal.

referenceDetails.name: Bulova Accutron Spaceview, 1972
referenceDetails.note: Christie’s lists a stainless-steel 1972 Spaceview with signed glass, silvered chapter ring, and exposed movement.

referenceDetails.name: Bulova Spaceview, 1973
referenceDetails.note: Christie’s also records later-period Spaceview examples from 1973, showing the model’s continued production run into the 1970s.

image.alt: Close-up of Accutron open-work movement used as fallback collection image

timeline.event: Accutron launched the world’s first tuning-fork electronic watch movement.
The Spaceview went on sale as a separate model after demand grew for the exposed-movement dealer display style.
Auction records show Spaceview production examples still appearing in the early 1970s, confirming the design’s long commercial life.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Spaceview helped popularize the idea that modern technology itself could be the design language of a watch. Its exposed tuning-fork layout, printed crystal chapter ring, and smooth sweep seconds made it one of the best-known electronic wristwatch designs of the 1960s and 1970s.

faqItems.question: Was the original Spaceview designed as a normal retail model from the start?
faqItems.answer: No. It began as a demonstration format to show the Accutron tuning-fork movement, then became a commercial model after customers responded to the exposed design.

faqItems.question: Why is the original Spaceview important?
faqItems.answer: It translated electronic watchmaking into a recognizable visual style, combining an exposed movement, printed crystal chapter ring, and the smooth seconds motion associated with the tuning-fork Accutron.

faqItems.question: What historic period does the Astronaut collection reference?
faqItems.answer: The official collection copy ties the line to Accutron’s space-race legacy, while the current product text for 26B205 specifically says it honors the original 1968 model.

faqItems.answer: Accutron says DNA is powered by the world’s first electrostatic movement, using twin turbines driven by wrist motion to generate energy stored in an accumulator that powers the hands.

timeline.event: Hodinkee reported the launch of the new Accutron line with two debut models, Spaceview 2020 and Spaceview DNA.
Accutron documentation says the brand unveiled the world’s first timepiece charged by electrostatic energy after a decade of research and development.
At launch, Hodinkee described DNA as the more modern expression of the new electrostatic platform, with a shield-shaped case and hooded lugs.
The official Accutron DNA collection page shows the line still active with references including 2ES8A001, 2ES8A002, 2ES8A003A, and 2ES8A004A.
Swiss engineer Max Hetzel files the first patent for an electronically driven tuning fork oscillator while working at Bulova.
Accutron model 214 launches — the world's first fully electronic watch, accurate to ±1 minute per month, far exceeding mechanical movements.
The Spaceview is introduced with an open dial showing the tuning fork mechanism; it becomes an instant icon.
Accutron timekeeping mechanisms are selected for use aboard NASA spacecraft and U.S. government satellites.
Accutron becomes the preferred watch of U.S. Presidents; LBJ and Nixon are both photographed wearing the Astronaut model.
Bulova discontinues the tuning fork movement as quartz technology proves cheaper, smaller, and even more accurate.
Bulova relaunches Accutron as a standalone brand with a new electrostatic energy-harvesting calibre, marking a fresh chapter in electronic watchmaking.

faqItems.question: How does a tuning fork watch work?
faqItems.answer: An electronic oscillator drives a tiny steel tuning fork at 360 Hz. The fork's stable frequency advances a ratchet gear, producing the smooth, continuous sweep associated with Accutron — very different from the tick of a mechanical escapement.

faqItems.question: Why was the Accutron discontinued in 1977?
faqItems.answer: The quartz revolution brought movements that were even more accurate than the tuning fork at a fraction of the cost. Bulova — inventors of the tuning fork concept — pivoted to quartz like every other major watchmaker.

faqItems.question: What powers the 2020 Accutron?
faqItems.answer: The revived brand uses a patented electrostatic generator that harvests energy from the tiny electrical charge difference between the wearer's skin and the air. No battery, no winding — just ambient charge.

faqItems.question: Are vintage Accutron watches still repairable?
faqItems.answer: Yes, though specialists are required. NOS (new old stock) parts are still available, and a small community of dedicated Accutron technicians keeps these movements running.

faqItems.question: Was the Accutron really used in space?
faqItems.answer: The movement itself — not a complete watch — was used as a timing mechanism in satellites and spacecraft. The design's precision and reliability made it ideal for applications where accuracy was mission-critical.

timeline.event: Aerowatch is founded in Saignelégier in the Les Franches-Montagnes region of the Swiss Jura, establishing itself as a craft watchmaker from the outset.
The brand builds a reputation for hand-engraved movements and guilloché dial work, skills rare even among Swiss houses.
Unlike many Swiss brands, Aerowatch survives the quartz crisis by doubling down on traditional craft and skeleton work rather than competing on price.
The Renaissance skeleton collection gains international recognition, establishing Aerowatch as a respected name in affordable fine craftsmanship.
Aerowatch launches its modern wristwatch collections, expanding beyond its traditional pocket-watch heritage to reach a broader audience while maintaining its craft-focused identity.
The centenary is celebrated with special editions, and the brand reflects on 100 uninterrupted years of Swiss family watchmaking.
Fourth-generation family ownership continues, with the brand maintaining its independence and Saignelégier base into a second century.

faqItems.question: What is guilloché?
faqItems.answer: Engine-turned engraving on metal using a rose engine lathe. The lathe cuts intricate repeating geometric patterns — barleycorn, clous de Paris, hobnail — that catch light in ways impossible to replicate by hand or printing.

faqItems.question: Is Aerowatch still family-owned?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The company has been continuously family-owned since its founding in 1910 in Saignelégier, making it one of Switzerland's longest-running independent watchmakers.

faqItems.question: Are Aerowatch movements made in-house?
faqItems.answer: Aerowatch primarily uses Swiss ébauches (notably ETA-based movements), with the brand's craft focused on exceptional dial work, hand engraving, and skeletonisation rather than movement development.

faqItems.question: What price range should I expect?
faqItems.answer: Most Aerowatch pieces sit between CHF 500 and CHF 4,000, making them one of the more accessible entry points into genuine Swiss craft watchmaking.
