Ajwain’s current official site presents the brand around heritage, cultural research, and limited-batch mechanical watches rather than a single Heritage product page.

keyCollections.name: Artisan
keyCollections.description: Limited-edition pieces showcasing Indian craftsmanship techniques like enamel work and hand-engraving.

timeline.event: Ajwain founded in India with the mission of celebrating Indian craftsmanship and cultural heritage through watchmaking.
First collection launches, featuring dials inspired by traditional Indian art forms.

faqItems.question: What makes Ajwain different from other Indian watch brands?
faqItems.answer: Ajwain focuses on cultural storytelling through dial art, drawing on centuries of Indian craftsmanship traditions like enamel work and miniature painting.

faqItems.question: What movements does Ajwain use?
faqItems.answer: Ajwain uses reliable Japanese and Swiss automatic movements, focusing its differentiation on dial artistry and Indian design heritage.

name: AKHOR
description: AKHOR Genève is an independent Geneva-based watchmaker embodying a vision without compromise, where technical excellence serves profound creativity. Each timepiece reflects an inner force, uniting noble materials and deeply personal expression.

keyCollections.name: Genève
keyCollections.description: AKHOR’s Genève collection page appears to map to the brand’s debut Le Temps en Équilibre / AK-10 family: Geneva-made, COSC-certified and Poinçon de Genève-certified watches built around a patented suspended dual-disc display architecture.

referenceDetails.name: AK-10 Steel White Sunburst
referenceDetails.note: Core time-only steel expression listed on the official collection page as part of Le Temps en Équilibre, the brand’s inaugural AK-10 family.

image.alt: AKHOR AK-10 steel diamond white honeycomb watch

referenceDetails.name: AK-10-D Steel Diamond White Honeycomb
referenceDetails.note: Diamond-set steel variant with white honeycomb upper disc and white sunburst lower disc; official page states 39mm steel case and hand-wound AK10 calibre.

image.alt: AKHOR AK-10-D Steel Diamond White Honeycomb

referenceDetails.name: AK-10-AU Gold Black Honeycomb
referenceDetails.note: Gold-cased variant using the same suspended two-disc concept, with black honeycomb upper dial and black sunburst lower dial.

timeline.event: AKHOR introduced its inaugural model to the public in September 2025, according to WorldTempus coverage cited by the brand press page.
Escapement Magazine covered AKHOR Le Temps en Équilibre on 28 November 2025 as the brand’s debut timepiece built around the floating dual-disc display.
AKHOR expanded the family with color editions such as Bleu Azur des Sommets in February 2026 and Vert Émeraude des Cimes in March 2026, as listed on the brand press page.
In April 2026 AKHOR announced that every watch in its collection would bear the Poinçon de Genève, reinforcing the Geneva positioning of the line.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is the clearest current expression of AKHOR’s Geneva identity: the collection is built in Geneva, carries COSC and Poinçon de Genève credentials, and centers on the patented floating-dial AK10 architecture that defines the maison’s launch-era design language.

image.alt: AKHOR AK-10-AU Gold Black Honeycomb watch

faqItems.question: Is Genève a separate AKHOR collection page today?
faqItems.answer: The current official site foregrounds Le Temps en Équilibre / AK-10 rather than a separate Genève landing page, so Genève is best treated as AKHOR’s Geneva-rooted debut family positioning rather than a clearly separated current sub-collection.

faqItems.question: What defines the AKHOR Genève family technically?
faqItems.answer: The watches use a patented suspended dual-disc display with a hand-wound AK10 movement and are positioned as Geneva-made haute horlogerie pieces with COSC and Poinçon de Genève certification.

keyCollections.name: Tourbillon
keyCollections.description: Showcase tourbillon models demonstrating AKHOR's ambition to compete at the highest level of Swiss horology.

timeline.event: AKHOR Genève founded in Geneva by Pascal Chichignoud with a vision of uncompromising independent haute horlogerie.
First timepieces unveiled, featuring high complications and Geneva-finished movements.

faqItems.question: What does AKHOR mean?
faqItems.answer: The name evokes the concept of timelessness and origin, reflecting the brand's philosophy of creating watches that transcend trends.

faqItems.question: Where are AKHOR watches made?
faqItems.answer: Entirely in Geneva, Switzerland, following the city's centuries-old tradition of haute horlogerie.

name: Akrivia
description: Akrivia is a micro-manufacture founded in Geneva in 2012 by watchmaker Rexhep Rexhepi, who trained at Patek Philippe before striking out independently. The brand produces extremely limited quantities of hand-finished watches that have rapidly gained cult status among serious collectors.

keyCollections.name: AK-06 Chronomètre
keyCollections.description: Akrivia’s AK-06 is the atelier’s pivotal non-tourbillon collection: a dial-free, chronometry-focused wristwatch that showcases its movement architecture on the front, pairs a 100-hour hand-wound calibre with zero-reset seconds, and marks a key transition from the brand’s early tourbillon-heavy identity toward pure timekeeping and movement symmetry.

referenceDetails.name: AK-06
referenceDetails.note: Core collection model on the official Akrivia site; presented as the workshop’s first watch to move beyond the tourbillon, with 100-hour reserve and zero-reset seconds.

image.alt: Akrivia AK-06 official movement close-up hero image

referenceDetails.name: AK-06 Gold
referenceDetails.note: Official AK-06 page shows Gold as a selectable version/variant under the collection page.

image.alt: Akrivia AK-06 official hero image used for Gold variant context

referenceDetails.name: AK-06 Grey
referenceDetails.note: Official AK-06 page shows Grey as a selectable version/variant under the collection page.

image.alt: Akrivia AK-06 stainless steel front view from Phillips Geneva Watch Auction XXIII

positioningOrTimeline.event: Akrivia debuted the AK-06 at Baselworld as the brand’s first non-tourbillon watch, introducing a more stripped-back, chronometry-led expression.
The official product launch positioned the AK-06 as a pure time-teller with a dial-free front, 100-hour reserve and zero-reset seconds for precise setting.
Christie’s highlighted a unique semi-skeletonised AK-06 from The Oak Collection, reinforcing the model’s importance to collectors and its custom-execution appeal.
A stainless-steel AK-06 achieved CHF 3,000,000 at Phillips Geneva Watch Auction XXIII, underscoring the collection’s modern-icon status in independent watchmaking.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The AK-06 matters because it crystallized Rexhep Rexhepi’s movement aesthetics and chronometric priorities without relying on a tourbillon. It is widely treated as a turning point in Akrivia’s trajectory, showing that the atelier’s finishing, architecture and technical refinement could command collector attention through pure timekeeping alone.

faqItems.question: When was the Akrivia AK-06 introduced?
faqItems.answer: Reputable launch coverage and later auction-house scholarship place the AK-06’s debut in 2017, at Baselworld.

faqItems.question: Why is the AK-06 important within Akrivia?
faqItems.answer: It is the brand’s first non-tourbillon watch and a major pivot toward pure timekeeping, open movement display and chronometric refinement.

timeline.event: Akrivia debuted the AK-06 at Baselworld as the brand’s first non-tourbillon watch, introducing a more stripped-back, chronometry-led expression.
The official product launch positioned the AK-06 as a pure time-teller with a dial-free front, 100-hour reserve and zero-reset seconds for precise setting.
Christie’s highlighted a unique semi-skeletonised AK-06 from The Oak Collection, reinforcing the model’s importance to collectors and its custom-execution appeal.
A stainless-steel AK-06 achieved CHF 3,000,000 at Phillips Geneva Watch Auction XXIII, underscoring the collection’s modern-icon status in independent watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: Chronomètre Contemporain
keyCollections.description: Rexhep Rexhepi’s defining classical chronometer line, introduced in 2018 as a more restrained, round-cased expression of the atelier’s values and later extended by the dead-beat-seconds Chronomètre Contemporain II.

referenceDetails.name: RRCC I
referenceDetails.note: Officially dated 2018 on the current collection page; the original model established the line with a round case, grand feu enamel dial, and zero-reset seconds.

referenceDetails.name: RRCC II
referenceDetails.note: Officially dated 2022 on the current collection page; preserves the family aesthetic while introducing an all-new calibre with independently driven dead-beat seconds and a new in-house conventional case.

referenceDetails.name: Only Watch 2021 debut piece
referenceDetails.note: Official news post states the first Chronomètre Contemporain II was presented for Only Watch in November 2021, ahead of the regular 2022 collection launch.

positioningOrTimeline.event: Chronomètre Contemporain I launches and establishes Rexhep Rexhepi’s more classical, round-cased collection with grand feu enamel dial and zero-reset seconds.
The original Chronomètre Contemporain wins the Men’s Watch Prize at the Grand Prix d’Horlogerie de Genève, accelerating recognition for the brand.
The first Chronomètre Contemporain II is presented for the Only Watch auction in November 2021.
Chronomètre Contemporain II enters the collection with a new movement featuring twin barrels and independently driven dead-beat seconds.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Chronomètre Contemporain family marks the point where Rexhep Rexhepi’s work moved from admired independent craft to widely recognized modern classic status. It translated the atelier’s finishing and chronometric obsession into a restrained three-hand format that became the signature platform for the contemporary Rexhep Rexhepi identity.

faqItems.question: When was the Chronomètre Contemporain introduced?
faqItems.answer: The original Chronomètre Contemporain I is officially dated 2018 on the current collection page, while the Chronomètre Contemporain II first appeared as an Only Watch piece in November 2021 before broader collection release in 2022.

faqItems.question: How does the Chronomètre Contemporain II differ from the first model?
faqItems.answer: According to the official collection page, the RRCC II keeps the family’s grand feu enamel aesthetic but uses an all-new movement with twin barrels, independently driven dead-beat seconds, zero-reset seconds, and a redesigned in-house conventional case.

timeline.event: Chronomètre Contemporain I launches and establishes Rexhep Rexhepi’s more classical, round-cased collection with grand feu enamel dial and zero-reset seconds.
The original Chronomètre Contemporain wins the Men’s Watch Prize at the Grand Prix d’Horlogerie de Genève, accelerating recognition for the brand.
The first Chronomètre Contemporain II is presented for the Only Watch auction in November 2021.
Chronomètre Contemporain II enters the collection with a new movement featuring twin barrels and independently driven dead-beat seconds.

keyCollections.name: Akrivia Tourbillon
keyCollections.description: A concise umbrella for Akrivia’s early tourbillon-led creations, spanning the AK-01 through AK-05 era and showing Rexhep Rexhepi’s progression from overt complications to increasingly refined, symmetry-driven horological expression.

referenceDetails.name: AK-01
referenceDetails.note: Launch model of Akrivia’s tourbillon line; monopusher chronograph paired with a tourbillon and presented by Hodinkee as the brand’s first tourbillon wristwatch launched in 2013.

image.alt: Akrivia AK-01 Tourbillon Chronograph Monopusher watch

referenceDetails.name: AK-04
referenceDetails.note: Officially dated 2015 on the current collection page, with regulator display and one-minute tourbillon used as seconds.

referenceDetails.name: AK-05
referenceDetails.note: Officially dated 2016; a time-only tourbillon emphasizing finishing, mirrored steel details, and the first Arabic numerals in the atelier’s line.

positioningOrTimeline.event: AK-01 launches as Akrivia’s first tourbillon wristwatch and debut model, combining a tourbillon with a monopusher chronograph.
AK-04 Tourbillon Régulateur appears, shifting the tourbillon family toward regulator-style precision display and stronger symmetry.
AK-05 Tourbillon Barrette-Miroir arrives as the fifth tourbillon creation, emphasizing finishing, mirrored steel accents, and Arabic numerals over added complications.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Before the Chronomètre Contemporain reframed public perception of the maker, Akrivia’s identity was built on tourbillon watches that mixed youthful ambition with old-school hand finishing. This family documents the atelier’s formative design language and technical evolution.

timeline.event: AK-01 launches as Akrivia’s first tourbillon wristwatch and debut model, combining a tourbillon with a monopusher chronograph.
AK-04 Tourbillon Régulateur appears, shifting the tourbillon family toward regulator-style precision display and stronger symmetry.
AK-05 Tourbillon Barrette-Miroir arrives as the fifth tourbillon creation, emphasizing finishing, mirrored steel accents, and Arabic numerals over added complications.

keyCollections.name: AK-09 Répétition Minutes
keyCollections.description: Minute repeater demonstrating mastery of acoustic complications alongside Rexhepi's signature finishing.

keyCollections.name: Tourbillon Vagabondage III
keyCollections.description: Misattributed collection name retained in source data, but intentionally unpublished because the official Vagabondage III record belongs to F.P. Journe rather than Akrivia.

timeline.event: Rexhep Rexhepi born in Kosovo; his family later emigrates to Switzerland.
Rexhepi begins training at Patek Philippe's Geneva manufacture, mastering movement finishing under the most demanding standards.
Rexhepi founds Akrivia in Geneva's Plan-les-Ouates district, aged 25 — one of the youngest to establish a true manufacture.
First watch, the AK-06 Chronomètre, launched to immediate collector acclaim. Waitlists form instantly.
Akrivia wins the GPHG (Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève) Mechanical Exception prize.
The AK-09 Répétition Minutes unveiled — a minute repeater with exceptional hand-finishing.
Rexhepi collaborates with Romain Gauthier on a joint complication piece, marking his peer status among the world's elite.

faqItems.question: Who is Rexhep Rexhepi?
faqItems.answer: Rexhep Rexhepi is a Kosovar-Swiss master watchmaker born in 1987. After training at Patek Philippe, he founded Akrivia at 25. He is widely regarded as one of the most talented independent watchmakers of his generation.

faqItems.question: How many watches does Akrivia produce each year?
faqItems.answer: Fewer than 20 pieces per year. Rexhepi finishes every movement himself, making Akrivia among the rarest watches in the world.

faqItems.question: Why are Akrivia watches sought after by collectors?
faqItems.answer: Collectors prize Akrivia for extraordinary hand-finishing — the bevelling, polishing, and anglage on every component is done by Rexhepi personally. Combined with a compelling personal story, the watches carry emotional weight beyond their craft.

faqItems.question: What is the price of an Akrivia watch?
faqItems.answer: Typically CHF 50,000 to over CHF 200,000 for complicated pieces. Secondary market prices often exceed retail significantly.

name: Al-Time
description: AL-Time is a young watch brand with a fresh attitude towards time, celebrating it as something precious and personal. Combining Swiss movements with clean, contemporary design, AL-Time creates modern mechanical and quartz timepieces that express individuality at accessible price points.

keyCollections.name: Classic
keyCollections.description: AL-Time’s Classic family is the brand’s affordable, contemporary-classic base offering, built around lightweight aluminum cases and minimalist Swiss-parts quartz functionality. On the current official site, the family is represented by the named lines Leger, Courage, and Rebel, positioned as everyday watches with strong graphic identity and low-wear comfort.

referenceDetails.name: Leger 18-1
referenceDetails.note: 40 mm quartz model in the Leger Classic category with aluminum body, mineral glass, 100 m water resistance, and Ronda Powertech Caliber 515.

referenceDetails.name: Courage
referenceDetails.note: Current AL-Time named line shown on the official homepage as part of the core offering.

referenceDetails.name: Rebel
referenceDetails.note: Current AL-Time named line shown on the official homepage as part of the core offering.

timeline.event: Official AL-Time image assets for Leger, Courage, and Rebel are stored in a 2019 uploads path, suggesting the Classic-family launch period.
The current AL-Time homepage still foregrounds Leger, Courage, and Rebel as the core named watch lines.
AL-Time’s story page positions the watch as an affordable, contemporary classic built around lightweight aluminum construction and a three-model lineup.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Classic label appears to function as AL-Time’s broad design language rather than a heavily separated sub-brand. For Watchatlas, mapping Classic to the trio of Leger, Courage, and Rebel creates a compact but defensible collection page grounded in current official navigation and product copy.

image.alt: AL-Time Leger from the Classic family

faqItems.question: What defines AL-Time Classic watches?
faqItems.answer: Official brand copy describes them as affordable, contemporary classics with lightweight aluminum cases and an easy everyday feel on the wrist.

faqItems.question: Which named models belong to the AL-Time Classic family?
faqItems.answer: The current official site presents Leger, Courage, and Rebel as the three core named lines associated with the brand’s classic offering.

keyCollections.name: Sport
keyCollections.description: AL-Time’s sport-oriented family centers on lightweight aluminum everyday watches sold through the brand’s shop categories, with stronger water resistance, luminous displays, and progressively bolder styling across Leger, Courage, and Rebel.

referenceDetails.name: Leger 18-1
referenceDetails.note: Official product page states 40 mm case, 100 m water resistance, luminescent display, and Swiss-parts Ronda 515 quartz movement in an aluminum-bodied watch.

referenceDetails.name: Courage 18-3
referenceDetails.note: Official category listing shows Courage as a distinct current sport line priced above Leger.

referenceDetails.name: Rebel collection
referenceDetails.note: Official category listing shows Rebel as the highest-priced core sport-oriented family on the current shop menu.

timeline.event: AL-Time’s published terms carry an effective date of May 2, 2018, establishing the brand’s operating web presence by that year.
Current sport-family references use 18-x and 19-x naming across Leger and Courage listings, indicating the line architecture was in place by the late 2010s.
The official homepage still foregrounds Leger, Courage, and Rebel as the brand’s main non-automatic ranges, with Leger, Courage, and Rebel shop categories active.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: For a small independent brand, Sport appears to function less as one labeled landing page than as the practical umbrella for AL-Time’s active aluminum quartz families. The official site consistently emphasizes lightweight construction, 100 m water resistance, luminescence, and accessible pricing.

image.alt: AL-Time lightweight sport watch from the Leger line

faqItems.question: What sits inside AL-Time’s sport-oriented range?
faqItems.answer: The current official shop structure groups the brand’s active lifestyle watches under Leger, Courage, and Rebel, with Leger clearly documented as an aluminum quartz watch family with 100 m water resistance and luminous display.

faqItems.question: Why use the slug "sport" when the site does not show a dedicated Sport page?
faqItems.answer: Because the assignment names the collection Sport, but the official site currently presents the range through subfamilies rather than a single Sport archive page; the packet therefore maps Sport to the brand’s active-use core lines and flags the gap below.

timeline.event: AL-Time founded in Switzerland by Alexandre Lez with a fresh, youthful approach to Swiss watchmaking.
First collection launches, targeting a younger audience seeking genuine Swiss quality at accessible prices.

faqItems.question: What is AL-Time's philosophy?
faqItems.answer: AL-Time celebrates time as something precious and personal, creating Swiss-made watches with a youthful aesthetic and accessible pricing.

faqItems.question: Are AL-Time watches Swiss Made?
faqItems.answer: Yes. AL-Time watches are designed and assembled in Switzerland, meeting the official Swiss Made criteria.

faqItems.question: What price range are AL-Time watches?
faqItems.answer: AL-Time positions itself in the accessible Swiss-made segment, offering watches that bring Swiss craftsmanship to a broader audience at price points well below traditional Swiss luxury brands while maintaining Swiss Made quality standards.

name: Alain Silberstein
description: Founded in 1990 by French architect and interior designer Alain Silberstein, the brand became an icon of 1990s avant-garde watchmaking. Inspired by Bauhaus primary colours and bold geometric shapes — circles, triangles, and squares — Silberstein's watches were instantly recognisable and radically different from traditional Swiss horology. The brand ceased regular production around 2012 but remains a cult favourite among collectors.

keyCollections.name: Krono
keyCollections.description: Alain Silberstein’s Krono family is the brand’s signature chronograph line, pairing mechanically ambitious calendar or timing layouts with the designer’s Bauhaus-inflected language of primary colours, geometric hands, and playful dial graphics.

referenceDetails.name: Krono Bauhaus
referenceDetails.note: Limited-edition automatic chronograph documented by Christie’s as a 40 mm titanium model, numbered example 127/250, circa 1995.

referenceDetails.name: Krono 2
referenceDetails.note: Sotheby’s lists Krono 2 as a limited-edition automatic annual-calendar chronograph with moon phases, circa 1993, using caliber 7751.

image.alt: Alain Silberstein Krono 2 annual calendar chronograph

referenceDetails.name: Krono Bauhaus2
referenceDetails.note: Sotheby’s editorial feature highlights the Bauhaus2 as a later expression of Silberstein’s signature primary-colour and geometric-hand chronograph style, illustrated with example no. 576/999 circa 2000.

image.alt: Alain Silberstein Krono Bauhaus2 on bracelet

timeline.event: Krono 2 appears in auction documentation as a limited-edition automatic annual-calendar chronograph with moon phases.
Christie’s documents the Krono Bauhaus as a limited-edition titanium automatic chronograph, showing the family’s mid-1990s expansion.
Sotheby’s illustrates the later Krono Bauhaus2, showing the continuation of the collection’s colourful Bauhaus design language into circa 2000.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Krono is the clearest expression of Alain Silberstein’s identity in wristwatches: complicated Swiss chronograph mechanics presented through instantly recognizable architectural graphics, playful symbolism, and bold primary-colour hands that made the brand collectible far beyond conventional tool-watch design.

image.alt: Alain Silberstein Krono Bauhaus2 chronograph on bracelet

faqItems.question: What defines an Alain Silberstein Krono watch?
faqItems.answer: The Krono line combines chronograph-focused complications with Alain Silberstein’s signature use of primary colours, geometric hands, and graphic Bauhaus-inspired dial layouts.

faqItems.question: Is Krono a single watch or a broader family?
faqItems.answer: It is a broader family. Verified examples include Krono Bauhaus, Krono 2, and Krono Bauhaus2, each sharing the chronograph concept while differing in complication set, case execution, and production era.

keyCollections.name: Marine
keyCollections.description: The Marine line translates Alain Silberstein’s colourful, geometric design language into sporty and diving-oriented cases, adding rotating bezels, luminous markers, and in some references high-complication calendars while retaining the brand’s unmistakably playful visual identity.

referenceDetails.name: Le Perpetual Marine
referenceDetails.note: Christie’s documents this black patinated stainless-steel limited edition as no. 017/100, circa 1993, with perpetual-calendar display visible through the back and a revolving bezel.

referenceDetails.name: Marine Perpetuel
referenceDetails.note: A closely related Christie’s listing records the stainless-steel Marine Perpetuel no. 047/100, circa 1993, underscoring the Marine family’s early use for complicated sporty models.

referenceDetails.name: Marine Krono
referenceDetails.note: The Marine name also appears on later chronograph executions; market and auction indexing confirm a Marine Krono variant within the collection, though official technical documentation was not located in this pass.

timeline.event: Christie’s documents Marine Perpetuel and Le Perpetual Marine examples, establishing the Marine family in the early 1990s.
These early Marine models pair rotating sport-watch bezels with perpetual-calendar mechanics, showing the collection was more than a simple diver.
An Ineichen auction catalogue records a Marine Krono example, confirming continued recognition of the Marine name on chronograph variants in the secondary market.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Marine shows how Silberstein adapted his whimsical Bauhaus vocabulary to a more robust sport-watch format, blending dive-watch cues such as rotating bezels and luminous markers with unexpectedly sophisticated complications that make the line distinctive among 1990s independents.

faqItems.question: Was Marine only a dive watch collection?
faqItems.answer: Not strictly. Verified Marine examples include sporty rotating-bezel watches with perpetual-calendar complications, indicating the line mixed diving cues with high-complication watchmaking.

faqItems.question: When does the Marine collection appear in the historical record?
faqItems.answer: Christie’s auction records show Le Perpetual Marine and Marine Perpetuel examples from circa 1993, making 1993 the safest documented introduction point for the collection.

keyCollections.name: Bolido
keyCollections.description: Bolido is Alain Silberstein’s curved rectangular/cushion-like design family from the brand’s independent 1990s period, known for mobile lugs, playful geometric hands and pushers, and colorful Bauhaus-inflected styling carried across time-only, power-reserve, and chronograph variants.

referenceDetails.name: Bolido Noir
referenceDetails.note: Antiquorum describes it as a limited edition of 500 examples from the late 1990s, with power-reserve sector and date in a curved rectangular steel case.

referenceDetails.name: Bolido Krono
referenceDetails.note: Christie’s documents a steel Bolido Krono example as No. 17/100, circa 1997, and explicitly states the model was made in 1997 in a limited edition of 100 pieces.

referenceDetails.name: Bolido Krono Titanium
referenceDetails.note: Antiquorum records a titanium Bolido Krono limited edition of 250 examples from the late 1990s.

timeline.event: Christie’s states the Bolido Krono limited edition of 100 pieces was made in 1997.
Auction cataloguing places Bolido Noir and Bolido Krono Titanium in the late 1990s, showing the line expanded into both time-only/power-reserve and chronograph executions.
Christie’s also catalogued a Bolido Krono example numbered 071/100 as circa 2000, indicating the model remained active in the market at the turn of the millennium.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Bolido captures Alain Silberstein’s signature vocabulary in one of his most distinctive case families: a curved rectangular body, animated primary-color hands and controls, and an architecture-first form that bridged playful design and serious Swiss mechanics.

faqItems.question: Is Bolido a single watch or a broader family?
faqItems.answer: It is better understood as a family: auction records show Bolido Noir, Bolido Krono, and titanium chronograph executions, alongside differences in complications and editions.

faqItems.question: Why is there no officialUrl in this packet?
faqItems.answer: Current official Alain Silberstein search results did not surface a reliable brand-hosted Bolido collection page, so the packet relies on reputable auction-house documentation instead of guessing an official URL.

keyCollections.name: Tourbillon
keyCollections.description: Alain Silberstein’s Tourbillon family captures the independent French designer’s mix of haute horlogerie and Bauhaus-inflected playfulness, spanning unique early-1990s experimental pieces through early-2000s limited editions such as the Tourbillon Volant and later Tourbillon d’Art variants.

referenceDetails.name: Alain Silberstein Tourbillon Volant
referenceDetails.note: Early-2000s limited-edition semi-skeletonized tourbillon with date; Phillips documented example no. 28 of 200 and described the model as released in the early 2000s.

referenceDetails.name: Alain Silberstein Tourbillon d'Art 'Black Light'
referenceDetails.note: Christie’s lists this semi-skeletonized stainless steel and lacquered model as no. 90/500, circa 2004, and places the broader Tourbillon Volant model introduction in the early 2000s.

referenceDetails.name: Alain Silberstein Tourbillon Krono
referenceDetails.note: Unique platinum tourbillon chronograph created circa 1997 to commemorate the 10th anniversary of Alain Silberstein’s watch company, according to Christie’s.

timeline.event: Alain Silberstein presented a series of 10 unique tourbillon watches at the Basel Fair, including distinctive experimental pieces documented by Christie’s.
The unique Tourbillon Krono was created to mark the 10th anniversary of the Alain Silberstein watch company.
The Tourbillon Volant line was released in the early 2000s, bringing Silberstein’s colorful geometric language into a limited-edition serially produced tourbillon.
Christie’s dates the Tourbillon d’Art 'Black Light' limited edition to circa 2004, showing the collection’s expansion into more decorative artisanal executions.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Tourbillon collection is the clearest expression of Alain Silberstein’s importance as a design-led independent: it applied a serious complication to unconventional colors, playful hands, unusual crowns, and even experimental cases, helping make the tourbillon feel less conservative and more artistic.

faqItems.question: What defines Alain Silberstein’s Tourbillon watches?
faqItems.answer: They combine high-watchmaking tourbillon mechanics with Alain Silberstein’s signature use of primary colors, geometric handset shapes, and playful Bauhaus-inspired design.

faqItems.question: Is the Tourbillon collection a single model line?
faqItems.answer: Not exactly. The collection umbrella spans early unique 1990s tourbillon experiments, the early-2000s Tourbillon Volant, and later variants such as Tourbillon d’Art executions.

timeline.event: French architect Alain Silberstein founds his eponymous watch brand in Paris, applying Bauhaus design principles — primary colours and geometric shapes — to watchmaking.
Debuts at Baselworld; the Krono chronograph with its distinctive circle-triangle-square hands becomes an instant talking point.
Launches the Marine dive collection, expanding beyond dress and sport chronographs.
Introduces limited-edition tourbillon models, proving the brand's range beyond colourful quartz and automatics.
Regular production winds down. The brand enters a dormant phase, though limited collaborations and special editions surface periodically.

faqItems.question: What makes Alain Silberstein watches so distinctive?
faqItems.answer: The hallmark is Bauhaus-inspired design: hands shaped as a circle, triangle, and square in primary colours (red, yellow, blue) against bold dials. No other watch brand looks quite like it.

faqItems.question: Is Alain Silberstein still making watches?
faqItems.answer: Regular production ceased around 2012. The brand is largely dormant, though limited editions and collaborations have appeared sporadically. Vintage pieces are highly sought after by collectors.

faqItems.question: Why are Alain Silberstein watches collectible?
faqItems.answer: Low production numbers, a completely unique design language, and the brand's dormant status have made vintage Silberstein pieces increasingly desirable on the secondary market.

name: Alba
description: Alba is a Japanese watch brand founded in 1979 as an affordable sub-brand of Seiko Corporation, primarily targeting the Asian market. Distributed across East and Southeast Asia, Alba produces affordable quartz and solar timepieces accessible to first-time watch buyers, with particular popularity in India, Singapore, and Hong Kong.

keyCollections.name: Active
keyCollections.description: Sport-oriented quartz watches with chronograph functions, targeting young active consumers across Asia.

keyCollections.name: Fashion
keyCollections.description: Trend-driven designs with bold colours and modern styling, aimed at younger demographics.

keyCollections.name: Solar
keyCollections.description: Eco-friendly solar-powered watches that reduce battery changes by using light-powered movement technology, positioned as an accessible everyday line within Alba’s broader affordable watch offering.

timeline.event: Seiko launches Alba in Japan as an affordable sub-brand targeting younger consumers.
Expands rapidly into Southeast Asian and Middle Eastern markets.
Introduces Giorgetto Giugiaro-designed models, borrowing from Seiko's automotive-inspired designs.
Refreshes brand identity across Asia with updated collections and modern marketing.

faqItems.question: What is the relationship between Alba and Seiko?
faqItems.answer: Alba is a sub-brand of Seiko Watch Corporation, using Seiko movements in more affordable cases and designs aimed at younger Asian and Middle Eastern consumers.

faqItems.question: What does 'Alba' mean?
faqItems.answer: 'Alba' means 'dawn' in Italian and Spanish, symbolising a fresh start — fitting for a brand aimed at young first-time watch buyers.

faqItems.question: Where are Alba watches available?
faqItems.answer: Primarily in Japan, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East. They're rarely sold in Europe or North America.

name: Alexander Shorokhoff
description: Alexander Shorokhoff is a German-Russian watch brand founded in 2010 by watchmaker Alexander Shorokhoff in Stuttgart, Germany. Known for artistic dials drawing on Russian Constructivist and avant-garde art movements, the brand produces hand-finished mechanical watches in limited series that blur the boundary between horology and visual art.

keyCollections.name: Heritage
keyCollections.description: Alexander Shorokhoff’s Heritage collection is the brand’s artisanal line dedicated to 19th-century Russian cultural heritage, combining comparatively classical case shapes with hand engraving, skeletonizing, enamelling, and named tributes such as Peter Tchaikovsky, Fyodor Dostoyevsky, Alexander Pushkin, and Leo Tolstoy.

referenceDetails.name: Alexander Shorokhoff Heritage Peter Tchaikovsky Big Alarm
referenceDetails.note: Europa Star identifies Peter Tchaikovsky as one of the named artisanal lines within the Heritage collection launched in 2003.

referenceDetails.name: Alexander Shorokhoff Heritage Fyodor Dostoyevsky
referenceDetails.note: Europa Star lists Fyodor Dostoyevsky among the core Heritage artisanal lines; the line exemplifies the collection’s hand-engraved, culturally themed approach.

referenceDetails.name: Alexander Shorokhoff Heritage Alexander Pushkin
referenceDetails.note: MasterHorologer reports the Pushkin line followed earlier Tchaikovsky, Tolstoi and Dostoevsky Heritage models and describes it as part of the Heritage collection.

timeline.event: Europa Star states the Heritage collection was launched in 2003 as an artisanal line dedicated to Russian cultural figures.
The Alexander Pushkin Heritage model was introduced after earlier Tchaikovsky, Tolstoi, and Dostoevsky pieces, expanding the collection’s literary and artistic tributes.
The Pushkin sub-line gained anniversary-era additions such as the Camomile model, described by an authorized dealer as created for the 25th anniversary of the Alexander Shorokhoff brand.
Recent brand and trade materials still present Heritage as one of Alexander Shorokhoff’s three core collections, underscoring its continuing role in the lineup.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Heritage is central to understanding Alexander Shorokhoff because it translates the founder’s Russian biography into collectible wristwatches that emphasize hand-finishing and named cultural storytelling rather than generic model families.

faqItems.question: What is the theme of the Alexander Shorokhoff Heritage collection?
faqItems.answer: It is dedicated to Russian art and cultural heritage of the 19th century, with watches named after figures such as Tchaikovsky, Dostoyevsky, Pushkin, and Tolstoy.

faqItems.question: When was the Heritage collection introduced?
faqItems.answer: Europa Star states the Heritage collection was launched in 2003.

keyCollections.name: Avantgarde
keyCollections.description: Bold, art-driven watch collection shaped by asymmetry, vivid color, and Russian constructivist inspiration, serving as the brand’s signature design language across many models.

keyCollections.name: Miss Avantgarde
keyCollections.description: Women’s interpretation of the brand’s avant-garde design ethos, using smaller case formats and artistic dial treatment while keeping the same expressive, collectible character.

timeline.event: Alexander Shorokhov arrives in Germany from Moscow as part of a Kohl-Gorbachev exchange programme for young managers.
Establishes a sales company for Poljot, Russia's most important watch brand, across European markets.
Launches 'Poljot-International' as his first own watch brand.
Founds the Alexander Shorokhoff Uhrenmanufaktur in Alzenau, Bavaria, under his own name.
Celebrates 25th anniversary; production reaches approximately 1,100 pieces per year.

faqItems.question: Is Alexander Shorokhoff a German or Russian brand?
faqItems.answer: Both. Founded by a Russian watchmaker in Germany, the brand bridges Russian artistic heritage with German engineering precision. Headquarters are in Alzenau, Bavaria.

faqItems.question: What makes Alexander Shorokhoff watches unique?
faqItems.answer: The dials. Each features hand-applied artistic techniques — engraving, enamel, lacquer — inspired by Russian cultural history. The brand's motto is 'Art on the Wrist.'

faqItems.question: Why is '60' at the 12 o'clock position?
faqItems.answer: Shorokhoff places '60' at the top of the dial instead of '12,' representing the 60 minutes of the hour — a distinctive design signature.

name: Alpina
description: Alpina was founded in 1883 in Geneva and played a significant role in standardising Swiss watchmaking practices through the Alpina Union. Today it is best known for its Startimer pilot watches and Alpiner sport models, offering Swiss manufacture movements at accessible price points.

keyCollections.name: Alpiner
keyCollections.description: Alpina’s core sport-watch family, spanning the heritage-led Alpiner 4 and newer Extreme models. The collection centers on robust, outdoor-oriented Swiss watches with legible dials, practical water resistance, and the brand’s long-running “Alpina 4” sports-watch philosophy.

referenceDetails.name: Alpiner 4 Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Current core three-hand Alpiner 4 model with 40mm steel case, rotating bezel, date, and AL-525 automatic movement.

image.alt: Alpina Alpiner watch product image from official site

referenceDetails.name: Alpiner Date Manufacture
referenceDetails.note: Higher-end current Alpiner variant listed in the official collection, showing the line’s step-up manufacture positioning.

image.alt: Alpina Alpiner watch product image from official site

referenceDetails.name: Alpiner Extreme Automatic Titanium
referenceDetails.note: Modern integrated-bracelet/outdoor expression within the wider Alpiner family; titanium case and bracelet, AL-525 automatic caliber.

image.alt: Alpina Alpiner Extreme Automatic Titanium official product image

timeline.event: Alpina introduced the original Alpina 4 sports-watch concept built around anti-magnetism, anti-shock protection, water resistance, and stainless-steel construction.
Alpina revived the concept with the modern Alpiner 4 collection, reestablishing Alpiner as the brand’s core all-terrain sports family.
The modern Alpiner 4 lineup expanded with new Automatic and GMT models, broadening the collection’s everyday-sport positioning.
Alpina expanded the Alpiner Extreme branch with integrated-bracelet executions, a notable evolution highlighted during the brand’s Watches and Wonders debut year.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Alpiner matters because it connects Alpina’s 1938 sports-watch claim to its modern, accessibly priced tool-watch offering. It is the collection where the brand’s durability message, mountain identity, and practical Swiss mechanical value are most clearly expressed.

image.alt: Alpina Alpiner Extreme Automatic Titanium official product image

faqItems.question: When was the modern Alpiner collection introduced?
faqItems.answer: Reputable watch coverage states Alpina revived the Alpina 4 concept as the modern Alpiner 4 collection in 2014.

faqItems.question: What defines the Alpiner family?
faqItems.answer: The collection combines Alpina’s outdoor-sport identity with practical specifications such as robust steel or titanium cases, strong water resistance, legible dials, and automatic calibers across multiple sub-lines.

keyCollections.name: Startimer Pilot
keyCollections.description: Startimer Pilot is Alpina’s aviation collection, built around legible cockpit-inspired dials, oversized pilot-watch cues, and accessible Swiss mechanical sports watches. The line ranges from simple automatics to heritage and manufacture-led interpretations, making it one of Alpina’s core modern pillars.

referenceDetails.name: Alpina Startimer Pilot Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Current-generation official model page describes the relaunched 40 mm automatic with AL-525 movement, 68-hour reserve, and 100 m water resistance.

referenceDetails.name: Alpina Startimer Pilot Heritage
referenceDetails.note: Hodinkee’s 2018 coverage documents a vintage-styled GMT expansion of the Startimer family.

referenceDetails.name: Alpina Startimer Pilot Heritage Manufacture
referenceDetails.note: Hodinkee’s 2023 review covers the heritage manufacture variant powered by Alpina’s bumper-style AL-709 calibre.

timeline.event: Alpina’s historical materials state that the Startimer collection dedicated to aviation was presented at Baselworld 2003.
Alpina historical book materials describe first deliveries of the new Startimer Pilot collection and related launch events held with Cessna and PrivatAir.
The Startimer Pilot Heritage introduced a vintage-inspired GMT branch to the family, broadening the collection beyond straightforward instrument-style pilots’ watches.
At Watches and Wonders 2026, Alpina unveiled a next-generation Startimer Pilot Automatic with a new 40 mm case and AL-525 movement on the official collection page.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Startimer Pilot is one of Alpina’s signature modern families, translating the brand’s sports-watch ethos into aviation form with strong value, long-running continuity, and a mix of entry mechanical, heritage, and manufacture-driven references.

faqItems.question: When was Alpina’s Startimer aviation collection introduced?
faqItems.answer: Alpina historical material indicates the aviation-dedicated Startimer collection was presented at Baselworld in 2003.

faqItems.question: What defines the current Startimer Pilot Automatic?
faqItems.answer: The current official Startimer Pilot Automatic is a 40 mm Swiss automatic pilot watch using Alpina’s AL-525 movement with a 68-hour power reserve and 100 m water resistance.

keyCollections.name: Seastrong Diver
keyCollections.description: Alpina’s Seastrong Diver family is the brand’s sea-going sports-watch line, spanning contemporary Diver Extreme models and Diver 300 Heritage variants with serious water resistance, rugged Swiss automatic calibres, and value-focused positioning within the modern Alpina catalog.

referenceDetails.name: Alpina Seastrong Diver Extreme Automatic GMT
referenceDetails.note: Current Seastrong collection flagship variant listed on Alpina’s official Seastrong collection page.

referenceDetails.name: Alpina Seastrong Diver Extreme Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Current 39x40.50 mm automatic diver with 300 m water resistance and AL-520 calibre; official product page confirms it as part of Seastrong.

referenceDetails.name: Alpina Seastrong Diver 300 Heritage
referenceDetails.note: Current heritage-styled Seastrong variant listed on Alpina’s official Seastrong collection page.

timeline.event: Alpina’s 140th anniversary materials described Seastrong as the brand’s dedicated sea realm alongside Startimer for air and Alpiner for earth.
Alpina issued a press release for the Seastrong Diver Extreme Automatic, expanding the contemporary Seastrong offering with new three-hand Extreme executions.
Watch coverage noted the 39 mm Seastrong Diver Extreme Automatic as a late-2024 addition, signaling the collection’s move toward more compact sizing.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Seastrong gives Alpina a clear, accessibly priced dive-watch pillar: modern 300 m sports models, heritage-inspired diver executions, and frequent special editions that reinforce the brand’s adventure-first identity.

faqItems.question: What kinds of watches are in Alpina’s Seastrong Diver family?
faqItems.answer: The current Seastrong family includes Diver Extreme Automatic GMT, Diver Extreme Automatic, and Diver 300 Heritage models, combining modern and heritage-oriented dive-watch styles.

faqItems.question: How is Seastrong positioned inside Alpina’s lineup?
faqItems.answer: Alpina’s own brand materials place Seastrong as the collection representing the sea, alongside Startimer for aviation and Alpiner for land-oriented sports watches.

image.alt: Alpina Seastrong Diver Extreme Automatic GMT

keyCollections.name: Alpiner Extreme
keyCollections.description: The integrated, more contemporary performance branch within Alpina’s Alpiner family. Alpiner Extreme models emphasize compact tonneau-inspired cases, strong water resistance, textured dials, and outdoor-ready execution across automatic, regulator, skeleton, quartz, solar, and special-edition variants.
keyReferences: Extreme Automatic Freeride World Tour Special Edition

referenceDetails.name: Extreme Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Core current Alpiner Extreme automatic execution in the official collection lineup.

image.alt: Alpina Alpiner Extreme official product image

referenceDetails.name: Alpiner Extreme Automatic Titanium
referenceDetails.note: Titanium-cased and titanium-bracelet version; Alpina describes it as the brand’s first 100% titanium watch.

image.alt: Alpina Alpiner Extreme Automatic Titanium official product image

referenceDetails.reference: Extreme Automatic Freeride World Tour Special Edition
referenceDetails.name: Extreme Automatic Freeride World Tour Special Edition
referenceDetails.note: Mountain-sport partnership edition in 39 x 40.5mm steel with AL-525 automatic movement; official page ties it to Alpina’s long-running Freeride World Tour relationship.

image.alt: Alpina Alpiner Extreme special edition official product image

timeline.event: The Alpiner Extreme Automatic appeared as a new contemporary sports-watch expression for Alpina, introducing the collection’s integrated, angular design language.
Alpina expanded Alpiner Extreme with integrated steel-bracelet versions, described by Monochrome as a first for the brand.
The Freeride World Tour Special Edition marked the ninth year of Alpina’s partnership with FWT, reinforcing the collection’s mountain-sport identity.
Current official lineup shows Alpiner Extreme broadened across automatic, regulator, skeleton, quartz, and Solarmetre variants.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Alpiner Extreme is important because it gives Alpina a more contemporary, integrated-sports-watch offer without abandoning the brand’s outdoor-tool ethos. It broadens Alpiner from heritage-inspired sports watches into a younger, design-forward segment while keeping accessible Swiss mechanical value at the center.

image.alt: Alpina Alpiner Extreme Automatic Titanium official product image

faqItems.question: When was Alpiner Extreme introduced?
faqItems.answer: Reputable watch coverage places the launch of the Alpiner Extreme Automatic in 2022, with the line expanding further in 2023.

faqItems.question: What kinds of watches are in the Alpiner Extreme range today?
faqItems.answer: The official collection page shows the range now includes automatic, regulator, skeleton, quartz, Solarmetre, titanium, and special-edition executions.

keyCollections.name: Comtesse
keyCollections.description: Alpina’s Comtesse is the brand’s women’s line, pairing the house’s sporty Swiss identity with more elegant proportions and finishes. The modern collection spans quartz ladies’ watches, while the name also has deeper historical roots inside Alpina’s postwar and late-20th-century catalog.

referenceDetails.name: Comtesse Quartz
referenceDetails.note: Current Alpina US product page for a Comtesse quartz model in the ladies catalog.

referenceDetails.name: Alpiner Comtesse Quartz
referenceDetails.note: Modern retailer-listed Comtesse variant showing the collection’s sporty-elegant positioning under Alpina’s current women’s offer.

referenceDetails.name: Comtesse Sport Quartz
referenceDetails.note: Named Comtesse Sport variant documented in specialist coverage of the collection relaunch era.

timeline.event: Alpina states it addressed demand for self-winding ladies’ watches in 1963, giving the Comtesse line an early historical anchor in the brand’s women’s offer.
Alpina’s historical book says names including Comtesse were added to the brand’s product lines during a difficult restructuring period in the early 1970s.
Alpina publicly reintroduced the Comtesse line as Comtesse Sport, positioning it as a revival of the brand’s ladies sport-watch tradition.
Comtesse remains a live Alpina collection on the brand’s current collection architecture and US product catalog.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Comtesse matters because it is Alpina’s dedicated women’s collection with both archival depth and a modern commercial role, connecting the brand’s sport-watch heritage to contemporary feminine sizing, gem-set options, and quartz accessibility.

faqItems.question: Is Comtesse a current Alpina collection?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Comtesse still appears as a current Alpina collection and current US product pages use the Comtesse name for ladies’ watches.

faqItems.question: Is Comtesse purely modern?
faqItems.answer: No. Alpina’s own historical material ties its women’s self-winding offer to 1963 and also names Comtesse among product lines used in the 1970s, before the line was reintroduced in modern form.

timeline.event: Gottlieb Hauser founds the Swiss Watchmakers Corporation (Union Horlogère Suisse) in Winterthur, establishing Alpina as a cooperative of watchmakers.
Alpina introduces the four pillars of a sport watch: anti-magnetic, water-resistant, shock-resistant, stainless steel — revolutionary standards decades ahead of their time.
Alpina creates the Alpina 4, setting the template for the modern sports watch.
Alpina ceases operations during the quartz crisis.
Frédérique Constant acquires Alpina, relaunching it with a fresh sporting identity.
Alpina launches the Horological Smartwatch — analogue Swiss watch with embedded activity tracking, without a digital screen.
Citizen Holdings acquires Frédérique Constant Group, including Alpina.
Expanded Alpiner Extreme with California dial variants. Debuted at Watches & Wonders Geneva 2025.
Launched Alpiner Extreme Solarmetre, brand first solar-powered collection (37.5mm, 10-month reserve in darkness).

faqItems.question: What makes Alpina watches special?
faqItems.answer: Alpina invented the concept of the modern sports watch in 1901, introducing anti-magnetic, shock-resistant, water-resistant construction decades before others. This functional innovation continues in every Alpiner and Startimer.

faqItems.question: Does Alpina make its own movements?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Alpina develops Swiss manufacture movements including the AL-710 and AL-718 pilot movement, produced at their manufacture in Plan-les-Ouates, Geneva.

faqItems.question: What is the price range for Alpina watches?
faqItems.answer: Most watches range from CHF 800 to CHF 3,000 — excellent value for Swiss-made sport watches with in-house movements.

faqItems.question: Is Alpina connected to Frédérique Constant?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Both brands are under Citizen Holdings since 2016, sharing the manufacture in Plan-les-Ouates, Geneva.

name: Alsta

hq.address: Baltic Chambers, 50 Wellington St, Glasgow G2 6HJ

description: Alsta is a vintage Swiss watch brand from La Chaux-de-Fonds, known primarily for the Nautoscaph diver watch from the late 1960s — famously associated with Steve McQueen, who was photographed wearing one at the Sebring 12 Hours. The brand represents a slice of 1960s professional diving history.
defunct_reason: Alsta ceased operations during the quartz crisis; the small La Chaux-de-Fonds dive watch specialist could not survive the collapse of demand for mechanical sports watches.

keyCollections.name: Nautoscaph
keyCollections.description: Alsta’s iconic skin-diver family, originally rooted in 1960s tool-watch design and revived in a modern form that keeps the line’s slim, adventure-ready character and heritage-driven identity.

keyCollections.name: Surf n Ski
keyCollections.description: Retro-styled dual-purpose sport watch line associated with Alsta’s heritage of robust, adventure-ready pieces designed to suit both aquatic and alpine environments.

timeline.event: Alsta established in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, producing sport and dive watches.
Nautoscaph diver watch introduced with the distinctive super-compressor case design.
The Nautoscaph appears on Richard Dreyfuss's wrist in the film Jaws, becoming one of cinema's most recognisable watch moments.
Brand revived by new owners, relaunching the Nautoscaph as a faithful reissue via Kickstarter.

faqItems.question: What is the Jaws connection?
faqItems.answer: In Steven Spielberg's 1975 Jaws, Richard Dreyfuss wears an Alsta Nautoscaph throughout the film. It's become one of the most famous movie watches in history.

faqItems.question: Is Alsta still making watches?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Revived in 2017, Alsta produces updated reissues of the Nautoscaph and Surf n Ski, staying true to the original 1960s designs.

name: ALTO
description: ALTO is an art-driven Swiss watch brand producing sculptural timepieces that blur the boundary between horology and fine art. Its ART-01 collection showcases bold dials and expressive design language inspired by contemporary artistic movements.

keyCollections.name: Sculptural Series
keyCollections.description: ALTO’s sculptural side is embodied by the ART 01 family, whose faceted sapphire, angular monobloc architecture, and art-first case design make the watch read like a small wearable sculpture as much as a contemporary mechanical watch.

referenceDetails.name: ALTO ART 01 First Edition
referenceDetails.note: Foundational expression of ALTO’s sculptural language, described by the brand as conceived from the outset as a single-block piece with a unique bevelled sapphire and sharply drawn case.

referenceDetails.name: ALTO ART 01 Monochrome Black
referenceDetails.note: 30-piece monochrome interpretation that emphasizes the family’s monolithic form with DLC-coated titanium and all-black execution.

referenceDetails.name: ALTO ART 01 Monochrome Grey
referenceDetails.note: 30-piece titanium variant that reframes the same case volume as a brutalist grey object, reinforcing the sculptural identity through material continuity.

timeline.event: ALTO launched the ART 01 as its debut watch, introducing the faceted sapphire-and-case architecture that defines the brand’s sculptural identity.
ALTO extended the design into Monochrome Black, using DLC-coated titanium to turn the ART 01 into a more explicitly monolithic object.
ALTO released Monochrome Grey, a matching 30-piece variant that highlighted the brutalist volume of the ART 01 case in bare grey titanium.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is the clearest lens through which to understand ALTO: the brand’s value proposition is not classical round-watch refinement but a sculptural, architecture-informed object whose case, sapphire, and dial are designed as one visual statement.

faqItems.question: What watch line represents ALTO’s sculptural approach?
faqItems.answer: The ART 01 line does. Its sharply faceted sapphire, angular case, and object-like presentation are the brand’s clearest sculptural statement.

faqItems.question: Are the monochrome models part of the sculptural story?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Monochrome Black and Monochrome Grey keep the ART 01 architecture intact while using black DLC and grey titanium to stress its monolithic form.

keyCollections.name: Limited Editions
keyCollections.description: ALTO’s limited-edition offering is currently expressed through small-run ART 01 variants that push the brand’s art-driven concept into collaborations and métiers d’art, including stone marquetry and artist-led sculptural executions rather than routine dial-color updates.

referenceDetails.name: ALTO ART 01 First Edition
referenceDetails.note: Launch reference for the ART 01 platform; grade 5 titanium case, A01 automatic micro-rotor movement, and the reverse-running seconds concept that defines the family.

referenceDetails.name: ALTO ART 01 Falcon Eye
referenceDetails.note: Limited to 12 pieces and presented by ALTO as its first 'Métier d'Art' piece, using falcon’s eye stone marquetry on the dial.

referenceDetails.name: ALTO x Bernar Venet ART 01
referenceDetails.note: Artist collaboration limited to 10 pieces in patinated bronze, translating Bernar Venet’s sculptural language into the ART 01 platform.

timeline.event: ALTO introduced the ART 01 and positioned it as the brand’s debut art-driven watch concept.
ALTO expanded ART 01 into the Falcon Eye, a 12-piece stone-marquetry edition presented as the maison’s first Métier d’Art piece.
ALTO unveiled the ART 01 Bernar Venet, a 10-piece artist collaboration in patinated bronze that sharpened the collection’s limited-edition identity.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: For ALTO, limited editions are not merely scarcity plays: they are the main vehicle for expressing the brand’s mix of independent horology, contemporary art, unusual materials, and highly specific creative partnerships within the ART 01 universe.

faqItems.question: What defines ALTO’s Limited Editions?
faqItems.answer: They are the small-run ART 01 executions that go beyond the standard titanium launch model through artist collaborations, métier d’art dial work, or unusual materials.

faqItems.question: Is Falcon Eye part of this limited-edition story?
faqItems.answer: Yes. ALTO presents Falcon Eye as a 12-piece ART 01 and describes it as the maison’s first Métier d’Art piece.

timeline.event: ALTO founded as a French SARL by Thibaud Guittard, headquartered in Paris.
ART-01 collection launched, blending horology with contemporary art.
Brand exhibited at Geneva Watch Days, expanding Swiss market presence.

faqItems.question: What makes ALTO different?
faqItems.answer: ALTO treats each watch as a wearable sculpture. The cases and dials are designed as fine-art objects first, timepieces second.

faqItems.question: Are ALTO watches functional daily wearers?
faqItems.answer: While fully functional with Swiss movements, ALTO watches are designed more as wearable art pieces — conversation starters rather than tool watches.

name: Amida
description: Amida is a historic Swiss watch brand known in the 1970s for the innovative Digitrend model, one of the world's first digital-display mechanical watches using a jumping hour window mechanism. The brand has been revived to celebrate this unique heritage in contemporary form.
defunct_reason: Amida ceased production around 1981 following the quartz crisis, which eliminated demand for its mechanical digital displays like the Digitrend.

keyCollections.name: Digitrend
keyCollections.description: AMIDA’s signature driver-style watch family, originally introduced in the 1970s and relaunched as a modern take on the mechanical digital-display concept that made the model distinctive.

keyCollections.name: Diver
keyCollections.description: Amida’s diver-focused collection, extending the brand’s revived Swiss identity with robust case construction and utility-first sports-watch styling for water-oriented use.

timeline.event: AMIDA marked its comeback on the official site, describing 2024 as the year of the brand’s return and the revival of the Digitrend line.
Amida SA founded in Grenchen, Switzerland, by Heinrich Brosi.
Introduces innovative automatic movements and begins exporting worldwide.
Launches the Digitrend — one of the world's first mechanical digital-display watches, a technical tour de force.
Quartz crisis forces production slowdown; the brand fades from the mainstream market.
Digitrend reissued for collectors, reviving interest in one of horology's most inventive 1970s designs.

faqItems.question: What was the Amida Digitrend?
faqItems.answer: A mechanical watch with a fully digital-style display — jumping hour and minute discs instead of hands. Introduced in 1974, it was years ahead of its time.

faqItems.question: Is Amida still active?
faqItems.answer: The original company wound down after the quartz crisis, but the Digitrend has been reissued and the brand's vintage pieces are prized by collectors.

name: Angelus
description: Angelus was founded in Le Locle in 1891 and became celebrated for its alarm complications and, notably, the first wristwatch chronograph with a seconds reset to zero in 1942. Revived in 2015 under the leadership of Frédéric Gasser, it now focuses on avant-garde skeletonised and high-complication pieces.
defunct_reason: Angelus, a specialist in alarm and chronograph complications since 1891, closed during the quartz crisis as demand for complex mechanical movements collapsed.
revival_attempt: Revived in 2015 by Frédéric Gasser and new investors in Le Locle, producing grand complications including tourbillons and skeletonised chronographs.

keyCollections.name: U10 Tourbillon Lumière
keyCollections.description: The U10 Tourbillon Lumière was the watch that relaunched modern Angelus in 2015, pairing a deconstructed rectangular architecture with an off-centred flying tourbillon, dead-beat seconds and a dramatic multi-window sapphire display inspired by vintage travel clocks but executed as contemporary haute horlogerie.

referenceDetails.name: U10 Tourbillon Lumière
referenceDetails.note: Launch limited edition in stainless steel; the rebirth model of revived Angelus.

image.alt: Angelus U10 Tourbillon Lumière front view

referenceDetails.name: Angelus U10 Tourbillon Lumière
referenceDetails.note: Baselworld 2015 launch piece with flying tourbillon, dead-beat seconds and 90-hour power reserve.

image.alt: Angelus U10 Tourbillon Lumière angled case view

referenceDetails.name: Tourbillon Lumière
referenceDetails.note: Angelus heritage page identifies the first revived Angelus model as the Tourbillon Lumière introduced in 2015.

image.alt: Angelus U10 Tourbillon Lumière side and tourbillon view

timeline.event: La Joux-Perret acquired the Angelus brand with the goal of developing a contemporary tourbillon-led collection in modern materials.
The first revived Angelus model, the Tourbillon Lumière, was introduced; Monochrome identifies this debut watch specifically as the U10 Tourbillon Lumière.
Angelus regrouped its contemporary tourbillons inside the L.A.B. collection, which the brand says continues the lineage of skeletonised tourbillons first introduced in 2015.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The U10 matters because it defined the revived Angelus not as a retro chronograph remake but as an experimental, architectural high-watchmaking brand built around transparent structures, unusual displays and tourbillon theatre.

image.alt: Angelus U10 Tourbillon Lumière hero image

faqItems.question: When was the Angelus U10 Tourbillon Lumière introduced?
faqItems.answer: Angelus heritage material and launch coverage place the U10 Tourbillon Lumière in 2015.

faqItems.question: Why is the U10 important in modern Angelus history?
faqItems.answer: It was the first major watch of the revived Angelus era and established the brand's contemporary, skeletonised tourbillon direction rather than a simple vintage reissue.

keyCollections.name: U20 Ultra-Skeleton
keyCollections.description: The U20 Ultra-Skeleton followed the U10 as Angelus’s second modern flagship, using a sapphire main plate, blued titanium bridges and a carbon-composite-and-titanium case to create a tourbillon movement that appears to float inside the watch.

referenceDetails.name: U20 Ultra-Skeleton Tourbillon
referenceDetails.note: Launch limited edition in NPT carbon-fibre and titanium; introduced ahead of Baselworld 2016.

image.alt: Angelus U20 Ultra-Skeleton Tourbillon angled front view

referenceDetails.name: Angelus U20 Ultra-Skeleton Tourbillon
referenceDetails.note: Launch article describes the sapphire base plate and floating movement architecture.

image.alt: Angelus U20 Ultra-Skeleton Tourbillon dial and movement view

referenceDetails.name: Ultra-Skeleton Tourbillon
referenceDetails.note: Represents the second step in revived Angelus’s modern, non-vintage-led tourbillon strategy after the U10.

image.alt: Angelus U20 Ultra-Skeleton Tourbillon side profile

timeline.event: Angelus returned with the U10 Tourbillon Lumière, establishing the revived brand's contemporary tourbillon direction.
The U20 Ultra-Skeleton Tourbillon was introduced as the second major model of the revived brand and officially positioned for Baselworld 2016.

Angelus's current L.A.B. collection states that its contemporary tourbillons continue the lineage of skeletonised tourbillons first introduced in 2015, placing models like the U20 in that core design ancestry.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The U20 is one of the clearest statements of revived Angelus design language: extreme transparency, architectural bridge work and a floating flying tourbillon that turned the brand’s technical ambitions into a recognizable visual identity.

faqItems.question: When was the Angelus U20 Ultra-Skeleton introduced?
faqItems.answer: Launch coverage ties the U20 Ultra-Skeleton Tourbillon to Baselworld 2016, making 2016 the documented introduction year.

faqItems.question: What defines the U20 Ultra-Skeleton visually?
faqItems.answer: Its movement is built around a transparent sapphire main plate with blued titanium bridges, creating the impression that the gears and flying tourbillon are suspended in space.

keyCollections.name: U30 Diver Tourbillon
keyCollections.description: 300m dive-rated tourbillon — an audacious combination of professional tool watch and grand complication.

keyCollections.name: U41 Big Date Tourbillon Rattrapante
keyCollections.description: Split-seconds chronograph with tourbillon and big date — technical bravado in a contemporary case.

keyCollections.name: U50 Executive Tourbillon Ultra-Slim
keyCollections.description: Dress tourbillon at the pinnacle of slim-case construction, echoing Angelus's historical expertise.

timeline.event: Angelus Watch Co founded in Le Locle by the Stolz brothers, beginning a tradition of alarm and complex complications.
Angelus creates the world's first wristwatch chronograph with split-seconds reset to zero — a landmark in complication history.
Angelus produces the first multi-axial tourbillon wristwatch.
Angelus ceases production during the quartz crisis.
Angelus revived by Frédéric Gasser in Le Locle with a mandate to produce high-complication modern pieces.
First contemporary Angelus collection launched at Watches & Wonders, featuring skeletonised tourbillons.
The U30 Diver Tourbillon unveiled — 300m-rated dive watch with a flying tourbillon.

faqItems.question: What made the original Angelus historically significant?
faqItems.answer: Angelus pioneered mechanical alarm wristwatches and, most notably, produced the world's first wristwatch chronograph with split-seconds reset to zero in 1942.

faqItems.question: When was Angelus revived and why?
faqItems.answer: Revived in 2015 by Frédéric Gasser in Le Locle — the same Swiss town where the brand was founded. The goal: honour the original's pioneering spirit in grand complications.

faqItems.question: What is the price range for Angelus watches?
faqItems.answer: Angelus occupies the high-end independent sector. Watches typically range from CHF 20,000 to CHF 80,000+, with grand complications exceeding CHF 100,000.

faqItems.question: Where are Angelus watches made?
faqItems.answer: The revived Angelus is manufactured in Le Locle, Switzerland, with all movements developed in-house.

name: Anoma

hq.address: Carpenter Court, 1 Maple Road, Bramhall, Stockport

description: Anoma is an independent watch brand known for artistic, sculptural timepieces that challenge conventional watch design. The brand produces pieces with highly artistic dials and unusual case forms, targeting collectors drawn to watchmaking as wearable art.

keyCollections.name: Sculptural
keyCollections.description: Anoma’s sculptural watches are conceived as wearable objects rather than conventional round watches, with organic case shapes and design-led forms that intentionally break the standard mould of traditional watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: Concept
keyCollections.description: Concept-driven pieces from Anoma that emphasize experimental, art-forward watch design and push beyond conventional wristwatch form, aligning with the brand’s sculptural, anomaly-led identity.

timeline.event: Anoma founded as an independent artistic watch brand focused on sculptural, unconventional timepieces.
First pieces unveiled, establishing the brand's identity in avant-garde horology.

faqItems.question: What does Anoma mean?
faqItems.answer: Derived from 'anomaly,' reflecting the brand's mission to create watches that defy convention and challenge expectations.

faqItems.question: Who is Anoma for?
faqItems.answer: Collectors who appreciate watchmaking as an art form and seek pieces that stand apart from mainstream designs.

name: anOrdain
description: AnOrdain is a small Glasgow-based watchmaker founded in 2016, best known for its enamel dials produced using the vitreous enamel technique — rare at any price point. The brand produces watches in very limited numbers, making them highly sought after by collectors who value craftsmanship over prestige.

hq.address: Glasgow, Glasgow City, Scotland, United Kingdom

keyCollections.description: anOrdain’s foundational watch, using a restrained round case and map-inspired numerals as the main canvas for the Glasgow maker’s hand-crafted vitreous enamel dials, including opaque and fumé executions across multiple sizes and movement options.

anOrdain launched the Model 1 Fumé, extending the collection with what it describes as the world’s first fumé enamel dial in the format.
anOrdain expanded the Model 1 into Small, Medium and Large sizes, adding new movement choices and introducing the Oxblood dial to the collection.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Model 1 is the watch that introduced anOrdain to the market and remains the clearest expression of the brand’s identity: hand-made vitreous enamel dials, map-inspired typography, and small-scale Scottish craft presented in a relatively accessible independent package.

faqItems.question: What defines the anOrdain Model 1?
faqItems.answer: It is anOrdain’s debut watch and the design that introduced the brand, built around hand-crafted vitreous enamel dials with map-inspired numerals and hands.

faqItems.question: Does the Model 1 only exist in one size or one dial style?
faqItems.answer: No. The current family spans Small, Medium and Large cases, core opaque-enamel colours, and a Model 1 Fumé branch with smoked-gradient enamel dials.

The collection was launched in 2019 and substantially revised in 2022 with a larger 39.5mm option, updated bespoke numerals, new colours, and evolved luminous hands.

timeline.event: anOrdain launched the original Model 2 as its field-watch interpretation with vitreous enamel dial work.
Hodinkee described the brown fumé Model 2 as the last design iteration before a full revamp, confirming the first-generation collection was still evolving.
anOrdain introduced the revised Model 2, adding a 39.5mm Large case, updated bespoke numerals, new colours, and heat-treated luminous hands.
The Model 2 platform expanded again with the launch of Model 2 Porcelain, showing the case had become the base for new dial materials beyond enamel.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Model 2 is the bridge between anOrdain’s artisanal dial identity and a more practical, sportier everyday watch format. It also serves as the architectural base for later material experiments, including porcelain, making it one of the brand’s key long-running pillars.
keyCollections.positioningOrTimeline: Launched in 2019 as the field-watch counterpart to Model 1, then revised in 2022 with a larger case and more mature dial/hand language. The collection remains central to anOrdain’s catalogue and later became the foundation for the Porcelain line.

faqItems.question: How is the Model 2 positioned within anOrdain’s range?
faqItems.answer: It is anOrdain’s field-watch collection, combining a more robust steel case and luminous details with the brand’s in-house dial craftsmanship.

faqItems.question: What changed in the revised Model 2?
faqItems.answer: The 2022 revision added a 39.5mm Large size, new enamel colours, updated numeral design, and evolved heat-treated hands with luminous tips.

keyCollections.name: Porcelain
keyCollections.description: anOrdain’s Porcelain line is a distinct in-house dial material programme built around true glazed porcelain rather than enamel or ceramic sheet substitutes. Introduced in 2025 on the Model 2 platform, it was developed over several years with research trips to Limoges and collaboration with potters in Stoke-on-Trent, then executed in-house by porcelain artist Cara Louise.

image.alt: anOrdain porcelain dial mould in workshop

referenceDetails.name: Model 2 Porcelain
referenceDetails.note: Official product page for the porcelain launch model; describes the watch as a true porcelain dial developed in-house over several years with Cara Louise making each dial by hand.

image.alt: anOrdain porcelain dial mould during production

referenceDetails.name: Model 2 Porcelain 36mm
