newsItems.title: Introducing: The Cartier Panthère De Cartier Collection, Re-Introduced For 2017
newsItems.summary: Hodinkee covered the return of Panthère de Cartier, noting the collection’s original 1983 launch and its reintroduction as a Cartier focus for 2017.

newsItems.title: Hands-On review of the new large model Panthère de Cartier
newsItems.summary: Hodinkee examined the large-model expansion and framed the Panthère as Cartier’s mass-appeal jewelry-watch hybrid icon.

newsItems.title: Watches and Wonders 2025: Panthère de Cartier watches: Jewelry transformations
newsItems.summary: Cartier presented new Panthère jewelry-watch interpretations combining lacquer, pavé diamonds and spessartites in abstract animal-pattern compositions.

newsItems.title: Revolution Awards 2025: Best Jewelry Watch — Cartier Panthère de Cartier
newsItems.summary: Revolution named the Panthère de Cartier Best Jewelry Watch in its 2025 awards, emphasizing its integration of jewelry design and watchmaking.

faqItems.question: When was the Cartier Panthère introduced?
faqItems.answer: The Panthère de Cartier watch collection was launched in 1983. Cartier later reintroduced it in 2017 after it had left regular production in the early 2000s.

faqItems.question: Why is it called Panthère?
faqItems.answer: Cartier says the watch takes its name from the bracelet of the same name; the ultra-flexible linked construction is meant to echo the movements of the maison’s emblematic panther.

faqItems.question: Is Panthère a watch or a jewelry watch?
faqItems.answer: Both. Cartier explicitly positions Panthère de Cartier as a jewelry watch, and that dual identity is central to the collection’s design appeal.

faqItems.question: What movement does the modern Panthère use?
faqItems.answer: Current core Panthère models use quartz movements.

funFacts.title: Bracelet as namesake
funFacts.body: The Panthère’s name refers to its bracelet, whose flexible construction is central to the design alongside the case.

funFacts.title: Large steel model
funFacts.body: The current range includes a Large steel model alongside smaller Panthère references.

timeline.event: Louis-François Cartier takes over his master's workshop in Paris, founding the Maison Cartier.
Louis Cartier creates the Santos wristwatch for aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont, pioneering the modern wristwatch.
The Tank watch is designed, inspired by the aerial view of WWI Renault FT tanks.
Cartier creates the Crash watch in London with its melted, surrealist case shape.
Cartier unveils the ID Two concept watch with no lubrication and no escapement, pushing horological innovation.
Santos de Cartier is relaunched with the QuickSwitch strap system and SmartLink bracelet adjustment.
Revived Tank a Guichets jumping hour at Watches & Wonders in gold and platinum variants including 200-piece limited edition.
Introduced first Santos de Cartier with full titanium bracelet. Expanded Panthere with gem-set animal-print models.

faqItems.question: Is Cartier a jeweller or a watchmaker?
faqItems.answer: Both. Founded as a jeweller in 1847, Cartier has been a leading watchmaker since 1904, producing both high-jewellery pieces and serious horological complications.

faqItems.question: Who owns Cartier today?
faqItems.answer: Cartier is the flagship brand of the Richemont Group, the Swiss luxury conglomerate founded by Johann Rupert.

pronunciation.note: The final syllable carries the French “-ier” sound.

funFacts.title: Design-first watchmaking
funFacts.body: Cartier is one of the few maisons whose most important watches are design icons as much as technical objects.

funFacts.title: Early wristwatch history
funFacts.body: The Santos is tied to aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont and the early move from pocket watches to wristwatches.

funFacts.title: Jeweller and watchmaker
funFacts.body: Cartier sits unusually comfortably across high jewelry and serious watch collecting.

whyMatters: Cartier is one of the few maisons whose most important watches are design icons as much as technical objects.

name: Casio
description: Casio is a Japanese electronics company founded in 1946 by Tadao Kashio in Tokyo, producing the world's first electronic calculator in 1957 before entering the watch market. Today Casio produces watches across multiple lines including G-Shock, Pro Trek, and Edifice, with the G-Shock — introduced in 1983 — achieving iconic status as a shock-resistant tool watch.

keyCollections.name: G-Shock
keyCollections.description: Casio’s iconic shock-resistant watch family, launched in 1983 and positioned around durability, rugged styling, and broad sub-collections spanning everyday, sport, outdoor, and premium full-metal designs.

keyCollections.name: Edifice
keyCollections.description: Casio’s motorsport-inspired analogue-digital watch line for buyers who want a sporty, technical look with professional styling and a performance-oriented identity across the collection.

keyCollections.name: Pro Trek
keyCollections.description: Casio’s outdoor adventure watch family built around hiking and climbing use cases, typically emphasizing ABC sensor features, solar power, and a practical tool-watch identity for nature-focused wearers.

keyCollections.name: Oceanus
keyCollections.description: Premium Casio titanium watch line built around slim cases, refined finishing, and high-tech convenience such as GPS, Bluetooth, solar charging, and radio timekeeping depending on model. Oceanus is positioned as a dressier, more technically advanced family within Casio’s watch portfolio.

timeline.event: Tadao Kashio founds Kashio Seisakujo in Tokyo as a subcontractor manufacturing parts.
Casio releases the world's first compact, all-electric calculator, establishing the company's electronics expertise.
Casio launches its first digital watch, the Casiotron, featuring an automatic calendar.
G-Shock debuts, designed by Kikuo Ibe to survive a 10-metre drop, 10-bar water resistance, and 10-year battery life.
Baby-G launches as a smaller, fashion-forward take on the G-Shock for women.
Introduction of GPS Hybrid Wave Ceptor technology in the G-Shock line.
Launched Summer Resort 2026 collection featuring color-changing polarized glass across compact models.

faqItems.question: Are Casio watches considered luxury?
faqItems.answer: Casio is primarily known for affordable, durable, and technologically advanced watches. While not luxury in the traditional Swiss sense, premium lines like G-Shock MR-G and Oceanus command higher prices.

faqItems.question: Where are Casio watches made?
faqItems.answer: Most Casio watches are made in factories across Japan, Thailand, and China. Premium models are assembled at the Yamagata factory in Japan.

name: Casio G-Shock
description: The Casio G-Shock was launched in 1983 by engineer Kikuo Ibe with the goal of creating an indestructible watch, resulting in the iconic DW-5000C that could survive a ten-metre drop. The G-Shock line has since expanded to hundreds of models and collaborations, becoming one of the best-selling watch families in history.

keyCollections.name: MR-G
keyCollections.description: G-SHOCK’s flagship full-metal line, positioned by Casio as the most premium expression of the brand with advanced materials, artisanal finishing, and a strong emphasis on Japanese craftsmanship.

keyCollections.name: MT-G
keyCollections.description: Metal Twisted G-SHOCK collection that blends stainless steel with resin or carbon-reinforced structures for premium toughness, refined finishing, and the brand’s signature shock resistance.

keyCollections.name: Frogman
keyCollections.description: G-SHOCK’s professional dive-watch family, built around ISO 200-meter water resistance and a long-running underwater tool-watch identity that Casio describes as the Frogman collection.

keyCollections.name: Casioak (GA-2100)
keyCollections.description: The octagonal GA-2100 family from G-SHOCK, nicknamed Casioak by enthusiasts for its Royal Oak-like bezel shape, and presented by Casio as the slim 2100 series with the brand’s shock-resistant structure.

timeline.event: Casio engineer Kikuo Ibe drops his father's watch and begins the 'Project Team Tough' to create an unbreakable watch.
The first G-Shock, the DW-5000C, launches with the Triple 10 concept: 10m drop, 10 bar, 10-year battery.
First Frogman (DW-6300) launches, establishing G-Shock as a serious tool watch for divers.
MR-G line debuts as the premium full-metal G-Shock, introducing titanium construction.
G-Shock Connected app launches, adding Bluetooth smartphone link across the range.
GA-2100 'CasiOak' launches, becoming one of the best-selling G-Shock models ever.
Over 30 new releases announced for 2026 including Summer Resort collection with polarized vapor deposition glass.

faqItems.question: What makes G-Shock so tough?
faqItems.answer: A hollow case structure with the module floating inside on cushioning material absorbs shocks. Combined with resin construction and screw-back cases, it exceeds military durability standards.

faqItems.question: Is G-Shock a separate brand from Casio?
faqItems.answer: No. G-Shock is a product line within Casio, though it has its own identity, marketing, and dedicated fan community.

faqItems.question: Who created G-Shock?
faqItems.answer: G-Shock was created by Casio engineer Kikuo Ibe, who in 1981 set out to build a watch that could survive a 10-metre drop. After over 200 prototypes and two years of development, the first G-Shock (DW-5000C) was released in April 1983, featuring a hollow case structure that cushioned the module inside.

name: Cédric Johner
description: Cédric Johner is a Swiss independent watchmaker and jeweller with over 30 years of experience, creating unique timepieces entirely by hand without computer-aided tools. Each watch is conceived as a singular, never-repeated piece that unites refined aesthetics with traditional artisanal watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: Abyss
keyCollections.description: Diver's watch with a distinctive cushion case and bold maritime aesthetic, showcasing Johner's independent spirit.

keyCollections.name: Colosso
keyCollections.description: Oversized sport watch with a powerful presence, blending contemporary design with haute horlogerie finishing.

timeline.event: Cédric Johner, a Swiss-born independent watchmaker, founds his eponymous brand in Geneva.
Launches the Abyss collection, establishing a bold design identity in the independent watchmaking scene.
Expands distribution in Asia and the Middle East, gaining recognition for distinctive case architecture.

faqItems.question: Who is Cédric Johner?
faqItems.answer: A Swiss independent watchmaker based in Geneva who creates bold, distinctively designed timepieces in small production runs, focusing on strong case architecture and diver-inspired aesthetics.

faqItems.question: Where can you buy Cédric Johner watches?
faqItems.answer: Through select authorised retailers in Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, as well as directly through the brand. Production numbers are limited.

name: Certina
description: Certina was founded in Grenchen, Switzerland in 1888 and has been part of the Swatch Group since 1983. The brand focuses on robust, reliable sport watches at mid-range price points, most notably its DS (Double Security) line, and maintains a strong presence in cycling and motorsport partnerships.

keyCollections.name: DS Action
keyCollections.description: Certina DS Action is the brand's sport-focused collection, spanning modern diver, GMT, chronograph, and everyday references under the Double Security design philosophy.

referenceDetails.name: Compact titanium diver
referenceDetails.note: Official current DS Action variant listed by Certina as a titanium 38 mm diver.

image.alt: Certina DS Action Diver 38mm Titanium watch

referenceDetails.name: Automatic GMT
referenceDetails.note: Official current GMT model in the DS Action family, using Certina's Powermatic 80 naming.

image.alt: Certina DS Action GMT Powermatic 80 watch

referenceDetails.name: Sport chronograph
referenceDetails.note: Official current chronograph variant shown within Certina's DS Action collection page.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: DS Action is Certina's broad sport-watch workhorse, where the brand concentrates its diver, travel, and chronograph options around robust everyday specifications.

faqItems.question: What is Certina DS Action?
faqItems.answer: It is Certina's sport collection, covering dive watches, GMT pieces, chronographs, and practical everyday models.

faqItems.question: Which DS Action references are official current examples?
faqItems.answer: Certina's collection page lists examples such as DS Action Diver 38mm Titanium, DS Action GMT Powermatic 80, and DS Action Chrono.

faqItems.question: What does DS refer to in DS Action?
faqItems.answer: DS refers to Certina's Double Security concept, the brand's long-running emphasis on water and shock resistance.

keyCollections.name: DS Podium
keyCollections.description: Certina DS Podium is the brand's sporty-elegant precision family, combining DS Concept case construction, quartz and Precidrive movements, 100 m water resistance, chronograph, GMT, and clean 40 mm three-hand references.

referenceDetails.name: DS Podium Chronograph 1/10 sec
referenceDetails.note: A blue-dial DS Podium chronograph with 1/10-second real-time display, Precidrive quartz technology, 11.83 mm height, and 10 bar water resistance.

image.alt: Certina DS Podium Chronograph 1/10 sec watch

referenceDetails.name: DS Podium 40mm
referenceDetails.note: A blue-dial DS Podium 40 mm with date at 6 o'clock, Precidrive quartz technology, 9.42 mm height, 20 mm lug spacing, and 10 bar water resistance.

referenceDetails.name: DS Podium GMT
referenceDetails.note: A blue-dial DS Podium GMT with second-time-zone display, Precidrive quartz technology, date window, 10.40 mm height, and 10 bar water resistance.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: DS Podium is useful as a collection page because it gathers Certina's sport-elegant precision watches into one searchable family, spanning timing, travel-time, and everyday three-hand formats while keeping the brand's DS Concept durability language.

image.alt: Certina DS Podium Chronograph 1/10 sec watch

faqItems.question: What kind of watch is Certina DS Podium?
faqItems.answer: It is Certina's sporty-elegant precision family, covering chronograph, GMT, and three-hand models.

faqItems.question: What is Precidrive in the DS Podium?
faqItems.answer: Certina describes Precidrive as quartz technology that delivers chronometer-level precision, with a deviation of about +/-10 seconds per year.

faqItems.question: How water resistant are the checked DS Podium references?
faqItems.answer: The checked official DS Podium references are listed with 10 bar, or 100 m, water resistance.

funFacts.title: DS Concept
funFacts.body: Certina's DS Concept section lists a sapphire crystal, crown gaskets, and reinforced caseback as part of the construction story.

funFacts.title: Functional breadth
funFacts.body: The official DS Podium family includes chronograph timing, GMT travel-time, and slim three-hand date executions.

keyCollections.name: DS-1
keyCollections.description: Certina’s DS-1 is the brand’s classic dress-leaning mechanical line: clean, versatile, and rooted in the DS Concept’s durability story while remaining positioned as an attainable Swiss-made everyday watch family.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: DS-1 is one of Certina’s key heritage-driven dress collections, translating the 1959 DS durability concept into a refined, broadly wearable mid-market mechanical line.

referenceDetails.name: DS-1 Powermatic 80
referenceDetails.note: Core three-hand mechanical DS-1 variant currently shown in the collection.

referenceDetails.name: DS-1 Big Date Powermatic 80
referenceDetails.note: Big-date variant currently listed in the DS-1 collection.

referenceDetails.name: DS-1 38mm
referenceDetails.note: Smaller unisex execution currently listed in the collection.

timeline.event: Certina’s current DS-1 collection page shows multiple active DS-1 references including Powermatic 80, Big Date, 38mm, Skeleton, Chrono Auto, and Day Date.
Certina’s DS Concept page states the Double Security concept has been synonymous with durability since 1959 and remains refined to this day.
Certina’s history page identifies the premiere of the DS Concept in 1959, with the first Certina with DS Concept unveiled that year.

faqItems.question: Is DS-1 a modern or historic Certina line?
faqItems.answer: It is a modern collection built around Certina’s historic DS durability concept and presented as a refined, heritage-linked mechanical family.

faqItems.question: What defines DS-1 positioning?
faqItems.answer: Classic styling, Swiss mechanical movements, and the DS Concept’s emphasis on robustness and everyday wearability.

timeline.event: Brothers Adolf and Alfred Kurth found Kurth Frères in Grenchen, Switzerland.
The company adopts the name Certina and registers the brand with its distinctive turtle logo.
Certina introduces the DS (Double Security) concept, a gasket and case-back system providing superior water and shock resistance.
The DS-2 sets a world record, surviving a fall from a plane at 60m altitude and continuing to run.
Certina becomes part of the Swatch Group (then SMH), securing its future during the quartz crisis.
Certina adopts Powermatic 80 movements across its automatic range, offering 80-hour power reserves at accessible prices.
Launched DS-X quartz GMT sports watch. Updated DS Action Diver 38mm Powermatic 80 in five references. Revived DS Cascadeur for 30th anniversary.

faqItems.question: What does DS stand for in Certina watches?
faqItems.answer: DS stands for 'Double Security,' Certina's patented system combining a reinforced case-back with special gaskets for enhanced water and shock resistance.

faqItems.question: Is Certina part of the Swatch Group?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Certina sits in the Swatch Group's mid-range segment alongside brands like Hamilton and Mido, using ETA and Powermatic movements.

faqItems.question: What is Certina's heritage in sport and diving?
faqItems.answer: Certina has a long association with sport and diving, particularly through its DS (Double Security) concept introduced in 1959. The brand has been a partner of various motorsport events and diving expeditions, and its DS Action Diver line continues this heritage with robust, ISO 6425-certified dive watches within Swatch Group's mid-range positioning.

name: Champs-Élysées
description: Inspired by childhood travels between Switzerland and France, vivid memories gave rise to the vision behind Champs-Élysées — a Swiss brand that captures the romance and elegance of that iconic Paris avenue. Each timepiece blends Swiss precision with French aesthetic inspiration, for those who carry a little Parisian magic on their wrist.

keyCollections.name: Classic
keyCollections.description: Elegant dress watches inspired by Parisian refinement, featuring clean dials and slim profiles.

timeline.event: Champs Élysées is established as a watch brand evoking the elegance of the famous Parisian avenue.

faqItems.question: What is Champs Élysées watches?
faqItems.answer: A small watch brand that takes its name and inspiration from the iconic Parisian boulevard, producing classically styled timepieces.

faqItems.question: What type of timepieces does Champs-Élysées offer?
faqItems.answer: Champs-Élysées is a watch brand that draws its name and aesthetic inspiration from the famous Parisian avenue. The brand offers timepieces that blend French elegance with watchmaking tradition, targeting customers who appreciate a sophisticated, Parisian-inspired design sensibility.

faqItems.question: Where is Champs-Élysées available?
faqItems.answer: Champs-Élysées watches are available through select retailers and online channels. The brand maintains a curated distribution approach aligned with its positioning as a distinctive, design-focused watch brand.

name: Chanel
description: Chanel entered watchmaking in 1987 and produces its timepieces in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, through its manufacture Chanel Horlogerie. The brand is notable for its bold, fashion-forward designs — particularly the J12 ceramic watch — as well as its development of in-house movements in partnership with Renaud & Papi.

keyCollections.name: J12
keyCollections.description: CHANEL’s signature ceramic sports watch collection, launched in 2000 and repeatedly updated through new calibers and sizes; the J12 is positioned as the House’s first unisex sports watch and a flagship for its ceramic expertise.

referenceDetails.name: J12 Watch Caliber 12.2, 33 MM - Black ceramic
referenceDetails.note: Current official CHANEL product page for a 33 mm J12 with Caliber 12.2.

referenceDetails.name: J12 Chronograph Watch, 41 mm - Black ceramic
referenceDetails.note: Chronograph variant demonstrating the wider J12 family and its sporty positioning.

referenceDetails.name: J12 28 mm watch - Black ceramic & Steel
referenceDetails.note: Smaller current-size J12 variant showing the collection’s size breadth.

timeline.event: CHANEL launched the J12, a ceramic watch that became a house icon.
CHANEL’s official communications noted the J12 relaunch with the Caliber 12.1 movement designed by Kenissi.
CHANEL’s current watch pages continue to describe the J12 as the first unisex sports watch by CHANEL.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The J12 is CHANEL’s best-known watch icon and a key proof point for how the House turned ceramic into a signature material in modern luxury watchmaking.

faqItems.question: What makes the J12 important?
faqItems.answer: CHANEL describes it as the first unisex sports watch by the House, and it is the model most closely associated with CHANEL ceramic watchmaking.

faqItems.question: Is the J12 still current?
faqItems.answer: Yes. CHANEL’s official site still lists multiple J12 references across different sizes and complications.

keyCollections.name: Première
keyCollections.description: CHANEL’s original women’s watch collection, introduced in 1987, defined by an octagonal case inspired by the N°5 bottle stopper and a jewelry-like bracelet treatment that has evolved through chain, ceramic, and strap interpretations.

referenceDetails.name: Première Ceramic Watch Black Ceramic & Steel - H2163
referenceDetails.note: Official current Première ceramic execution with diamonds and black lacquered dial.

referenceDetails.name: Première Ceramic Watch White Ceramic & Steel - H2132
referenceDetails.note: Official current white ceramic Première variant.

referenceDetails.name: Première Galon watch - Yellow gold
referenceDetails.note: Recent Première-family interpretation showing the collection’s ongoing evolution beyond the classic bracelet watch format.

timeline.event: CHANEL created its first watch for women: the Première.
The octagonal case was inspired by the stopper of the N°5 fragrance bottle.
CHANEL’s financial results press release referenced the launch of the PREMIÈRE GALON, indicating ongoing collection development.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Première is the foundational CHANEL watch line for women and the clearest bridge between the House’s fashion codes and its watchmaking identity.

faqItems.question: What inspired the Première case shape?
faqItems.answer: CHANEL says the octagonal case evokes the stopper of the N°5 fragrance bottle.

faqItems.question: Why is Première important in CHANEL watch history?
faqItems.answer: It is the House’s first watch for women and remains a core symbol of CHANEL’s jewelry-watch language.

image.alt: Chanel Première watch with octagonal black dial and gold-and-leather chain bracelet
image.source: Chanel official product image via Première collection/product page

keyCollections.name: BOY·FRIEND
keyCollections.description: Rectangular CHANEL watch collection launched in 2015 that blends masculine watch codes with the House’s feminine elegance; its customizable straps, clean geometry, and androgynous styling make it one of the brand’s most distinctive modern watch families.

referenceDetails.name: BOY·FRIEND Watch Small version, steel, quilted pattern calfskin strap and second strap included
referenceDetails.note: Small steel version with quilted calfskin strap; official CHANEL product page confirms the BOY·FRIEND naming and current retail presentation.

referenceDetails.name: BOY·FRIEND Watch Medium version, steel, quilted pattern calfskin strap and second strap included
referenceDetails.note: Medium steel version with interchangeable strap system; official CHANEL page describes the collection as bold and restrained.

referenceDetails.name: BOY·FRIEND Watch Small version, BEIGE GOLD and diamonds, quilted pattern calfskin strap and second strap included
referenceDetails.note: Precious-metal/dress interpretation showing the collection’s range beyond steel models.

timeline.event: CHANEL states the original alligator leather strap part of the BOY·FRIEND watch was created in 2015.
The collection established a rectangular, gender-blurring aesthetic built around balance between boldness and restraint.
CHANEL continues to sell multiple BOY·FRIEND executions in steel, BEIGE GOLD, diamonds, and strap variants on its official watch pages.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: BOY·FRIEND is CHANEL’s clearest modern case study in translating couture-style codes into a unisex watch language, making it useful for tracking how the House balances fashion identity with watchmaking breadth.

faqItems.question: When was BOY·FRIEND introduced?
faqItems.answer: CHANEL’s current BOY·FRIEND pages point to 2015 as the creation year for the original BOY·FRIEND strap family, which anchors the collection’s modern launch story.

faqItems.question: What defines the BOY·FRIEND style?
faqItems.answer: A rectangular case, restrained geometry, and a deliberately androgynous design language that CHANEL describes as a blend of boldness and restraint.

keyCollections.name: Monsieur de CHANEL
keyCollections.description: CHANEL’s men’s haute horlogerie collection built around a circular case, jumping hour, and retrograde minute display; it is positioned as a technically ambitious line with front-to-back design symmetry and an in-house movement story.

referenceDetails.name: Monsieur Watch White gold, opaline dial with jumping hour and 240° retrograde minute
referenceDetails.note: Official CHANEL product page for the white-gold Monsieur with jumping hour and retrograde minute display.

referenceDetails.name: Monsieur Watch BEIGE GOLD, opaline dial with jumping hour and 240° retrograde minute
referenceDetails.note: BEIGE GOLD Monsieur variant listed under the collection hub.

referenceDetails.name: Monsieur Watch Platinum and Grand Feu enamel dial with jumping hour and 240° retrograde minute
referenceDetails.note: Platinum version showing the collection’s high-complication positioning.

timeline.event: CHANEL’s reporting describes La MONTRE MONSIEUR as the first CHANEL watch with a movement, anchoring the collection’s modern debut story.
The Monsieur line established CHANEL’s digital-inspired display language with jumping hour and retrograde minutes.
CHANEL continues to present Monsieur de CHANEL as a current men’s collection with multiple references and materials.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Monsieur de CHANEL is the House’s most explicit statement of technical watchmaking ambition, useful for distinguishing CHANEL’s complication-led pieces from its fashion-first watch icons.

faqItems.question: What complication defines Monsieur de CHANEL?
faqItems.answer: The signature display pairs a jumping hour with a retrograde minute, presented in a circular, highly graphic layout.

faqItems.question: Is Monsieur de CHANEL still offered?
faqItems.answer: Yes. CHANEL’s official collection page still lists the Monsieur de CHANEL family and multiple current references.

timeline.event: Coco Chanel opens her first millinery shop in Paris, beginning the Chanel fashion empire.
Chanel enters watchmaking with the Première, inspired by the Place Vendôme and the N°5 cap.
The J12 launches, making high-tech ceramic a desirable material in luxury watchmaking.
Monsieur de Chanel debuts with the in-house Calibre 1, Chanel's first proprietary men's movement.
The J12 is redesigned with the in-house Calibre 12.1 (based on Kenissi), marking a new era of horological independence.
Celebrated J12 25th anniversary with J12 Bleu in new matte blue ceramic. Became first-ever title sponsor of the Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race.

faqItems.question: Does Chanel make its own watch movements?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Chanel co-owns the Kenissi manufacture (with Tudor/Rolex Group) and has developed proprietary calibres like the Calibre 1 and Calibre 12.1.

faqItems.question: Is the Chanel J12 a serious watch?
faqItems.answer: Absolutely. The J12 is widely regarded as one of the most important watches of the 21st century, pioneering ceramic as a luxury material and now housing manufacture movements.

faqItems.question: What is the Chanel Première watch?
faqItems.answer: The Première, launched in 1987, was Chanel's first watch and remains an icon. Designed to evoke the stopper of the No. 5 perfume bottle and the octagonal shape of Place Vendôme, it established Chanel as a serious player in watchmaking. The Première is offered in various sizes and complications, including the ultra-thin Édition Originale.

name: Charles Girardier
description: Charles Girardier is a revived Geneva watchmaking house with roots dating to 1809, a fine maison that lay dormant since the death of its founder in 1839 and has been reawakened with exceptional in-house calibres. The Signature Mysterieuse and Synchronaut GMT collections honour the timeless tradition of Genevan haute horlogerie.

keyCollections.description: Core Charles Girardier collection built around the revived house’s signature mysterious monogram and flying-tourbillon craftsmanship, expressed through Geneva-made haute horlogerie references with guilloché and Grand Feu enamel work.

referenceDetails.name: Signature Mystérieuse®, Flying Tourbillon
referenceDetails.note: 41 mm flagship reference in white gold; the brand describes it as the iconic Signature Mystérieuse model with flying tourbillon and Grand Feu enamel.

referenceDetails.name: Ice Blue
referenceDetails.note: 37 mm white-gold variant from the 1809 Signature Mystérieuse collection; the brand associates this reference with the GPHG-winning Fleur de Sel lineage.

referenceDetails.name: Green Grey
referenceDetails.note: 37 mm rose-gold variant listed by the brand within the 1809 Signature Mystérieuse collection.

timeline.event: The brand’s official site presents the 1809 Signature Mystérieuse line as an established core collection with multiple 37 mm and 41 mm variants.
Charles Girardier’s movement page details the CG SM-1809 caliber, reinforcing the collection’s technical identity with peripheral rotor winding and a flying tourbillon.
The house history page connects the revived brand narrative to the 1809 Signature Mystérieuse family and the GPHG-recognized Fleur de Sel reference.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: 1809 is the brand’s most identifiable legacy-driven collection: it links the revived maison to its historical namesake while anchoring the modern catalog with a recognizable flying-tourbillon signature and artisan dial work.

faqItems.question: What defines the 1809 collection?
faqItems.answer: It is Charles Girardier’s core collection built around Signature Mystérieuse references, flying tourbillons, and enamel-dial craftsmanship.

faqItems.question: Why is 1809 important to the brand?
faqItems.answer: It ties the modern house to its historical namesake while showcasing the brand’s most recognizable design language and complication.

keyCollections.name: Terre de Lumière
keyCollections.description: Art-focused pieces combining stone and enamel dials inspired by natural landscapes and light.

timeline.event: Charles Girardier, a Genevan watchmaker, establishes his workshop, earning renown for precision pocket watches.
Patrick Ulm revives the Charles Girardier name as a modern independent brand based in Geneva.
Debuts at Watches & Wonders Geneva, presenting the 1809 collection with guilloché and stone dials.

faqItems.question: Is Charles Girardier a historical or modern brand?
faqItems.answer: Both. The original Charles Girardier was an 1809 Geneva watchmaker. The brand was revived in 2020 by Patrick Ulm, combining historical heritage with contemporary independent watchmaking.

faqItems.question: Where are Charles Girardier watches made?
faqItems.answer: In Geneva, Switzerland. The brand emphasises traditional Genevan craftsmanship including hand-guilloché dials and artisanal finishing.

name: Charriol
description: Charriol is a Swiss watch and jewellery house founded in Geneva in 1983 by Philippe Charriol, renowned for its signature cable-twist bracelet inspired by Celtic motifs. Today led by his daughter Coralie Charriol, the brand continues to craft distinctive Swiss-made timepieces blending bold design heritage with contemporary elegance.

keyCollections.name: St-Tropez
keyCollections.description: Charriol St-Tropez is the brand's signature cable-bracelet watch collection, spanning current St-Tropez, St-Tropez Icon, and St-Tropez Slim models across multiple case sizes.

referenceDetails.name: St-Tropez 30mm STN30SWD530306
referenceDetails.note: A current St-Tropez 30 mm quartz reference shown on Charriol's official St-Tropez watches page.

referenceDetails.name: St-Tropez Icon
referenceDetails.note: A current official sub-family of the St-Tropez watch line.

referenceDetails.name: St-Tropez Slim
referenceDetails.note: A Slim sub-family shown from the official St-Tropez collection navigation.

timeline.event: Charriol associates 1983 with the St-Tropez collection's origin in its brand materials.
The current official site organizes the family into St-Tropez, St-Tropez Icon, and St-Tropez Slim watch pages.
Official listings include quartz calibre references with mother-of-pearl dials, cable bracelets, and 20 mm to 34 mm case sizes.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: St-Tropez is Charriol's defining watch signature, translating the maison's twisted-cable jewellery language into a recognizable Swiss watch collection.

faqItems.question: What is Charriol St-Tropez?
faqItems.answer: St-Tropez is Charriol's signature cable-bracelet watch collection.

faqItems.question: Which St-Tropez watch lines are shown officially?
faqItems.answer: Charriol's official pages show St-Tropez, St-Tropez Icon, and St-Tropez Slim watch families.

keyCollections.name: Celtic
keyCollections.description: Charriol Celtic is an active Swiss watch collection built around the maison's Celtic legacy, with current Celtic Legacy watches in 24 mm, 30 mm, and 40 mm executions.

timeline.event: Philippe Charriol founds the brand in Geneva after leaving Cartier.
First collection launched featuring the signature cable-twist motif.
Philippe Charriol dies in a racing accident at Circuit Paul Ricard.
Coralie Charriol appointed CEO.
St-Tropez Navigator collection unveiled at Watches & Wonders.

faqItems.question: What is Charriol known for?
faqItems.answer: Charriol is renowned for its signature cable-twist bracelet design, inspired by Celtic motifs. The St-Tropez collection, featuring this distinctive twisted cable, has been the brand's icon since its founding in 1983.

faqItems.question: Who founded Charriol?
faqItems.answer: Philippe Charriol founded the brand in Geneva in 1983 after leaving Cartier. He tragically died in a racing accident at Circuit Paul Ricard in 2019, and the brand is now led by his daughter Coralie Charriol as CEO.

faqItems.question: Where are Charriol watches made?
faqItems.answer: Charriol watches are Swiss-made, with the brand headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. The company combines Swiss watchmaking standards with distinctive design elements drawn from Celtic art and Mediterranean style.

faqItems.question: What price range are Charriol watches?
faqItems.answer: Charriol occupies the accessible luxury segment, offering Swiss-made timepieces that are more attainable than haute horlogerie brands while maintaining premium design and craftsmanship.

faqItems.question: What are Charriol's main collections?
faqItems.answer: The key collections include St-Tropez (the iconic cable-twist bracelet watch), Celtic (classic with Clous de Paris dials), Forever (fashion-forward artistic dials), and Navigator (sport-inspired, launched at Watches & Wonders 2023).

name: Chopard
description: Founded in Sonvilier in 1860 by Louis-Ulysse Chopard and now based in Meyrin near Geneva, Chopard is a family-owned luxury watchmaker and jeweller under the co-presidency of Caroline and Karl-Friedrich Scheufele. The brand is known for its Happy Diamonds collection and, more recently, its Haute Horlogerie L.U.C. movement range.

keyCollections.description: Chopard Happy Diamonds is the maison's playful diamond-watch family, built around freely moving diamonds and current Happy Diamonds Icons and Joaillerie references.

faqItems.question: What is Chopard Happy Diamonds?
faqItems.answer: Happy Diamonds is Chopard's diamond-watch family built around freely moving diamonds inside or around the watch design.

faqItems.answer: Chopard's official category page lists Happy Diamonds Icons references such as 209415-5004, 209426-5201, and 203957-1214.

keyCollections.name: Alpine Eagle
keyCollections.description: Sport-chic luxury watch collection from Chopard, introduced as a contemporary reinterpretation of the St. Moritz and defined by Lucent Steel™, Alpine inspiration, and eagle-iris dial detailing.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Alpine Eagle is Chopard’s modern steel sports-watch pillar: it translates the brand’s St. Moritz heritage into a current, highly recognizable design language centered on Lucent Steel™, integrated bracelet styling, and a clear outdoor-luxury identity.

referenceDetails.name: St. Moritz lineage
referenceDetails.note: Chopard states the collection is a contemporary reinterpretation of the St Moritz, the first watch created in 1980 by Karl-Friedrich Scheufele.

referenceDetails.name: Lucent Steel bracelet/case material
referenceDetails.note: Official collection and product pages describe the metal as Lucent Steel™, the signature material for the Alpine Eagle line.

referenceDetails.name: Dial inspiration
referenceDetails.note: Chopard describes the dial motif as being inspired by the iris of an eagle, reinforcing the collection’s nature-led identity.

Chopard continues expanding the line with new dial and case variations, including updated Alpine Eagle references on the official site.
The collection remains a core Chopard sports-watch family on the brand’s current watch universe pages.

keyCollections.name: L.U.C
keyCollections.description: Chopard’s haute horlogerie family, built around in-house movements and complications, with a reputation for chronometer certification, Geneva Seal standards, and technically ambitious dress watches.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: L.U.C is the collection that defines Chopard’s manufacture credibility: it marks the brand’s move into full in-house movement production and anchors its highest watchmaking with micro-rotor calibres, chronometers, and complications.

referenceDetails.name: First in-house calibre
referenceDetails.note: Hodinkee and Chopard history materials describe 1996 as the debut of Chopard’s first in-house movement, calibre 1.96, which launched the L.U.C line.

referenceDetails.name: Foundational collection watch
referenceDetails.note: The L.U.C 1860 is widely identified as the first watch in the L.U.C collection, built around the inaugural manufacture calibre.

referenceDetails.name: Long power-reserve family
referenceDetails.note: Hodinkee notes the L.U.C Quattro arrived in 2011 and is one of the collection’s hallmark technically advanced movements.

The L.U.C family expands beyond the founding 1860 model into more technical dress-watch expressions.
L.U.C Quattro extends the line’s technical reputation with an extended power-reserve architecture.

keyCollections.description: Chopard’s Mille Miglia is the brand’s long-running racing-inspired watch family, built around chronographs and sporty, automotive details tied to the classic road rally partnership. The collection emphasizes mechanical performance, masculine elegance, and driving ergonomics, with annual Race Edition updates keeping it current.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: It is one of Chopard’s most recognizable sport-watch lines and a lasting expression of the brand’s motorsport identity, refreshed through yearly editions while retaining the same core codes.

faqItems.question: What kind of watches are in Mille Miglia?
faqItems.answer: Primarily sporty chronographs and related racing-inspired mechanical watches.

timeline.event: Louis-Ulysse Chopard founds the company in Sonvilier, Switzerland, specialising in precision pocket watches.
Karl Scheufele III acquires Chopard, bringing it under the Scheufele family ownership that continues today.
Happy Diamonds concept is created, with free-floating diamonds dancing between sapphire crystals.
L.U.C 1.96 in-house calibre debuts, marking Chopard's entry into serious manufacture watchmaking.
Chopard commits to 100% ethical gold across all its jewellery and watch production — 'The Journey to Sustainable Luxury.'
Alpine Eagle launches as Chopard's flagship luxury sports watch in proprietary Lucent Steel A223.
Revived L.U.C Quattro for 25th anniversary (9-day power reserve). Debuted first platinum Alpine Eagle 41 XP CS. L.U.C Grand Strike honored as best striking watch.

faqItems.question: Is Chopard family-owned?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Since 1963, Chopard has been owned and run by the Scheufele family. Karl-Friedrich and Caroline Scheufele serve as co-presidents.

faqItems.question: What is Lucent Steel?
faqItems.answer: Lucent Steel A223 is Chopard's proprietary alloy — hypoallergenic, harder than conventional steel, with a distinctive lustre. It's also made partly from recycled materials.

name: Christiaan Van Der Klaauw
description: Christiaan van der Klaauw is a Dutch watchmaker and astronomical complication specialist, founding his atelier in the Netherlands in 1974. His watches feature some of the most accurate and visually spectacular astronomical displays found in any wristwatch, including real-time planet positions and celestial mechanics.

keyCollections.name: Planetarium
keyCollections.description: Christiaan van der Klaauw’s Planetarium is the brand’s signature astronomical watch family, centered on a mechanical display of planetary orbits and positioned as one of the atelier’s most technically distinctive creations. The collection sits within the broader astronomical masterpieces group and is repeatedly highlighted as a hallmark complication of the maison.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: It represents the brand’s most identifiable astronomical complication and a clear expression of the atelier’s focus on handcrafted celestial watchmaking.

The Planetarium remained a core model inside the collection of astronomical masterpieces on the official site.
The brand continued to describe the Planetarium as a handmade astronomical watch with a planetary display and other celestial complications.

faqItems.question: What does the Planetarium display?
faqItems.answer: It is designed to show the orbits of the planets in a mechanical astronomical display.

faqItems.question: Which collection does Planetarium belong to?
faqItems.answer: It appears in the brand’s collection of astronomical masterpieces.

faqItems.answer: It is known for Christiaan van der Klaauw's three-dimensional mechanical moon display, used across several astronomical complications.

timeline.event: Christiaan van der Klaauw, a Dutch watchmaker, establishes his workshop in Leiden, the Netherlands.
Creates his first astronomical clock, establishing his niche in celestial complications.
The CVDK Planetarium wristwatch debuts, the most compact planetarium complication ever fitted in a wristwatch.
Launches the Real Moon module with 3D lunar surface representation, patented and exclusive to CVDK.

faqItems.question: What makes Christiaan van der Klaauw special?
faqItems.answer: CVDK is one of very few watchmakers specialising in astronomical complications. Their Planetarium is the world's smallest wrist-worn planetarium, showing real planetary orbits.

faqItems.question: Is CVDK a Dutch brand?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Based in Leiden, Netherlands, it is one of the few high-end independent watchmakers outside Switzerland, bringing a distinctly Dutch approach to horology.

faqItems.question: What astronomical complications does CVDK offer?
faqItems.answer: CVDK specialises in astronomical complications including planetariums (showing the orbits of planets in the solar system), moon phase displays with realistic 3D moons, real-time celestial charts, and sunrise/sunset indicators. The Real Moon collection even features a miniature moon crafted from actual meteorite material.

name: Christie's
description: Christie's is one of the world's two leading fine art and collectibles auction houses, founded in London in 1766. Its watch department holds major sales in Geneva, New York, and Hong Kong, regularly achieving record prices for important vintage and modern timepieces.

hq.address: 8 King Street, St James's, London SW1Y 6QT

keyCollections.name: Important Watches
keyCollections.description: Flagship biannual auction series in Geneva and New York featuring the world's most significant collector timepieces.

keyCollections.name: Online Watch Auctions
keyCollections.description: Regular themed online sales making rare and vintage watches accessible to a global collecting audience.

timeline.event: James Christie founds Christie's auction house in London.
Christie's establishes dedicated watch auctions, capitalising on the growing collector market.
Sells the Paul Newman Rolex Daytona for $17.75 million, a world record for any wristwatch at auction at the time.
Patek Philippe Grandmaster Chime sells for $31.19 million at Christie's Only Watch auction, setting a new all-time record.

faqItems.question: Is Christie's a watch brand?
faqItems.answer: No. Christie's is a fine art and luxury auction house. In the watch world, it is one of the 'Big Three' auction houses (alongside Sotheby's and Phillips) that sell rare and collector timepieces.

faqItems.question: Where does Christie's hold watch auctions?
faqItems.answer: Primarily in Geneva (May and November) and New York, with additional online-only sales throughout the year.

faqItems.question: What are some record-setting watch sales at Christie's?
faqItems.answer: Christie's has overseen numerous record-breaking watch sales, including the Paul Newman Daytona (Rolex Cosmograph Daytona Reference 6239) which sold for $17.75 million in 2017, and the Patek Philippe Grandmaster Chime Ref. 6300A-010 which sold for $31.19 million at the Only Watch 2019 charity auction, the highest price ever paid for a watch at auction.

name: Christophe Claret
description: Christophe Claret is a master watchmaker and movement developer based in Le Brassus, Switzerland, who has designed major complications for numerous prestigious brands. His eponymous label, launched in 2009, produces spectacular grand complication watches including tourbillons with striking mechanisms and highly unusual displays.

keyCollections.name: Maestro
keyCollections.description: Christophe Claret Maestro is a domed, sculptural haute-complication watch line built around a seven-day power reserve, cone-shaped large date display, and a three-dimensional MEMO reminder function.

timeline.event: Maestro was introduced around SIHH 2017 and covered by Hodinkee, Monochrome, Deployant, and Quill & Pad.

keyCollections.name: Poker
keyCollections.description: Christophe Claret Poker is the watchmaker's mechanical Texas Hold'em automaton, a limited gaming complication that extends the brand's playful casino-watch trilogy after Blackjack and Baccara.

timeline.event: Coverage from Monochrome and other watch media places Poker in Christophe Claret's mid-2010s gaming-watch trilogy.

keyCollections.name: X-TREM-1
keyCollections.description: X-TREM-1 is Christophe Claret’s radical magnetic time-display watch, combining an inclined flying tourbillon, retrograde indications, and suspended steel spheres inside sapphire tubes for one of the brand’s most avant-garde statements.

referenceDetails.name: Christophe Claret X-TREM-1

referenceDetails.name: Damascus steel variant
referenceDetails.note: The Jewellery Editor documents a Damascus steel version and reiterates the magnetic hour/minute display concept.

referenceDetails.name: X-TREM-1 Pinball

timeline.event: GPHG records X-TREM-1 with a 2012 launch date.
WatchTime and other media covered X-TREM-1 as an engineering-first magnetic time display.
Christie’s later auction coverage described it as the first model in a new generation of highly exclusive watches.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: X-TREM-1 is the signature Christophe Claret concept watch: it translated the brand’s appetite for theatrical mechanics into a globally recognizable collector piece.

faqItems.question: How does X-TREM-1 show the time?
faqItems.answer: With magnetically driven steel spheres traveling inside sapphire tubes for the hours and minutes display.

faqItems.question: What is the defining complication of X-TREM-1?
faqItems.answer: Its combination of a flying tourbillon and a magnet-based linear time display.

timeline.event: Christophe Claret founds his movement manufacture in Le Locle, initially creating complications for other prestigious brands.
Delivers his first minute repeater movement, beginning a reputation as the go-to supplier of chiming complications.
Launches watches under his own name for the first time, debuting the 21 Blackjack — a working card game on the wrist.
X-TREM-1 debuts with magnetically levitated hour markers, pushing the boundaries of horological innovation.
Poker watch launches, featuring a fully playable poker hand dealt by the movement's micro-mechanics.

faqItems.question: Did Christophe Claret make movements for other brands?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Before launching his own collection, Claret's manufacture created complex movements — particularly minute repeaters — for houses like Harry Winston, Ulysse Nardin, and others.

faqItems.question: What are Christophe Claret's 'game' watches?
faqItems.answer: Claret is famous for integrating fully functional games into watch movements, including Blackjack, Poker, Baccara, and dice games, all using real micro-mechanical randomisation.

faqItems.question: What is the price range of Christophe Claret watches?
faqItems.answer: Christophe Claret watches typically range from approximately CHF 60,000 to over CHF 500,000, reflecting the extreme complexity and hand-finishing involved. Many pieces feature striking complications like minute repeaters, Westminster chimes, or innovative game mechanisms, placing them firmly in the haute horlogerie category.

name: Christopher Ward
description: Christopher Ward is a British watch brand founded in 2004 by Christopher Ward, Mike France, and Peter Ellis in Maidenhead, as a direct-to-consumer alternative to Swiss luxury. Known for the C60 diver and C65 Trident, the brand produces Swiss-made watches including its in-house Calibre SH21 at considerably below Swiss luxury market prices.

keyCollections.name: C60 Trident
keyCollections.description: Christopher Ward’s core dive-watch family, known for the trident-tipped seconds hand, multiple case sizes and materials, and robust Swiss-built performance across the range.

keyCollections.name: C65 Series
keyCollections.description: Vintage-inspired Christopher Ward collection that draws on mid-century tool-watch proportions, domed crystals, and retro styling while keeping the line broadly focused on modern usability.

keyCollections.name: C1 Moonglow
keyCollections.description: Dress watch collection centered on Christopher Ward’s moonphase concept, pairing a luminous moon display with a tide indicator and the brand’s in-house modification for a distinctive, modern dress-watch identity.

timeline.event: Chris Ward, Mike France, and Peter Ellis found Christopher Ward in London as a direct-to-consumer watch brand.
C60 Trident Pro launches, establishing the brand's diver identity and best-selling model.
Moves production to Biel/Bienne, Switzerland, and begins using COSC-certified movements across the range.
Launches the SH21 in-house movement, CW's first proprietary calibre with a 120-hour power reserve.
Introduces the twin-flag logo, completing a brand identity evolution towards a cleaner, more premium look.
Launched C12 Loco jumping hour and C63 Sealander Stones limited editions (150 pcs each in four variants).
Debuted in-house Calibre CW-002 with true traveller GMT in new C63 Sealander True GMT. Announced SoHo New York showroom.

faqItems.question: Why is Christopher Ward so affordable for Swiss-made?
faqItems.answer: By selling directly online without retail markups, CW offers Swiss-made watches with COSC movements and in-house calibres at a fraction of traditional retail prices.

faqItems.question: Does Christopher Ward have its own movement?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The Calibre SH21 is their in-house movement, offering a 120-hour power reserve. They've since expanded the SH family with GMT and chronograph variants.

name: Chronoswiss
description: Chronoswiss was founded in Munich in 1982 by Gerd-Rüdiger Lang and was one of the first brands to revive traditional watchmaking aesthetics — engine-turned dials, coin-edge bezels — in the modern era. The brand relocated to Lucerne in 2012 and continues producing its signature regulator displays and classical complications.

keyCollections.name: Régulateur
keyCollections.description: Chronoswiss Régulateur is the independent brand's defining regulator-display family, rooted in the 1987 serial regulator wristwatch and continued through Manufacture, Classic and Grand Regulator references.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Régulateur is the Chronoswiss idea in its most concentrated form: a regulator dial that separated the time indications and gave the brand a recognizable identity in independent mechanical watchmaking.

timeline.event: Chronoswiss says it launched the world's first serially produced wristwatch with a regulator-style dial, powered by its refined caliber 122.
Chronoswiss identifies ReSec as the start of its modern 3D regulator era, expanding the regulator idea into a more sculptural display language.
The brand still presents regulator-display watches as part of its current Evolution and Heritage-side catalog.

faqItems.question: Why is the Régulateur important to Chronoswiss?
faqItems.answer: Chronoswiss says its 1987 Régulateur was the world's first serially produced wristwatch with a regulator-style dial, making it central to the brand's identity.

faqItems.answer: It is Chronoswiss' contemporary open regulator style, separating time indications while exposing sculptural dial and movement architecture.

timeline.event: Gerd-Rüdiger Lang founds Chronoswiss in Munich, Germany, with a mission to revive mechanical watchmaking during the quartz crisis.
Launches the Régulateur, the first modern wristwatch with a regulator dial, establishing the brand's signature.
Chronoswiss relocates its headquarters from Munich to Lucerne, Switzerland.
Oliver Ebstein, a Swiss entrepreneur, acquires Chronoswiss and begins modernising the brand.
Introduces the Open Gear ReSec, combining a regulator layout with a jumping seconds complication.

faqItems.question: What is a regulator dial?
faqItems.answer: A regulator dial separates hours, minutes, and seconds onto individual sub-dials instead of sharing one axis. Originally used in precision clocks, Chronoswiss pioneered the layout for wristwatches.

faqItems.question: Is Chronoswiss Swiss or German?
faqItems.answer: Founded in Munich, Germany, in 1983, Chronoswiss moved to Lucerne, Switzerland, in 2012. It's now a Swiss brand, though its German mechanical heritage is part of its identity.

timeline.event: Joseph Lapanouse founds the company in Hölstein, Switzerland, manufacturing pin-pallet escapement watches.
Armand Lapanouse patents a movement frame for Roskopf watches, improving robust movement production.
Cimier becomes the first to industrialise pin-pallet chronograph production, selling 20 million calibres of the 'Cimier Sport.'
Peak production reaches 1.5 million pieces per year with over 500 employees in Bubendorf.
The Lapanouse family discontinues Cimier during the quartz crisis.
Cimier is revived, re-entering the market with a focus on affordable Swiss mechanical watches.
Develops the Big Matic automatic module for the Unitas 6497-1 movement.

faqItems.question: What happened to Cimier during the quartz crisis?
faqItems.answer: Cimier invested heavily in quartz development but the Lapanouse family ultimately pulled out in 1985. The brand was revived in 2003 with a renewed focus on mechanical watches.

faqItems.question: What was the Cimier Sport?
faqItems.answer: A groundbreaking affordable chronograph from the 1960s using a simplified pin-pallet escapement. It was a massive commercial success, with 20 million calibres sold worldwide.

name: Citizen
description: Founded in Tokyo in 1930, Citizen is one of the world's largest watch manufacturers and a leader in technical innovation, most notably its Eco-Drive technology which powers watches from any light source without a battery. The Citizen group also owns Bulova, Frederique Constant, and Alpina, among others.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Eco-Drive is central to Citizen’s identity: it ties together sustainability, convenience, and mass-market accessibility while remaining one of the most recognizable watch technologies in the category.

timeline.event: Citizen continues to foreground Eco-Drive across its U.S. site as a major watch family and a core brand technology.
The official technology page states that Eco-Drive was invented in 1976 as the world’s first light-powered analog quartz watch.

faqItems.question: Does Eco-Drive need battery changes?
faqItems.answer: No. Eco-Drive converts light into stored energy, so routine battery replacements are not needed.

faqItems.question: How long can an Eco-Drive watch run in the dark?
faqItems.answer: Citizen states that fully charged Eco-Drive watches can run for more than six months in total darkness, with some models lasting longer under power-save modes.

timeline.event: Shokosha Watch Research Institute is established in Tokyo, the precursor to Citizen Watch.
The first pocket watch is produced and named 'Citizen' by Tokyo mayor Shinpei Goto, wishing it to be accessible to all citizens.
Citizen introduces the first titanium wristwatch, the X-8 Chronometer, pioneering the use of titanium in watches.
Citizen releases the first analogue solar-powered watch, laying the groundwork for Eco-Drive technology.
Eco-Drive launches commercially, eventually becoming the core technology across nearly all Citizen watches.
Citizen acquires Bulova, expanding its portfolio in the North American market.
Eco-Drive Satellite Wave debuts, syncing time via GPS satellite signals anywhere on Earth.
Caliber 0100 achieves ±1 second per year accuracy, the world's most accurate wristwatch at the time.

Marked 50th anniversary of Eco-Drive technology with global launch event and limited-edition models. ATTESA won iF Design Award 2026.

faqItems.question: What is Eco-Drive?
