keyCollections.description: Squelette is Claude Meylan’s signature skeletonized watch family, built around exposed movements, decorative bridges, and the brand’s Vallée de Joux emphasis on turning technical architecture into visible, sculptural watchmaking.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is the clearest expression of Claude Meylan’s identity: movement decoration, openness, and sculptural finishing used as the main design language rather than a hidden technical layer.

timeline.event: Claude Meylan’s history page explicitly states that ‘l’art du Squelette’ is pushed toward new horizons, confirming skeletonization as a core brand pillar.
The same official history text explains that the maison decorates and ‘déshabille’ each movement element, directly supporting the collection’s open-worked character.
The current site copy positions the brand as offering rare and historic movements while refining a new art of sculpted pieces, matching the Squelette concept.

faqItems.question: What defines Squelette at Claude Meylan?
faqItems.answer: The collection focuses on skeletonized watches that reveal the movement through open dials and decorated bridges.

faqItems.question: Is Squelette a current collection?
faqItems.answer: Yes. It appears in the brand’s active story and collection presentation on the official site.

referenceDetails.name: L’art du Squelette
referenceDetails.note: Official history-page phrasing establishing skeletonization as a core maison theme.

referenceDetails.name: Skeleton watchmaking concept
referenceDetails.note: Translated shorthand for the collection’s open-worked movement language.

referenceDetails.name: Skeletonised timepieces
referenceDetails.note: Paraphrase of the existing collection description supplied in the assignment.

timeline.event: Claude Meylan family begins watchmaking in the Vallée de Joux, Switzerland.
Establishes reputation for skeleton watchmaking and complications.
Launches the iconic Tortue collection with its distinctive tortoise-shaped case.
Develops in-house minute repeater movements, cementing haute horlogerie credentials.
Continues as a small independent manufacture specialising in skeletonised and complicated watches.

faqItems.question: What is Claude Meylan known for?
faqItems.answer: Claude Meylan is renowned for skeleton watches and complications, particularly minute repeaters, handcrafted in the Vallée de Joux tradition.

faqItems.question: Is Claude Meylan an independent brand?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Claude Meylan remains a small, family-owned independent manufacture in the Vallée de Joux, Switzerland.

name: Concepto
description: Concepto is a Swiss watch case and component manufacturer that has also produced watches under its own name. The brand represents the technical manufacturing expertise of the Vallée de Joux region.

keyCollections.name: Tourbillon
keyCollections.description: Accessible tourbillon watches demonstrating Concepto's movement manufacturing expertise.

keyCollections.name: Minute Repeater
keyCollections.description: Complicated timepieces featuring minute repeater mechanisms made in their La Chaux-de-Fonds manufacture.

timeline.event: Concepto Watch Factory founded in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, specialising in movement manufacturing.
Develops tourbillon and minute repeater calibres for third-party brands.
Launches own-branded watches alongside continued movement supply to other manufacturers.
Expands capability to produce full watches and complications in-house.

faqItems.question: What does Concepto do?
faqItems.answer: Concepto is both a watch brand and a movement manufacturer based in La Chaux-de-Fonds, producing tourbillons, minute repeaters, and other complications.

faqItems.question: Does Concepto make movements for other brands?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Concepto Watch Factory supplies movements and complications to various Swiss watch brands in addition to producing its own timepieces.

name: Corum
description: Corum was founded in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1955 and is best known for its unconventional designs, particularly the Coin Watch (made from genuine gold coins), the Admiral's Cup with its 12-sided case, and the Bubble with its oversized domed crystal. The brand is now owned by China Haidian Holdings.

keyCollections.name: Admiral
keyCollections.description: CORUM’s Admiral is the house’s nautical sport-chic icon, defined by its dodecagonal case, maritime pennant hour markers, and a 2026 refresh that adds new case architecture, redesigned dials, reimagined pennants, an integrated interchangeable bracelet, and an in-house caliber.

referenceDetails.name: Admiral 39
referenceDetails.note: Steel case and bracelet reference in the current 39 mm Admiral family.

referenceDetails.name: Admiral 39
referenceDetails.note: Titanium Admiral 39 reference; CORUM notes it is the first skeletonized Admiral and first executed in titanium.

referenceDetails.name: Admiral 36
referenceDetails.note: Current 36 mm Admiral reference, reflecting the collection’s new smaller format.

timeline.event: CORUM marks the Admiral’s 60th anniversary with a redesigned collection and new in-house calibers.
The brand introduces six new Admiral 39 references and five new Admiral 36 references as part of the refresh.
CORUM highlights five major evolutions: new case architecture, redesigned dials, reimagined pennants, an integrated interchangeable bracelet, and a proprietary movement.

faqItems.question: What defines the Admiral collection?
faqItems.answer: Its nautical identity is centered on the dodecagonal case and pennant-style hour markers.

faqItems.question: What is notable about the latest update?
faqItems.answer: CORUM says the current refresh replaces the previous Admiral line with new 39 mm and 36 mm references and a new in-house caliber.

keyCollections.name: Golden Bridge
keyCollections.description: CORUM’s Golden Bridge is the maison’s transparent, architecture-first icon, built around the linear baguette movement that became a defining signature in 1980 and remains central to the collection’s modern sapphire, titanium, and classic gold interpretations.

referenceDetails.name: Golden Bridge Classic
referenceDetails.note: Current Golden Bridge Classic reference listed on the official collection page.

referenceDetails.name: Golden Bridge Classic
referenceDetails.note: Current Golden Bridge Classic reference listed on the official collection page.

referenceDetails.name: Golden Bridge Classic
referenceDetails.note: Current Golden Bridge Classic reference from the official collection page, preserving the linear movement architecture.

timeline.event: CORUM presents six new Golden Bridge references, including sapphire, titanium, and Golden Bridge Miss executions.
The brand describes the new series as reconnecting the model with the spirit of transparency that defined its earliest versions.
CORUM highlights the Golden Bridge as a sculptural, transparent watch concept centered on its baguette movement.

faqItems.question: What makes Golden Bridge distinctive?
faqItems.answer: Its linear baguette movement is part of the visual identity, so the movement architecture is exposed rather than hidden.

faqItems.question: Is Golden Bridge still being developed?
faqItems.answer: Yes. CORUM’s current site presents multiple modern variants, including sapphire-case and titanium interpretations.

keyCollections.name: Bubble
keyCollections.description: CORUM Bubble is the maison's oversized, domed-crystal cult watch family, launched in 2000 under Severin Wunderman and known for its magnifying sapphire crystal, 47 mm cases, and graphic limited-edition dials.

referenceDetails.name: Original Bubble
referenceDetails.note: The first Bubble established the collection's dramatically domed crystal and oversized case as a deliberate break from conventional watch design.

referenceDetails.name: Bubble 47 Dragon
referenceDetails.note: Dragon and skull editions show how Bubble became a canvas for bold limited-edition graphics and pop-culture dial treatments.

referenceDetails.name: Bubble x Label Noir Central Tourbillon
referenceDetails.note: The Label Noir unique piece shows Bubble's later high-complication side, placing a central tourbillon inside the collection's theatrical case architecture.

image.alt: Corum Bubble x Label Noir central tourbillon

timeline.event: Severin Wunderman launches the Bubble, inspired by a 1960s diving watch with a pressure-resistant domed crystal.
The Bubble reaches peak early production, with WorldTempus reporting sales as high as 20,000 pieces that year.
Production pauses after Wunderman's death, turning the original Bubble run into a remembered cult chapter for CORUM.
CORUM relaunches Bubble as a platform for limited editions and graphic dial experiments.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Bubble matters because it is CORUM at its most playful and anti-conventional: a technically simple automatic watch transformed into a recognisable collector object by a huge crystal, optical distortion, and fearless dial art.

image.alt: Corum Bubble watch with moon and dragon dial

gallery.alt: Corum Bubble moon and dragon limited edition
Corum Bubble dragon eye limited edition

faqItems.question: When did the Corum Bubble launch?
faqItems.answer: WorldTempus traces the Bubble to 2000, when Severin Wunderman created the oversized domed-crystal watch.

faqItems.question: Why does the Bubble look distorted?
faqItems.answer: Its thick domed sapphire crystal works like a magnifying glass, enlarging and visually warping the dial as part of the design.

faqItems.question: Is the Bubble a current main Corum collection?
faqItems.answer: CORUM's current site emphasizes Admiral, Golden Bridge, and Heritage; Bubble is considered a cult and heritage collection rather than a current official catalogue pillar.

funFacts.title: Optical signature
funFacts.body: The crystal is not just protective glass; its globe-like distortion is the collection's defining visual device.

funFacts.title: Dial canvas
funFacts.body: Bubble became a vehicle for skulls, dragons, pop-art ideas, and collaborations because the huge crystal amplifies the dial.

keyCollections.name: Coin Watch
keyCollections.description: Corum’s Coin Watch is the maison’s emblematic heritage concept: a timepiece built from a genuine coin, combining collectible numismatic material, ultra-thin watchmaking, and a long-running identity linked to exclusivity and prestige.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Corum continues to frame Coin Watch as a core heritage icon on its official site, including a 2026 revival made from a $50 American Eagle gold coin, which confirms the concept’s ongoing relevance to the brand identity.

referenceDetails.name: Heritage Coin
referenceDetails.note: 2026 Heritage reissue described by Corum as a new Coin crafted from a $50 American Eagle gold coin.

referenceDetails.name: Coin Watch
referenceDetails.note: Corum explicitly describes the Coin Watch as one of the key heritage icons in the collection.

referenceDetails.name: C36.082.MY0.4N Heritage
referenceDetails.note: Official product reference for the 2026 Heritage Coin watch.

timeline.event: Corum continued to foreground its heritage icons, including Coin Watch, on the official website.
The brand’s official site emphasized the Heritage collection as a place for rare reissues and confidential pieces.
Corum highlighted the Coin Watch concept again in its Heritage storytelling, reinforcing its long-term brand role.

faqItems.question: Is Coin Watch a current Corum collection?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Corum places Coin Watch within its Heritage collection and has recently introduced a new Heritage Coin piece.

faqItems.question: What makes Coin Watch special?
faqItems.answer: The watch is distinguished by its use of an authentic coin as the case basis, giving it strong collectible and historical appeal.

timeline.event: Gaston Ries and René Bannwart found Corum in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland.
Introduces the Coin Watch, crafted from a US  gold coin, becoming a brand icon.
Launches the Admiral's Cup collection with nautical signal flag markers.
Unveils the Golden Bridge, featuring a linear baguette movement visible through sapphire.
Introduces the Bubble collection with its oversized domed crystal.
Acquired by China Haidian Holdings, entering a new era of ownership.
Management buyout on 70th anniversary returned brand to Swiss ownership, ending Citychamp era. Led by Haso Mehmedovic.
Debuted at Watches & Wonders 2026 with revamped Admiral collection. Reduced distribution to approx 70 points of sale.

faqItems.question: What is Corum most famous for?
faqItems.answer: Corum is best known for the Golden Bridge (a linear movement in a transparent case), the Admiral with nautical flag markers, and the Coin Watch made from real gold coins.

faqItems.question: Where is Corum based?
faqItems.answer: Corum is headquartered in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, where it has been producing watches since 1955.

faqItems.question: Who owns Corum today?
faqItems.answer: Corum was acquired by China Haidian Holdings in 2013, which provides financial backing while maintaining Swiss manufacturing.

name: Credor
description: Credor is a Japanese haute horlgerie brand created by Seiko in 1974 to produce its highest-end mechanical timepieces. Based in the Shinshu Watch Studio, Credor produces hand-finished spring-drive and maki-e lacquered watches that represent the pinnacle of Seiko's craft, with production limited to very small numbers.

keyCollections.name: Eichi
keyCollections.description: Credor’s hand-crafted minimalist masterpiece line, centered on the Eichi concept of refined simplicity, porcelain dials, and elite Micro Artist Studio craftsmanship within the brand’s highest-elegance universe.

timeline.event: Credor celebrated its 50th anniversary and highlighted the Eichi II in official brand news.

keyCollections.name: Signo
keyCollections.description: Credor’s Signo collection focuses on elegant dress watches with refined Japanese aesthetics, precious-metal executions, and a formal design language that emphasizes slimness, polish, and decorative dial work.

keyCollections.name: Node
keyCollections.description: Credor’s Node collection is presented as a contemporary expression of Japanese watchmaking, blending refined design language with the brand’s craftsmanship-led positioning and Seiko Group heritage.

timeline.event: Seiko launches Credor (from French "crête d'or" meaning "crest of gold") as its luxury division.
Introduces ultra-thin quartz models establishing Credor as a high-end dress watch brand.
Launches the Eichi I Spring Drive, finished by Seiko's Micro Artist Studio.
Eichi II debuts with porcelain dial and hand-finished Spring Drive movement.
Continues as Seiko's pinnacle luxury line, mostly sold in the Japanese domestic market.

faqItems.question: What does Credor mean?
faqItems.answer: Credor comes from the French "crête d'or" meaning "crest of gold." It is Seiko's luxury watch division, positioned above Grand Seiko.

faqItems.question: Are Credor watches available outside Japan?
faqItems.answer: Credor watches are primarily sold in Japan, though some models are available through select international retailers and auctions.

name: Cyrus Genève
description: Cyrus Genève is an independent Geneva watchmaker founded in 2010, pioneering the world's first timepiece with two fully functional crowns and extraordinary three-dimensional dial architecture. The brand's avant-garde technical innovations include a patented linear time display, retrograde calendar and a unique vertical tourbillon.

keyCollections.name: Klepcys
keyCollections.description: Klepcys is Cyrus Genève’s signature architectural collection, defined by a cushion-shaped case, elongated lugs, twin functional crowns and strongly three-dimensional dials that showcase the brand’s complication-driven, avant-garde approach to high watchmaking.

referenceDetails.name: Klepcys collection
referenceDetails.note: The original collection was launched in 2011 and appears on official and GPHG references as the core Cyrus line.

referenceDetails.name: Functional double crown layout
referenceDetails.note: Official collection copy highlights the twin-crown, cushion-case construction as a brand signature.

referenceDetails.name: Master watchmaker Jean-François Mojon
referenceDetails.note: Cyrus states that Mojon is the mastermind behind its creations, and the collection is closely associated with his complication work.

timeline.event: Klepcys is introduced as Cyrus Genève’s early signature collection.
The Klepcys GMT Retrograde expands the line with the brand’s first automatic movement and a more travel-oriented complication set.
Cyrus continues expanding Klepcys with DICE and other technical derivatives, reinforcing the line as the maison’s complication platform.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Klepcys is important because it is the collection where Cyrus Genève’s identity is most recognisable: bold case architecture, mechanical theatrics and a steady stream of novel complications that define the brand in the independent-high-horology space.

faqItems.question: What defines the Klepcys collection visually?
faqItems.answer: Its cushion-shaped case, elongated lugs, pronounced three-dimensional dials and twin crown architecture.

faqItems.question: Why is Klepcys important to Cyrus Genève?
faqItems.answer: It is the brand’s signature family and the platform for many of its most notable complications.

keyCollections.name: Kambys
keyCollections.description: Cyrus Kambys is the maison's tonneau-shaped manual-wind power-reserve watch, using three sliding cylinders and a seven-day double-barrel movement to turn remaining autonomy into the central display.

timeline.event: aBlogtoWatch reported the new Cyrus Kambys ahead of Baselworld 2013, with a movement by Jean-Francois Mojon.
Cyrus Genève founded by Julien Tomasi and Laurent Lecamp in Geneva, Switzerland.
Debuts the Klepcys collection, establishing the brand's bold horological identity.
Introduces complications including retrograde displays and vertical tourbillons.
Continues to develop innovative complications with strong architectural design language.

faqItems.question: What kind of watches does Cyrus Genève make?
faqItems.answer: Cyrus Genève creates high-end complicated watches with bold, architectural designs, specialising in innovative displays and tourbillons.

faqItems.question: Is Cyrus Genève independent?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Cyrus Genève is an independent Swiss watchmaker based in Geneva, focused on haute horlogerie complications.

name: Czapek & Cie
description: Czapek & Cie was revived in Geneva in 2012, drawing on the legacy of François Czapek, who co-founded what later became Patek Philippe before departing in 1845. The neo-vintage brand produces limited-edition, beautifully finished pieces with in-house movements and has quickly attracted a dedicated collector following.
defunct_reason: The original Czapek & Cie partnership ended when François Czapek departed in 1845 to form his own firm; the Czapek name effectively disappeared from horology by the late 19th century.
revival_attempt: Revived in Geneva in 2012 by Xavier de Roquemaurel and Philippe Chronopoulos, producing neo-vintage watches with in-house movements inspired by Czapek's role as co-founder of what became Patek Philippe.

keyCollections.name: Quai des Bergues
keyCollections.description: Czapek’s founding-era dress-watch collection, named for the Geneva quay where François Czapek first worked. The line pairs classical round cases, hand-finished dials, and the brand’s signature twin subdials with modern haute-horlogerie construction, including a micro-rotor era in later references and a strong heritage-led identity.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is the collection that marked Czapek & Cie’s renaissance and established the brand’s most explicitly heritage-driven dress-watch language.

timeline.event: Czapek’s collection page continued to present Quai des Bergues as a core heritage line within the brand’s modern portfolio.
The brand’s shop pages described the collection as launched in 2015 and tied to François Czapek’s first Geneva atelier.
Modern references continued to emphasize the collection’s 7-day manual-wind architecture and twin de-centered subdials.

referenceDetails.name: Quai des Bergues N° 33
referenceDetails.note: First production model of the revived collection; historically inspired dress watch with twin subdials.

referenceDetails.name: Quai des Bergues 33bis
referenceDetails.note: Collection reference associated with early recognition and the Public Prize at GPHG 2016, per brand text.

referenceDetails.name: Quai des Bergues N° 25 Ter
referenceDetails.note: Current shop reference highlighted on the official site, with grand feu enamel and the line’s signature case language.

faqItems.question: Is Quai des Bergues a sports watch?
faqItems.answer: No. It is positioned as an elegant, heritage-led dress-watch collection with classical proportions and traditional finishing.

faqItems.question: What defines the collection visually?
faqItems.answer: The round case, twin de-centered subdials, and historic-inspired dial layouts are the most recognizable signatures.

keyCollections.name: Place Vendôme
keyCollections.description: Czapek & Cie’s Place Vendôme collection is the maison’s platform for exceptional fine watchmaking, pairing classical inspiration with technically ambitious complications such as tourbillon, second time zone and dual-escapement constructions.

referenceDetails.name: Tourbillon Suspendu Ici et Ailleurs
referenceDetails.note: Czapek describes the first models of the Place Vendôme line as including this tourbillon-and-second-time-zone watch.

referenceDetails.name: Place Vendôme Complicité
referenceDetails.note: Official copy says the line later added the dual-escapement Complicité, launched in 2023.

referenceDetails.name: Place Vendôme collection
referenceDetails.note: The collection is named after the Paris square where François Czapek opened a boutique in 1850, linking modern Czapek to the brand’s historical roots.

timeline.event: Czapek launches the Place Vendôme collection as part of the revived maison’s early portfolio.
The maison marks a new milestone with the launch of Place Vendôme Complicité, a dual-escapement timepiece.
The Place Vendôme collection remains active as Czapek’s designated venue for exceptional watchmaking projects.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Place Vendôme matters because it anchors Czapek’s most elaborate and classical high-complication work, showing how the revived brand translates historical references into contemporary fine watchmaking.

faqItems.question: What kinds of watches belong to Place Vendôme?
faqItems.answer: It is Czapek’s collection for exceptional projects, including tourbillon and dual-escapement complications.

faqItems.question: Why is it called Place Vendôme?
faqItems.answer: The name references the Paris square where François Czapek opened a boutique in 1850.

keyCollections.name: Antarctique
keyCollections.description: Czapek & Cie’s Antarctique is the maison’s integrated-bracelet sport-chic collection, built around a slim steel/titanium profile, in-house automatic movement and a design language that balances technical finish with contemporary, everyday wearability.

referenceDetails.name: Calibre SXH5
referenceDetails.note: Official pages identify SXH5 as the first movement entirely conceived in-house by Czapek and the engine of the original Antarctique line.

referenceDetails.name: Antarctique Terre Adélie
referenceDetails.note: Czapek states that the first Antarctique model, Terre Adélie, was released on 26 May 2020.

referenceDetails.name: Passage de Drake
referenceDetails.note: Official pages describe Passage de Drake as an early design concept and a notable branch of the Antarctique line.

timeline.event: Czapek releases the first Antarctique model, Terre Adélie, and launches the line in May.
The Antarctique S extends the family with a smaller 38.5 mm case and the same in-house movement family.
Czapek continues to expand Antarctique with special dials and variants while emphasizing the integrated-bracelet concept.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Antarctique matters because it gave Czapek a modern sport-chic platform with an in-house movement and a highly adaptable design code, helping the revived maison claim a recognizable place in contemporary independent watchmaking.

faqItems.question: When did Antarctique launch?
faqItems.answer: Czapek says the first model, Terre Adélie, was released on 26 May 2020.

faqItems.question: What movement powers the Antarctique?
faqItems.answer: The collection is built around the in-house Calibre SXH5 and its later derivatives.

timeline.event: Franciszek Czapek founds Czapek & Cie after dissolving his partnership with Antoni Patek (Patek Philippe).
Opens Paris boutique at Place Vendôme 28; becomes watchmaker to Emperor Napoleon III.
Czapek dies; the brand ceases production and enters dormancy.
Harry Guhl revives Czapek & Cie in Geneva, launching a successful Kickstarter campaign.
Debuts the Quai des Bergues collection with an in-house micro-rotor movement.
Launches the Antarctique, an integrated-bracelet sports watch that becomes a bestseller.
Celebrated 10th anniversary with Time Jumper limited edition featuring half-hunter cover with 3D guilloche.
Unveiled Antarctique Titanium Cosmic Blue at Watches & Wonders 2026, featuring SXH5 first fully in-house movement.

faqItems.question: What is the connection between Czapek and Patek Philippe?
faqItems.answer: Franciszek Czapek was Antoni Patek's original partner. They founded Patek, Czapek & Cie in 1839, which was dissolved in 1845. Patek went on to found Patek Philippe, while Czapek founded Czapek & Cie.

faqItems.question: Is Czapek & Cie a new or heritage brand?
faqItems.answer: Both. Originally founded in 1845 by Franciszek Czapek, the brand was dormant for over a century before being revived in 2012 by Harry Guhl.

name: D1 Milano
description: We are creative misfits, we are design enthusiasts — we have no rules except one: reinventing icons since 2013. Born in Milan, D1 Milano produces ultra-thin, colourful and fashion-forward timepieces that distil the city's design culture into accessible, personality-driven watches for a global young audience.

keyCollections.name: Polycarbon
keyCollections.description: D1 Milano Polycarbon is the brand's lightweight polycarbonate watch family, built around colorful cases, accessible sizing, and contemporary fashion-watch styling.

referenceDetails.name: Shadow
referenceDetails.note: Official current Polycarbon model using the collection's lightweight case architecture and dark monochrome styling.

referenceDetails.name: White Sketch
referenceDetails.note: Official current Polycarbon variant with a graphic white sketch treatment listed by D1 Milano.

image.alt: D1 Milano Polycarbon White Sketch watch

referenceDetails.name: Navy Blue
referenceDetails.note: Official current Polycarbon colorway showing the collection's simple case-and-bracelet form in blue.

image.alt: D1 Milano Polycarbon Navy Blue watch

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Polycarbon is a clear expression of D1 Milano's design-led positioning: bold color, lightweight materials, and a watch shape closer to fashion architecture than traditional Swiss sports watch codes.

faqItems.question: What is D1 Milano Polycarbon?
faqItems.answer: Polycarbon is D1 Milano's lightweight polycarbonate watch collection, focused on colorful everyday designs.

faqItems.question: Which Polycarbon models are current official examples?
faqItems.answer: D1 Milano's official collection page lists examples such as Shadow, White Sketch, Navy Blue, Cloudburst, Military Green, and Space Grey.

faqItems.question: Why is Polycarbon important for D1 Milano?
faqItems.answer: It captures the brand's accessible design-watch identity more directly than its dressier steel collections.

keyCollections.name: Ultra Thin
keyCollections.description: D1 Milano Ultra Thin is the brand's slim steel watch family, pairing minimalist dials, thin cases, and fashion-led colorways across bracelet and specialty variants.

referenceDetails.name: Ocean
referenceDetails.note: Official current Ultra Thin bracelet model with a blue dial execution.

image.alt: D1 Milano Ultra Thin Ocean watch

referenceDetails.name: Geo
referenceDetails.note: Official current Ultra Thin bracelet model using a geometric dial treatment.

image.alt: D1 Milano Ultra Thin Geo watch

referenceDetails.name: Moss
referenceDetails.note: Official current Ultra Thin bracelet model in a green Moss colorway.

image.alt: D1 Milano Ultra Thin Moss watch

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Ultra Thin is the cleanest expression of D1 Milano's minimalist side, turning the brand's architectural case shape into a slim, versatile dress-casual watch line.

image.alt: D1 Milano Ultra Thin Ocean watch

faqItems.question: What is D1 Milano Ultra Thin?
faqItems.answer: Ultra Thin is D1 Milano's slim watch family, built around restrained dials and thin steel cases.

faqItems.question: Which Ultra Thin models are current official examples?
faqItems.answer: D1 Milano lists Ultra Thin examples including Ocean, Geo, Moss, Linen, Anthracite, Chocolate, and Light Blue.

faqItems.question: How does Ultra Thin fit within D1 Milano?
faqItems.answer: It is the brand's minimalist dress-casual line, contrasting with the lighter Polycarbon and more open-worked Skeleton families.

keyCollections.name: Skeleton
keyCollections.description: D1 Milano Skeleton is the brand's open-worked mechanical line, using visible movement architecture inside the company's slim, design-forward case language.

referenceDetails.name: Gun Metal
referenceDetails.note: Official current Skeleton bracelet model in a dark gun-metal finish.

image.alt: D1 Milano Skeleton Gun Metal watch

referenceDetails.name: Silver
referenceDetails.note: Official current Skeleton bracelet model in silver-tone finishing.

referenceDetails.name: Rose Gold
referenceDetails.note: Official current Skeleton bracelet model with rose-gold-tone finishing.

image.alt: D1 Milano Skeleton Rose Gold watch

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Skeleton gives D1 Milano a mechanical-looking showcase line, translating the brand's clean urban styling into open-worked dials and visible movement detail.

image.alt: D1 Milano Skeleton Gun Metal watch

faqItems.question: What is D1 Milano Skeleton?
faqItems.answer: It is D1 Milano's open-worked watch collection, showing movement architecture through a contemporary dial layout.

faqItems.question: Which Skeleton models are current official examples?
faqItems.answer: D1 Milano lists Skeleton bracelet models including Gun Metal, Silver, and Rose Gold on its official product pages.

faqItems.question: How does Skeleton differ from Polycarbon?
faqItems.answer: Skeleton focuses on visible mechanical-style architecture, while Polycarbon is centered on lightweight colored cases.

timeline.event: Dario Spallone founds D1 Milano in Milan, Italy, with a vision for contemporary Italian watch design.
Polycarbon collection launches, becoming the brand's iconic bestseller with its bold colours.
Expands globally with flagship stores in Dubai, Milan, and online distribution.
Introduces the Skeleton collection, moving into mechanical watches while maintaining Italian design DNA.

faqItems.question: Where is D1 Milano from?
faqItems.answer: D1 Milano is an Italian watch brand founded in Milan in 2013, known for its bold, minimalist designs and use of colourful polycarbonate materials.

faqItems.question: Are D1 Milano watches Swiss-made?
faqItems.answer: D1 Milano watches are designed in Italy. Some models use Japanese Miyota movements; the brand focuses on contemporary design rather than Swiss heritage.

name: Damasko
description: Damasko is a German watch brand founded in 1994 in Geisenhausen, Bavaria, known for developing a proprietary ice-hardening process that makes their steel cases and bracelets significantly harder than standard 316L steel. The brand produces technically rigorous pilot and diver watches using German movements.

keyCollections.name: DA3x
keyCollections.description: Damasko’s DA3x family is positioned as a rugged pilot-tool watch line with hardened steel construction, strong legibility, and the brand’s durability-first engineering approach.

keyCollections.name: DC5x
keyCollections.description: Damasko’s DC5x collection is the brand’s chronograph line, using hardened steel cases, the DAMASKO System crown protection, and a clear professional-tool-watch orientation with strong mechanical robustness.

keyCollections.name: DS30
keyCollections.description: Damasko’s DS30 is a compact three-hand sports watch built in submarine steel with hardened surfaces, a screwed crown system, and a slim, highly durable everyday-tool profile.

timeline.event: Konrad Damasko founds Damasko in Barbing, Germany, applying aerospace materials technology to watchmaking.
Ends supply partnership with Sinn, begins producing complete watches under its own brand.
DC56 chronograph certified as official Eurofighter test pilot watch.
Releases first watches with Damasko's own in-house movement, reducing dependence on ETA.
Continues to develop proprietary hardened alloys and silicon components for movements.

faqItems.question: What makes Damasko special?
faqItems.answer: Damasko uses proprietary ice-hardened steel (up to 64 HRC) and aerospace-derived materials technology, making their watches extremely scratch-resistant and durable.

faqItems.question: Does Damasko make its own movements?
faqItems.answer: Yes, since 2014 Damasko has produced in-house movements. Earlier models used Swiss ETA movements.

faqItems.question: What was the connection between Damasko and Sinn?
faqItems.answer: Damasko supplied hardened watchcases to Sinn until 2002, when the partnership ended and Damasko began producing complete watches.

name: Dan Henry
description: Dan Henry is an American watch brand founded in 2016 by William Kerber (pen name Dan Henry), inspired by vintage watches of the 1960s and 1970s. The brand produces limited-edition vintage-style timepieces referencing classic genres — compax chronographs, cushion-case pilots, tropical divers — using Swiss movements at honest prices.

keyCollections.description: Dan Henry’s 1962 collection is a vintage-inspired racing chronograph line that channels 1960s motorsport aesthetics through panda-style dial options and a compact, enthusiast-friendly design language.
Dan Henry’s 1970 collection is a vintage-style automatic diver line built around an inner rotating bezel, dual-crown layout, and bold 1970s-inspired proportions with modern everyday practicality.
Dan Henry’s 1964 collection is a mid-century-inspired Gran Turismo chronograph family that emphasizes clean, dressier proportions and a motorsport heritage theme across its variants.

timeline.event: Vintage watch collector Dan Henry launches his eponymous brand, offering affordable vintage-inspired timepieces.
The 1970 diver watch becomes a hit in the microbrand community for its value and design.
Introduces the 1962 racing chronograph, quickly selling out.
Expands lineup while maintaining limited production runs and accessible pricing.

faqItems.question: Who is Dan Henry?
faqItems.answer: Dan Henry is a vintage watch collector who founded the brand to create affordable watches inspired by iconic timepieces from the 1960s and 1970s.

faqItems.question: Are Dan Henry watches limited edition?
faqItems.answer: Yes, most Dan Henry models are produced in limited quantities, often numbered to match the year that inspired the design (e.g., 1,964 pieces for the 1964 model).

name: Daniel Roth
description: Daniel Roth was an influential independent watchmaker who trained at Breguet before founding his own brand in Le Sentier in 1988, known for his distinctive ellipse-within-a-rectangle case profile. The brand was acquired by Bvlgari in 2000 and the Daniel Roth name was subsequently retired.
defunct_reason: Bulgari, which acquired Daniel Roth in 2000, discontinued production under the Daniel Roth name around 2015 after failing to develop a coherent identity for the brand within the LVMH portfolio.
revival_attempt: Relaunched in 2023 under LVMH with watchmaking at La Fabrique du Temps (previously a Louis Vuitton factory), producing fewer than 100 pieces annually.

keyCollections.name: Papillon
keyCollections.description: Signature double-sided jumping hour complication displayed through two windows, a Daniel Roth icon.

keyCollections.name: Tourbillon
keyCollections.description: Hand-finished tourbillon watches showcasing Roth's training at Breguet and mastery of classical complications.

keyCollections.name: Ellipsocurvex
keyCollections.description: Daniel Roth Ellipsocurvex expresses the brand's double-ellipse case language, now best represented by current Extra Plat references in platinum, rose gold and openworked rose gold.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Ellipsocurvex silhouette is the visual signature that lets a Daniel Roth watch read as Daniel Roth at a glance, and the revived Extra Plat line shows how that case vocabulary is being carried forward today.

image.alt: Daniel Roth Extra Plat Platinum official image

gallery.alt: Daniel Roth Extra Plat Rose Gold official image
Daniel Roth Extra Plat Rose Gold Skeleton official image

referenceDetails.name: Extra Plat Platinum
referenceDetails.note: Official current Extra Plat reference in platinum, presented by Daniel Roth as a refined continuation of the maison's thin double-ellipse dress-watch vocabulary.

image.alt: Daniel Roth Extra Plat Platinum official image

referenceDetails.name: Extra Plat Rose Gold
referenceDetails.note: Official current Extra Plat reference in rose gold, described by Daniel Roth as returning with an open caseback.

image.alt: Daniel Roth Extra Plat Rose Gold official image

referenceDetails.name: Extra Plat Rose Gold Skeleton
referenceDetails.note: Official current openworked Extra Plat reference, extending the double-ellipse case language into a transparent rose-gold execution.

image.alt: Daniel Roth Extra Plat Rose Gold Skeleton official image

faqItems.question: What does Ellipsocurvex mean on Watchatlas?
faqItems.answer: On Watchatlas it is used for Daniel Roth's distinctive double-ellipse case language, represented here with current official Extra Plat references.

faqItems.question: Which Daniel Roth watches are represented here?
faqItems.answer: This page uses official source material for Extra Plat Platinum, Extra Plat Rose Gold and Extra Plat Rose Gold Skeleton.

timeline.event: Master watchmaker Daniel Roth founds his eponymous brand after years at Breguet, where he revived the tourbillon.
Introduces the signature double-ellipse case design that becomes the brand's visual identity.
Launches the Papillon, an innovative jumping-hour complication unique to the brand.
Bulgari acquires Daniel Roth; production continues under Bulgari's watch division.
Daniel Roth brand is gradually absorbed into Bulgari's own collections; individual Daniel Roth-branded watches become collector items.

faqItems.question: Is Daniel Roth still making watches?
faqItems.answer: Daniel Roth as a standalone brand was acquired by Bulgari in 2000 and gradually integrated into Bulgari's collections. Vintage Daniel Roth pieces are highly collectible.

faqItems.question: What is Daniel Roth famous for?
faqItems.answer: Daniel Roth is celebrated for his double-ellipse case design, the Papillon jumping-hour complication, and his work reviving the tourbillon at Breguet before founding his own brand.

name: Daniel Wellington
description: Daniel Wellington is a Swedish watch brand founded in 2011 by Filip Tysander in Stockholm, named after a British gentleman he met while backpacking. The brand achieved rapid global growth through social media marketing and is known for minimalist watches with interchangeable NATO and leather straps at accessible prices.

keyCollections.name: Classic
keyCollections.description: Daniel Wellington’s Classic line is the brand’s signature slim dress-watch family, built around a minimalist dial, clean proportions, and interchangeable NATO or leather straps that keep the look understated and versatile.

keyCollections.name: Petite
keyCollections.description: Petite is Daniel Wellington’s smaller-cased collection, keeping the same clean, minimalist styling but in a more delicate format designed for slimmer wrists and lighter visual presence.

keyCollections.name: Iconic
keyCollections.description: Iconic is Daniel Wellington’s more statement-led watch family, pairing the brand’s minimalist DNA with a slightly bolder case presence and applied indices for a sharper, more modern everyday look.

timeline.event: Filip Tysander founds Daniel Wellington in Uppsala, Sweden, inspired by a British gentleman he met while travelling.
Becomes one of the fastest-growing watch brands globally through Instagram influencer marketing.
Named fastest-growing private company in Europe with M revenue.
Expands into jewellery and accessories beyond watches.
Reports operating losses as the brand faces market saturation and changing consumer trends.
Timex Group acquired majority stake. Brand continues independent operation from Stockholm under new ownership.

faqItems.question: Where are Daniel Wellington watches made?
faqItems.answer: Daniel Wellington watches are designed in Sweden and manufactured in China using Japanese Miyota quartz movements.

faqItems.question: Why is it called Daniel Wellington?
faqItems.answer: Founder Filip Tysander named the brand after a British gentleman called Daniel Wellington whom he met while travelling, who wore a vintage watch on a NATO strap.

name: David Candaux
description: David Candaux is an independent Swiss watchmaker creating exceptional timepieces from his atelier at Le Solliat in the Vallée de Joux, guided by a philosophy uniting heart and mind. His collections feature proprietary complications including a patented 30° inclined tourbillon and the Magic Crown ergonomic system, each watch backed by a 10-year warranty.

keyCollections.name: DC6
keyCollections.description: David Candaux’s flagship collection line, introduced as a highly architectural titanium tourbillon watch with dual sapphire domes, a hand-engraved guilloché surface, and the brand’s patented Magic Crown approach to ergonomic high watchmaking.

referenceDetails.name: DC6 Titanium
referenceDetails.note: The official DC6 page states the model launched in 2018 and identifies it as the flagship of the collection.

referenceDetails.name: DC6 Night Forest
referenceDetails.note: The official site groups DC6 Night Forest within the DC6 family and says the Pointes du Risoux guilloché has been a DC6 signature since 2018.

referenceDetails.name: DC6 family on collection index
referenceDetails.note: The collection overview page lists DC6 alongside the brand’s other core families, confirming it as a named collection line rather than a one-off model.

timeline.event: The brand’s official collection pages continue to present DC6 as a central family within the David Candaux catalog.
The DC6 Titanium page states the line was launched in 2018 and built around dual sapphire domes plus a 30° inclined tourbillon.
The DC6 Night Forest page reinforces DC6 design DNA by describing the Pointes du Risoux guilloché as a signature since 2018.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: DC6 is the brand’s clearest entry point into David Candaux’s architecture-first watchmaking: it combines a patented ergonomic crown system, substantial hand-finishing, and a distinctive open-worked display that establishes the maison’s identity.

faqItems.question: What makes DC6 the flagship of David Candaux?
faqItems.answer: The official site describes DC6 Titanium as the flagship of the collection, highlighting its dual sapphire domes, titanium construction, and inclined tourbillon.

faqItems.question: When was DC6 introduced?
faqItems.answer: The official DC6 Titanium page says the line was launched in 2018.

keyCollections.name: DC9
keyCollections.description: Ultra-exclusive complication watch with innovative architecture and hand-finished movement components.

timeline.event: Independent watchmaker David Candaux founds his brand in Le Noirmont, Switzerland.
Debuts the DC6, a groundbreaking timepiece with suspended tourbillon and innovative architecture.
Gains recognition in independent watchmaking circles for exceptional hand-finishing and creative complications.
Continues producing extremely limited numbers of haute horlogerie pieces.

faqItems.question: How many watches does David Candaux make per year?
faqItems.answer: David Candaux produces only a handful of watches per year, each entirely hand-finished by Candaux himself in his Le Noirmont atelier.

faqItems.question: What is David Candaux known for?
faqItems.answer: David Candaux is known for innovative watch architecture, particularly suspended tourbillons and creative movement construction, all executed with exceptional hand-finishing.

name: De Bethune
description: De Béthune was founded in L'Auberson, Switzerland in 2002 by David Zanetta and master watchmaker Denis Flageollet, and has since established itself as one of the most technically and aesthetically inventive independent manufactures. The brand is known for its innovative use of materials including titanium, silicon, and white gold in movement components.

keyCollections.name: DB25
keyCollections.description: DB25 is De Bethune’s classical round-case family, now used for elegant calendar, moon-phase, and chronograph executions that pair restrained proportions with the brand’s signature hand-finishing and technical refinement. The line acts as the maison’s more traditional counterpoint to its experimental and reversible creations, while still carrying unmistakably modern De Bethune architecture.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: DB25 matters because it represents De Bethune’s enduring classical platform: a family through which the brand reinterprets historic complications, from perpetual calendar to chronograph, with contemporary materials and finishing.

timeline.event: De Bethune continued revamping its 40 mm DB25 line with the Perpetual Sky, an active official collection entry.
The DB25 family remains a live platform on the official site, including Monopusher Chronograph and Starry Varius executions.
The brand described the DB25L as having launched in 2009, framing the family’s modern continuity and recent evolution.

faqItems.question: What is DB25’s positioning within De Bethune?
faqItems.answer: It is the brand’s classical round-case family, serving as a platform for refined, more traditional-looking complications and dial treatments.

faqItems.question: Is DB25 a single reference or a broader collection?
faqItems.answer: It is a broader family with multiple references and sub-variants, including Perpetual Sky, Starry Varius, and Monopusher Chronograph.

referenceDetails.name: Perpetual Sky
referenceDetails.note: Current official DB25 perpetual calendar reference.

referenceDetails.name: Starry Varius
referenceDetails.note: Official DB25 execution with diamond-set case and constellation motif.

referenceDetails.name: Monopusher Chronograph
referenceDetails.note: Official DB25 chronograph execution framed as a tribute to classic watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: DB27
keyCollections.description: De Bethune DB27 is an official collection of the brand's Titan Hawk-era self-winding watches, best treated as an archive-style collection rather than a live model family.

image.alt: De Bethune DB27 collection watch image

keyCollections.name: DB28
keyCollections.description: De Bethune DB28 is the maison's signature experimental collection, built around floating lugs, sculptural titanium architecture, open horological displays, and high-complication variants.

referenceDetails.name: DB28GS Swordfish
referenceDetails.note: Official product copy describes Swordfish as a diving watch continuing the sport line started with DB28GS Grand Bleu, with attention to time and immersion legibility.

referenceDetails.name: DB28
referenceDetails.note: Official product copy frames this DB28 as a reinterpretation of De Bethune classics, emphasizing the patented floating-lug system and avant-garde horological vision.

referenceDetails.name: DB28
referenceDetails.note: Official product data lists this second DB28 reference in the current collection, sharing the collection's floating-lug architecture and bold De Bethune identity.

referenceDetails.name: DB28 Tourbillon
referenceDetails.note: Official product copy presents the DB28 Tourbillon as a high-complication execution with a rose-gold case, diamond setting, and ultra-light 30-second tourbillon indication.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: DB28 is the line most collectors associate with De Bethune's modern identity: floating lugs, futuristic materials, sculptural movements, and classical finishing reimagined as avant-garde watchmaking.

faqItems.question: What defines the De Bethune DB28?
faqItems.answer: The official product pages emphasize the DB28's floating lugs, lightness, avant-garde architecture, and modern De Bethune styling.

faqItems.question: Is DB28 a single reference?
faqItems.answer: No. The current official DB28 collection includes multiple references, including Swordfish, DB28, and DB28 Tourbillon executions.

faqItems.question: Why is DB28 important for De Bethune?
faqItems.answer: It is the collection that most visibly carries the brand's contemporary experimental identity while preserving high-end mechanical finishing.

keyCollections.name: DB28XP
keyCollections.description: De Bethune DB28XP is the ultra-thin, experimental branch of the DB28 family, represented by official press releases for meteorite, Kind of Blue, Steel Wheels, and tourbillon executions.

referenceDetails.name: DB28XP Meteorite
referenceDetails.note: An official De Bethune press release from March 2021 presents the DB28XP Meteorite with dedicated press images and technical data files.

referenceDetails.name: DB28XP Kind of Blue
referenceDetails.note: An August 2023 official press entry documents the DB28XP Kind of Blue, including downloadable press images and technical data.

image.alt: De Bethune DB28XP Kind of Blue watch

referenceDetails.note: An October 2024 official press release presents the DB28XP Steel Wheels Tourbillon, with image and technical data downloads.

image.alt: De Bethune DB28XP Steel Wheels Tourbillon watch

timeline.event: De Bethune publishes official press material for the DB28XP Meteorite.
The DB28XP Kind of Blue appears in De Bethune's official press lounge.
De Bethune publishes official material for the DB28XP Steel Wheels Tourbillon.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: DB28XP gives De Bethune a focused page for collectors tracking the brand's thinnest and most experimental DB28 expressions, from meteorite dials to blue titanium styling and Steel Wheels tourbillon mechanics.

image.alt: De Bethune DB28XP Kind of Blue watch

gallery.alt: De Bethune DB28XP Steel Wheels Tourbillon watch

faqItems.question: What is the De Bethune DB28XP?
faqItems.answer: DB28XP is a specialized branch of the DB28 family, documented by De Bethune through official press releases for Meteorite, Kind of Blue, and Steel Wheels variants.

faqItems.question: Which DB28XP references are official examples?
faqItems.answer: Official De Bethune press pages include DB28XP Meteorite, DB28XP Kind of Blue, DB28XP Steel Wheels, and DB28XP Steel Wheels Tourbillon.

faqItems.question: Why does DB28XP matter for collectors?
faqItems.answer: It concentrates De Bethune's experimental DB28 language into a highly specific family with distinct material, color, and tourbillon expressions.

funFacts.title: Press-backed trail
funFacts.body: The DB28XP line has multiple dedicated entries in De Bethune's official press lounge.

funFacts.title: Tourbillon branch
funFacts.body: De Bethune separately documents the DB28XP Steel Wheels Tourbillon as a 2024 press release.

keyCollections.name: DB28XS
keyCollections.description: The DB28XS is De Bethune’s compact 38.7–39 mm interpretation of the DB28, preserving the floating-lug architecture and open, contemporary aesthetic while scaling the icon down for slimmer wrists and broader everyday wear.

referenceDetails.name: DB28XS Steel Wheels
referenceDetails.note: Official De Bethune launch article describing the compact openworked DB28XS and explicitly positioning it as a more intimate version of the icon.

referenceDetails.name: DB28XS Sea Tourbillon
referenceDetails.note: Official De Bethune journal page describing the blued-titanium sea-themed tourbillon variant and its 30-second rotation concept.

referenceDetails.name: DB28XS Aérolite
referenceDetails.note: Official De Bethune launch article for the 2024 meteorite-based DB28XS, showing the line’s continued material experimentation.

timeline.event: The DB28XS line was presented in official De Bethune communications as the compact, more intimate extension of the DB28 family.
De Bethune unveiled the DB28XS Aérolite, a meteorite-dial interpretation that pushed the collection’s material experimentation further.
Official collection-page language described the DB28XS range as 38.7 mm watches with hours, minutes, power reserve indication, and tourbillon options.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: DB28XS is the compact branch of the DB28 family, important because it brings De Bethune’s signature floating-lug design to a smaller wrist profile without losing the brand’s technical identity.

keyCollections.name: DB29
keyCollections.description: De Bethune DB29 is the brand's Maxichrono Tourbillon collection page, centred on a high-complication chronograph-tourbillon architecture with coaxial chronograph indications.

referenceDetails.name: DB29 Maxichrono Tourbillon DB29RS1
referenceDetails.note: The current model shown on De Bethune's official DB29 collection page.

image.alt: De Bethune DB29 Maxichrono Tourbillon DB29RS1 watch

keyCollections.name: DBD
keyCollections.description: Digital-display collection using rotating discs to show jumping hours and trailing minutes in an unconventional layout.

keyCollections.name: DB Eight
keyCollections.description: De Bethune DB Eight is an official eight-sided-case collection; the brand does not expose multiple current model references for it.

image.alt: De Bethune DB Eight collection watch

keyCollections.name: DB Kind of Two
keyCollections.description: DB Kind of Two is De Bethune’s reversible, double-faced watch family, built around a single case that offers two distinct identities on opposite sides. The concept merges classical and contemporary aesthetics while showcasing the maison’s technical ingenuity in managing display orientation, case turning, and dial architecture.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: This family is important because it crystallizes De Bethune’s talent for building technically complex, emotionally expressive watches that can transform their character entirely through a reversible case and dual-display architecture.

timeline.event: The collection remains represented on De Bethune’s official site through an active Grande Complication product page.
De Bethune’s official journal and press materials continue to frame the family as a two-faced concept built around reversible wearing and dual identities.
A newer DB Kind of Two Jumping GMT announcement shows the family remains creatively active and evolving.

faqItems.question: What is the core idea behind DB Kind of Two?
faqItems.answer: A reversible watch architecture with two very different dial faces, allowing the same timepiece to present different personalities and functions.

faqItems.question: Is DB Kind of Two a single watch or a collection family?
faqItems.answer: It is best treated as a collection family, with multiple executions such as Tourbillon, Grande Complication, and Jumping GMT variants.

timeline.event: David Zanetta and Denis Flageollet co-found De Bethune in L'Auberson, Switzerland.
Introduces the world's lightest tourbillon using titanium and silicon components.
Debuts the DB28, which becomes the brand's most iconic model with its floating lugs.
Wins the Aiguille d'Or (Golden Hand) at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève.
Introduces patented triple pare-chute shock absorber system.
Launches the DB Kind of Two Tourbillon, combining classical aesthetics with contemporary innovation.
Denis Flageollet becomes sole owner; continues pushing boundaries in metallurgy and movement technology.
Released five new models in 2025, continuing to push avant-garde independent haute horlogerie.
Released smallest-ever Kind of Blue tourbillon (38.7mm) and two downsized Starry Varius models at Geneva Watch Days.
Collaborated with Louis Vuitton on LVDB-03 Louis Varius Project Sympathique clock-and-watch set (12 pieces).

faqItems.question: What makes De Bethune special?
faqItems.answer: De Bethune is renowned for technological innovation including the lightest tourbillon, patented shock absorbers, and mastery of blued titanium, combined with a distinctive starry-sky dial aesthetic.

faqItems.question: Who makes De Bethune movements?
faqItems.answer: All De Bethune movements are designed and manufactured in-house by master watchmaker Denis Flageollet and his team in L'Auberson, Switzerland.

name: DE RIJKE & CO.
description: DE RIJKE & CO. is an independent watch brand producing limited-edition timepieces with a focus on artisanal craft and bespoke finishing. The brand operates within the independent watchmaking community with a collector-focused approach.

keyCollections.name: DR01
keyCollections.description: The brand's debut timepiece featuring Dutch design sensibility with a Swiss automatic movement and maritime influences.

timeline.event: Pieter de Rijke founds DE RIJKE & CO., bringing Dutch design to Swiss-made watchmaking.
Debuts the DR01 collection, combining maritime heritage with modern micro-brand aesthetics.

faqItems.question: Where is DE RIJKE & CO. from?
faqItems.answer: DE RIJKE & CO. is a Dutch watch brand that combines Netherlands-inspired design with Swiss-made movements.

name: Dennison
description: Dennison traces its origins to Aaron Lufkin Dennison, who patented an air and watertight watch case in 1872, and was revived by Geneva-born designer Emmanuel Gueit to bring mid-century case shapes back to life. Each timepiece honours a storied heritage in case manufacture while channelling a distinctly modern aesthetic.

keyCollections.name: Heritage
keyCollections.description: Classic timepieces paying homage to Dennison's Victorian-era watchmaking roots with traditional design elements.

keyCollections.name: Modern
keyCollections.description: Contemporary reinterpretations of British watchmaking heritage with updated materials and movements.

timeline.event: Aaron Lufkin Dennison, known as the father of American watchmaking, establishes watch case manufacturing in Birmingham, England.
Dennison Watch Case Company becomes one of the largest case makers in England.
Original Dennison factory closes as the British watch industry declines.
Dennison brand revived, honouring the legacy of Aaron Lufkin Dennison's contributions to watchmaking.

faqItems.question: Who was Aaron Lufkin Dennison?
faqItems.answer: Aaron Lufkin Dennison (1812–1895) is known as the father of American watchmaking. He pioneered mass production of interchangeable watch parts before moving to England.

faqItems.question: Is Dennison a British brand?
faqItems.answer: The modern Dennison brand honours the legacy of the original Dennison Watch Case Company founded in Birmingham, England in 1872, rooted in British and American watchmaking heritage.

name: Dior
description: Christian Dior entered watchmaking through its fashion house in the 1970s and today produces watches in La Chaux-de-Fonds through Dior Horlogerie. The brand is particularly known for its Dior VIII and Chiffre Rouge collections, blending haute couture aesthetic sensibility with Swiss watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: Grand Bal
keyCollections.description: Haute couture watches with oscillating weights inspired by the movement of Dior ball gowns, featuring precious materials.

keyCollections.name: La D de Dior
keyCollections.description: Elegant ladies' watch with a distinctive oval case and minimalist aesthetic, available in precious metals and gems.

keyCollections.name: Dior VIII
keyCollections.description: Contemporary women's watch combining high-tech ceramic with haute couture design codes.

keyCollections.name: Grand Soir
keyCollections.description: High jewellery watches featuring extraordinary gem-setting and artistic dial designs inspired by Dior's couture fabrics.

timeline.event: Christian Dior founds his fashion house in Paris with backing from Marcel Boussac.
Dior launches its first watch collection under licence, entering the luxury watch market.
Establishes Dior Horlogerie in La Chaux-de-Fonds, bringing watchmaking in-house.
Launches the Dior VIII, combining ceramic with haute couture design.
Introduces the Grand Bal collection with its innovative oscillating weight inspired by ball gowns.
LVMH takes full ownership of Christian Dior SE, integrating watch operations further.
Relaunched Chiffre Rouge mens watch line with higher-end complications, targeting luxury watchmaking credibility.

faqItems.question: Does Dior make its own watch movements?
faqItems.answer: Dior has its own watchmaking facility in La Chaux-de-Fonds. Some models use in-house calibres, while others use movements from Swiss specialists.

faqItems.question: What is the Dior Grand Bal?
faqItems.answer: The Grand Bal is Dior's signature haute couture watch collection, featuring an oscillating weight designed to mimic the swirl of a Dior ball gown, decorated with feathers, fabrics, or gems.

name: Dominique Renaud
description: The Dominique Renaud brand — the second expression of Haute Horlogerie by Dominique Renaud — explores watchmaking at the absolute frontier of complication and artisanship. Co-founder of the legendary Renaud & Papi manufacture, Renaud now creates extraordinarily intricate timepieces in extremely limited numbers for the most dedicated collectors.

keyCollections.name: DR01 Twelve First
keyCollections.description: Debut timepiece limited to 12 pieces, featuring a revolutionary escapement and seconds mechanism designed over years of research.

timeline.event: Dominique Renaud co-founds Renaud & Papi (now Audemars Piguet Renaud & Papi), the renowned complications specialist.
Launches his own brand, Dominique Renaud, to explore radical horological ideas independently.
Debuts the DR01 Twelve First, featuring an innovative constant-force escapement, limited to 12 pieces.

faqItems.question: Who is Dominique Renaud?
faqItems.answer: Dominique Renaud is a legendary Swiss watchmaker who co-founded Renaud & Papi (now part of Audemars Piguet), before launching his own brand in 2018 to pursue radical horological innovations.

faqItems.question: What is special about the DR01?
faqItems.answer: The DR01 Twelve First features a revolutionary escapement system developed over years of research, limited to just 12 pieces, representing Renaud's personal vision for the future of timekeeping.

name: Done Watches
description: Founded in Neuchâtel in 2016, DONE Watches is an independent brand creating mechanical timepieces where every detail is considered and nothing is left to chance. The brand's name reflects its uncompromising philosophy: a watch is only released when it is truly DONE — perfectly finished in every respect.

keyCollections.name: Mechanics
keyCollections.description: Swiss-made mechanical watches offering honest, straightforward design with quality movements at accessible prices.

timeline.event: Done Watches founded in Switzerland, aiming to create honest, well-made timepieces at fair prices.
Establishes direct-to-consumer model, cutting out traditional retail markups.

faqItems.question: What is Done Watches' philosophy?
faqItems.answer: Done Watches focuses on offering well-made Swiss timepieces with transparent pricing and honest design, without the inflated costs of traditional luxury branding.

name: Dornblüth & Sohn
description: Dornblüth & Sohn is a German independent watchmaker based in Kalbe, Germany, founded by Dieter Dornblüth. Working with his son, the atelier hand-assembles small quantities of precision mechanical watches entirely on-site, using traditional German watchmaking techniques to achieve movement quality rivalling far more expensive brands.

keyCollections.description: The 99.0 is Dornblüth & Sohn’s foundational hand-wound watch family, a classic Glashütte-style three-hand design with small seconds, a 42 mm case, and an emphasis on traditional German finishing and movement architecture.

referenceDetails.name: 99.0 (1) ST
referenceDetails.note: Official product page for the stainless-steel 99.0 variant with case, dial, and movement specifications.

referenceDetails.name: 99.0 collection overview
referenceDetails.note: Official brand collection page listing the 99.0 family as part of the current catalogue.

referenceDetails.name: Calibre 99.0
referenceDetails.note: Official French collection page with the movement and case details for the caliber-based line.

timeline.event: The official Dornblüth & Sohn site continues to list 99.0 among its current core collections.
The 99.0 family is presented as the classic small-seconds watch within the brand catalogue.
Official specifications emphasize a 42 mm case, hand-wound movement, and traditional Glashütte-style finishing.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: 99.0 is the canonical Dornblüth & Sohn entry point and an important reference for the brand’s identity: compact, traditional, hand-finished German watchmaking with clear family continuity.

faqItems.question: What type of watch is the 99.0?
faqItems.answer: It is a hand-wound, small-seconds mechanical watch in Dornblüth & Sohn’s classic dress-watch style.

faqItems.question: What size is the 99.0 case?
faqItems.answer: The official page lists a 42 mm case diameter.

keyCollections.description: Power reserve variant with a hand-engraved balance cock, showcasing traditional German finishing techniques.

keyCollections.name: Quintus
keyCollections.description: Regulator-style dial with separate hour, minute, and second displays, highlighting classical Glashütte tradition.

timeline.event: Master watchmaker Dirk Dornblüth founds Dornblüth & Sohn in Kalbe, Saxony-Anhalt, Germany.
Launches the 99.0, establishing the brand's identity of hand-finished German watchmaking at accessible prices.
Gains cult following among watch enthusiasts for exceptional hand-finishing at modest prices.
Expands lineup with power reserve and regulator variants while maintaining small-batch production.
Continues as one of the most respected independent German watchmakers, producing all movements in-house.

faqItems.question: Why is Dornblüth & Sohn so respected?
faqItems.answer: Dornblüth & Sohn offers hand-finished in-house movements with traditional German finishing (hand-engraved balance cocks, blued screws) at prices far below comparable Swiss brands.

faqItems.question: Where is Dornblüth & Sohn based?
faqItems.answer: The brand is based in Kalbe, Saxony-Anhalt, Germany — not in the traditional Glashütte watchmaking region, but producing work that rivals its more famous neighbours.

name: Doxa
description: Founded in Le Locle in 1889, Doxa gained legendary status among divers with the introduction of the Sub in 1967, which pioneered the bright orange dial that became iconic in professional diving. The brand, relaunched multiple times, continues to produce the Sub in faithful tribute to the original.

keyCollections.name: SUB 300

keyCollections.whyItMatters: SUB 300 is one of the clearest entry points into DOXA's dive-watch identity: compact cushion-case proportions, color-coded dials, and a decompression-scale bezel carried into a modern catalogue.

faqItems.question: What kind of watch is the DOXA SUB 300?
faqItems.answer: It is a professional-style dive-watch collection built around DOXA's recognizable cushion case, dive bezel, and color-coded dial system.

faqItems.answer: DOXA's current collection page lists variants including Professional, Sharkhunter, Searambler, Caribbean, Divingstar, Aquamarine, Whitepearl, and Sea Emerald.

timeline.event: Georges Ducommun founds Doxa in Le Locle, Switzerland, initially producing pocket watches.
Doxa wins Grand Prix at the Swiss National Exhibition in Bern.
Launches the SUB 300T, one of the first purpose-built dive watches with an orange dial for underwater visibility.
Jacques Cousteau's U.S. Divers organisation consults on the SUB 300T design.
Brand revived under new ownership, reintroducing the iconic SUB line.
Romeo F. Jenny becomes CEO, overseeing the brand's 130th anniversary celebrations.
Maintained focus on dive watch heritage with continued SUB collection releases and growing collector interest.
Launched SUB 250T GMT, re-engineered SUB 750T with slimmer case, and limited ceramic SUB 300 (11 pcs, Ahmed Seddiqi exclusive).
Debuted SUB 200 II with larger 44mm case and five dial colors.

faqItems.question: What does 'Doxa' mean?
faqItems.answer: Doxa comes from the Greek word (Δόξα) meaning 'belief' or 'glory'. In Christian contexts it refers to divine glory.

faqItems.question: Why is Doxa famous?
faqItems.answer: Doxa is best known for its dive watches, particularly the SUB 300T from 1967, which pioneered the orange dial for underwater legibility and the no-decompression bezel.

name: Dumoreau
description: Dumoreau is an independent French watchmaker producing limited-edition watches with a strong emphasis on classical finishing and traditional horological values. The brand occupies a niche position within the independent watchmaking scene.

keyCollections.name: Orion

keyCollections.name: Spartan

timeline.event: Jérôme Dumoreau founds Dumoreau as an independent French watchmaking brand focused on accessible haute horlogerie aesthetics.
Launches first collection via crowdfunding, gaining attention for open-dial designs at competitive price points.

faqItems.question: Where is Dumoreau based?
faqItems.answer: Dumoreau is a French watch brand creating watches that blend French design sensibility with Swiss mechanical movements.

faqItems.question: What makes Dumoreau different?
faqItems.answer: Dumoreau focuses on offering open-worked and skeleton-style dials at accessible price points, bringing haute horlogerie aesthetics to a wider audience.

name: Dwiss
description: DWISS, founded in 2011 by Rafael Simoes Miranda, is a Swiss microbrand redefining timepieces through radical design innovation. The most design-awarded Swiss microbrand, DWISS explores new forms of time display, unconventional materials and bold architectural concepts — always with full creative independence and Swiss engineering at its core.

faqItems.answer: DWISS presents M3 as a displaced-hours collection with an unconventional dial layout instead of a traditional central-hour display.

faqItems.answer: DWISS's archived product data includes bracelet and rubber-strap variants in colors such as black, blue, green, and white.

timeline.event: Rafael Simões Miranda founds DWISS (Design Watch Independent Switzerland Studio) to create design-forward mechanical watches.
Wins the Red Dot Design Award for the M1 Silver, establishing DWISS's reputation for innovative watch design.
Launches the M3 with wandering-hours complication, becoming the brand's signature piece.

faqItems.question: What does DWISS stand for?
faqItems.answer: DWISS stands for 'Design Watch Independent Switzerland Studio', reflecting its focus on design innovation in Swiss watchmaking.

faqItems.question: What is the wandering hours display?
faqItems.answer: The wandering-hours complication uses rotating discs that pass over a minute scale to indicate the time, avoiding traditional watch hands entirely.

name: Eberhard & Co.
description: Eberhard & Co. is a Swiss watch brand founded in 1887 by Georges-Edouard Eberhard in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, known as the first manufacturer to produce a wrist chronograph. The Chrono 4 — featuring four counters aligned horizontally — and the Contograf are among the brand's most celebrated models.

keyCollections.name: Chrono 4
keyCollections.description: Chrono 4 is Eberhard & Co.’s signature chronograph family, defined by its patented layout of four horizontally aligned counters, a distinctive design cue that the brand presents as a major technical and visual innovation.

keyCollections.name: Extra-Fort
keyCollections.description: Extra-Fort is one of Eberhard & Co.’s heritage chronograph lines, rooted in the brand’s long-running sporting tradition and currently presented in modern automatic and split-seconds variants with a refined classic character.

keyCollections.name: Tazio Nuvolari
keyCollections.description: Tazio Nuvolari is Eberhard & Co.’s motorsport-themed collection, created as a tribute to the legendary racing driver and expressed through chronographs that emphasize speed, sporting heritage, and vintage racing cues.

keyCollections.name: Traversetolo
keyCollections.description: Traversetolo is Eberhard & Co.’s classic time-and-date family built around a traditional movement conceived in the 1950s, presented as a large, reliable everyday watch with a restrained, heritage-driven aesthetic.

timeline.event: Georges-Emile Eberhard founds the company in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, at just 22 years old.
Inaugurates a grand five-storey headquarters on rue Leopold Robert, becoming a La Chaux-de-Fonds landmark.
Georges and Maurice Eberhard, sons of the founder, take over leadership of the company.
Launches the Chrono 4, patented as the world's first chronograph with four aligned counters.

faqItems.question: Where is Eberhard & Co. based?
faqItems.answer: Eberhard & Co. is headquartered in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, the historic heart of Swiss watchmaking, where it has been based since 1887.

faqItems.question: What is the Chrono 4?
faqItems.answer: The Chrono 4 is Eberhard & Co.'s signature patented chronograph featuring four horizontally aligned sub-dials, a world first when introduced in 2004.

Launches Class-1 collection and becomes official timekeeper for sailing regattas.

faqItems.question: What does 'Edox' mean?
faqItems.answer: The name Edox is a portmanteau of the Greek words for 'time' (edor) and 'glory' (doxa), reflecting the brand's mission to create glorious timepieces.

faqItems.question: What is the Delfin?
faqItems.answer: The Edox Delfin, introduced in 1961, was the first watch to use a double O-ring crown sealing system for water resistance, a significant technical innovation.

name: Egeiro

The brand exhibits at Geneva Watch Days as one of the new voices in independent watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: V1

faqItems.answer: Egeiro comes from the Greek word meaning 'to awaken' or 'to arise', reflecting the brand's aim to revive vintage watchmaking aesthetics.

faqItems.answer: Egeiro watches are designed in England and use Swiss automatic movements, hand-assembled with a focus on British motoring heritage.

faqItems.answer: Elka watches were produced as affordable American-market timepieces, typically using Swiss movements in cases assembled domestically.

name: Emmanuel Bouchet
description: Emmanuel Bouchet is a Swiss independent watchmaker based in Les Bayards, Neuchâtel, creating technically ambitious timepieces driven by his passion for mechanical innovation and aesthetic refinement. His Complication One, with its double retrograde instantaneous jump mechanism, established the brand as a benchmark for independent horological invention.

keyCollections.name: Complication One
keyCollections.description: Emmanuel Bouchet’s signature high-complication line, launched at the end of 2014 and now framed as a decade-spanning platform for the brand’s slow-time philosophy, with an integrated in-house movement, jumping indications, and a front-facing escapement architecture.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: It is the brand-defining collection: the first eponymous watch from Emmanuel Bouchet and the clearest expression of his approach to deconstructing time through mechanical display.
