Introduces new case shapes and dial configurations, expanding the Complication One family.

faqItems.question: What is special about Emmanuel Bouchet watches?
faqItems.answer: Emmanuel Bouchet is known for his architectural movement design featuring mirror-polished bridges visible through the dial, creating a distinctive three-dimensional visual effect.

faqItems.question: Where is Emmanuel Bouchet based?
faqItems.answer: Emmanuel Bouchet is based in Switzerland, creating independent haute horlogerie pieces with hand-finished movements.

name: Epos
description: Since 1983, EPOS has cultivated the art of Swiss mechanics, creating watches where complications, craftsmanship and refined dial artistry converge. Based in Grenchen, the brand is particularly celebrated for its ornate guilloché dials, enamel work and intricate engravings — delivering exceptional decorative Swiss watchmaking at compelling price points.

keyCollections.name: Originale
keyCollections.description: Classic dress watch collection with open-heart dials and skeleton options showcasing mechanical movements.

keyCollections.name: Sportive
keyCollections.description: Sport-oriented collection including divers and pilots' watches with robust specifications.

keyCollections.name: Emotion
keyCollections.description: Ladies' collection featuring elegant case designs with diamond settings and mother-of-pearl dials.

keyCollections.name: Perfection
keyCollections.description: Slim dress watches with moonphase and calendar complications for formal occasions.

timeline.event: Peter Hofer founds Epos in Biel/Bienne, Switzerland, dedicated to preserving traditional Swiss mechanical watchmaking.
Establishes international distribution, becoming known for skeleton and open-heart watches at accessible prices.
Expands the collection with the Oeuvre d'Art series featuring hand-engraved and enamelled dials.
Maintained its position producing affordable Swiss mechanical watches with skeleton and open-heart designs.

faqItems.question: What does 'Epos' mean?
faqItems.answer: Epos comes from the Greek word meaning 'word' or 'story', reflecting the brand's commitment to telling the story of traditional mechanical watchmaking.

faqItems.question: What is Epos known for?
faqItems.answer: Epos specialises in mechanical watches featuring skeleton dials, open hearts, and classical complications at relatively accessible price points, keeping traditional Swiss craft alive.

name: Eterna
description: Eterna is a Swiss watch brand founded in 1856 by Josef Girard and Urs Schild in Grenchen, Switzerland, responsible for developing the automatic ball-bearing rotor system in 1948 that became the foundation of ETA movements. The brand is also credited with developing the first five-ball-bearing rotor, a technology it licensed widely.
defunct_reason: Eterna filed for bankruptcy in 2020 after years of financial difficulty under the Festina Group.
revival_attempt: Acquired by new investors circa 2021 and relaunched as Eterna Watches. Current range includes Kontiki and 1940 Chronograph lines. Website active at eterna.com.

keyCollections.name: KonTiki
keyCollections.description: Eterna KonTiki is the brand's historic sport-watch family inspired by Thor Heyerdahl's Kon-Tiki expedition, spanning Super KonTiki divers, bronze limited editions, 4 Hands automatics, Voyage models, and Royal KonTiki GMT references.

referenceDetails.name: Super KonTiki Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Eterna's official product feed lists the Super KonTiki Automatic with ETA 2824-2 movement, rotating bezel, 44 mm steel case, sapphire crystal, and date.

referenceDetails.name: KonTiki Bronze
referenceDetails.note: Eterna's official product copy marks the KonTiki Bronze as a 70th-anniversary limited edition tied directly to Thor Heyerdahl's KonTiki expedition story.

referenceDetails.name: Royal KonTiki GMT
referenceDetails.note: Eterna's official KonTiki collection feed lists Royal KonTiki GMT references as travel-time sport watches inside the wider KonTiki family.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: KonTiki is Eterna's clearest collector-facing name because it links a real adventure narrative to a durable sport-watch vocabulary, while giving the modern catalogue a recognizable diver and GMT anchor.

faqItems.question: What is Eterna KonTiki?
faqItems.answer: KonTiki is Eterna's adventure-inspired sport-watch family, named for Thor Heyerdahl's Kon-Tiki expedition and represented by divers, GMT watches, and limited editions.

faqItems.question: Which KonTiki models are official examples?
faqItems.answer: Eterna's official store feed includes Super KonTiki Automatic, KonTiki Bronze, KonTiki 4 Hands, KonTiki Voyage, Lady KonTiki, and Royal KonTiki GMT examples.

funFacts.title: Expedition link
funFacts.body: Eterna's official KonTiki Bronze copy explicitly ties the watch to Thor Heyerdahl's legendary KonTiki expedition.

funFacts.title: Diver backbone
funFacts.body: The official Super KonTiki Automatic specification includes a rotating bezel, sapphire crystal, and 44 mm steel case.

keyCollections.name: Eternity
keyCollections.description: Eterna’s Eternity collection is a slim, classical dress-watch line that emphasizes refined proportions, understated styling, and the brand’s long movement-making heritage.

keyCollections.name: Tangaroa
keyCollections.description: Eterna Tangaroa is a KonTiki-adjacent dress-sport collection currently represented by automatic and moonphase chronograph references, combining steel cases, sapphire crystals, Swiss automatic movements, and calendar-rich complications.

referenceDetails.name: Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph Grey / Steel
referenceDetails.note: Eterna's official Tangaroa product page describes a self-winding Valjoux 7751 chronograph with date, 24-hour display, day, month, moon phase, and chronograph indications.

image.alt: Eterna Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph grey steel watch

referenceDetails.name: Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph White / Steel
referenceDetails.note: A white-dial steel variant from Eterna's official Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph product variants.

image.alt: Eterna Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph white steel watch

referenceDetails.name: Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph White / Brown Leather
referenceDetails.note: A white-dial brown-leather variant from Eterna's official Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph product variants.

image.alt: Eterna Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph brown leather watch

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Tangaroa gives Eterna's modern catalogue a more complicated dress-sport lane than core KonTiki divers, concentrating calendar, moonphase, and chronograph functions in a recognizable automatic family.

image.alt: Eterna Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph grey steel watch

gallery.alt: Eterna Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph white steel watch
Eterna Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph brown leather watch

faqItems.question: What is Eterna Tangaroa?
faqItems.answer: Tangaroa is an Eterna dress-sport family, currently represented on the official store by Moonphase Chronograph variants and related KonTiki Tangaroa references.

faqItems.question: What movement does the Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph use?
faqItems.answer: Eterna's official product text says the Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph uses a self-winding Valjoux 7751 calibre.

funFacts.title: Calendar-rich chronograph
funFacts.body: The official Tangaroa Moonphase Chronograph copy lists date, day, month, 24-hour display, moon phase, and chronograph functions.

funFacts.title: KonTiki overlap
funFacts.body: Eterna's official KonTiki collection feed also lists an Eterna KonTiki Tangaroa reference, showing the family overlap in the current store data.

keyCollections.name: Heritage
keyCollections.description: Eterna Heritage is the brand's vintage-inspired long-tail line, currently best represented by the official 1942 Heritage Automatic pulsometer family with colorful dials, leather straps, and classic automatic chronograph-adjacent styling.

referenceDetails.name: 1942 Heritage Automatic Blue
referenceDetails.note: Eterna's official product feed lists this blue-dial 1942 Heritage Automatic as a Heritage/Pulsometer model on black leather.

referenceDetails.name: 1942 Heritage Automatic Salmon
referenceDetails.note: A salmon-dial variant from Eterna's official 1942 Heritage Automatic product variants.

referenceDetails.name: 1942 Heritage Automatic Lime
referenceDetails.note: A lime-dial variant from Eterna's official 1942 Heritage Automatic product variants.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Heritage lets Eterna keep a visible bridge to its mid-century design vocabulary, giving the catalogue a retro-styled, color-forward alternative to KonTiki sport watches and contemporary dress models.

faqItems.question: What is Eterna Heritage?
faqItems.answer: Heritage is Eterna's vintage-inspired family, currently represented in the official store by 1942 Heritage Automatic pulsometer variants.

faqItems.question: Which Heritage references are official examples?
faqItems.answer: Eterna's official product feed lists 1942 Heritage Automatic variants such as 1942.41.80.1177, 1942.41.40.1177, and 1942.41.30.1177.

funFacts.title: Color spread
funFacts.body: The official 1942 Heritage Automatic product variants include blue, navy, lime, and salmon dial options.

funFacts.title: Pulsometer handle
funFacts.body: Eterna's official product handle identifies the 1942 Heritage Automatic as a pulsometer-linked heritage watch.

timeline.event: Josef Girard and Urs Schild found Eterna in Grenchen, Switzerland.
Invents the ball-bearing automatic winding rotor, a revolutionary mechanism that becomes the industry standard.
Sponsors Thor Heyerdahl's Kon-Tiki raft expedition across the Pacific, inspiring the legendary KonTiki collection.
Establishes ETA SA as its movement-making subsidiary, which later becomes the world's largest watch movement manufacturer.
Acquired by China Haidian Holdings, beginning a new chapter for the brand.
Continued rebuilding under new ownership after previous financial difficulties, with limited new releases.

faqItems.question: What is the connection between Eterna and ETA?
faqItems.answer: Eterna founded ETA in 1856 as its movement-making division. ETA (named from the first and last letters of 'Eterna') eventually became the world's largest supplier of Swiss watch movements, now part of the Swatch Group.

faqItems.question: What is the five-ball-bearing logo?
faqItems.answer: Eterna's logo of five small balls represents the five ball bearings used in the brand's revolutionary 1948 automatic winding rotor system, which became the standard for automatic watches.

name: Exaequo - Salvador Dalí
description: EXAEQUO creates artistic watches in official partnership with the Gala – Salvador Dalí Foundation, producing timepieces where surrealist art and Swiss horology are inseparable. Each collection draws on Dalí's iconic imagery and dreamlike aesthetic — wearable works of art that challenge time itself.

keyCollections.name: Soft Watch
keyCollections.description: Surrealist timepiece inspired by Dalí's iconic melting clocks from 'The Persistence of Memory', featuring a flexible case.

keyCollections.name: Cyclopean Eye
keyCollections.description: Bold watch featuring the recurring Dalí motif of an eye, with artistic dial designs licensed from the Dalí estate.

timeline.event: ExAequo launches a licensed collection of watches inspired by the works of Salvador Dalí, with approval from the Dalí Foundation.
The Soft Watch becomes a cult collectible, directly referencing Dalí's melting clocks with its flexible silicone case.

faqItems.question: Are ExAequo Dalí watches official?
faqItems.answer: Yes, ExAequo watches are officially licensed by the Gala-Salvador Dalí Foundation, which manages the artist's intellectual property.

faqItems.question: What makes the Soft Watch special?
faqItems.answer: The Soft Watch has a flexible case that drapes over the wrist like Dalí's famous melting clocks from 'The Persistence of Memory', making it a wearable piece of surrealist art.

name: Eza
description: Eza is a German watch brand with roots dating to 1910 in Schwenningen, revived in 2015 by Sebastian Walter with a focus on clean, honest dive watches. The 1972 and Sealander models reference mid-century German tool watch design while featuring Swiss movements and quality finishing at accessible price points.
defunct_reason: The original Eza watchmaking business in Schwenningen, Germany closed in the 1980s during a broader collapse of regional German watch manufacturing.
revival_attempt: Revived in 2015 by Sebastian Walter with a focus on honest, tool-focused dive watches referencing mid-century German design, now well regarded in the microbrand community.

keyCollections.name: Sealander
keyCollections.description: Eza Sealander is the brand’s dive-watch line, built around vintage-inspired tool-watch styling and professional water resistance, with the collection positioned as Eza’s nautical counterpart to its pilot models.

timeline.event: Collection remains listed on Eza Watches official site as Sealander.

keyCollections.name: AirFighter
keyCollections.description: Eza AirFighter is a pilot-watch collection with large, highly legible dials and aviation-first design cues, presented as a modern take on classic military observer watches.

timeline.event: Collection remains listed on Eza Watches official site as AirFighter.
Michael Rieder founds EZA (Eichstätter Zeitmesser und Armbanduhren) in Eichstätt, Bavaria, Germany.
Launches the Sealander dive watch, quickly gaining a following among microbrand enthusiasts for its build quality and value.

faqItems.question: What does EZA stand for?
faqItems.answer: EZA stands for 'Eichstätter Zeitmesser und Armbanduhren' (Eichstätt Timepieces and Wristwatches), named after its Bavarian hometown.

faqItems.question: Where are EZA watches made?
faqItems.answer: EZA watches are designed in Germany and assembled using Swiss automatic movements, offering German engineering with Swiss mechanical heart.

name: F.P. Journe
description: F.P. Journe was founded in Geneva in 1999 by François-Paul Journe, who had already established his reputation making tourbillon pocket watches by hand in a Paris attic. The manufacture produces around 900 watches per year and is considered by many collectors to represent the pinnacle of contemporary independent watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: Chronomètre à Résonance
keyCollections.description: F.P. Journe’s breakthrough twin-movement chronometer built around acoustic resonance between two balances, a hallmark concept that turned a historic horological idea into one of the brand’s defining signatures.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: It is one of the most important independent-watchmaking concepts of the modern era: technically distinctive, historically rooted, and central to F.P. Journe’s identity.

timeline.event: F.P. Journe introduced the first Résonance wristwatch, establishing the brand’s resonance concept in modern wristwatch form.
F.P. Journe’s official heritage article explains the resonance principle and the watch’s twin-movement architecture.
The brand marked the 20th anniversary of Chronomètre à Résonance with an official unveiling of a new generation.

referenceDetails.name: Chronomètre à Résonance
referenceDetails.note: Official current collection page for the resonance chronometer.

referenceDetails.name: Chronomètre à Résonance 20th anniversary update
referenceDetails.note: Official 2020 announcement of the new generation and the 20-year celebration.

referenceDetails.name: Résonance heritage article
referenceDetails.note: Official heritage article describing the phenomenon and the twin independent movements.

keyCollections.name: Tourbillon Souverain
keyCollections.description: F.P. Journe’s Tourbillon Souverain is the signature constant-force tourbillon line, defined by the remontoir d’égalité, deadbeat seconds, and the brand’s precision-first approach. It is the collection that launched the F.P. Journe brand identity and remains one of its most recognizable horological statements.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is the foundational F.P. Journe wristwatch concept: the first model in the Souveraine collection, and the first wristwatch to combine a tourbillon with a remontoir d’égalité, cementing the brand’s technical reputation.

referenceDetails.name: Tourbillon Souverain
referenceDetails.note: Current Classique/Souveraine collection page describing the 1999 launch and the remontoir d’égalité concept.

referenceDetails.name: Tourbillon Souverain | Calibre 1498
referenceDetails.note: Patrimony/brass collection page noting production from 1999 to 2003 and that it was the world’s first wristwatch with a remontoire.

referenceDetails.name: Tourbillon Souverain | Calibre 1519
referenceDetails.note: Later generation Tourbillon Souverain page highlighting the 20th-anniversary update and the vertical tourbillon presentation.

timeline.event: F.P. Journe launched the first Tourbillon Souverain with remontoir d’égalité in wristwatch form.
The new generation added deadbeat seconds and refined the dial layout with enamel hour dial at 3 o’clock.
The current collection still presents Tourbillon Souverain as a flagship Classique/Souveraine model.

faqItems.question: What makes Tourbillon Souverain special?
faqItems.answer: It pairs a tourbillon with a remontoir d’égalité, giving the watch both visual drama and a precision-focused constant-force system.

faqItems.question: Is this the original F.P. Journe tourbillon?
faqItems.answer: It is the first Tourbillon Souverain wristwatch and the model that launched the brand in 1999.

keyCollections.name: Chronomètre Bleu
keyCollections.description: Distinctive tantalum-cased watch with vivid blue dial, housing the in-house 1304 calibre. One of Journe's most iconic pieces.

keyCollections.name: Octa
keyCollections.description: F.P. Journe's Octa is the manufacture's automatic movement family, built around the long-running Octa calibre architecture and expressed through complications such as Automatique Reserve, Lune, Divine, and later Automatique references.

referenceDetails.name: Octa Automatique Reserve
referenceDetails.note: F.P. Journe's official page presents Octa Automatique Reserve as part of the Octa Collection and identifies the current calibre family as 1300.3.

image.alt: F.P. Journe Octa Automatique Reserve watch

referenceDetails.name: Octa Lune
referenceDetails.note: F.P. Journe's official Octa Lune page identifies the watch as part of the Retrospective Octa Collection and lists calibre 1300.3 in the page title.

referenceDetails.name: Octa Divine
referenceDetails.note: F.P. Journe's official Octa Divine page presents the model as an Octa-family automatic watch using calibre 1300.3.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Octa is central to F.P. Journe because it turned the brand's precision-first thinking toward an automatic calibre platform, giving collectors a coherent family of long-running complications rather than a single isolated model.

image.alt: F.P. Journe Octa Automatique Reserve watch

faqItems.question: What is F.P. Journe Octa?
faqItems.answer: Octa is F.P. Journe's automatic calibre family, launched as a collection in 2001 and used across automatic complications.

faqItems.question: Which Octa references are useful starting points?
faqItems.answer: Official F.P. Journe pages provide useful entry points through Octa Automatique Reserve, Octa Lune, and Octa Divine.

faqItems.question: Why does Octa matter to collectors?
faqItems.answer: Octa matters because it established F.P. Journe's automatic movement platform and connected that platform to multiple complications.

funFacts.title: Launched as a collection
funFacts.body: F.P. Journe's official Automatique page states that Francois-Paul Journe launched the Octa collection in 2001.

funFacts.title: Shared calibre platform
funFacts.body: The official Octa Automatique Reserve, Octa Lune, and Octa Divine pages all point to calibre 1300.3.

keyCollections.name: Élégante
keyCollections.description: F.P. Journe’s women’s electromechanical watch collection built around a motion detector, standby mode, and automatic exact-time reset, blending jewelry-like styling with a genuinely inventive energy-saving timekeeping concept.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Élégante matters because it translated a novel electromechanical idea into a distinctive women’s collection, widening F.P. Journe’s design language beyond its men’s classics while preserving technical seriousness.

timeline.event: F.P. Journe introduced its first ladies’ collection, Élégante, at its January annual show in Geneva.
The brand launched Élégante in American première in New York.
F.P. Journe’s official Élégante pages continue to describe the standby-mode concept and the collection’s 40 mm and 48 mm variants.

referenceDetails.name: Élégante collection
referenceDetails.note: Official landing page for the collection.

referenceDetails.name: Ref. EL
referenceDetails.note: Reference designation used across the official collection pages.

referenceDetails.name: Calibre 1210
referenceDetails.note: Electromechanical movement identified on official Élégante pages.

faqItems.question: What makes Élégante different from a normal quartz watch?
faqItems.answer: It uses a motion detector and standby behavior so the watch can stop after being motionless, then reset itself to the correct time when worn again.

faqItems.question: Is Élégante only a ladies' line?
faqItems.answer: It was introduced as F.P. Journe’s first ladies’ collection, and the current official site still presents it as a distinct women’s-oriented concept.

timeline.event: François-Paul Journe is born in Marseille, France.
At age 20, Journe builds his first tourbillon pocket watch as a self-taught exercise.
Founds Montres Journe SA in Geneva, launching the Tourbillon Souverain as the first wristwatch.
Introduces the Chronomètre à Résonance, the first production wristwatch using resonance for precision.
Wins the first of three Aiguille d'Or grand prizes at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève.
Chanel acquires a 20% stake in the company, providing long-term stability while maintaining independence.
Launched the Furtif, the brand first integrated-bracelet watch with tungsten carbide and new caliber 1522.

faqItems.question: What does 'Invenit et Fecit' mean?
faqItems.answer: F.P. Journe's motto 'Invenit et Fecit' is Latin for 'He invented it and made it', signifying that every movement is designed and manufactured entirely in-house.

faqItems.question: How many watches does F.P. Journe produce per year?
faqItems.answer: F.P. Journe produces approximately 800-1,000 watches per year, making it one of the most exclusive modern watchmakers. Each piece is hand-finished in the Geneva manufacture.

name: Fabergé
description: Originally founded in 1842 in St Petersburg by Gustav Fabergé and made legendary by his son Peter Carl Fabergé through the iconic Imperial Easter Eggs, the Fabergé name was revived in watchmaking in the 21st century. Today, Fabergé Timepieces — produced in Geneva — blend the house's heritage of extraordinary craftsmanship with Swiss haute horlogerie, creating colourful, gem-set watches that honour the Fabergé legacy of artistry and surprise.

hq.address: 7 Grafton Street, London W1S 4EJ, United Kingdom

keyCollections.name: Compliquée Peacock
keyCollections.description: Haute horlogerie piece featuring an animated peacock that fans its tail to display the hours, with hand-painted enamel dial.

keyCollections.name: Lady Compliquée
keyCollections.description: Ladies' complication watch with rotating gemstone hour markers and mother-of-pearl dial artistry.

keyCollections.name: Visionnaire
keyCollections.description: Men's collection showcasing visible movements through sapphire cases and open-worked architecture.

keyCollections.name: Flirt
keyCollections.description: Playful ladies' collection with interchangeable coloured gemstone bezels and whimsical dial designs.

timeline.event: Gustav Fabergé founds the House of Fabergé as a jewellery firm in Saint Petersburg, Russia.
Peter Carl Fabergé creates the first Imperial Easter Egg for Tsar Alexander III, beginning the legendary Fabergé egg tradition.
The October Revolution forces the Fabergé family to flee Russia, closing the original workshop.
Fabergé brand is acquired and relaunched as a luxury jewellery and watch house, honouring the original craft traditions.
Launches the Compliquée Peacock watch, winning the Prix du Public at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève.
Christie London auctioned the historic Winter Egg of 1913. Launched Faberge x 007 Goldfinger Egg Objet (50 pcs).

faqItems.question: Does Fabergé make watches?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the modern Fabergé brand produces haute horlogerie watches alongside fine jewellery, continuing the house's tradition of extraordinary craftsmanship with gemstone setting and enamelwork.

faqItems.question: Is today's Fabergé connected to the original?
faqItems.answer: The modern Fabergé brand honours the heritage of the original House of Fabergé founded in 1842, though it has changed ownership multiple times since the Russian Revolution.

name: Farer

hq.address: Hazelwood Farm, Bottle Lane, Warfield, Bracknell RG42 5RX

description: Farer is a British watch brand founded in 2015 by Tom Fowlkes in London, known for colourful, travel-inspired GMT and field watches combining vintage Americana aesthetics with Swiss-made quality. The brand's vibrant dial colours and two-tone cases have earned it a devoted following among enthusiasts.

keyCollections.name: Lander
keyCollections.description: Farer’s Lander collection is a versatile GMT field-watch line built around compact proportions, travel-ready functionality, and the brand’s colorful outdoor-inspired design language.

keyCollections.name: Aqua Compressor
keyCollections.description: Farer’s Aqua Compressor collection is a titanium dive-watch line inspired by 1960s super-compressor case architecture, using internal rotating bezel design and modern materials for everyday tool-watch wear.

keyCollections.name: World Timer
keyCollections.description: Farer’s World Timer collection is a travel-watch line that presents 24 key cities at a glance and uses a Sellita-based movement customized for the collection’s globe-trotting function.

keyCollections.name: Chrono
keyCollections.description: Farer’s chronograph offering is presented as a racing-inspired collection with bold colourways and bi-compax or motorsport-leaning layouts, reflecting the brand’s lively design language and emphasis on distinct visual identity.

timeline.event: Jason Fried founds Farer in London, aiming to create colourful, design-led watches inspired by mid-century British travel and exploration.
Launches debut collection with distinctive multi-colour fumé dials, quickly gaining recognition in the microbrand world.
Opens a showroom in London and expands the collection with GMTs, world timers, and chronographs.

faqItems.question: Where does the name 'Farer' come from?
faqItems.answer: Farer evokes the spirit of travel and exploration, derived from the Old English 'farer' meaning traveller or voyager, fitting the brand's adventurous design ethos.

faqItems.question: Where are Farer watches made?
faqItems.answer: Farer watches are designed in London and assembled in Switzerland using Swiss automatic movements. The brand is known for its vivid, hand-finished fumé dials.

name: Favre Leuba
description: Favre-Leuba, founded in Le Locle in 1737, is one of Switzerland's oldest watch brands and an early pioneer of diving and altitude complications, including the world's first wristwatch altimeter in 1962. The brand was revived in 2016 under Indian ownership with a focus on adventure sports watches.
defunct_reason: The company name was sold in 1985 due to the ongoing quartz crisis, ending the continuous independent operation of this brand founded in 1737 — one of the oldest in Swiss watchmaking.
revival_attempt: Revived in 2016 under Titan Company (Tata Group); later acquired by Silvercity Brands AG in 2023, with a focus on altitude and adventure complications including the world's first wristwatch altimeter.

keyCollections.name: Raider
keyCollections.description: Robust sport watch collection including the iconic Bivouac with altimeter and barometer, and Sea King diver.

keyCollections.name: Chief
keyCollections.description: Favre Leuba’s Chief is the brand’s cushion-shaped dress-sport family, drawing on mid-century heritage while serving as the cornerstone of the maison’s modern revival through refined proportions, contemporary materials, and increasingly complicated executions.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Chief anchors Favre Leuba’s relaunch strategy: it translates archive-inspired design into a current product family that can support both entry and high-complication references.

timeline.event: Favre Leuba publicly frames the Chief collection as the cornerstone of its renaissance.
The line expands into higher complication territory with the Chief Tourbillon and later the Chief Skeleton.
The collection retains its cushion case identity as the central visual signature across modern executions.

referenceDetails.name: Chief collection
referenceDetails.note: Core modern collection built around the cushion-shaped case and heritage-inspired design language.

referenceDetails.name: Chief Tourbillon
referenceDetails.note: Officially presented as the brand’s first tourbillon in the Chief line.

referenceDetails.name: Chief Skeleton
referenceDetails.note: Official 2025 skeletonized evolution of the Chief collection.

faqItems.question: What defines the Chief collection visually?
faqItems.answer: A cushion-shaped case and heritage-led styling define the collection across its modern references.

faqItems.question: Is Chief important to Favre Leuba’s current strategy?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Favre Leuba describes Chief as the cornerstone of its renaissance and uses it to launch more complicated models.

keyCollections.name: Bivouac
keyCollections.description: Legendary adventure watch first introduced in 1962, featuring a mechanical altimeter and aneroid barometer for mountaineers.

timeline.event: Abraham Favre registers as a watchmaker in Le Locle, establishing what becomes the second-oldest watch brand in the world.
Henry-Augustus Favre partners with Auguste Leuba, creating the Favre-Leuba name.
Introduces the Bivouac, the first wristwatch with a built-in altimeter and barometer.
Launches the Bathy depth gauge watch for divers, another industry first.
Tata Group's Titan Company acquires the brand, beginning a revival of Favre-Leuba.
Brand changes hands to Silvercity Brands AG, continuing production from Grenchen, Switzerland.

faqItems.question: How old is Favre-Leuba?
faqItems.answer: Favre-Leuba dates back to 1737, making it the second-oldest watch brand in the world after Blancpain (founded 1735). It has nearly 290 years of continuous heritage.

faqItems.question: What is the Bivouac?
faqItems.answer: The Bivouac, introduced in 1962, was the world's first wristwatch with a built-in mechanical altimeter and barometer, designed for mountaineers and explorers.

name: Fears
description: Fears, a British luxury watch brand with 179 years of heritage, is based in Bristol. Relaunched in 2015 to champion British watchmaking, Fears produces refined mechanical watches in limited numbers with Swiss movements — bridging Victorian craft sensibility with the values of the modern independent watchmaking movement.

keyCollections.name: Brunswick
keyCollections.description: Fears Brunswick is the brand’s elegant hand-wound flagship family, defined by a slim round case, stepped dial architecture, refined British finishing, and a positioning that leans dressy while remaining everyday wearable.

referenceDetails.name: Brunswick 38 White
referenceDetails.note: A core Brunswick variant listed in the current collection page.

referenceDetails.name: Brunswick 38 'Charcoal Rose'
referenceDetails.note: A contemporary variant in the Brunswick family, shown on the current collection page.

referenceDetails.name: Brunswick 40 Filton 'Raven Black'
referenceDetails.note: A larger Brunswick variant in the current lineup, reflecting the family’s expansion beyond the original 38 mm format.

timeline.event: Fears’ current collection page describes Brunswick as the brand’s elegantly understated hand-wound watch collection.
The brand history page states that Brunswick was the second wristwatch released after Fears’ relaunch.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Brunswick functions as Fears’ flagship design language: it is where the brand’s restrained British aesthetics, compact proportions, and hand-wound character are most clearly expressed.

faqItems.question: What kind of watch is Brunswick?
faqItems.answer: It is Fears’ hand-wound, elegant everyday collection and the brand’s key dress-leaning family.

faqItems.question: What design cues define Brunswick?
faqItems.answer: A slim case, stepped dial, refined finishing, and understated proportions are the main hallmarks.

keyCollections.name: Redcliff
keyCollections.description: Fears Redcliff is the brand’s contemporary everyday collection, named for Redcliff Street in Bristol and positioned as a slim, versatile, modern time-and-date family that bridges the company’s heritage and its relaunch-era design language.

referenceDetails.name: Redcliff Date (2016)
referenceDetails.note: Described by Fears as the original watch of the new era and the first watch of the relaunched brand.

referenceDetails.name: Redcliff 39.5 Date Raven Black
referenceDetails.note: A current Redcliff variant described by Fears as an elegant and sophisticated everyday timepiece.

referenceDetails.name: Redcliff 39.5 'ES'
referenceDetails.note: The Endurance Specification model, presented by Fears as its first modern tool watch of the modern era.

timeline.event: Fears launched the original Redcliff Date as the first watch of the brand’s modern era.
The Redcliff collection page describes the line as re-imagined with a new Swiss automatic movement and a slim yet robust case.
The current lineup includes the Redcliff 39.5 family, showing the collection’s expansion into multiple dial and specification variants.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Redcliff is important because it is the relaunch-era entry point for Fears: a modern, slim everyday watch family that carries the brand’s heritage name forward in a contemporary format.

faqItems.question: Why is it called Redcliff?
faqItems.answer: The name comes from Redcliff Street in Bristol, where the brand was founded in 1846.

faqItems.question: Is Redcliff a sports watch?
faqItems.answer: It is primarily an everyday time-and-date collection, though the ES variant pushes it toward modern tool-watch territory.

timeline.event: Edwin Fear establishes a watchmaking business in Bristol, England, making it one of Britain's oldest watch brands.
The brand becomes a respected name in British horology, supplying quality timepieces across the West Country.
Nicholas Bowman-Scargill, a descendant of the founder, relaunches Fears as a contemporary British watch brand with Swiss movements.

faqItems.question: Is Fears a British brand?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Fears was founded in Bristol, England in 1846 by Edwin Fear, making it one of the oldest continually held British watch brands. It was relaunched in 2016 by a family descendant.

faqItems.question: Where are Fears watches made?
faqItems.answer: Fears watches are designed in Bristol and assembled in Switzerland using Swiss automatic movements, blending British design heritage with Swiss mechanical craftsmanship.

name: Felipe Pikullik
description: Felipe Pikullik is an independent watchmaking atelier from Berlin, shaping contemporary horology through bold design and technical mastery. One of the world's most distinctive independent voices, Pikullik creates exceptional timepieces that fuse Central European artistic rigour with the highest standards of hand-finished watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: N°1
keyCollections.description: Debut independent creation showcasing hand-finished movement with distinctive bridge architecture and guilloché dial work.

timeline.event: Felipe Pikullik establishes his independent watchmaking atelier, focusing on hand-crafted timepieces with artisanal finishing.
Presents his first independent creation, demonstrating mastery of traditional finishing techniques including hand guillochage.

faqItems.question: Who is Felipe Pikullik?
faqItems.answer: Felipe Pikullik is an independent watchmaker creating hand-finished timepieces with exceptional artisanal detail, specialising in guilloché work and traditional movement finishing.

faqItems.question: How many watches does he produce?
faqItems.answer: As an independent artisan watchmaker, Felipe Pikullik produces a very limited number of pieces per year, each extensively hand-finished.

name: Ferdinand Berthoud
description: Ferdinand Berthoud is a brand revived by Chopard in 2015, honouring the 18th-century French-Swiss master horologist who made major contributions to marine chronometry. The brand produces extremely limited and technically ambitious timepieces inspired by Berthoud's original precision instruments.
defunct_reason: Ferdinand Berthoud died in 1807, and the workshop ceased after his passing; the brand had no commercial successor.
revival_attempt: Revived by Chopard in 2015 as an ultra-high-end brand honouring Berthoud's contributions to marine chronometry, producing extremely limited grand complications in small series.

keyCollections.name: Chronomètre FB 1
keyCollections.description: Ferdinand Berthoud Chronomètre FB 1 is the maison's debut modern chronometer family, pairing an octagonal case with a tourbillon, constant force and fusee-and-chain architecture inspired by historical marine chronometers.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Chronomètre FB 1 established the revived Ferdinand Berthoud language: extreme chronometric engineering, exposed marine-clock inspiration and very limited production aimed at collectors of modern independent haute horlogerie.

image.alt: Ferdinand Berthoud Chronomètre FB 1.1 front view

timeline.event: Chronométrie Ferdinand Berthoud introduced the first Chronomètre FB 1 collection with an octagonal case and suspended tourbillon movement.
Chronomètre FB 1 won the Aiguille d'Or, the top prize at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève.
The FB 1R.6-1 added a regulator-style display and carburised steel case to the FB 1 family.

referenceDetails.name: Chronomètre FB 1.1
referenceDetails.note: The first modern Ferdinand Berthoud model, using the FB-T.FC calibre with tourbillon, fusee-and-chain constant force and central seconds.

referenceDetails.name: Chronomètre FB 1.2
referenceDetails.note: A gold-and-ceramic FB 1 execution using the same constant-force architecture and mobile-cone power-reserve concept.

referenceDetails.name: Chronomètre FB 1R.6-1
referenceDetails.note: A 20-piece regulator-style FB 1 variant with direct-drive centre seconds, fusee-and-chain constant force and a hardened carburised-steel case.

keyCollections.name: Chronomètre FB 2RE
keyCollections.description: Chronomètre FB 2RE is Ferdinand Berthoud's second modern collection, moving the maison into a round case with central hours, minutes and deadbeat seconds while retaining fusee-and-chain constant force with a one-second remontoir d'egalite.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: FB 2RE is pivotal because it proves Ferdinand Berthoud's chronometric identity can survive outside the original octagonal FB 1 case, translating the house vocabulary into a round, enamel-dial watch with a different constant-force architecture.

image.alt: Ferdinand Berthoud Chronomètre FB 2RE.2 front view

gallery.alt: Ferdinand Berthoud Chronomètre FB 2RE launch references

timeline.event: Ferdinand Berthoud unveiled Chronomètre FB 2RE as its second modern collection and first round-cased line.
Official newsletters presented the FB 2RE launch references around Geneva Watch Days.
The FB 2RE won the Chronometry Prize at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève.

referenceDetails.name: Chronomètre FB 2RE.1
referenceDetails.note: White-gold launch variant covered alongside FB 2RE.2, establishing the collection's round case, central three-hand layout and remontoir architecture.

image.alt: Ferdinand Berthoud Chronomètre FB 2RE.1 and FB 2RE.2

referenceDetails.name: Chronomètre FB 2RE.2
referenceDetails.note: Official black-dial variant with a rose-gold case, grand-feu enamel dial, panoramic window and deadbeat central seconds.

keyCollections.name: Chronomètre FB 1L
keyCollections.description: Chronomètre FB 1L extends Ferdinand Berthoud's fusee-and-chain tourbillon platform into an astronomical moon display, adding a patented moon-age indication and a separate waxing-or-waning display.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: FB 1L gives the original Chronomètre FB 1 architecture a distinct astronomical identity, showing how the brand can layer poetic complications onto its rigorous constant-force tourbillon base.

image.alt: Ferdinand Berthoud Chronomètre FB 1L.1 front view

gallery.alt: Ferdinand Berthoud Chronomètre FB 1L moon-display watch

timeline.event: Ferdinand Berthoud introduced the Chronomètre FB 1L family with a complex moon display.
The launch references included FB 1L.1 and FB 1L.4 variants documented in official and specialist coverage.
The line expanded the FB 1 tourbillon platform with a patented moon-age display and waxing-or-waning indicator.

referenceDetails.name: Chronomètre FB 1L.1
referenceDetails.note: Official moon-display reference with fusee-and-chain tourbillon architecture and a dedicated moon-age indication.
referenceDetails.material: 18-carat white gold with black ceramic lugs

referenceDetails.name: Chronomètre FB 1L.4
referenceDetails.note: Titanium launch variant documented alongside FB 1L.1, using the same astronomical display concept in a lighter case execution.
referenceDetails.material: Ceramised titanium with white-gold central container

timeline.event: The original Ferdinand Berthoud is born in Plancemont, Neuchâtel, going on to become one of the greatest horologists and marine chronometer makers of the 18th century.
Ferdinand Berthoud becomes a master watchmaker in Paris, beginning decades of pioneering work on marine chronometers.
Karl-Friedrich Scheufele (co-president of Chopard) revives the Ferdinand Berthoud name as an independent haute horlogerie brand.
Launches the Chronomètre FB 1, winning the Aiguille d'Or at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève.
Won Revolution Awards 2025 Watch of the Year for the Naissance d'une Montre 3, cementing the brand's status in haute horlogerie.

faqItems.question: What is the connection to Chopard?
faqItems.answer: The modern Chronométrie Ferdinand Berthoud was founded by Karl-Friedrich Scheufele, co-president of Chopard, as a separate entity dedicated to reviving the legacy of the 18th-century master horologist.

faqItems.question: Who was the original Ferdinand Berthoud?
faqItems.answer: Ferdinand Berthoud (1727-1807) was a Swiss-French horologist and scientist who served as Horologist-Mechanic to the King and the Navy, renowned for his pioneering marine chronometers.

name: Fleming
description: Fleming is a contemporary independent watch brand producing limited-edition timepieces with a focus on clean design and quality Swiss movements. The brand is positioned within the growing collector-focused independent watch segment.

hq.address: Edinburgh, City of Edinburgh, Scotland, United Kingdom

keyCollections.name: Dorado
keyCollections.description: Sport-luxe timepiece with luminous sandwich dial, 200m water resistance, and broad-arrow hands for underwater legibility.

timeline.event: Jamie Fleming founds Fleming Watch Company, creating sport watches that blend vintage military design cues with modern specifications.
Launches the debut collection, gaining attention from watch enthusiasts for thoughtful design and build quality at microbrand pricing.

faqItems.question: What kind of watches does Fleming make?
faqItems.answer: Fleming creates sport-oriented watches inspired by vintage military and dive watch design, offering Swiss automatic movements with solid build quality at accessible prices.

faqItems.question: Where is Fleming based?
faqItems.answer: Fleming is an independent microbrand creating design-driven sport watches with Swiss mechanical movements.

name: Formex
description: Formex is a Swiss watch brand founded in 2011, known for its patented suspension case system that isolates the movement from shocks and temperature changes. Based in Baar, Zug, the brand produces sporty watches at competitive prices using Swiss movements with a focus on innovative engineering.

keyCollections.name: Essence
keyCollections.description: Formex’s core Essence collection is a modern Swiss-made line built around the brand’s patented case suspension system and COSC-certified chronometer positioning, offered in multiple sizes and finishes for everyday versatility.

keyCollections.name: Reef
keyCollections.description: Formex’s Reef diver collection is the brand’s professional dive-focused line, built for underwater use with 300m water resistance and the patented case suspension system for comfort and impact resistance.

keyCollections.name: Element
keyCollections.description: Formex’s Element collection is a rugged GMT-oriented watch line that adds travel utility to the brand’s signature engineering-focused approach, including the suspension-system platform and interchangeable styling options.

timeline.event: Formex founded in Switzerland, initially producing watches with a focus on robust, sporty designs.
Raphael Granito acquires and relaunches Formex with the patented case suspension system as its core innovation.
Essence Automatic launched, establishing the brand's modern identity with COSC-certified movements and the suspension case.
Reef 300m diver released, expanding the lineup into professional dive territory.
Continued gaining traction as a Swiss microbrand with its patented case suspension system and COSC-certified models.

faqItems.question: What is Formex's case suspension system?
faqItems.answer: A patented system that decouples the movement from the case using four spring-loaded elements, protecting against shocks, vibrations and temperature changes.

faqItems.question: Where are Formex watches made?
faqItems.answer: Designed and assembled in Switzerland using Swiss-made COSC-certified movements, with the brand based in Baar, Canton of Zug.

name: Fortis
description: Fortis was founded in Grenchen in 1912 and holds the distinction of being the official watch supplier to Russian cosmonauts aboard the International Space Station and Mir. The brand produces robust pilot and cosmonaut watches built for professional use in demanding environments.

keyCollections.name: Cosmonauts
keyCollections.description: The official watch of the Russian space programme since 1994, worn on the Mir space station and ISS.

keyCollections.name: Flieger
keyCollections.description: Fortis’s pilot-watch collection, built around maximum legibility, mission-focused robustness, and aviation-specific features like second-time-zone bezels and pilot collaboration cues, positioning it as the brand’s cleanest modern flight instrument line.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Flieger is the collection that most clearly translates Fortis’s aviation heritage into a modern tool-watch format, and the official site emphasizes readability, pilot collaboration, and official use by elite squadrons.

referenceDetails.name: Flieger F-43 Bicompax
referenceDetails.note: Current flagship-style product page on the official Flieger collection.

referenceDetails.name: Synchroline®
referenceDetails.note: Pilot-alignment feature described on the collection page as allowing ±5-second synchronization.

referenceDetails.name: 12H Bezel with second Time Zone
referenceDetails.note: Collection-level aviation utility feature described on the official page.

timeline.event: Fortis’s Flieger family received a major update with new colors and refreshed references, as covered by watch media and reflected in the current official collection pages.
The official collection page highlights pilot-specific design elements including Synchroline® and enhanced readability.
Fortis states that elite pilots and squadrons have chosen its watches as official timekeeping instruments.

faqItems.question: What does Flieger mean here?
faqItems.answer: It is Fortis’s pilot-watch family, focused on legibility, robustness, and flight-oriented usability.

faqItems.question: Is this a modern collection?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The current official collection page and product pages show it as an active line with current references.

image.alt: Fortis Flieger F-43 Bicompax Original on Block Bracelet

keyCollections.name: Marinemaster
keyCollections.description: Fortis’s dive-oriented tool-watch collection, positioned as one of the brand’s oldest lines and engineered for underwater durability, modern grip, and high-performance daily wear with 300m to 500m water resistance across the current range.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Marinemaster is the collection that most clearly expresses Fortis’s long-form tool-watch philosophy outside space and aviation: a durable, legible dive instrument with modern materials, a distinctive Gear Bezel, and genuine professional-grade water resistance.

referenceDetails.name: Marinemaster M-40
referenceDetails.note: Current 300m diver from the official collection page.

referenceDetails.name: Marinemaster M-44
referenceDetails.note: Current 500m diver from the official collection page.

referenceDetails.name: Gear Bezel
referenceDetails.note: The collection’s signature bezel concept, described by Fortis as its most gripping and functional tool-watch bezel.

timeline.event: Fortis states it has been building the Marinemaster since 1954.
Fortis introduced a refreshed Marinemaster collection with M-40 and M-44 models in nature-inspired colorways.
Fortis launched the first Marinemaster with DLC coating, extending the line’s durability story.

faqItems.question: How deep is the Marinemaster rated?
faqItems.answer: The current official collection page shows the M-40 at 300m and the M-44 at 500m.

faqItems.question: What defines the Marinemaster visually?
faqItems.answer: The Gear Bezel, bold colorways, and a robust modern tool-watch profile are the collection’s clearest identifiers.

timeline.event: Walter Vogt founds Fortis in Grenchen, Switzerland.
Fortis collaborates with John Harwood to produce the world's first commercially available automatic wristwatch.
Fortis becomes the official watch supplier for the Russian space agency, used on the Mir space station.
Celebrates 100th anniversary with limited-edition models.
Jupp Philipp acquires Fortis, relaunching the brand with a modernised design language and block-colour approach.
Launched two DLC-coated Flieger models (Werk 7, 100 pcs each) and Vagabond V-40 GMT. Expanded Kenissi-powered Werk 11 and 13 calibres.

faqItems.question: Was Fortis really the first automatic watch?
faqItems.answer: Yes — in 1926, Fortis partnered with John Harwood to produce the world's first series-produced automatic wristwatch.

faqItems.question: Is Fortis still used in space?
faqItems.answer: Fortis has been the official watch of the Russian space programme since 1994 and has been worn on over 30 space missions aboard Mir and the ISS.

name: Fossil
description: Fossil is an American fashion watch brand founded in 1984 by Tom Kartsotis in Richardson, Texas, known for vintage-inspired designs across a wide range of fashion brands. Through its licensing operation, Fossil Group produces watches for brands including Michael Kors, Emporio Armani, and Kate Spade, alongside its own collections.

keyCollections.name: Grant
keyCollections.description: Fossil’s Grant collection is a long-running dressy chronograph family known for Roman numeral markers and vintage-inspired styling, with multiple stainless-steel and leather variants still listed on the official store.

keyCollections.name: Neutra
keyCollections.description: Fossil’s Neutra collection is a clean, modern chronograph-focused line with slim profiles, straightforward dials, and broad material and color variations that keep it squarely in the brand’s everyday contemporary style lane.

keyCollections.name: Gen 6
keyCollections.description: Fossil’s Gen 6 collection is the brand’s smartwatch line, built around Wear OS connectivity, health and wellness tracking, NFC-style payment features, and customizable digital watch faces in a mainstream fashion-tech format.

timeline.event: Tom Kartsotis founds Fossil in Richardson, Texas, inspired by his father's vintage watch collection.
Fossil goes public on NASDAQ, fuelling rapid expansion into global markets.
Acquires licence to produce Emporio Armani watches, beginning a major licensed brands strategy.
Acquires Misfit Wearables, entering the smartwatch and connected-device market.
Sells smartwatch intellectual property to Google for $40 million, though continues producing Wear OS devices.
Full-year revenue fell 12% to $1.004 billion as the company reported narrowing losses but remained unprofitable. Reported Q4 and FY2025 results in March 2026.
Fully exited smartwatch market. Net sales fell 12.3 percent to USD 1 billion. Secured USD 150M credit facility for turnaround.

faqItems.question: Is Fossil a luxury brand?
faqItems.answer: Fossil positions itself as an affordable fashion watch brand with vintage-inspired design. It's not luxury, but offers strong design at accessible price points.

faqItems.question: What other watch brands does Fossil Group own?
faqItems.answer: Fossil Group produces watches for Michael Kors, Emporio Armani, Diesel, DKNY, Kate Spade and Skagen, among others.

name: Franck Muller
description: Franck Muller was founded in Geneva in 1991 by Franck Muller and watchmaker Vartan Sirmakes, rapidly gaining fame for its baroque, over-the-top aesthetic and complex Grand Complications — particularly tourbillons, perpetual calendars, and minute repeaters packed into its signature Cintrée Curvex case. The brand became a symbol of 1990s luxury excess and continues to produce highly complicated timepieces at its Genthod manufacture.

keyCollections.name: Cintrée Curvex
keyCollections.description: Franck Muller’s signature curved-case collection, defined by its tonneau-like Cintrée Curvex silhouette, immediately recognizable numerals, and a broad family of elegant and highly complicated watches that serve as the brand’s visual shorthand.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is the house shape for Franck Muller: the collection most responsible for the brand’s instant visual identity and its reputation for technically ambitious, decorative luxury watches.

referenceDetails.name: 1752 QZ
referenceDetails.note: Example model shown on the official Cintrée Curvex family page.

image.alt: Franck Muller Cintrée Curvex 1752 QZ watch

referenceDetails.name: 8880 CC AT
referenceDetails.note: Chronograph reference shown on the official men’s Cintrée Curvex page.

image.alt: Franck Muller Cintrée Curvex 8880 CC AT chronograph

referenceDetails.name: 7880 HR JN S6 II
referenceDetails.note: Réhaut-style Cintrée Curvex variant shown in the official Cintrée Curvex family gallery.

image.alt: Franck Muller Cintrée Curvex 7880 HR JN S6 II watch

timeline.event: Franck Muller’s official Cintrée Curvex pages continue to present the curved case as the brand’s most distinctive silhouette.
The family pages show multiple sub-lines and complications, including skeleton, chronograph, grande date, and réhaut variants.
The collection remains central to Franck Muller’s modern identity across men’s and ladies’ pages.

faqItems.question: Is Cintrée Curvex the signature Franck Muller shape?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Franck Muller’s official pages explicitly describe Cintrée Curvex as the brand’s iconic and most distinctive silhouette.

faqItems.question: Does the line include complications?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The official family pages display variants such as chronographs, skeletons, grand date pieces, and réhaut models.

image.alt: Franck Muller Cintrée Curvex collection watches

keyCollections.name: Vanguard
keyCollections.description: Franck Muller Vanguard is the maison's modern sporty tonneau collection, using angular cases, applied numerals, and many chronograph, tourbillon, and themed executions.

referenceDetails.name: Vanguard chronograph
referenceDetails.note: Official Vanguard chronograph reference family shown by Franck Muller among the core Vanguard models.

image.alt: Franck Muller Vanguard V 45 CC DT watch

referenceDetails.name: Vanguard small seconds date
referenceDetails.note: Official Vanguard time-and-date reference family that shows the collection's sporty tonneau case without chronograph registers.

image.alt: Franck Muller Vanguard V 45 SC DT watch

referenceDetails.name: Vanguard tourbillon
referenceDetails.note: Official Vanguard tourbillon reference family, showing how the sporty case is used for high-complication executions.

image.alt: Franck Muller Vanguard V 45 T BR watch

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Vanguard is Franck Muller's contemporary sports-luxury platform, translating the brand's tonneau-case personality into a broader, bolder and more modular collection.

faqItems.question: What is Franck Muller Vanguard?
faqItems.answer: Vanguard is the brand's modern sporty tonneau collection, with chronograph, time-and-date, tourbillon, yacht, and other themed variants.

faqItems.question: Which Vanguard references are official examples?
faqItems.answer: Franck Muller's official page shows examples including V 45 CC DT, V 45 SC DT, and V 45 T BR reference families.

faqItems.question: How does Vanguard fit Franck Muller?
faqItems.answer: It keeps the brand's curving case identity but gives it a sportier and more contemporary visual language.

keyCollections.name: Long Island
keyCollections.description: Elegant rectangular case inspired by Art Deco design, offering a refined alternative to the Cintrée Curvex.

keyCollections.name: Crazy Hours
keyCollections.description: Franck Muller Crazy Hours is the brand's playful jumping-hour complication, using scrambled numerals and a mechanical hour jump to make time display deliberately theatrical.

referenceDetails.name: Classic Crazy Hours
referenceDetails.note: Official Crazy Hours reference family with the collection's signature randomized numeral layout.

image.alt: Franck Muller Crazy Hours 8880 CH watch

referenceDetails.name: Color Dreams Crazy Hours
referenceDetails.note: Official Crazy Hours Color Dreams variant, pairing the jumping-hour concept with Franck Muller's multicolor numeral vocabulary.

image.alt: Franck Muller Crazy Hours Color Dreams watch

referenceDetails.name: 30th Anniversary Crazy Hours
referenceDetails.note: Official Crazy Hours anniversary model shown by Franck Muller among the collection's later executions.

image.alt: Franck Muller Crazy Hours 30th Anniversary watch

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Crazy Hours is one of Franck Muller's clearest signatures because it turns an otherwise simple hours-and-minutes display into a memorable mechanical trick.

faqItems.question: What is Franck Muller Crazy Hours?
faqItems.answer: Crazy Hours is a jumping-hour complication with numerals placed out of order around the dial.

faqItems.question: How does Crazy Hours tell time?
faqItems.answer: The hour hand jumps to the correct hour numeral even though the numerals are arranged in a deliberately scrambled order.

faqItems.question: Which Crazy Hours examples appear on Franck Muller's official page?
faqItems.answer: Official examples include 8880 CH, 8880 CH Color Dreams, and Crazy Hours 30th Anniversary variants.

timeline.event: Franck Muller and Vartan Sirmakes found the Franck Muller brand in Genthod, Geneva.
Launches the Cintrée Curvex with a tourbillon inside a curved case — a technical first.
Introduces the Aeternitas Mega, featuring 36 complications and over 1,400 components, one of the most complicated wristwatches ever.
Watchland manufacture in Genthod fully operational, housing all production and complications under one roof.
Crazy Hours featured in Revolution Watch's '30 Pioneering Watches' list. Profiled by Forbes for its strategy of succeeding as an independent luxury brand outside the Rolex-dominated market.
Round Triple Mystery nominated for GPHG Ladies Complication. Opened new boutiques in Jakarta and Hong Kong IFC Mall.

faqItems.question: Why is Franck Muller called the 'Master of Complications'?
faqItems.answer: Franck Muller earned this title for producing some of the most complicated wristwatches ever made, including the Aeternitas Mega with 36 complications.

faqItems.question: Where are Franck Muller watches made?
faqItems.answer: All watches are designed and manufactured at Watchland, the brand's sprawling manufacture in Genthod near Geneva, Switzerland.

name: Fratello
description: Fratello is a leading independent watch media and community platform founded in the Netherlands in 2004 by Robert-Jan Broer. Beyond publishing, the brand has produced its own watch collaborations with manufacturers including Seiko and H. Moser & Cie., becoming an influential voice bridging media and product in the watch world.

keyCollections.name: Fratello × Unimatic
keyCollections.description: Limited-edition collaborations with Italian microbrand Unimatic, featuring unique dials and colourways.

timeline.event: Robert-Jan Broer launches Fratello Watches as one of the first dedicated online watch blogs.
Fratello coins 'Speedy Tuesday', creating a global community around vintage and modern Omega Speedmasters.
Omega collaborates with Fratello to release an official Speedy Tuesday limited edition — a first for a watch blog.
Fratello expands into watch collaborations and limited editions under its own brand.

faqItems.question: Is Fratello a watch brand or a media company?
faqItems.answer: Fratello started as one of the world's first watch blogs in 2004 and has since expanded into limited-edition watch collaborations while maintaining its media platform.

faqItems.question: What is Speedy Tuesday?
faqItems.answer: A weekly feature created by Fratello in 2012 celebrating the Omega Speedmaster, which became so popular Omega released an official Speedy Tuesday limited edition.

name: Frederique Constant
description: Frédérique Constant was founded in Geneva in 1988 by Peter and Aletta Stas and became known for bringing in-house watchmaking to the accessible segment of the market. The brand was acquired by Citizen Watch Co. in 2016 and continues to produce classically styled watches with in-house manufacture movements.

keyCollections.name: Classics
keyCollections.description: Frederique Constant’s Classics is the brand’s core dress-watch family: clean, timeless cases, Roman-numeral and guilloché signatures, and a wide spread of everyday complications that express the maison’s affordable-luxury identity.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is the foundation collection that most clearly defines the brand’s classical, value-driven positioning across quartz and mechanical variants.

timeline.event: The official Classics collection page continues to center the line as the brand’s core elegant dress-watch family.
Frederique Constant’s 2024 consumer brochure highlights Classics as embodying the essence of classic design.
The US official collection page shows a broad Classics range spanning heart beat, moonphase, chronograph, and carrée variants.

referenceDetails.name: Classic Heart Beat Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Representative Classic model with the signature heart-beat aperture and traditional styling.

referenceDetails.name: Classic Heart Beat Moonphase Date
referenceDetails.note: Shows the collection’s blend of classic dial layout with moonphase/date complications.

referenceDetails.name: Classics Carrée Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Represents the rectangular dress-watch side of the Classics family.

faqItems.question: What defines Classics at Frederique Constant?
faqItems.answer: The line is defined by pure lines, timeless styling, Roman numerals, guilloché textures, and approachable classic watchmaking.

faqItems.question: Is Classics only mechanical?
faqItems.answer: No. The collection spans quartz and mechanical pieces, with many models emphasizing everyday complications.

keyCollections.name: Slimline
keyCollections.description: Slimline is Frederique Constant’s ultra-thin collection, focused on refined proportions and elegant case architecture while spanning quartz, automatic, and high-end in-house movements for a more minimalist interpretation of the maison’s classic style.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Slimline demonstrates how Frederique Constant translates traditional Swiss watchmaking into a thinner, more understated form without losing the brand’s emphasis on value and mechanical credibility.

timeline.event: The official Slimline page continues to describe the line as ultra-thin and available in quartz, automatic, and high-end in-house movements.
Brand materials present Slimline as a modern, elegant interpretation of classic watch design.
The current official collection page highlights Slimline Heart Beat Automatic among the men’s offerings.

referenceDetails.name: Slimline Heart Beat Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Representative ultra-thin Slimline model with the brand’s signature heart-beat display.

referenceDetails.name: Slimline quartz models
referenceDetails.note: Shows that the line spans quartz as well as mechanical movements.

referenceDetails.name: Slimline in-house manufacture movements
referenceDetails.note: Captures the collection’s higher-end movement positioning.

faqItems.question: What is the defining trait of Slimline?
faqItems.answer: Its defining trait is an ultra-thin profile with refined, elegant proportions.

faqItems.question: What movement types does Slimline include?
faqItems.answer: The collection spans quartz, automatic, and high-end in-house movements.

keyCollections.name: Highlife
keyCollections.description: Highlife is Frederique Constant’s integrated-bracelet sports collection, originally launched in 1999 and revived in 2020 with modernized proportions, quick-change bracelets, and COSC-certified variants that bridge sporty versatility and refined Swiss dress-sport styling.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Highlife is the clearest example of the brand’s ability to reinterpret an archived design into a contemporary sports collection without abandoning accessible Swiss watchmaking.

timeline.event: Frederique Constant launched the first Highlife models with an integrated strap concept.
The Maison revived Highlife and brought the collection back into focus with new models.
The current official collection page shows Highlife Automatic, Highlife Automatic COSC, and Highlife Chronograph Automatic variants.

referenceDetails.name: Highlife Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Core three-hand model in the revived integrated-bracelet family.

referenceDetails.name: Highlife Automatic COSC
referenceDetails.note: Chronometer-certified version emphasizing the sport-luxury side of the line.

referenceDetails.name: Highlife Chronograph Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Complication-forward Highlife variant for the integrated sports collection.

faqItems.question: What makes Highlife different from Classics?
faqItems.answer: Highlife uses a more modern integrated-bracelet sports architecture, while Classics is the brand’s traditional dress-watch foundation.

faqItems.question: Does Highlife include COSC-certified models?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The revived family includes COSC-certified variants.

keyCollections.name: Horological Smartwatch
keyCollections.description: Pioneering connected watch that combines a traditional analogue dial with smart activity tracking.

timeline.event: Peter and Aletta Stas found Frédérique Constant in Geneva, aiming to make Swiss luxury accessible.
Develops its first in-house movement, the FC-910, a heart-beat manufacture calibre.
Launches the Horological Smartwatch, the first Swiss-made connected analogue watch.
Citizen Watch Group acquires Frédérique Constant, providing resources for further in-house manufacture development.
Launched a new Perpetual Calendar model, praised for its elegant design and accessible luxury positioning.
Redesigned Classic Perpetual Calendar Manufacture at Watches & Wonders: 40mm case, 72-hour power reserve. Launched 37th anniversary Elements collection with stone dials.

faqItems.question: Is Frédérique Constant a manufacture?
faqItems.answer: Yes — Frédérique Constant develops and produces several in-house movements at its Plan-les-Ouates facility in Geneva, including tourbillon calibres.

faqItems.question: What is their motto?
faqItems.answer: 'Live your passion' — reflecting the founders' belief that Swiss luxury watchmaking should be accessible to passionate collectors, not just the ultra-wealthy.

name: Furlan Marri
description: Furlan Marri is a Swiss watch brand founded in 2021 producing vintage-inspired timepieces at accessible price points, quickly gaining traction through strong direct-to-consumer marketing and limited drops. The brand's pieces feature hand-applied indices and domed crystals that echo mid-century Swiss design.

keyCollections.name: Mechaquartz
keyCollections.description: Furlan Marri’s Mechaquartz line is the brand’s foundational chronograph family, pairing vintage-inspired mid-century styling with Seiko mechaquartz calibres that deliver a mechanical-style chronograph sweep at an accessible price. The current collection mixes permanent references and periodic special editions while keeping the line’s signature Tasti Tondi-inspired design language.

referenceDetails.name: Ardesia Blu
referenceDetails.note: Current official Mechaquartz model in the collection; official collection page schema lists price and direct product URL.

image.source: Furlan Marri official collection page schema

referenceDetails.name: Sabbia Rosa
referenceDetails.note: Current official Mechaquartz model in the collection; also covered by Hodinkee as a 2025 permanent-collection addition.

image.alt: Furlan Marri Sabbia Rosa Mechaquartz chronograph
image.source: Furlan Marri official collection page schema

referenceDetails.name: Nero Sabbia
referenceDetails.note: Current official Mechaquartz model listed on the official collection page.

image.alt: Furlan Marri Nero Sabbia Mechaquartz chronograph
image.source: Furlan Marri official collection page schema

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Mechaquartz is the collection that established Furlan Marri’s reputation for unusually strong vintage styling and dial finishing at entry-level pricing, while also anchoring the brand’s accessible first tier even after expansion into more expensive mechanical watches.

image.alt: Furlan Marri Sabbia Rosa from the Mechaquartz collection
image.source: Furlan Marri official collection page schema

faqItems.question: What movement does the Furlan Marri Mechaquartz collection use?
faqItems.answer: Current Mechaquartz models use Seiko mechaquartz calibres, with Hodinkee specifically citing the VK64 in the 2025 Ardesia Blu and Sabbia Rosa releases.

faqItems.question: Why is the Mechaquartz collection important to Furlan Marri?
faqItems.answer: It was the brand’s launch collection, the basis of its Kickstarter success in 2021, and the family linked by Furlan Marri to its GPHG Horological Revelation Prize for the Mechaquartz model Mr. Grey.

timeline.event: Furlan Marri launched on Kickstarter with Mechaquartz chronographs, the collection that introduced the brand to collectors.
The Mechaquartz model Mr. Grey won the GPHG Horological Revelation Prize, giving the young brand immediate industry visibility.
Furlan Marri expanded the permanent Mechaquartz collection with the Sabbia Rosa and Ardesia Blu references.
The anniversary Meteorite Octa revisited the Mechaquartz format as a limited special edition, showing the line still acts as a platform for experimental releases.

keyCollections.name: Cornes de Vache
keyCollections.description: Furlan Marri’s Cornes de Vache is the brand’s vintage-leaning dress-watch family built around its signature horn-shaped lugs, pairing mid-century styling cues with accessible modern execution and Swiss automatic movements in current sector-dial references.

referenceDetails.name: Blue Sector
referenceDetails.note: Current Cornes de Vache sector-dial variant listed by Furlan Marri at CHF 1,250 on the collection page.

image.alt: Furlan Marri Cornes de Vache Blue Sector
image.source: Furlan Marri official collection page schema

referenceDetails.name: Salmon Sector
referenceDetails.note: Current Cornes de Vache sector-dial variant listed by Furlan Marri at CHF 1,250 on the collection page; schema shows reference 2154-A in the product URL.

image.source: Furlan Marri official collection page schema

referenceDetails.name: White Sector
