faqItems.question: When was the IWC Portugieser introduced?
faqItems.answer: The collection traces its origin to 1939, when IWC delivered the first oversized wristwatches inspired by nautical deck-watch precision; the modern collection revival was formally named Portugieser in 1993.

faqItems.question: Why is the Portugieser so large compared with vintage dress watches?
faqItems.answer: Because the original concept used a high-precision pocket-watch movement inside a wristwatch case, creating an unusually large and highly legible design for its era.

faqItems.question: What are the defining design traits of a Portugieser?
faqItems.answer: Key cues include a clean open dial, applied Arabic numerals, slim feuille hands, a railway-style minute track, and proportions inspired by marine instruments.

faqItems.question: What is the best-known Portugieser today?
faqItems.answer: The Portugieser Chronograph is arguably the best-known modern reference thanks to its balanced vertical sub-dial layout and long-running role in the collection.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: According to Phillips citing IWC archives, only 690 examples of the original reference 325 were sold between 1939 and 1981, making the earliest Portugiesers exceptionally scarce.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2
funFacts.body: Many vintage Portugieser watches imported into Portugal can be identified by a hand-stamped Portuguese customs hallmark on the lug, a small historical clue tied directly to the collection’s name.

keyCollections.name: Ingenieur
keyCollections.description: IWC’s Ingenieur is the brand’s engineering-led sports watch family, born as an antimagnetic tool watch in 1955 and repeatedly reinterpreted through technical and design milestones, most notably Gérald Genta’s 1976 Ingenieur SL and the integrated-bracelet revival launched in 2023.

referenceDetails.description: The 2023 relaunch that revisits the 1970s SL design with modern ergonomics, functional bezel screws, updated finishing, and a contemporary integrated bracelet sports-watch execution.

timeline.event: IWC introduces the Ingenieur as an antimagnetic wristwatch for civilian use, establishing the collection’s engineering-first identity.
Gérald Genta designs the Ingenieur SL, reference 1832, giving the line its most iconic integrated-bracelet sports-watch form.
IWC overhauls the Ingenieur family with a new AMG-linked generation that keeps the Genta-era shape while broadening the lineup with sportier and more complex models.
At Watches and Wonders on March 27, 2023, IWC relaunches the Ingenieur Automatic 40, directly inspired by the 1970s Ingenieur SL reference 1832.
IWC adds the Ingenieur Automatic 35, shrinking the revived design into a more compact 35 mm format.
IWC expands the modern range with the Ingenieur Automatic 42 in dark olive green ceramic and the titanium Ingenieur Perpetual Calendar 41.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Ingenieur matters because it combines a genuine technical backstory—antimagnetic watchmaking, materials know-how, and robust everyday engineering—with one of IWC’s strongest design narratives. It links mid-century tool-watch purpose, Gérald Genta’s 1970s luxury-sports design language, and IWC’s modern expertise in finishing, ceramics, titanium, and practical complications.

newsItems.title: IWC Schaffhausen launches the Ingenieur Automatic 40 in Geneva
newsItems.summary: On March 27, 2023, IWC reintroduced the Ingenieur as the Ingenieur Automatic 40, explicitly inspired by Gérald Genta’s 1970s Ingenieur SL reference 1832 and presented under the ‘Form und Technik’ theme at Watches and Wonders.

newsItems.summary: Hodinkee covered IWC’s smaller 35 mm Ingenieur, describing it as a direct follow-up to the 2023 revival and a more compact take on the integrated-bracelet sports watch.

newsItems.summary: On April 14, 2026, IWC introduced the first colored-ceramic execution of the modern Genta-derived Ingenieur design, expanding the line’s materials story with a dark olive green ceramic model.

newsItems.title: The IWC Schaffhausen Ingenieur Perpetual Calendar 41 crafted with a lightweight titanium case and bracelet
newsItems.summary: Also on April 14, 2026, IWC added a titanium Ingenieur Perpetual Calendar 41, combining the revived integrated-bracelet design with Kurt Klaus’s perpetual calendar architecture.

faqItems.question: What does ‘Ingenieur’ mean?
faqItems.answer: Ingenieur means ‘engineer’ in German and French, a fitting name for a collection built around technical problem-solving and engineering-minded watchmaking.

faqItems.question: When was the IWC Ingenieur introduced?
faqItems.answer: The Ingenieur was introduced in 1955 as an antimagnetic wristwatch, though the most famous design chapter began with Gérald Genta’s Ingenieur SL reference 1832 in 1976.

faqItems.question: Why is the Ingenieur SL 1832 so important?
faqItems.answer: Reference 1832 is the defining Gérald Genta version of the Ingenieur, known for its integrated bracelet, distinctive bezel, and design language that directly inspired the 2023 revival.

faqItems.question: Is the modern Ingenieur still an integrated-bracelet sports watch?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The current collection is built around the revived integrated-bracelet sports-watch format, with sizes including 35, 40, and 42 mm, plus more complicated models such as the Perpetual Calendar 41.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: At Watches and Wonders 2023, IWC displayed a newly rediscovered original Gérald Genta drawing of the Ingenieur SL and said it had been officially certified by the Gérald Genta Heritage Association.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2
funFacts.body: According to Phillips, the original Ingenieur SL reference 1832 was produced in remarkably small numbers—about 543 pieces across steel and two-tone examples from 1976 to 1984.

name: Jacob & Co.
description: Jacob & Co. was founded in New York in 1986 by Jacob Arabo, initially as a high jewellery brand before expanding into high-complication watchmaking. The brand is known for spectacular, often outrageous designs including the Astronomia with its rotating multi-axis display, targeting the ultra-high-net-worth market with no shortage of theatrical flair.

timeline.event: Named the fastest-growing Swiss watch brand of 2025 by the Morgan Stanley/LuxeConsult Swiss Watcher report, with revenues of $180 million (+14%) and 3,975 units (+24%). Opens 38 new stores worldwide including five mono-brand boutiques.

faqItems.question: When was Jacob & Co. founded?
faqItems.answer: Jacob Arabo founded Jacob & Co. as a jewellery house in New York in 1986 and extended into watchmaking in 2002.

faqItems.question: What is the Astronomia?
faqItems.answer: The Astronomia is a high-complication line introduced in 2014, built around a rotating three-dimensional movement carrying a tourbillon, a miniature globe and other satellites.

faqItems.question: Who was Jacques Bianchi?
faqItems.answer: A Marseille-based watchmaker who in 1982 released the JB200, a professional dive watch used by French Navy divers and local diving shops in the south of France.

faqItems.question: Is Jacques Bianchi still made today?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The brand was revived as Jacques Bianchi Marseille by Fabrice Pougez and Simo Tber and relaunched the JB200 via Kickstarter in 2021.

name: Jaeger-LeCoultre
description: Founded in Le Sentier in 1833 by Antoine LeCoultre, Jaeger-LeCoultre has registered more than 1,400 calibres and 430 patents, making it one of the most prolific manufactures in watchmaking history. The Manufacture Royale — one of the most complete watchmaking facilities in the world — produces everything from escapements to cases in-house, and is the creator of the Reverso, Atmos clock, and Master Compressor.

faqItems.question: Where is Jaeger-LeCoultre based?
faqItems.answer: The manufacture has been located in Le Sentier, in Switzerland's Vallée de Joux, since Antoine LeCoultre founded his workshop there in 1833.

faqItems.question: What is the Reverso?
faqItems.answer: The Reverso is a rectangular wristwatch with a reversible case, originally designed in 1931 for polo players who wanted to protect the crystal.

faqItems.question: Who owns Jaeger-LeCoultre?
faqItems.answer: Jaeger-LeCoultre has been part of the Richemont Group since 2000.

name: Jaquet Droz
description: Jaquet Droz, named after 18th-century automaton and watch pioneer Pierre Jaquet-Droz, was revived as a brand by the Swatch Group in 2000. Under a radical 2024-2025 transformation, it closed all retail and now produces approximately 100 bespoke pieces per year, specialising in six-figure métiers d'art, automata and one-of-a-kind commissions sold exclusively from La Chaux-de-Fonds.
defunct_reason: The original Jaquet-Droz workshop, famous for its automata and precision pocket watches, dissolved in the late 19th century following the deaths of its founders and their heirs.
revival_attempt: Revived by the Swatch Group in 2000 as a dedicated high watchmaking brand specialising in enamel dials, automata, and bird paintings, directly inspired by Pierre Jaquet-Droz's mechanical sculptures.

keyCollections.name: Grande Seconde
keyCollections.description: The Grande Seconde is Jaquet Droz’s emblematic off-center signature collection, built around the brand’s historic large seconds display and a refined two-register dial architecture that links modern haute horlogerie to Pierre Jaquet-Droz’s eighteenth-century pocket-watch heritage.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: It is the brand’s defining collection: the one most directly associated with Jaquet Droz’s identity, design language, and historical continuity from pocket watches to contemporary wristwatches.

referenceDetails.name: Grande Seconde
referenceDetails.note: Official collection page describing the line as inspired by Pierre Jaquet-Droz’s 1784 pocket watch and central to the brand.

referenceDetails.name: Grande Seconde Tourbillon

The official brand site continues to describe Grande Seconde as the collection that spreads its aegis over the brand.
Current official pages and manuals keep the Grande Seconde family active across multiple complications and materials.

faqItems.question: What defines the Grande Seconde design?
faqItems.answer: A large off-center seconds register paired with a smaller hours-and-minutes dial, rooted in Pierre Jaquet-Droz’s historical pocket-watch design language.

faqItems.question: When did the modern Grande Seconde debut?
faqItems.answer: Jaquet Droz’s official history states it was presented in 2002.

keyCollections.name: Petite Heure Minute
keyCollections.description: The Petite Heure Minute is Jaquet Droz’s compact, off-centered canvas for métiers d’art, using its small hours-and-minutes architecture to showcase miniature painting, enamel, engraving, lacquer, minerals, and mother-of-pearl with strong decorative emphasis.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: It is the maison’s most versatile artistic platform, giving craftsmen a highly recognizable dial layout while preserving the brand’s hallmark off-center elegance.

Current manuals and variant pages confirm the line remains active across multiple configurations.

faqItems.question: What makes Petite Heure Minute distinctive?
faqItems.answer: Its off-centered time display leaves ample dial space for decorative arts and textured materials.

faqItems.question: Is Petite Heure Minute still an active Jaquet Droz family?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The current official website and manuals still list the collection and its variants.

keyCollections.name: The Bird Repeater
keyCollections.description: A high-complication automata minute repeater centered on hand-engraved birds and an expressive animated dial, carrying forward Jaquet Droz’s historic bird automata language into a 47 mm contemporary wristwatch.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: It is one of Jaquet Droz’s clearest modern signatures: an automata-plus-minute-repeater showcase that links the brand’s 18th-century mechanical artistry with present-day high watchmaking.

referenceDetails.name: Bird Repeater
referenceDetails.note: Official current page lists the 47 mm red-gold minute repeater with 8 distinct animations and numerus clausus 8.

The Tropical Bird Repeater shows the same bird-automata-minute-repeater formula adapted into a new scene and palette.

keyCollections.name: Loving Butterfly Automaton
keyCollections.description: The Loving Butterfly Automaton is Jaquet Droz’s poetic automaton-watch series that turns the Petite Heure Minute-style dial into a miniature stage, animating a cherub and butterfly through a crown-activated mechanism while showcasing the maison’s blend of métiers d’art and mechanical theater.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: It is one of the clearest modern expressions of Jaquet Droz’s automaton heritage, connecting the brand’s eighteenth-century kinetic artistry to a contemporary, highly collectible mechanical showcase.

referenceDetails.name: Loving Butterfly Automaton

The official site still places the model among the maison’s flagship automaton watches alongside Bird Repeater, Charming Bird, and Lady 8 Flower.

faqItems.question: What is the Loving Butterfly Automaton based on?
faqItems.answer: The official story ties it to Henri-Louis Jaquet-Droz’s historic automaton sketch of a cherub drawn by a butterfly.

faqItems.question: How is the automaton activated?
faqItems.answer: The official page says a crown push-button triggers the animated mechanism.

timeline.event: Pierre Jaquet-Droz begins producing longcase clocks from his family farm in La Chaux-de-Fonds.
Jaquet-Droz and Jean-Frédéric Leschot present the Writer, Draughtsman and Musician automata, a landmark in mechanical art.
Establishes workshops in Geneva and London, becoming one of the first European watchmakers with direct presence in China.
Pierre Jaquet-Droz dies; the workshops gradually wind down in the following decades.
The Swatch Group acquires the Jaquet Droz name and relaunches the brand as a dedicated high-watchmaking maison.
Jaquet Droz moves into its new Atelier d'Art in La Chaux-de-Fonds, centralising métiers d'art work.
Presents the Loving Butterfly Automaton, a contemporary homage to its 18th-century mechanical heritage.

Under CEO Alain Delamuraz, completes a radical transformation: closes all 176 retail points, reduces annual output from 5,000 to approximately 100 bespoke pieces, and repositions as a six-figure métiers d'art atelier selling exclusively from La Chaux-de-Fonds.

faqItems.question: Who founded Jaquet Droz?
faqItems.answer: Pierre Jaquet-Droz, a Swiss watchmaker and automaton-maker born in 1721, who founded the manufacture in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1738.

faqItems.question: Is Jaquet Droz independent?
faqItems.answer: No. Since 2000 Jaquet Droz has been part of the Swatch Group's prestige and luxury division, operating from La Chaux-de-Fonds.

faqItems.question: What is Jaquet Droz best known for?
faqItems.answer: Métiers d'art — grand feu enamel, miniature painting, engraving — and complex bird and figurative automata that trace back to the founder's 18th-century mechanical sculptures.

name: JC Biver
description: JC Biver is the personal watch brand of Jean-Claude Biver, the legendary Swiss watch executive who revived Blancpain, transformed TAG Heuer, and built Hublot into a global brand. Launched in 2024, it represents a return to pure independent watchmaking for one of the industry's most influential figures.

keyCollections.name: Biver Automatique

The Carillon Tourbillon Biver debuts — a minute repeater with tourbillon in 42 mm precious-metal cases — at a very limited production.
The time-only Biver Automatique launches with a micro-rotor movement, broadening the range beyond grand complications.
