Expands the Automatique collection at Dubai Watch Week 2025 with 11 new references featuring guilloché, enamel, gem-set and hardstone dials. Appoints James Marks as CEO to scale operations.

faqItems.question: Who is behind Biver Watches?
faqItems.answer: Swiss industry veteran Jean-Claude Biver — known for reviving Blancpain and building Hublot — together with his son Pierre Biver.

faqItems.question: Is JC Biver independent?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Biver Watches is an independent family-owned maison based in Switzerland, not affiliated with any large group.

name: Jean-Marc Fleury
description: Jean-Marc Fleury is an independent Haute Horlogerie Atelier based in Geneva. Building on a decade of experience in high complications, the atelier produces very limited-edition timepieces where exceptional dial artistry and hand-finished movements represent the intimate scale of true artisan watchmaking at its most personal.

faqItems.question: When was Fleury Manufacture founded?
faqItems.answer: Jean-Marc Fleury founded Fleury Manufacture in 2017 in Choulex, near Geneva, after more than 25 years in the watch industry including a decade at Patek Philippe.

faqItems.question: What is the ZEN?
faqItems.answer: The ZEN is the brand's first watch, powered by the in-house hand-wound calibre FM01 and presented with a gem-set dial evoking constellations.

keyCollections.name: ZEN
keyCollections.description: First Fleury Manufacture watch, powered by the in-house calibre FM01, with a gem-set constellation dial.

timeline.event: Jean-Marc Fleury founds Fleury Manufacture in Choulex, on the outskirts of Geneva.
Brand unveils the calibre FM01 and its first watch, ZEN.

name: Jochen Benzinger
description: Jochen Benzinger is a German master engraver and watchmaker based in Ispringen, near Pforzheim, known internationally for his extraordinary skeletonised and hand-engraved movements. Working with established brands and as an independent, Benzinger is considered one of the finest artisans in contemporary fine watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: Skeleton
keyCollections.description: Hand-skeletonised and engraved movements built on modified ETA and Unitas base calibres, Benzinger's signature specialty.

keyCollections.name: Guilloché Dials
keyCollections.description: Hand-guilloché dials produced on century-old rose and straight-line engines, supplied to independent brands and used in Benzinger's own watches.

keyCollections.name: Subscription Series
keyCollections.description: Limited numbered series sold directly and through partners, combining bespoke dial work with classical case architecture.

timeline.event: Jochen Benzinger begins his training at the Pforzheim Goldsmiths' School.
Founds his own workshop in Pforzheim, initially working for the local jewellery industry.
Shifts focus toward guilloché and hand-skeletonisation for watch brands including IWC, Chronoswiss and Glashütte Original.
Releases watches under his own name, combining skeletonised movements with hand-engraved dials.
Expands a long-running relationship with Fabergé, producing guilloché work for their Imperial eggs and jewellery watches.

faqItems.question: What is Jochen Benzinger known for?
faqItems.answer: Hand guilloché, engraving and skeletonisation. Benzinger is regarded as one of the finest engine-turning artisans working today, producing dials and skeletonised movements for his own brand and for many established houses.

faqItems.question: Where is the Benzinger workshop?
faqItems.answer: In Pforzheim, Germany — the historic centre of German jewellery and fine metalwork — where he works with around twenty hand-operated engines, many over a century old.

name: Jowissa
description: Elegant Swiss timepieces for women and men. Jowissa creates signature design watches that all have a case made of stainless steel with a sapphire crystal — combining slim, refined Swiss aesthetics with reliable movements. A trusted name in dress watchmaking since 1951, offering genuine Swiss elegance at accessible price points.

faqItems.question: Where does the name Jowissa come from?
faqItems.answer: Jowissa is a contraction of "Josef Wyss AG", the name of the company founded by Josef Wyss in 1951 in Bettlach, Switzerland.

faqItems.question: What are Jowissa watches known for?
faqItems.answer: Jowissa produces affordable Swiss Made watches, often with a signature faceted crystal.

keyCollections.name: Facet
keyCollections.description: Jowissa’s Facet is the brand’s signature crystal-cut women’s watch family, defined by faceted glass and jewel-like styling that echo diamond cuts and emphasize color, sparkle, and affordable Swiss-made fashion-watch positioning. The collection appears in current official site navigation and in Jowissa’s collection-group pages as one of four facet-inspired lines.

referenceDetails.name: Facet
referenceDetails.note: Official homepage and collection pages present Facet as a current women’s watch line with diamond-cut glass and jewel styling.

referenceDetails.name: Facet Princess
referenceDetails.note: Official collection-group page lists Facet Princess as a sister line within the Facets family.

timeline.event: Facet is visible on Jowissa’s current official site and collection-group pages.
Jowissa’s homepage highlights Facet Oval Petite and related faceted-glass women’s models.
The brand’s facet-inspired collection-group page frames Facet as one of four diamond-cut themed families.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Facet is a core Jowissa identity line because it condenses the brand’s faceted-glass signature into a recognizable women’s collection and serves as a bridge between fashion styling and Swiss-made watch positioning.

keyCollections.name: Tiro
keyCollections.description: Tiro is Jowissa's dress-oriented Swiss-made watch line centered on a 38 mm ladies' format with faceted crystal, sunray dials, rhinestone hour markers, three-hand display, and a date window, offered on polished bracelets or glossy straps in multiple colorways.

referenceDetails.name: Tiro Swiss Ladies Watch J6.246.M
referenceDetails.note: Official ladies' Tiro collection listing shows this as a current gold/white 38 mm variant in the line.

image.alt: Jowissa Tiro Swiss Ladies Watch J6.246.M gold and white

referenceDetails.name: Tiro Swiss Ladies Watch J6.243.M
referenceDetails.note: Official ladies' Tiro collection listing shows this as a current gold/black 38 mm variant in the line.

image.alt: Jowissa Tiro Swiss Ladies Watch J6.243.M gold and black

referenceDetails.name: Tiro Swiss Ladies Watch J6.248.M
referenceDetails.note: Official product page for a rose gold and purple Tiro model within the same 38 mm Swiss-made ladies' family.

image.alt: Jowissa Tiro Swiss Ladies Watch J6.248.M product family image

timeline.event: Jowissa states on its official site that the company was founded in Bettlach, Switzerland in 1951, providing the historical backdrop for later Tiro models.
The current Tiro collection images on Jowissa's CDN carry 2025 version stamps, showing the collection remained actively merchandised with refreshed media in 2025.
Jowissa's current U.S. collection page presents Tiro as an active ladies' collection with 13 products and a brand-written collection description focused on glamour and faceted glass.

Jowissa's current men's category pages also reference Tiro, indicating the name extends beyond the ladies' dress line even though the official ladies' collection page remains the clearest source for this assignment.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Tiro is a useful Jowissa collection because the brand itself gives a concise, design-led identity for it: glamorous Swiss-made dress watches with faceted crystal styling, making it one of the clearer current collection stories on the site.

image.alt: Jowissa Tiro Swiss Ladies Watch from the Tiro collection

faqItems.question: What are the defining design cues of the Jowissa Tiro collection?
faqItems.answer: Jowissa describes Tiro as a glamorous ladies' watch family with a 38 mm case, faceted glass, sunray dial, rhinestone markers, three hands, and a date window.

faqItems.question: What straps or bracelets does Jowissa show for Tiro?
faqItems.answer: The official collection text says Tiro is offered with polished gold bracelets or glossy patent-leather-style straps in multiple colors, and current listings also show silicone-strap executions.

keyCollections.name: Magno
keyCollections.description: Magno is Jowissa’s men’s collection built around a new 40 mm case, bold edges, and a range of dials that includes moon-phase executions. It is positioned as a smart-casual everyday line that keeps the brand’s decorative, Swiss-made character while leaning more strongly into masculine proportions.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Magno broadens Jowissa’s men’s assortment with a larger case format and a more versatile dress-casual look, while retaining the brand’s color and surface treatment language.

timeline.event: Jowissa’s live collection pages describe Magno as a men’s line with a new 40 mm case and multiple dial executions.
Jowissa published a blog post about new classic additions to the Magno collection.
The Magno collection page continues to list moon-phase and non-moon-phase references in current stock.

referenceDetails.name: Magno collection page
referenceDetails.note: Official men’s collection landing page.

referenceDetails.name: Magno Moon variant
referenceDetails.note: Moon-phase subline visible on the current collection page.

referenceDetails.name: Magno Swiss Men's Watch J4.544.L
referenceDetails.note: Representative current Magno SKU on the collection page.

faqItems.question: Is Magno a dress watch line?
faqItems.answer: It is best described as a smart-casual men’s collection with dress-watch cues and moon-phase options.

faqItems.question: What is the core case size?
faqItems.answer: The official copy highlights a new 40 mm case.

keyCollections.name: LeWy
keyCollections.description: LeWy is Jowissa’s edgy men’s watch family, spanning three-hand and chronograph variants and built around a sharper case profile, signature crystal-cut styling, and a contemporary sport-dress positioning that bridges everyday wear with a more assertive look.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: LeWy became one of Jowissa’s core men’s lines because it translated the brand’s colorful, faceted aesthetic into a more masculine, modern case language that still reads distinctly Jowissa.

timeline.event: Jowissa continues to market LeWy as an active men’s collection and still lists LeWy 3 and LeWy 9 variants on the collection pages.
Jowissa’s blog introduced the new LeWy men’s collection on 24 July 2018.
The current LeWy landing page describes the latest LeWy chronographs as a strikingly cool range with subtle design differences and an edgier case.

referenceDetails.name: LeWy landing page
referenceDetails.note: Official collection-group page for the family.

referenceDetails.name: LeWy 3 collection page
referenceDetails.note: Official product-family page describing the three-hand style.

referenceDetails.name: LeWy 9 product family
referenceDetails.note: Chronograph sub-line shown on the LeWy collection page.

faqItems.question: What kind of watches are in LeWy?
faqItems.answer: LeWy includes men’s watches offered in three-hand and chronograph formats.

faqItems.question: What is the design idea behind LeWy?
faqItems.answer: The line emphasizes a sharper, more assertive case while keeping Jowissa’s signature crystal-cut identity.

timeline.event: Josef Wyss founds Jowissa in Bettlach, Switzerland, starting production in his home with two employees.
Dedicated factory built next to the Wyss family residence to accommodate growing production.
Josef Wyss' sons Erich, Manfred and Leander take over and formally establish the Jowissa brand.

name: Junghans
description: Junghans was founded in Schramberg, Germany in 1861 and grew to become one of the world's largest watch manufacturers by the early 20th century. Today the brand is known for the Max Bill collection — an icon of Bauhaus-influenced design — and for its radio-controlled Mega Solar technology.

timeline.event: Launches the Aquaris collection, its first modern professional dive watch rated to 500m, powered by a Grand Seiko-derived calibre J830 with Junghans modifications. Priced from EUR 2,690.

faqItems.question: Where is Junghans based?
faqItems.answer: Junghans has been based in Schramberg, in Germany's Black Forest, since its founding in 1861.

faqItems.question: What is the Max Bill collection?
faqItems.answer: The Max Bill line is based on watch and clock designs created for Junghans from the 1950s onward by Swiss Bauhaus artist and designer Max Bill.

keyCollections.name: Max Bill
keyCollections.description: Junghans Max Bill is the brand’s long-running minimalist line based on Max Bill’s Bauhaus-informed watch design language, pairing pared-back dials, disciplined typography, and functional clarity with modern Junghans movements.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Max Bill is one of Junghans’ signature identities: it bridges mid-century Swiss-German design history with a still-current product family, making it both an aesthetic cornerstone and an important commercial pillar.

referenceDetails.name: max bill Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Core three-hand expression in the collection; the official collection page describes the line as a near-unchanged Bauhaus design icon for decades.

referenceDetails.name: max bill Chronoscope
referenceDetails.note: Chronograph variant referenced within the official shop as a related model in the Max Bill family.

referenceDetails.name: max bill Regulator
referenceDetails.note: Official product page highlights the line’s distinctive typography and regulator dial layout.

timeline.event: Junghans’ official collection page described Max Bill as a timeless Bauhaus watch line that has remained almost unchanged for about six decades.
The brand continued selling multiple Max Bill variants, including automatic and regulator executions, through the official shop.
The collection’s typography and dial language remained a defining feature, reinforcing the Max Bill design code.

faqItems.question: Who is Max Bill in this context?
faqItems.answer: Max Bill was the designer whose Bauhaus-influenced watch forms became the basis of this Junghans family.

faqItems.question: Why is the line so recognizable?
faqItems.answer: Because its restrained dial, typography, and proportions stay very close to the original design logic, even in modern variants.

image.alt: Junghans max bill Chronoscope official product image

keyCollections.name: Meister
keyCollections.description: Junghans Meister is the brand’s classic dress-watch family: elegant, domed, finely finished watches that Junghans positions as a centerpiece of its collection and a long-running expression of German craftsmanship.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Meister is the heritage anchor of Junghans’ modern catalog, linking the company’s mid-century design language to its current dress and complication offerings.

referenceDetails.name: Meister Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Current core automatic entry within the Meister family.

referenceDetails.name: Meister Chronoscope
referenceDetails.note: Chronograph variant repeatedly shown in the Meister assortment and press materials.

referenceDetails.name: Meister Worldtimer
referenceDetails.note: Travel-oriented model within the collection, listed on official Meister product pages.

timeline.event: Junghans continued to present Meister as a core collection on official product and catalog pages.

faqItems.question: What kind of watches are in Meister?
faqItems.answer: Primarily elegant dress watches and related complications, such as automatics, chronographs, and world timers.

faqItems.question: Is Meister still active today?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Junghans’ official site currently maintains a dedicated Meister collection page with active models.

keyCollections.name: FORM
keyCollections.description: Junghans FORM is the brand’s contemporary design collection, centered on clean, reduced case architecture, concave dials, and a practical mix of quartz and automatic models. It sits between minimalist Bauhaus-adjacent styling and everyday wearability, with both ladies’ models and sporty chronographs in the wider line.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: FORM is an important bridge collection for Junghans because it translates the brand’s design heritage into a modern, wearable daily line that remains distinct from max bill and Meister.

timeline.event: Junghans continued to publish FORM-related press releases, including FORM A Chronoscope coverage in July 2024.
The Junghans site still lists FORM as an active collection alongside Meister, max bill, and Performance.
Current product pages show FORM variants such as FORM Quarz and FORM A Automatic in the collection structure.

referenceDetails.name: FORM collection page
referenceDetails.note: Official collection landing page with minimalist positioning text.

referenceDetails.name: FORM A Automatic
referenceDetails.note: Representative automatic model page in the FORM family.

referenceDetails.name: FORM A Chronoscope press release
referenceDetails.note: Official June/July 2024 press coverage for a FORM A Chronoscope variant.

faqItems.question: Is FORM only a quartz collection?
faqItems.answer: No. The line includes both quartz and mechanical/automatic models.

faqItems.question: What is the design idea behind FORM?
faqItems.answer: Junghans presents it as a reduced, functional, and visually clear design family with strong everyday versatility.

keyCollections.description: Junghans 1972 is the brand's sport-watch family inspired by its 1972 Olympic timing heritage, currently represented by colorful Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 chronographs and radio-controlled Mega Solar models.

referenceDetails.name: 1972 Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 Green
referenceDetails.note: Junghans' official product record describes a green 1972 Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 with historic Junghans lettering, black totalisers, and a double-stripe dial.

image.alt: Junghans 1972 Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 green watch

referenceDetails.name: 1972 Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 Turquoise
referenceDetails.note: Junghans' official product record lists this turquoise execution with the same 43.3 mm case, sapphire crystal, and sport-stripe dial language.

image.alt: Junghans 1972 Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 turquoise watch

referenceDetails.name: 1972 Mega Solar
referenceDetails.note: Junghans' official product API lists this 1972 Mega Solar with a radio-controlled solar movement, sapphire crystal, and stainless steel bracelet.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The 1972 family lets Junghans connect a real timing-history chapter with current accessible sport watches, giving the brand a more athletic counterpoint to Max Bill, Meister, and FORM.

image.alt: Junghans 1972 Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 green watch

gallery.alt: Junghans 1972 Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 turquoise watch

timeline.event: Junghans' official manufacturing history marks 1972 as a major company milestone tied to precision timing.
Junghans' official product API lists 1972 Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 references with colorful sport dials.
The same official product feed lists 1972 Mega Solar models with multi-frequency radio-controlled solar movements.

faqItems.question: What is Junghans 1972?
faqItems.answer: 1972 is Junghans' sport-watch family, connecting the brand's timing heritage to current Chronoscope and Mega Solar models.

faqItems.question: Which 1972 references are current examples?
faqItems.answer: Junghans' current official product API includes 1972 Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 references and 1972 Mega Solar references.

faqItems.question: How does 1972 differ from Max Bill?
faqItems.answer: Max Bill is Junghans' minimalist design line, while 1972 is the sportier family with chronograph and solar-radio-controlled models.

funFacts.title: Radio-controlled option
funFacts.body: The 1972 Mega Solar product record lists a multi-frequency radio-controlled solar movement.

funFacts.title: Sports Edition colors
funFacts.body: Junghans' 1972 Chronoscope Sports Edition 2026 records include bold green, turquoise, and orange dial executions.

name: Junkers
description: Junkers is a German watch brand launched in 1998 by POINTtec, producing aviation-inspired timepieces named in honour of Professor Hugo Junkers, the pioneering German aircraft designer. The watches draw on Bauhaus design principles — clean lines, geometric forms, and functional clarity — with movements by Swiss and German manufacturers.

keyCollections.name: Bauhaus
keyCollections.description: Junkers’ Bauhaus line is a minimalist dress-watch family explicitly tied to the Bauhaus philosophy and to Hugo Junkers’ historic connection with the movement, with clean typography, restrained geometry, and multiple size and movement variants.

keyCollections.name: Ju 52
keyCollections.description: Junkers’ Ju 52 line celebrates the iconic Ju 52 aircraft with pilot and chronograph styling, aircraft-history branding, and highly recognisable aviation design cues that connect the watches directly to the brand’s heritage narrative.

keyCollections.name: G38
keyCollections.description: Junkers’ G38 collection references the pioneering Junkers G38 airliner and sits within the brand’s broader aircraft-led design language, with cockpit-inspired cues and aviation storytelling that reinforce the model family’s historical theme.

keyCollections.name: Eisvogel
keyCollections.description: A dress-leaning Junkers collection associated with the Eisvogel aircraft theme, aligning with the brand’s Bauhaus-influenced design language and its wider aviation heritage.

timeline.event: Hugo Junkers founds Junkers Flugzeugwerke, pioneering all-metal aircraft and supporting the emerging Bauhaus movement.
Willi Birk founds Pointtec in Bavaria to produce heritage-inspired German wristwatches.
Pointtec launches the Junkers watch brand, using the Junkers aviation heritage under licence.
Introduction of the Bauhaus and Ju 52 collections, which become the brand's best sellers.
Expanded Bauhaus collection marks the centenary of the Bauhaus movement.

faqItems.question: Is Junkers related to the aircraft manufacturer?
faqItems.answer: The brand is licensed from the heritage of Junkers Flugzeugwerke, founded by aviation pioneer Hugo Junkers in 1919. The watches are made by the German company Pointtec and draw their design language from historic Junkers aircraft and the Bauhaus movement.

faqItems.question: Where are Junkers watches made?
faqItems.answer: In Germany, by Pointtec Product Marketing GmbH, using Swiss and German movements across quartz and mechanical collections.

name: Kari Voutilainen
description: Kari Voutilainen founded his atelier in Môtiers, Switzerland in 2002 after training at the Watchmaking School of Le Locle and working at several prestigious manufactures. He is widely regarded as one of the world's finest living independent watchmakers, known for flawlessly executed movements and dials in the classical tradition.

timeline.event: Wins GPHG 2025 artistic crafts category with the Vingt-8 GML SOUYOU (Japanese lacquer). Announces retirement of the Vingt-8 movement with the final 28MPR Moonphase Power Reserve. Steps back from CEO role at Urban Jürgensen to focus on watchmaking.

faqItems.question: Where is Kari Voutilainen based?
faqItems.answer: Voutilainen's atelier is located in Môtiers, in the Val-de-Travers region of Switzerland, where he founded his independent workshop in 2002.

faqItems.question: What is Voutilainen known for?
faqItems.answer: The atelier is known for hand-finished movements, traditional guilloché dials, and limited annual production. Kari Voutilainen has won multiple GPHG awards.

keyCollections.name: Vingt-8
keyCollections.description: Kari Voutilainen’s core round time-only line, introduced as the first model built around the in-house calibre 28 and known for classical case proportions, hand-guilloché dials, and refined high-end finishing.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Vingt-8 is the foundational modern Voutilainen collection: it marks the brand’s move toward an in-house movement architecture while preserving the atelier’s traditional visual language and artisanal dial work.

referenceDetails.name: Core time-only Vingt-8
referenceDetails.note: Launch-model time-only execution around the in-house calibre 28, with classical round case and guilloché dial.

referenceDetails.name: Vingt-8R power-reserve variant
referenceDetails.note: A complication-led variation of the same family, noted by FHH as launched in 2013.

referenceDetails.name: Vingt-8 ISO read-off variant
referenceDetails.note: A later interpretation of the family with an unusual time display, cited by FHH as presented in 2017.

timeline.event: The Vingt-8 line remains a core Voutilainen platform referenced by official and auction sources, including modern catalogue examples and atelier portfolio pages.
Contemporary Voutilainen portfolio pages continue to frame the calibre VINGT-8 as a landmark in the workshop’s history and philosophy.
Auction records continue to describe Vingt-8 as a rare, made-to-order independent watch with hand-finished components and direct-impulse escapement.

faqItems.question: What is Vingt-8?
faqItems.answer: It is Kari Voutilainen’s core round wristwatch family built around the brand’s in-house calibre 28 and finished in a traditional artisanal style.

faqItems.question: What makes it notable?
faqItems.answer: It is widely treated as a milestone for the atelier because it combined a fully developed in-house movement approach with the brand’s signature hand-finishing and guilloché work.

keyCollections.name: 28ti
keyCollections.description: Inverted-movement variant of the Vingt-8 displaying the calibre 28 on the dial side.

keyCollections.name: Observatoire
keyCollections.description: Time-only line based on a restored stock of vintage Peseux 260 observatory chronometer movements.

keyCollections.name: Masterpiece
keyCollections.description: Kari Voutilainen's Masterpiece line is a tiny, high-complication family of largely unique decimal repeater and chronograph watches, created with the atelier's hallmark hand-finishing, guilloche dials, and traditional case-making philosophy.

referenceDetails.name: Masterpiece 6 Decimal Repeater
referenceDetails.note: Official Voutilainen portfolio page for the early decimal repeater with power-reserve indication; the atelier describes the decimal repeater sequence as hours, ten-minute intervals, then minutes.

referenceDetails.name: Masterpiece 7 Decimal Repeater
referenceDetails.note: Official Voutilainen portfolio page for a Masterpiece decimal repeater, preserving the collection's rare high-complication lineage.

referenceDetails.name: Masterpiece 8 Decimal Repeater
referenceDetails.note: Official Voutilainen portfolio page says Masterpiece 8 builds on the decimal minute repeater concept and adds a second-time-zone display.

timeline.event: Phillips dates the debut of Voutilainen's decimal repeater under the Masterpiece 6 name to 2004.
The AHCI member catalogue documented the Masterpiece 6, Masterpiece 7, and Decimal Repeater 8 together, showing Masterpiece as an established complication family by then.
Voutilainen's site published the Masterpiece Chronograph II as a unique series of 10 pieces, extending the Masterpiece name beyond decimal repeaters.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Masterpiece captures the most experimental and prestigious side of Kari Voutilainen's oeuvre: early decimal repeating wristwatches, mostly unique executions, and later small-series complications that helped establish his reputation among independent high-watchmaking collectors.

faqItems.question: What defines the Voutilainen Masterpiece collection?
faqItems.answer: It is the atelier's high-complication Masterpiece family, best known for decimal repeater wristwatches and later limited chronograph executions with extensive hand finishing.

faqItems.question: Are Masterpiece watches regular-production models?
faqItems.answer: No. Available evidence points to unique pieces or very small series, with decimal repeaters described by Phillips as never produced in series and the Masterpiece Chronograph II listed by Voutilainen as a 10-piece series.

gallery.alt: Voutilainen Masterpiece 6 Decimal Repeater dial detail

name: Kerbedanz
description: Independent haute horlogerie Maison based in Neuchâtel since 2011, KERBEDANZ was first renowned for its exceptional tourbillons — the largest in the world — and has since expanded into sumptuous complications and bespoke métiers d'art. Each KERBEDANZ piece is crafted to be entirely unique, built around the collector's singular vision.

faqItems.question: Where is Kerbedanz based?
faqItems.answer: Kerbedanz is based in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, and was founded in 2011.

faqItems.question: What is the Maximus tourbillon?
faqItems.answer: Launched in 2017, the Maximus houses a central flying tourbillon with a 27mm cage, presented as the largest tourbillon ever fitted in a wristwatch.

keyCollections.name: Maximus
keyCollections.description: High-complication line built around the KRB-08 central flying tourbillon with a 27mm cage.

keyCollections.name: Cadanz
keyCollections.description: Cadanz is Kerbedanz’s broader-audience mechanical collection introduced in 2021, pairing the brand’s distinctive 2 o’clock crown, central guilloché styling, and varied date-display executions with serially produced three-hand and date models in multiple sizes.

referenceDetails.name: Cadanz by Kerbedanz Cruise Date
referenceDetails.note: Press and sponsored launch coverage describe the Cruise Date as a 41 mm Cadanz variant with hours spelled out from 1 to 12 and an evanescent date display.

image.alt: Kerbedanz Cadanz by Kerbedanz collection image used in launch coverage

referenceDetails.name: Cadanz by Kerbedanz Signature Date
referenceDetails.note: Launch materials identify Signature as a Cadanz family branch distinguished by 12-3-6-9 typography and date display treatments.

referenceDetails.name: Cadanz by Kerbedanz Boutique Edition
referenceDetails.note: Launch materials identify Boutique Edition as an exclusive Cadanz edition available through Kerbedanz’s website.

positioningOrTimeline.event: Kerbedanz announced Cadanz as a new collection moving the brand beyond one-off pieces and micro-series toward a broader audience.
Launch materials stated the line already included more than 30 references and three case sizes: 32, 36, and 41 mm.
The Cruise, Signature, Idyll, and Boutique Edition branches defined the initial family, with multiple materials, dial colors, and date-display executions.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Cadanz is important because it marks Kerbedanz’s transition from highly singular halo pieces into a more accessibly positioned mechanical family without abandoning brand signatures such as the 2 o’clock crown, decorative dial center, and customization-driven approach.

image.alt: Kerbedanz Cadanz collection image from launch coverage

faqItems.question: What is the role of Cadanz in Kerbedanz’s lineup?
faqItems.answer: Cadanz was launched as Kerbedanz’s broader, more serially produced mechanical collection, complementing the brand’s better-known unique and high-complication pieces.

faqItems.question: What design cues distinguish Cadanz watches?
faqItems.answer: Launch materials emphasize the 2 o’clock crown position, central guilloché pattern, multiple date-display styles, and a wide mix of sizes, materials, and straps.

timeline.event: Kerbedanz founded in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, initially producing bespoke commissions.
First public collection presented at Baselworld.
Maximus Tourbillon launched with the KRB-08 central flying tourbillon.
Cadanz Cruise Date 41 released as the brand's steel entry-level line.

name: Kikuchi Nakagawa
description: Kikuchi Nakagawa is a Japanese independent watch brand founded by Yusuke Kikuchi and Tomonari Nakagawa in Tokyo. The brand specializes in restrained, hand-finished dress watches inspired by the 1930s to 1950s, with collections such as Murakumo, Ichimonji, and Genmon built around black-polished steel cases, elegant hands, and classical dial layouts.

keyCollections.name: Murakumo
keyCollections.description: A signature time-only watch with a black-polished steel case, elevated hands, and quiet classical proportions.

keyCollections.name: Ichimonji
keyCollections.description: Kikuchi Nakagawa’s restrained dress-watch line, built around the brand’s signature monochrome finishing, a compact classical case, and highly disciplined dial and hand details that sit between vintage inspiration and modern Japanese independent craftsmanship.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Ichimonji is one of the brand’s defining core references: it crystallizes Kikuchi Nakagawa’s design language into a compact, highly finished dress-watch format and remains central to how collectors identify the maison.

referenceDetails.name: Ichimonji
referenceDetails.note: Official product page with movement, case, dial, and price details; the watch is listed at 22,000 USD before tax.

referenceDetails.name: Murakumo
referenceDetails.note: The signature sibling collection repeatedly referenced by official navigation and contemporary coverage.

referenceDetails.name: Genmon
referenceDetails.note: The later collection that shares the same overall family architecture and is listed as an active watch line on the official site.

timeline.event: SJX covered the introduction of the Ichimonji as a new Kikuchi Nakagawa model family.
The official site continues to list Ichimonji among the brand’s active watches.
Current official product details specify the KN001 movement, 36.8mm case, and 22,000 USD pre-tax price.

faqItems.question: What movement does Ichimonji use?
faqItems.answer: The official page lists the KN001, made by Vaucher Manufacture Fleurier, with automatic winding and 48 hours of power reserve.

faqItems.question: How large is the case?
faqItems.answer: The official specification lists a 36.8mm case diameter and 45.3mm lug-to-lug.

keyCollections.name: Genmon
keyCollections.description: A later collection extending Kikuchi Nakagawa’s monochrome classicism with refined case and dial details.

timeline.event: Koji Kikuchi and Masao Nakagawa found Kikuchi Nakagawa in Tokyo, combining Japanese decorative arts with Swiss-level watchmaking.
Debut of the Murakumo, featuring Urushi lacquer dials crafted by specialist artisans.
Brand gains international recognition in the independent watchmaking community for its artisanal dial work.

faqItems.question: What makes Kikuchi Nakagawa dials special?
faqItems.answer: Each dial is hand-decorated using traditional Japanese techniques such as Urushi lacquer and guilloché, making every piece unique.

faqItems.question: How many watches does Kikuchi Nakagawa produce?
faqItems.answer: Production is extremely limited, typically fewer than 50 pieces per year, emphasising artisanal quality over volume.

seoTitle: Kikuchi Nakagawa - Japanese Independent Watchmaker | Watchatlas
seoDescription: Kikuchi Nakagawa is a Japanese independent watchmaker by Yusuke Kikuchi and Tomonari Nakagawa, known for Murakumo, Ichimonji and Genmon.
whyMatters: Kikuchi Nakagawa matters as one of Japan’s most focused independent dress-watch makers: extremely restrained design, painstaking case finishing, and a clear devotion to pre-war and mid-century watch aesthetics.
knownFor: Founders Yusuke Kikuchi and Tomonari Nakagawa

name: KOBOLD
description: Kobold is an American watch brand founded in 1999 by Michael Kobold in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, initially as a Carnegie Mellon University entrepreneurship project. Known for expedition-grade field and dive watches including the Soarway Seal and Polar Surveyor Chronograph, Kobold has outfitted US Navy SEALs and mounted Everest expeditions.

keyCollections.name: Phantom
keyCollections.description: Kobold’s Phantom is part of the brand’s Soarway tool-watch family and is positioned as a rugged chronograph associated with expedition-grade construction, a Soarway case, and the brand’s adventure-first identity.

timeline.event: Kobold’s current site materials continue to reference the Phantom as a Soarway-family model, with the broader Phantom line also appearing in newer Phantom SL and Phantom Black Ops product pages.

keyCollections.name: Soarway Diver Seal
keyCollections.description: Extreme 1,000-meter Kobold diver built around the signature Soarway case and the iconic Seal design language, pairing oversized tool-watch proportions with Swiss automatic movement and a rugged, expedition-first character.

keyCollections.name: Spirit of America
keyCollections.description: Kobold’s American-made milestone watch, originally created to bring watchmaking back to the U.S., combining patriotic provenance with a robust field-watch build and Swiss automatic movement.

timeline.event: Michael Kobold founds Kobold Watch Company, becoming the first watch brand to sell directly over the Internet.
Release of the Phantom Chronograph featuring the signature Soarway case, co-designed with Sir Ranulph Fiennes.
Launch of the Soarway Diver Seal, a 1,000m diver designed by James Gandolfini.
Spirit of America Automatic released — first watch with a US-made case in nearly 40 years.
Michael Kobold becomes the first watchmaker to summit Mount Everest.

faqItems.question: Where are Kobold watches made?
faqItems.answer: Components are made in Germany and Switzerland, with final assembly at Kobold's atelier in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA.

faqItems.question: What is the Soarway case?
faqItems.answer: A proprietary case design created by Michael Kobold with explorer Sir Ranulph Fiennes, built for extreme expedition conditions.

name: Konstantin Chaykin
description: Konstantin Chaykin is a Russian independent watchmaker and founder of the Moscow Watch Institute, known for designing mechanical watches with automata and whimsical display complications. He is best known for the Joker, featuring a clown face with eyes indicating hours and a crescent-shaped mouth indicating minutes.

keyCollections.name: Joker
keyCollections.description: Iconic wristwatch with a smiling face complication using hour and minute discs as eyes and a mouth indicator, Chaykin's most recognisable creation.

keyCollections.name: Wristmons
keyCollections.description: Wristmons is Konstantin Chaykin’s long-running character-watch universe, beginning with the Joker and expanding into a broad roster of anthropomorphic, theme-driven models that use the brand’s face-display idea to combine horology, humor, and collectability.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: It is the umbrella collection that made Chaykin internationally recognizable, giving him a visually distinctive design language and a platform for dozens of creative variants.

timeline.event: The original Joker was introduced at BaselWorld as the first Wristmon.
Brand coverage marked the fifth anniversary of the Wristmons collection and highlighted its rapid growth.
Konstantin Chaykin unveiled Joker Classic and described the Wristmons family as numbering over 30 unique and limited editions.

referenceDetails.name: Original Joker
referenceDetails.note: The first Wristmon and origin point for the collection.

referenceDetails.name: Joker Classic
referenceDetails.note: 2024 evolution of the foundational Wristmon concept.

referenceDetails.name: Joker Mask
referenceDetails.note: Mask-themed extension of the Wristmons line.

faqItems.question: What are Wristmons?
faqItems.answer: A family of character-faced watches built around Chaykin’s anthropomorphic dial concept.

faqItems.question: What started the line?
faqItems.answer: The original Joker, introduced in 2017 at BaselWorld.

keyCollections.name: Genius Temporis
keyCollections.description: Elegant dress watch with a jumping hour and wandering minutes display, showcasing Chaykin's technical creativity beyond character watches.

timeline.event: Konstantin Chaykin establishes his independent watchmaking workshop in Saint Petersburg, Russia.
Accepted as a candidate member of the Académie Horlogère des Créateurs Indépendants (AHCI).
Becomes a full AHCI member — the only Russian member in the academy's history.
Launches the Joker, which becomes an instant icon and the brand's signature piece.
Awarded the WIPO Medal for Inventors for his contribution to technical sciences.

Unveils the ThinKing — at 1.65 mm the thinnest watch ever made, with double mystery displays, limited to 12 pieces at CHF 400,000. Launches the Louis Erard x Chaykin Unfrogettable collaboration and the Venus Wristmon inspired by Botticelli.

faqItems.question: Where is Konstantin Chaykin based?
faqItems.answer: The brand was founded in Saint Petersburg and later moved production to Moscow, Russia. Chaykin is the only Russian member of the AHCI.

faqItems.question: What is the Joker watch?
faqItems.answer: A wristwatch with a smiling face where the eyes are rotating hour and minute discs, creating an animated clown-like expression. It became a viral sensation in the watch world.

name: Krayon
description: Krayon is a Swiss independent watch brand founded by Rémi Maillat in Neuchâtel in 2017, known for the Anywhere — a unique timepiece displaying the equation of time and true solar noon for any location on Earth by adjusting the watch's crown. A technically ambitious achievement in independent watchmaking, with pieces priced from around $500,000.

keyCollections.name: Everywhere
keyCollections.description: The brand's sole model, a mechanical watch displaying sunrise and sunset times for any location on Earth, adjustable via the crown.

timeline.event: Rémi Maillat founds Krayon in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, after years developing the sunrise/sunset complication.
Debuts the Everywhere at Baselworld, the world's first mechanical watch showing sunrise and sunset for any location.
Wins the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève Innovation Prize for the Everywhere.

faqItems.question: What does the Krayon Everywhere do?
faqItems.answer: It mechanically calculates and displays sunrise and sunset times for any location on Earth. The wearer sets their coordinates via the crown — no electronics involved.

faqItems.question: How many watches does Krayon make?
faqItems.answer: Production is extremely limited, with only a handful of pieces made per year, each individually customised for the owner's location.

name: Kross Studio
description: Kross Studio is a Swiss luxury brand founded in 2020, producing highly unconventional timepieces and limited-edition collector objects that challenge traditional watch conventions. Known for collaborations with properties including Dune and Star Wars, the brand targets collectors seeking sculptural, artistic expression in mechanical form.

keyCollections.name: Star Wars Collection
keyCollections.description: Licensed collaboration with Lucasfilm featuring sculpted Star Wars-themed table clocks and tourbillon wristwatches, including the Death Star and TIE Fighter.

keyCollections.name: Batman Collection
keyCollections.description: DC-licensed pieces featuring a Batmobile desk clock and Batman-themed tourbillon wristwatch with bespoke case architecture.

timeline.event: Marco Tedeschi and Julien Bonzom found Kross Studio in Switzerland, combining haute horlogerie with pop-culture licensing.
Launches the Death Star Tourbillon in collaboration with Lucasfilm, attracting global attention.
Releases the Batmobile desk clock and Batman tourbillon wristwatch in partnership with Warner Bros / DC.
Rebrands to Marco Tedeschi at Watches & Wonders 2026, unveiling the MT1.1 Tourbillon 7 Jours in tantalum. Chanel acquires a 30% stake in the newly carved-out Kross Manufacture production arm.

faqItems.question: What is Kross Studio known for?
faqItems.answer: High-end tourbillon watches and desk clocks inspired by pop-culture franchises like Star Wars and Batman, officially licensed and produced in Switzerland.

faqItems.question: Where is Kross Studio based?
faqItems.answer: The brand is headquartered in Switzerland, combining Swiss watchmaking expertise with bold, franchise-inspired designs.

name: Kudoke
description: Kudoke is a small German watchmaking atelier founded by Stefan Kudoke in Glashütte, known for its hand-engraved movement plates and skeletonised watches produced in extremely limited numbers. The brand combines traditional German finishing with a contemporary artistic approach.

keyCollections.name: KudOktopus
keyCollections.description: Signature hand-engraved skeletonised watch featuring an octopus motif across the dial and movement, showcasing Kudoke's engraving mastery.

keyCollections.name: KUDOKE 2
keyCollections.description: KUDOKE 2 is Stefan Kudoke’s award-winning, hand-finished entry model: a restrained 39 mm steel or rose-gold watch with a dial-side 24-hour display at 12 o’clock, combining German artisanal engraving with a calm, classical wearing profile.

referenceDetails.name: Core steel model
referenceDetails.note: The foundational version with the signature dial-side 24-hour display and hand-engraved sky disc.

referenceDetails.name: Black dial version
referenceDetails.note: A darker galvano-black interpretation emphasizing the day-night display at 12 o’clock.

referenceDetails.name: Rose gold case version
referenceDetails.note: 18 ct rose-gold case variant with matching finishing options and dial-side sky disk.

timeline.event: Kudoke continued to highlight KUDOKE 2 variants alongside newer brand developments.
KUDOKE 2 British Heritage expanded the line through a special limited edition collaboration.
KUDOKE 2 won the GPHG Petite Aiguille, helping establish the model as the brand’s breakout reference.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: KUDOKE 2 is the model that most clearly defines Stefan Kudoke’s modern identity: technically distinctive but accessible compared with haute-horlogerie independents, and widely recognized through award and collaboration visibility.

timeline.event: Stefan Kudoke, a trained watchmaker and engraver, founds Kudoke in Germany, specialising in hand-engraved timepieces.
Launches the KudOktopus, which becomes the brand's most iconic and recognisable piece.
Wins the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève 'Petit Aiguille' Prize for the KudOktopus.

faqItems.question: What makes Kudoke watches unique?
faqItems.answer: Every watch features hand-engraved decoration by Stefan Kudoke himself, a skill that takes years to master. Each piece is essentially a miniature work of art.

faqItems.question: Where is Kudoke based?
faqItems.answer: The brand is based in Germany. Stefan Kudoke trained at the German School of Watchmaking and is a member of the AHCI.

name: Kurono Tokyo
description: Kurono Tokyo is a Japanese independent watch brand created by Hajime Asaoka, offering more accessible mechanical watches that carry the design DNA of his exclusive handmade atelier pieces. The brand is known for Art Deco-inspired cases, carefully tuned dial colors, limited online releases, salon editions, and collector-focused series such as Classic, Grand, and Chronograph models.

keyCollections.name: Classic Series
keyCollections.description: Kurono Tokyo’s Classic Series is the brand’s accessible, art-deco-leaning core line: compact, high-polish, time-first watches that translate Hajime Asaoka’s design language into more attainable daily wear while preserving the brand’s refined dial balance and strong typographic identity.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Classic Series is the entry point to Kurono’s design philosophy, where the brand’s collector-accessible mission, compact proportions, and art-deco cues are distilled into its most recognizable everyday watches.

timeline.event: Kurono’s official site continues to feature the Classic Series as one of the brand’s main watch families.
The brand describes the Classic Series as the line that launched Hajime Asaoka’s vision for a more accessible timepiece.
Kurono’s current site still positions the Classic range as the reminder of the brand’s humble beginnings.

faqItems.question: When did the Classic Series begin?
faqItems.answer: Kurono’s first series, Bunkyo Tokyo, launched in June 2019 and is described by the brand as the start of its accessible watchmaking effort.

faqItems.question: What defines the Classic Series?
faqItems.answer: Simple, art-deco-inspired watches with a focus on legibility, proportion, and Asaoka’s signature design DNA.

referenceDetails.name: Bunkyo Tokyo
referenceDetails.note: The first-ever Kurono series, launched in June 2019 and tied to the accessible Classic lineage.

referenceDetails.name: Classic Series
referenceDetails.note: Brand collection page describing the accessible, art-deco-inspired core line.

referenceDetails.name: Classic Reiwa
referenceDetails.note: A Classic-series example introduced in December 2019, showing the line’s more refined two-part dial execution.

keyCollections.name: Grand Series
keyCollections.description: Kurono Tokyo’s Grand Series is the brand’s artisan-led flagship family, centered on urushi dials, complex finishing, and higher craft density while still aiming to remain attainable relative to traditional haute horlogerie and to showcase Hajime Asaoka’s most ambitious design and material work within Kurono.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Grand Series is Kurono’s clearest statement that accessible pricing and serious craft are not mutually exclusive: it packages lacquer work, special casebacks, and elevated finishing into the brand’s most prestigious collection.

timeline.event: Kurono states that the Grand Series masterpiece was first introduced only once in 2019.
Kurono released the 2024 Anniversary Reiwa as a Grand Series masterpiece and said the line would be retired after that launch.
The brand describes the Grand Series as its most demanding and complex collection in terms of traditional craftsmanship.

faqItems.question: What defines the Grand Series?
faqItems.answer: It focuses on artisan-level craft, especially urushi dials and distinctive finishing details.

faqItems.question: Is the Grand Series still active?
faqItems.answer: Kurono’s 2024 anniversary messaging said the Reiwa line would be retired after that release, while the Grand family remains the brand’s highest-craft showcase.

referenceDetails.name: Grand Akane
referenceDetails.note: Kurono’s first artisan-level timepiece, introduced in November 2020, with a hand-crafted urushi dial.

referenceDetails.name: Grand Series
referenceDetails.note: Official umbrella collection page describing the line as Kurono’s most demanding and complex collection.

referenceDetails.name: 2024 Anniversary Reiwa
referenceDetails.note: Grand Series masterpiece announced in 2024; brand said the Reiwa line would be permanently retired after this launch.

keyCollections.name: Complications Series
keyCollections.description: Kurono Tokyo’s Complications Series applies the brand’s art-deco vocabulary to mechanically more involved watches, pairing higher-function layouts with the same disciplined typography, polished finishing, and collector-friendly limited-production ethos that define the label’s more accessible line.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: It marks the point where Kurono expands beyond time-only formats while keeping the visual restraint and accessibility that made the brand distinctive, giving collectors a more functional but still highly legible design language.

timeline.event: The official collection page continues to define the series as art-deco inspired and function-forward.
Kurono’s site groups Complications as a main collection beside Classic and Grand, showing its strategic importance.
Recent Kurono launches continue to reinforce the brand’s use of complications as design-led collector pieces.

faqItems.question: What makes the Complications Series different?
faqItems.answer: It adds functions beyond simple time display while keeping Kurono’s clean, graphic design identity.

faqItems.question: Is it still limited-production?
faqItems.answer: Yes; Kurono’s watch families are generally released in limited runs and often sell out quickly.

referenceDetails.name: Complications Series
referenceDetails.note: Official collection page for Kurono’s complication-focused line.

referenceDetails.name: Chronograph 2
referenceDetails.note: A complication model that illustrates the series’ function-first approach with subdials and a more elaborate layout.

referenceDetails.name: Réserve de Marche Sensu N.O.S.
referenceDetails.note: Power-reserve complication example showing the series’ mechanical and visual complexity.

keyCollections.name: Special Projects
keyCollections.description: Kurono Tokyo’s Special Projects is the brand’s experimental lane for limited-run, more expressive interpretations of Hajime Asaoka’s Art Deco design language, often using unusual dial materials, custom typography, and one-off thematic ideas that sit apart from the core range.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is the collection where Kurono Tokyo signals design direction, collector scarcity, and material experimentation without leaving its accessible-indie identity.

referenceDetails.name: 37mm Inseki
referenceDetails.note: 2026 special project with a meteorite dial and white lacquer ring; limited production and not repeated.

referenceDetails.name: Anniversary Malachite
referenceDetails.note: 2026 special project on the brand site; a new anniversary-themed execution in the Special Projects line.

referenceDetails.name: 34mm Star Dial
referenceDetails.note: A recent Special Projects release referenced by independent watch coverage as part of the line’s continued evolution.

timeline.event: Kurono Tokyo continued the Special Projects cadence with the Calligra Special Project, reinforcing the line as a venue for limited-run, more characterful dial concepts.
The brand followed with additional Special Projects executions, including the Réserve de Marche / Sensu NOS variant discussed by watch media as a more expressive, limited interpretation.
The Special Projects label was used again for later limited releases, culminating in 2026 coverage of the Inseki meteorite edition.

faqItems.question: What makes Special Projects different from Kurono’s core collections?
faqItems.answer: It is the line for more experimental, limited-run designs that move beyond the standard catalog while still keeping Kurono’s compact proportions and Art Deco DNA.

faqItems.question: Are Special Projects watches repeated?
faqItems.answer: Typically no; recent coverage describes these as limited production pieces and, in some cases, not repeated.

timeline.event: Master independent watchmaker Hajime Asaoka launches Kurono Tokyo as a more accessible sister brand to his bespoke haute horlogerie work.
First releases sell out within minutes, establishing Kurono's reputation for extreme demand and limited availability.
Expands the collection with chronographs while maintaining the direct-to-consumer, limited-drop model.
Releases the Jubilee Sensu EOL 'Shiraai' in icy blue to celebrate founder Hajime Asaoka's 60th birthday.
Launches the radical crownless Diver's Watch with a watch-within-a-watch 35mm/46mm architecture ($2,700). Introduces the Special Projects 37mm Inseki with Muonionalusta meteorite dial.

faqItems.question: Who is behind Kurono Tokyo?
faqItems.answer: Hajime Asaoka, one of Japan's most respected independent watchmakers, created Kurono Tokyo as a more accessible brand while his main atelier produces bespoke haute horlogerie pieces.

faqItems.question: Why are Kurono watches so hard to buy?
faqItems.answer: Each release is extremely limited and sold direct-to-consumer through the Kurono website, often selling out within minutes of launch.

seoTitle: Kurono Tokyo - Hajime Asaoka Designed Japanese Watches | Watchatlas
seoDescription: Kurono Tokyo is Hajime Asaoka’s accessible Japanese watch line, known for Art Deco design, salon editions, Grand Series and complications.
whyMatters: Kurono Tokyo matters because it translates Hajime Asaoka’s independent Japanese watchmaking language into a more reachable format without losing the graphic restraint, dial nuance, and launch culture that made the brand globally collectible.
knownFor: Limited online releases and salon editions

name: L. Leroy
description: L. Leroy is one of France's most prestigious historic watchmaking houses, founded in 1785 and renowned for precision marine chronometers and complicated pocket watches that set records at international expositions. The revived brand continues the tradition of French fine watchmaking with modern mechanical timepieces.

keyCollections.name: Osmior
keyCollections.description: Osmior is L. Leroy’s flagship high-complication family, centered on traditional grand-watchmaking cues such as tourbillon-level finishing, enamel and precious-metal execution, and the brand’s long-standing chronometric authority expressed in a modern luxury format.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Osmior functions as the house’s prestige statement, anchoring L. Leroy’s contemporary identity in high complication craft, certification discipline, and museum-inspired design cues.

referenceDetails.name: Osmior single push-button chronograph
referenceDetails.note: Official manual names the Osmior line and explains its single-pusher chronograph architecture.

referenceDetails.name: Chronometer certification
referenceDetails.note: Official manual says each watch is checked at the National Observatory in Besançon and individually certified as a chronometer.

referenceDetails.name: Movement L411.1
referenceDetails.note: Official manual lists the movement specs, including 28,800 vph, column-wheel control, double barrel, and more than 48 hours of power reserve.

timeline.event: The Osmior manual identifies the single push-button chronograph as part of the line and links it to the brand’s private museum inspiration.
The same manual documents official chronometer certification through the National Observatory in Besançon.
The manual gives a detailed movement spec sheet for calibre L411.1, underscoring the line’s technical positioning.

faqItems.question: What kind of watches are in Osmior?
faqItems.answer: Osmior is the brand’s prestige family, with a focus on high-end mechanical watchmaking and a single-pusher chronograph example in the official documentation.

faqItems.question: Is Osmior connected to historical L. Leroy watches?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The manual says its watchmakers drew inspiration from exceptional timepieces in the brand’s private museum.

keyCollections.name: Marine
keyCollections.description: L. Leroy’s Marine line is a nautical-heritage collection inspired by the house’s long history as watchmaker to the French Navy, translating deck-chronometer language into modern wristwatches with a formal, maritime identity and certified precision focus.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Marine line is one of the clearest expressions of L. Leroy’s historical legitimacy: it ties present-day wristwatches to the company’s chronometer-making role for naval service and marine navigation.

referenceDetails.name: Ligne Marine
referenceDetails.note: Official collection page describes the Marine line and its historical naval inspiration.

referenceDetails.name: Marine automatic chronograph
referenceDetails.note: Official instructions explain the Marine automatic chronograph and its sea-chronometer inspiration.

referenceDetails.name: Marine automatic deck chronometer
referenceDetails.note: Official instructions explain the deck chronometer variant and its Besançon certification path.

timeline.event: The official collection page describes Marine as a contemporary line built to perpetuate the brand’s naval chronometry tradition.
The Marine chronograph manual states that the design was inspired by deck chronometers used by sailors.
The Marine deck chronometer manual states each watch is checked at the Observatory of Besançon and certified as a chronometer.

faqItems.question: What is the Marine collection based on?
faqItems.answer: It is based on L. Leroy’s historical role as watchmaker to the French Navy and on the visual language of deck chronometers.

faqItems.question: Does Marine have certified chronometer variants?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The official manual says the deck chronometer version is individually certified after Besançon checks.

keyCollections.name: Chronograph Monopoussoir
keyCollections.description: Single-pusher chronograph collection showcasing traditional French chronometric precision in a refined case design.

timeline.event: Basile Charles Le Roy founds L. Leroy in Paris, establishing a dynasty of French horologists.
Appointed official chronometer maker to the French Navy, cementing the brand's reputation for precision.
Creates the Leroy 01, then the most complicated watch in the world with 24 complications, showcased at the Paris Exposition.
Brand is revived by Miguel Rodriguez, re-establishing production and continuing the tradition of French haute horlogerie.

faqItems.question: What is L. Leroy's historical significance in watchmaking?
faqItems.answer: Founded in 1785, L. Leroy served as the official chronometer maker to the French Navy and created the Leroy 01 in 1900 — then the world's most complicated watch with 24 complications.

faqItems.question: Where is L. Leroy based today?
faqItems.answer: L. Leroy is headquartered in Bienne, Switzerland, continuing its tradition of French-rooted haute horlogerie with Swiss craftsmanship.

faqItems.question: What are L. Leroy's main collections?
faqItems.answer: The brand's key collections include the Osmior (tourbillons and grand complications), the Marine (inspired by naval chronometer heritage), and the Chronograph Monopoussoir (single-pusher chronographs).

faqItems.question: Is L. Leroy an independent brand?
faqItems.answer: Yes, L. Leroy operates as an independent watchmaker. The brand was revived in 2004 by Miguel Rodriguez and continues to produce limited-series luxury timepieces.

faqItems.question: What is the price range for L. Leroy watches?
faqItems.answer: L. Leroy watches are positioned in the luxury segment, with prices typically ranging from CHF 20,000 to over CHF 100,000 for their tourbillon and grand complication models.

name: Laco
description: Laco is a German watch brand founded in 1925 by Lacher & Co. in Pforzheim, Germany. One of five manufacturers selected by the German Luftwaffe in World War II to produce the standardised B-Uhr pilot watch, Laco today produces faithful re-editions of these historic pilot watches alongside modern aviator and sport models.

keyCollections.name: Flieger
keyCollections.description: Laco’s signature pilot-watch family, rooted in historic instrument-watch design and built around the brand’s long aviation heritage with highly legible dials and classic tool-watch proportions.

keyCollections.name: Squad
keyCollections.description: Laco’s professional tool-watch collection for demanding conditions, emphasizing rugged construction, extreme reliability, and practical details such as strong water resistance and functional legibility.

keyCollections.name: Classics
keyCollections.description: Laco’s Bauhaus-influenced dress collection focused on simple geometry, clean readability, and restrained German design, offering elegant everyday watches that emphasize form, function, and heritage.

timeline.event: Frieda Lacher and Ludwig Hummel found Lacher & Co. (Laco) in Pforzheim, Germany.
Selected as one of only five manufacturers to produce B-Uhr pilot's watches for the German Luftwaffe during World War II.
Factory severely damaged during Allied bombing of Pforzheim; production slowly resumes post-war.
Laco re-establishes itself as a heritage pilot's watch brand, reviving its historic Flieger designs for modern collectors.
Celebrates its 100th anniversary with the #restoremylaco campaign and a limited-edition Mission 2025 collection of 100 pieces inspired by a 1950s Laco design.

faqItems.question: What is a B-Uhr?
faqItems.answer: Beobachtungsuhr (observation watch) — large pilot's watches made to Luftwaffe specifications during WWII. Only five companies were authorised to produce them, and Laco was one.

faqItems.question: Where is Laco based?
faqItems.answer: Pforzheim, Germany — a historic centre of German watchmaking and precision manufacturing since the 18th century.

name: Laine
description: Laine is an independent watch brand occupying the artisanal end of the watchmaking spectrum, producing timepieces in limited quantities with a focus on craft and design.

keyCollections.name: V38
keyCollections.description: Laine’s V38 is the brand’s compact 38mm hand-finished dress-watch line, pairing hand-turned guilloché dials, a slim case, and a heavily finished Vaucher base movement for collectors who want the Laine aesthetic in a smaller, more wearable format.

referenceDetails.name: V38 guilloche
referenceDetails.note: Core guilloché configuration for the 38mm line.

referenceDetails.name: V38 triple guilloche
referenceDetails.note: Variant listed on the official V38 page.

referenceDetails.name: V38 Moonfrosting
referenceDetails.note: Named dial option on the official V38 page.

timeline.event: Official V38 product page highlights the 38mm collection and its guilloché-based variants.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The V38 makes Laine’s artisanal finishing more accessible in size terms while keeping the brand’s signature hand-work, so it serves as a gateway model within the collection.

faqItems.question: What movement does the V38 use?
faqItems.answer: The official page says the V38 is powered by a Vaucher 5401 base with extensive finishing work.

faqItems.question: What is the case size?
faqItems.answer: The V38 is presented as a 38mm watch on the official product page.

keyCollections.name: Geomar.1
keyCollections.description: Vintage-inspired dive watch with a clean, Scandinavian-influenced design and reliable mechanical movement.

timeline.event: Torsti Laine, a Finnish watchmaker, founds Laine in Finland, producing hand-finished mechanical watches with Nordic design sensibility.
V38 gains recognition in the independent watch community for its value and hand-finishing quality.
Launches the Geomar.1 dive watch, expanding beyond dress watches while maintaining the brand's artisanal ethos.
Releases the V38 Seitsemäs, a 38mm hand-wound dress watch with sector dial, continuing its Finnish-designed, micro-brand ethos.

faqItems.question: Where are Laine watches made?
faqItems.answer: Designed and assembled in Finland by founder Torsti Laine, using Swiss movements that are hand-finished and decorated in-house.

faqItems.question: What makes Laine special?
faqItems.answer: Exceptional hand-finishing at an accessible price point, produced by a single watchmaker in Finland — offering independent watchmaking quality without the typical premium.

name: Lang & Heyne
description: Lang & Heyne is a micro-manufacture founded in Dresden in 2001 by Marco Lang and Mirko Heyne, producing watches in tiny quantities — often fewer than 50 pieces per year — with movement components made entirely in-house. The brand is revered within the independent watchmaking community for the extraordinary quality of its movement finishing.

keyCollections.name: Friedrich August I
keyCollections.description: Signature large-format wristwatch named after the Saxon ruler, featuring a distinctive three-quarter plate movement with hand-engraved balance cock.

keyCollections.name: Augustus I
keyCollections.description: Elegant time-only watch with a sector dial, named after August the Strong, showcasing the brand's obsessive hand-finishing.

keyCollections.name: König Johann
keyCollections.description: Complication watch named after King Johann of Saxony, featuring a power reserve indicator and the brand's hallmark Dresden finishing.

timeline.event: Marco Lang and Mirko Heyne found Lang & Heyne in Dresden, Germany, reviving Saxon watchmaking traditions.
Mirko Heyne departs (joining Nomos Glashütte), but the company name is retained.
Marco Lang is accepted as a member of the AHCI, recognising his mastery as an independent watchmaker.
Brand produces around 50 watches per year, with all models named after rulers from the Fürstenzug mural in Dresden.
Debuts the Friedrich August III with a jumping hour and retrograde minute display, reinforcing its position as one of the finest German ateliers.

faqItems.question: Why are Lang & Heyne watches named after rulers?
faqItems.answer: Each model is named after a ruler depicted in the Fürstenzug, a famous 19th-century mural in Dresden showing the rulers of Saxony. Founder Marco Lang visits the mural upon completing each new design.

faqItems.question: How many watches does Lang & Heyne produce?
faqItems.answer: Approximately 50 watches per year, each extensively hand-finished in their Dresden workshop with techniques inspired by Saxon horological traditions.

name: Laurent Ferrier
description: Laurent Ferrier founded his eponymous brand in Geneva in 2010 after a distinguished career at Patek Philippe spanning over three decades. The brand produces a small number of beautifully restrained watches each year, prized by collectors for their exceptional movement finishing and understated classical design.

keyCollections.name: Galet
keyCollections.description: Signature collection with pebble-shaped cases, available in Classic, Square, and Micro-Rotor variants, embodying restrained elegance and exceptional finishing.

keyCollections.name: Sport Auto
keyCollections.description: Sporty interpretation of the Galet in a cushion case with a racing-inspired aesthetic, nodding to Laurent Ferrier's career as a Le Mans racing driver.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Sport Auto is Laurent Ferrier’s integrated-bracelet sports-watch idea, linking the brand’s soft case language to Laurent Ferrier’s racing biography rather than copying the usual Gerald Genta template.

image.source: Laurent Ferrier official Sport Auto 40 page

referenceDetails.name: Original Sport Auto
referenceDetails.note: Blue-dial titanium Sport Auto that established the line.

image.source: Laurent Ferrier official Sport Auto Blue page

referenceDetails.name: Serie Atelier V Sport Auto 40
referenceDetails.note: A 40 mm Sport Auto expression within Laurent Ferrier’s atelier series.

image.source: Laurent Ferrier official Sport Auto 40 page

referenceDetails.name: Sport Auto 79
referenceDetails.note: Gold-toned Sport Auto variant tied to the brand’s racing memory.

timeline.event: Laurent Ferrier introduces Sport Auto as a sporty titanium expression of the brand’s design language.
Sport Auto 40 brings the line into the Serie Atelier format.
Sport Auto 79 extends the family with a racing-memory variant.
