newsItems.summary: The official product page supplies current imagery and reference context for Sport Auto 40.

newsItems.title: Sport Auto Blue remains documented by Laurent Ferrier
newsItems.summary: The official product page anchors the original blue-dial Sport Auto branch.

faqItems.question: What is Laurent Ferrier Sport Auto?
faqItems.answer: Sport Auto is Laurent Ferrier’s sporty cushion-case integrated-bracelet line.

faqItems.question: Why is Sport Auto tied to racing?
faqItems.answer: It nods to Laurent Ferrier’s history as a Le Mans racing driver.

keyCollections.name: Classic Origin
keyCollections.description: Entry point to the brand featuring a hand-wound movement with sector dial, offering Laurent Ferrier's hallmark finishing at a more accessible level.

timeline.event: Laurent Ferrier, after 37 years at Patek Philippe, founds his eponymous brand in Geneva with racing partner François Servanin.
Wins the GPHG Men's Watch Prize with the Galet Classic Tourbillon Double Spiral at the brand's debut.
Wins the GPHG Horological Revelation Prize for the Galet Square.
Wins the GPHG Men's Complication Prize, establishing Laurent Ferrier as a serial award winner.
Introduces the Sport Auto 40 in new dial variants and wins GPHG recognition for the École collection. Opens a new atelier space in Geneva to expand production capacity.

faqItems.question: What did Laurent Ferrier do before founding his brand?
faqItems.answer: He spent 37 years at Patek Philippe, reaching the rank of technical director. He also worked on the prototype of the Genta-designed Nautilus and raced at Le Mans, finishing 3rd in 1979.

faqItems.question: What defines a Laurent Ferrier watch?
faqItems.answer: Understated elegance, exceptional hand-finishing, and the signature 'Galet' (pebble) case shape. The brand favours subtle sophistication over overt complexity.

name: Lebois & Co
description: Founded in 1934, Lebois & Co is an independent Swiss watch brand committed to combining traditional watchmaking expertise with bold, contemporary design. The brand produces mechanical timepieces that honour Swiss craft heritage while engaging with the progressive aesthetics of the modern independent watch scene.

keyCollections.name: Avantgarde Date
keyCollections.description: Core collection reviving the brand's 1930s heritage with a clean, vintage-inspired date watch featuring sector dials and domed crystals.

keyCollections.name: Heritage Chronograph
keyCollections.description: Heritage Chronograph is Lebois & Co’s main modern chronograph family, translating the brand’s 1930s and 1940s inspirations into a broad, collector-facing lineup of vintage-led references with sector, numeral, script, baton, and more recent craft-forward interpretations.

referenceDetails.name: Script Chronograph 324.406
referenceDetails.note: Official current product page for the Script variant, part of the Heritage Chronograph family.

referenceDetails.name: Sector Chronograph 324.442
referenceDetails.note: Official product page describing a disciplined 1930s design language translated into a modern collector’s chronograph.

referenceDetails.name: Numeral Chronograph 324.497
referenceDetails.note: Official product page referencing the Christie’s timepiece that sparked the brand’s revival; current Heritage Chronograph variant.

timeline.event: Lebois & Co’s official about page says the Heritage Chronograph prototypes were revealed in 2022, marking the modern project’s public debut.
The brand positions Heritage Chronograph as a revival inspired by 1930s and 1940s Lebois chronographs.
Current product pages show the family expanding into named variants such as Script, Sector, Numeral, and Linéaire, confirming the collection’s breadth.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Heritage Chronograph matters because it is the central expression of Lebois & Co’s revival strategy: historically grounded, enthusiast-shaped, and broad enough to support multiple dial languages while staying anchored in one chronograph identity.

timeline.event: Lebois & Co. originally established in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, producing quality timepieces.
Thomas Baillod revives the dormant Lebois & Co. brand, honouring its heritage with modern reinterpretations.
Successfully launches the Avantgarde Date via crowdfunding, establishing a loyal collector following.
Launches the Venturist Chronograph with a Sellita SW510 movement, expanding beyond dive and dress watches.

faqItems.question: Is Lebois & Co. a new brand?
faqItems.answer: Originally founded in 1934, the brand was dormant for decades before being revived in 2014 by Thomas Baillod, who reinterprets the original heritage for modern collectors.

faqItems.question: Where is Lebois & Co. based?
faqItems.answer: La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland — one of the traditional centres of Swiss watchmaking.

name: Lederer
description: Lederer is an independent watchmaking atelier founded in 1986 by Bernhard Lederer, whose 40-year experimental approach fuses rigorous mechanical science with horological history inspired by Breguet and George Daniels. The house is best known for its patented Dual Detent Escapement with twin remontoirs d'égalité, crafted entirely in-house with hand-finished movements of exceptional precision.

keyCollections.name: Central Impulse Chronometer
keyCollections.description: The brand's signature piece featuring a patented central impulse escapement visible on the dial, combining 18th-century horological theory with modern execution.

timeline.event: Bernhard Lederer, a German-born master watchmaker based in Switzerland, founds Lederer to pursue his vision of a central impulse chronometer.
Debuts the Central Impulse Chronometer, featuring a patented escapement delivering impulse directly to the balance wheel.
Wins widespread acclaim from horological experts for the innovation and finishing of the Central Impulse Chronometer.
Presents the Central Impulse Chronometer Model C at Watches & Wonders, continuing to develop proprietary high-precision escapement technology.

faqItems.question: What is Lederer's central impulse escapement?
faqItems.answer: A patented mechanism that delivers energy directly to the centre of the balance wheel rather than via a lever, inspired by 18th-century clockmaking principles and resulting in more consistent timekeeping.

faqItems.question: How many watches does Lederer produce?
faqItems.answer: Extremely limited — Bernhard Lederer works as a solo independent watchmaker, producing only a handful of pieces each year.

name: Leica
description: Leica, the legendary German optics company, produces a small range of watches in partnership with Swiss manufacturers, applying its precision engineering philosophy to horology. The watches reflect Leica's Bauhaus-influenced design language — minimal, functional, and precisely executed.

keyCollections.name: ZM
keyCollections.description: Leica’s ZM collection is the brand’s watchmaking line, led by the ZM 1 and ZM 2, and defined by a camera-inspired design language, a patented push-crown time-setting system, and made-in-Germany mechanical execution.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: The ZM line extends Leica’s visual and engineering identity from cameras into horology, turning brand heritage into a distinctive modern mechanical-watch platform.

timeline.event: Leica continued to present the ZM 1 and ZM 2 family as its core watch collection on the official watch pages.
The brand expanded the line with Urban Green variants while keeping the same ZM platform and technical architecture.
Leica’s watch pages describe the ZM models as limited-production, Made in Germany timepieces.

referenceDetails.name: Leica ZM 1
referenceDetails.note: Five-function hand-wound model with the patented push-crown and Leica-inspired design cues.

referenceDetails.name: Leica ZM 2
referenceDetails.note: Seven-function version adding GMT and day/night indication.

referenceDetails.name: Leica ZM 2 Monochrom
referenceDetails.note: Black PVD monochrome execution of the ZM 2 concept.

faqItems.question: What does ZM stand for?
faqItems.answer: Leica uses ZM as the watch collection name for its mechanical watch line centered on the ZM 1 and ZM 2.

faqItems.question: What makes the ZM line distinctive?
faqItems.answer: Its camera-inspired push-crown, Made in Germany construction, and Leica design language distinguish it from conventional dress or tool watches.

timeline.event: Ernst Leitz founds the optical company in Wetzlar, Germany, that would become Leica.
Launches the Leica I camera, revolutionising photography with the 35mm format.
Enters the watchmaking market with the L1 and L2 watches, later renamed ZM 1 and ZM 2, designed and manufactured in Germany.
Expands the L-series watch line with the L2, featuring a titanium case and Leica-designed dial inspired by classic rangefinder cameras.

faqItems.question: Does Leica make watches?
faqItems.answer: Yes — Leica entered watchmaking in 2018 with the ZM series, precision mechanical watches designed in-house in Germany with the same optical-engineering philosophy that drives their cameras.

faqItems.question: What does Leica's name mean?
faqItems.answer: LEItz CAmera — derived from founder Ernst Leitz's surname combined with 'camera.' The company originated in optical instruments before expanding to photography and watches.

name: Lic-Leather
description: Artisanal brand combining fine leather craftsmanship with watchmaking, producing bespoke straps and leather watch accessories alongside its own timepiece collection. Lic-Leather serves collectors who value the harmony between a beautifully made watch and an equally fine strap.

keyCollections.name: Classic Strap Collection
keyCollections.description: Handmade leather watch straps crafted in Switzerland using premium hides, available in various styles from vintage to contemporary.

timeline.event: LIC Leather established in Switzerland, specialising in handmade luxury leather watch straps and accessories.

faqItems.question: What does LIC Leather make?
faqItems.answer: Handmade premium leather watch straps and accessories, crafted in Switzerland with attention to material quality and finishing.

faqItems.question: Is LIC Leather a watch brand?
faqItems.answer: LIC Leather is primarily an accessory brand specialising in watch straps rather than complete watches.

name: Linde Werdelin
description: Linde Werdelin was founded in 2002 by Danes Morten Linde and Jorn Werdelin, combining high-horology craftsmanship with instrument-grade tool-watch design for extreme adventure sports. Known for its Oktopus and Spido collections, the brand uniquely bridges Danish design ethos with Swiss movement expertise.

keyCollections.name: SpidoLite
keyCollections.description: SpidoLite is Linde Werdelin's lightweight, skeletonised sports-watch family, using open-worked architecture, titanium or carbon variants, and adventure-focused design language.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: SpidoLite is one of the clearest expressions of Linde Werdelin's design philosophy: reduce mass, preserve robustness, and expose the mechanics through a distinctive case architecture.

referenceDetails.name: SpidoLite Titanium - 3D Movement
referenceDetails.note: Official SpidoLite Titanium page describes the line's lightweight open-worked case concept and titanium construction.

referenceDetails.name: SpidoLite Nord
referenceDetails.note: Official SpidoLite Nord product page identifies the Nord as a limited-edition titanium execution in the SpidoLite family.

referenceDetails.name: SpidoLite 3DTP Carbon - 3D Movement
referenceDetails.note: Official Spido collection page lists the 3DTP Carbon variant as part of the SpidoLite family.

timeline.event: The official Spido page presents SpidoLite as an active collection alongside SpidoSpeed.
The brand describes SpidoLite as originating from an Everest-inspired quest for a lighter yet durable watch.
Current product pages continue to emphasize titanium construction, custom movements, and skeletonised execution.

faqItems.question: What makes SpidoLite different from a typical sports watch?
faqItems.answer: Its defining trait is the heavily weight-optimised, open-worked case architecture rather than a conventional solid sports case.

faqItems.question: Which materials are associated with SpidoLite?
faqItems.answer: The official lineup emphasizes lightweight materials and constructions such as titanium and carbon executions.

keyCollections.name: Oktopus
keyCollections.description: Professional dive watch rated to 1,000 metres, designed to pair with Linde Werdelin's digital diving instrument.

keyCollections.name: 3-Timer
keyCollections.description: Multi-timezone GMT watch built for adventure travel, combining three time zone displays in a robust sports case.

timeline.event: Morten Linde and Jorn Werdelin found the brand in Denmark, born from a skiing accident that inspired a watch-plus-instrument concept.
First watch collection goes to market after five years of R&D on the watch-plus-instrument platform.
Linde Werdelin watches used on the first confirmed free climb to the summit of Mount Everest.
Launches the SpidoLite, which becomes the brand's most iconic skeletonised sports watch.
Returns with a limited-edition SpidoLite II in carbon-composite case, marking a renewed focus after a quieter period, targeting adventure-sport enthusiasts.

faqItems.question: What makes Linde Werdelin unique?
faqItems.answer: They pioneered the concept of high-end mechanical watches that can be paired with clip-on digital instruments for skiing and diving — the only luxury brand to do so.

faqItems.question: Where is Linde Werdelin from?
faqItems.answer: Founded by two Danes (Morten Linde and Jorn Werdelin) with headquarters in London and Copenhagen. Watches are made in Switzerland.

name: Löbner
description: LÖBNER is the German benchmark in the measurement of short times and records. Its rich history, dating back generations of precision-instrument making in Germany, informs a contemporary collection of sport and timing watches that embody Teutonic rigor — functional, precise and built to endure.

keyCollections.name: Intemporal
keyCollections.description: Debut collection featuring clean Bauhaus-inspired design with a distinctive domed dial and slender case, representing a modern German design philosophy.

timeline.event: Clemens Löbner founds the brand in Germany, aiming to create minimalist watches inspired by Bauhaus design principles.
Launches the Intemporal collection, gaining attention for its restrained aesthetic and quality finishing.

faqItems.question: What is Löbner's design philosophy?
faqItems.answer: Minimalist, Bauhaus-inspired design focused on clean lines, domed dials, and restrained elegance — quintessentially German in approach.

faqItems.question: Where is Löbner based?
faqItems.answer: Germany, continuing the country's tradition of precision engineering and functional design in watchmaking.

name: Longines
description: Founded in Saint-Imier in 1832, Longines is a Swiss watch brand associated with the winged-hourglass logo, which the brand dates to 1889. Now part of the Swatch Group, it produces elegant sports and heritage watches and maintains a presence in equestrian sport and tennis.

keyCollections.name: Spirit
keyCollections.description: Longines Spirit is the brand's modern pilot-inspired family, built around explorer imagery, chronometer credentials, GMT utility, and clean aviation-watch clarity.

referenceDetails.name: Longines Spirit L3.410.4.93.6

Spirit Zulu Time extends the line into GMT and dual-time use.
Spirit Zulu Time 1925 marks the centenary of Longines dual-time watch history.
Spirit Pilot and Spirit Pilot Flyback expand the collection's technical flight-watch branch.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Spirit gives Longines a credible modern aviation family, translating the brand's historical pilot and explorer associations into a clean contemporary tool-watch language.

faqItems.question: What is Spirit trying to capture?
faqItems.answer: It is Longines' modern pilot-watch family, framed around explorers, flight, and chronometer precision.

faqItems.question: When did Spirit launch?
faqItems.answer: The collection debuted in 2020.

faqItems.question: What is Zulu Time?
faqItems.answer: It is Longines' GMT or dual-time branch inside the Spirit family.

faqItems.question: How does Spirit differ from HydroConquest?
faqItems.answer: Spirit is aviation-led and chronometer-minded; HydroConquest is the dive-watch platform.

funFacts.title: Explorer story
funFacts.body: Longines built Spirit around historic pilots and explorers rather than pure aviation nostalgia.

funFacts.title: Chronometer focus
funFacts.body: The line is strongly associated with chronometer certification and everyday precision.

keyCollections.name: HydroConquest
keyCollections.description: Longines HydroConquest is the brand's core dive collection: practical, modern, and aimed at buyers who want a capable sports watch with broad mainstream appeal.

referenceDetails.name: HydroConquest L3.779.4.90.6

timeline.event: Longines launches HydroConquest as its modern dive-watch line.
A ceramic-bezel refresh sharpens the collection's tool-watch appeal.
HydroConquest GMT brings the line into dual-time territory.
Longines continues to use HydroConquest as an event-ready sports platform.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: HydroConquest is Longines' benchmark sports diver, combining real capability, broad availability, and the brand's strongest accessible mechanical sports-watch proposition.

newsItems.title: HydroConquest collection
newsItems.summary: Official Longines collection material for the modern dive line.

faqItems.question: Is HydroConquest Longines' main diver?
faqItems.answer: Yes. It is the core dive-watch family in the modern Longines catalog.

faqItems.question: When did HydroConquest launch?
faqItems.answer: The collection debuted in 2007.

faqItems.question: Does HydroConquest come with GMT?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Longines added GMT variants to give the line travel-watch usefulness.

faqItems.question: What is the appeal of HydroConquest?
faqItems.answer: It offers serious sports-watch capability without leaving Longines' mainstream value proposition.

funFacts.title: Gateway diver
funFacts.body: HydroConquest is often the first mechanical dive watch many Longines buyers consider.

funFacts.title: 2007 debut
funFacts.body: The line is modern enough to feel current but established enough to be a staple.

funFacts.title: GMT came later
funFacts.body: The dual-time version broadened the collection beyond diving alone.

funFacts.title: Ceramic helped
funFacts.body: The ceramic-bezel generation gave HydroConquest more visual bite and durability.

keyCollections.name: Master Collection
keyCollections.description: Longines’ Master Collection is the brand’s enduring classic-mechanical dress line, pairing restrained styling with moonphase, annual calendar, chronograph, and other refined complications across a broad range of case sizes.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is the core Longines dress-complication family: it concentrates the brand’s elegant, heritage-led identity in a highly readable, broadly merchandised collection that sits squarely in the accessible-luxury sweet spot.

The collection is framed by Longines as the embodiment of horological craftsmanship and timeless elegance.
Current references showcase complications and modern mechanical specs, including silicon balance-springs and long power reserves.

faqItems.question: What kind of watches are in the Master Collection?
faqItems.answer: Primarily elegant automatic dress watches, including date models and more complicated variants such as moonphase and calendar executions.

faqItems.question: Where does it sit in Longines’ lineup?
faqItems.answer: It is one of Longines’ core classic-mechanical families and is positioned for customers seeking traditional styling and strong value.

image.alt: Longines Master Collection watch worn on the wrist

keyCollections.name: Heritage
keyCollections.description: Longines Heritage is the brand’s vintage-inspired pillar, grouping re-editions and historically rooted designs that reinterpret 1930s to 1950s Longines models with contemporary mechanical watchmaking and faithful design cues.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Heritage is one of Longines’ most important positioning pillars because it connects the brand’s deep archive to current commercial collections, giving the company a clear historical narrative across multiple sub-families.

referenceDetails.name: Heritage pillar
referenceDetails.note: Official Heritage landing page describes the pillar as confirming the brand’s legacy and grouping heritage-derived product families.

referenceDetails.name: Heritage Classic

referenceDetails.name: Flagship Heritage
referenceDetails.note: Official page states Flagship has been an emblematic line since the late 1950s and ties it to the gold medallion caravel caseback.

timeline.event: The current Heritage pillar page lists active sub-lines including Legend Diver, Ultra-Chron, Pilot Majetek, Conquest Heritage, Flagship Heritage, Avigation, and Heritage Classic.
Heritage Classic is presented as drawing on 1930s and 1940s Longines models.
Conquest Heritage is presented as a tribute to the original Conquest models first protected in 1954.

faqItems.question: What does Longines Heritage cover?
faqItems.answer: It groups vintage-inspired collections and re-editions that reinterpret earlier Longines designs.

faqItems.question: Is Heritage a single watch model?
faqItems.answer: No. It is a broader pillar containing several heritage-led lines such as Heritage Classic and Flagship Heritage.

timeline.event: Auguste Agassiz establishes a watch trading business in Saint-Imier, Switzerland, which becomes Longines.
Longines' history includes the Lindbergh Hour Angle Watch, developed in association with Charles Lindbergh.
Longines becomes part of the Swatch Group.

faqItems.question: What does the Longines logo represent?
faqItems.answer: Longines uses a winged hourglass as its logo.

faqItems.question: Which group owns Longines?
faqItems.answer: Longines is part of the Swatch Group.

name: Lorier

hq.address: 215 W 104th St, Unit 1409, New York, NY 10025

description: Lorier is an American independent watch brand founded in 2015 by Lauren Katz and Lorenzo Ortega in New York City. Known for vintage-inspired dive watches at accessible price points, the Neptune series references mid-century diver aesthetics with modern Swiss movements.

keyCollections.name: Neptune
keyCollections.description: Lorier’s Neptune is the brand’s flagship vintage-inspired dive watch line, pairing compact proportions and rotating bezel styling with a Swiss automatic movement and multiple colourway options at an accessible entry-level price point.

keyCollections.name: Falcon
keyCollections.description: Lorier’s ruggedly elegant field watch, shaped by mid-century explorer aesthetics and balanced proportions, with a compact 36mm case, strong lume, and a distinctly vintage tool-watch personality.

keyCollections.name: Fox
keyCollections.description: A bold sport watch with a larger case and robust construction, aimed at enthusiasts seeking wearable, value-driven mechanical timepieces.

keyCollections.name: Gemini
keyCollections.description: Lorier’s compact vintage-style chronograph line, inspired by space-race-era design cues and positioned as an approachable mechanical chronograph with a classic, wearable profile.

timeline.event: Lauren Katz and Lorenzo Ortega co-found Lorier in New York City, aiming to offer vintage-inspired watches at accessible prices.
The Neptune dive watch launches to immediate acclaim in the online watch enthusiast community, establishing Lorier's design identity.
Lorier expands its line-up with the Falcon field watch, broadening its appeal beyond dive-watch fans.
The brand releases limited-edition colourways and collaborations, cementing its status as a cult favourite in the affordable-watch community.
Releases the Gemini III automatic chronograph in updated colourways, and introduces a new Zephyr field watch collection, with both models selling out rapidly.

faqItems.question: Where are Lorier watches made?
faqItems.answer: Lorier watches are designed in New York City and use Swiss-made movements, assembled to deliver reliable, vintage-inspired timepieces at accessible price points.

faqItems.question: What makes Lorier different from other affordable watch brands?
faqItems.answer: Lorier focuses on authentic vintage aesthetics — particularly 1960s and 70s dive-watch references — combined with quality Swiss movements, creating watches that appeal to both new collectors and seasoned enthusiasts.

name: Lorige
description: Lorige is a watch brand inspired by its founders' motorsport universe. As an innovative brand, Lorige creates dynamic sport watches that channel the adrenaline of circuit racing — bold case shapes, technical dials and mechanical precision that speak directly to enthusiasts of both haute horlogerie and high-speed competition.

keyCollections.name: Racing Sport
keyCollections.description: Lorige's core motorsport-inspired collection, featuring bold dials, chronograph complications and technical detailing that evoke the adrenaline of circuit racing.

keyCollections.name: Circuit
keyCollections.description: A dynamic sport watch series drawing on racetrack aesthetics — contrasting colours, legible displays and robust Swiss movements built for the fast lane.

timeline.event: Lorige is founded in Switzerland by motorsport enthusiasts, with a vision to bring racing aesthetics into haute horlogerie.
The brand launches its first flagship collection, blending Swiss mechanical precision with bold, competition-inspired design.
Lorige expands its presence at international watch fairs, gaining recognition among sport-watch collectors.
Debuts the Immatériel with a flying tourbillon in a lightweight titanium-ceramic case, continuing its high-complication, low-volume approach.

faqItems.question: What inspires Lorige's designs?
faqItems.answer: Lorige draws inspiration from motorsport — circuit racing, the instruments of race cars, and the culture of speed — translating these into dynamic, technically sophisticated Swiss timepieces.

faqItems.question: Are Lorige watches Swiss-made?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Lorige is a Swiss watch brand that uses quality Swiss movements and adheres to the standards of Swiss watchmaking craftsmanship.

name: Louis Erard
description: Louis Erard is an independent Swiss watch brand founded in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1929 as a watchmaking school. Production moved to Le Noirmont in 1991. Known for classically styled watches at accessible mid-range price points, the brand has attracted attention through collaborations with prominent figures including Alain Silberstein and Vianney Halter.

hq.address: Rue de l'Ouest 2, 2340 Le Noirmont, Switzerland

keyCollections.name: Noirmont
keyCollections.description: Louis Erard Noirmont gathers the brand's classic small-seconds and regulator watches, using restrained dials, Jura references, and accessible mechanical executions.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Noirmont is the clearest expression of Louis Erard's house style: independent Swiss watchmaking, regulator and small-seconds displays, and strong value without chasing conventional luxury-brand codes.

faqItems.question: What kind of collection is Louis Erard Noirmont?
faqItems.answer: It is a core Louis Erard family built around small-seconds and regulator watches with classic mechanical-watch proportions.

faqItems.question: Why are regulators important to Noirmont?
faqItems.answer: The regulator display is one of Louis Erard's signature formats, separating time indications into a more architectural dial layout.

faqItems.question: Which official Noirmont models are shown here?

faqItems.question: What is Louis Erard Noirmont X?
faqItems.answer: It is Louis Erard's collaboration-focused collection, using the brand's regulator and small-seconds formats as platforms for outside creative partners.

faqItems.question: Which collaborators appear in Noirmont X?
faqItems.answer: Official current examples include collaborations with GoS, KUDOKE, Alain Silberstein, Konstantin Chaykin, Vianney Halter, and others.

faqItems.question: Why does Noirmont X matter?
faqItems.answer: It lets Louis Erard offer independent-watchmaking personality and artist-led design at a more approachable price position than many bespoke collaborations.

keyCollections.name: Noirmont Métiers d'Art
keyCollections.description: Louis Erard Noirmont Métiers d'Art is the brand's craft-focused collection, gathering enamel, hand engraving, guilloché, marquetry, stone dials, and artist collaborations under its accessible fine-watchmaking strategy.
keyReferences: Fil d'Or Louis Erard x Wire Art

referenceDetails.reference: Fil d'Or Louis Erard x Wire Art
referenceDetails.name: Fil d'Or Louis Erard x Wire Art
referenceDetails.note: Louis Erard's official product copy describes Fil d'Or as a Wire Art collaboration that turns wire craft into a new artistic watchmaking decoration.

image.alt: Louis Erard Fil d'Or Louis Erard x Wire Art watch

referenceDetails.name: Louis Erard Gravée Main
referenceDetails.note: Louis Erard's official product copy says Gravée Main marks a new milestone in its Métiers d'Art series, with hand engraving across case, bezel, lugs, crown, and buckle.

referenceDetails.name: Émail Grand Feu II
referenceDetails.note: Louis Erard's official product copy frames Émail Grand Feu II as a return to Grand Feu enamel, noting kiln firing above 800 degrees Celsius and limited dial production capacity.

image.alt: Louis Erard Émail Grand Feu II watch

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Noirmont Métiers d'Art gives Louis Erard a clear craft platform, turning techniques usually associated with much higher price tiers into repeatable limited-series watches that still fit the brand's accessible independent identity.

image.alt: Louis Erard Fil d'Or Louis Erard x Wire Art watch

gallery.alt: Louis Erard Émail Grand Feu II watch

faqItems.question: What is Louis Erard Noirmont Métiers d'Art?
faqItems.answer: It is Louis Erard's craft-focused collection, with official examples spanning wire art, hand engraving, Grand Feu enamel, guilloché, stone dials, and related métiers d'art executions.

faqItems.question: Which official Noirmont Métiers d'Art models are shown here?
faqItems.answer: The page uses official Louis Erard examples including Fil d'Or Louis Erard x Wire Art, Louis Erard Gravée Main, and Émail Grand Feu II.

funFacts.title: Hand engraving focus
funFacts.body: Louis Erard's official Gravée Main copy says every metal element is hand-engraved and finished, including the case, bezel, lugs, crown, and buckle.

funFacts.title: Enamel difficulty
funFacts.body: The official Émail Grand Feu II copy says the enamel colours are fired in a kiln at more than 800 degrees Celsius.

keyCollections.description: Louis Erard 2340 is the brand's integrated-bracelet family, named after the Le Noirmont postal code and positioned as a foundational modern line rather than a limited-edition release.

referenceDetails.name: Louis Erard 2340 Mint
referenceDetails.note: Official product data identifies this as a Mint-dial 2340 and describes the family as Louis Erard's first watch with an integrated bracelet.

referenceDetails.name: Louis Erard 2340 Mauve
referenceDetails.note: Official product data lists the Mauve execution as a current 2340 variant with the same integrated-bracelet architecture.

referenceDetails.name: Louis Erard 2340 Forest
referenceDetails.note: Official product data lists Forest among the color-led 2340 executions, keeping the collection centered on contemporary daily-wear design.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: 2340 marks Louis Erard's move into integrated-bracelet sport-luxury territory while keeping the brand's accessible, design-forward independent identity anchored in Le Noirmont.

faqItems.question: What does Louis Erard 2340 mean?
faqItems.answer: Louis Erard's official product copy says 2340 refers to the postal code of Le Noirmont, the brand's home.

faqItems.question: What kind of watch is the 2340?
faqItems.answer: It is Louis Erard's integrated-bracelet watch family, built around a new case, bracelet, and movement direction for the brand.

faqItems.question: Which official 2340 variants are shown here?
faqItems.answer: The page uses official product data for Mint, Mauve, and Forest references from the current Louis Erard catalog.

timeline.event: Louis Erard is founded in La Chaux-de-Fonds as a watchmaking school by Louis Erard and André Perret, establishing an independent watchmaking identity rooted in the Swiss Jura's horological tradition.
The company is sold and production moves to Le Noirmont in the Swiss Jura, where it remains headquartered today.
Manuel Emch takes the helm as CEO, reorienting Louis Erard towards bold collaborations and artisanal watchmaking, prioritising innovation over conformity.
The Noirmont X collaboration series launches with Alain Silberstein, generating significant collector enthusiasm and international press coverage.
Louis Erard introduces the 2340 collection, marking a new technical and aesthetic chapter with an in-house movement and bold case design.

Dubbed the 'King of Collabs' by the Financial Times. Releases the Konstantin Chaykin Unfrogettable at Dubai Watch Week 2025. Launches the 2340 integrated-bracelet sports watch as a permanent collection.

faqItems.question: Is Louis Erard truly independent?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Louis Erard has remained independent since its founding in 1929, which is central to its identity and enables the creative risk-taking that defines its collaboration programme.

faqItems.question: What makes Louis Erard's Noirmont X collaborations special?
faqItems.answer: The Noirmont X series invites renowned watchmakers and artists — including Alain Silberstein and Vianney Halter — to reimagine Louis Erard pieces, producing truly unique limited editions that challenge conventional watchmaking aesthetics.

name: Louis Moinet
description: Louis Moinet is a brand revived in Saint-Blaise in 2004 in honour of the French watchmaker who invented the chronograph in 1816, predating other claimants by decades. The brand produces limited-edition chronographs and complications, often incorporating meteorite or other unusual dial materials.
defunct_reason: Louis Moinet died in 1853, and the brand name died with him; he had operated as a personal watchmaker rather than a commercial enterprise.
revival_attempt: Revived in Saint-Blaise in 2004 by Jean-Marie Schaller, honouring Moinet as the inventor of the chronograph in 1816; the brand produces limited-edition chronographs and complications.

keyCollections.name: Mechanical Wonders
keyCollections.description: Louis Moinet's flagship collection of highly complex mechanical timepieces, featuring exotic materials such as meteorite, lunar rock and Martian minerals alongside sophisticated complications.

keyCollections.name: Cosmic Art
keyCollections.description: An artistic collection incorporating genuine space materials — lunar meteorite, Martian rock, asteroid fragments — into dials, celebrating the cosmos as a canvas.

keyCollections.name: Memoris
keyCollections.description: A high-complication chronograph collection unique to Louis Moinet, featuring a jumping hours display and retrograde mechanism that pay homage to Louis Moinet's invention of the chronograph.

keyCollections.name: Around the World in 8 Days
keyCollections.description: A limited-edition collection featuring a world-time complication and an 8-day power reserve, referencing Jules Verne's adventurous spirit and the brand's connection to exploration.

timeline.event: Historical Louis Moinet completes the world's first chronograph — the Compteur de Tierces — beating at 216,000 vibrations per hour, a record that stood for a century.
Jean-Marie Schaller revives the Louis Moinet name in Saint-Blaise, Switzerland, establishing Les Ateliers Louis Moinet as an independent luxury watch brand.
Louis Moinet is officially recognised with a Guinness World Record for producing the world's first chronograph, affirming the historical achievement of its namesake.
A second Guinness World Record is awarded for the first high-frequency stopwatch, further cementing Louis Moinet's place in horological history.
The Louis Moinet 1816 Chronograph wins Best Chronograph at the Middle East Watch & Jewellery Awards, honouring the 209th anniversary of the original invention.
Reveals new Space Mystery editions featuring meteorite and lunar-material dials, and the Memoris Spirit chronograph, continuing its space-themed horological storytelling.
Presents limited-edition Astronef collection at Watches & Wonders 2026, incorporating fragments of a newly authenticated Martian meteorite.

faqItems.question: Did Louis Moinet really invent the chronograph?
faqItems.answer: Yes. A 2012 Guinness World Record confirms that historical watchmaker Louis Moinet completed the world's first chronograph — the Compteur de Tierces — in 1816, predating previously credited inventors.

faqItems.question: When was the modern Louis Moinet brand founded?
faqItems.answer: The modern brand, Les Ateliers Louis Moinet, was established in 2004 by Jean-Marie Schaller in Saint-Blaise, Switzerland, to honour and continue the legacy of the 19th-century master watchmaker.

name: Louis Vuitton
description: Louis Vuitton entered watchmaking in 2002 with the acquisition of Geneva manufacture La Fabrique du Temps, which it uses to develop in-house movements for its Tambour collection. Positioned at the intersection of fashion luxury and serious horology, LV's watch ambitions have grown significantly under the LVMH umbrella.

keyCollections.name: Tambour
keyCollections.description: Louis Vuitton's signature watch collection since 2002, featuring the distinctive drum-shaped case (tambour means 'drum' in French) in a wide range of complications and materials.

keyCollections.name: Escale
keyCollections.description: A world-time and travel-inspired collection, reflecting Louis Vuitton's heritage as a maker of luxury trunks for globe-trotters, with multi-timezone complications and vivid dials.

keyCollections.name: LV One Click
keyCollections.description: A contemporary, jewellery-forward collection featuring a distinctive one-click interchangeable strap system, aimed at a fashion-conscious female audience.

keyCollections.name: Tambour Street Diver
keyCollections.description: A sportif interpretation of the iconic Tambour, combining urban aesthetics with dive-watch specifications and a rubber strap for an active lifestyle.

timeline.event: Louis Vuitton founds his Maison in Paris, specialising in luxury trunks and luggage — laying the foundation for one of the world's most recognisable luxury houses.
Louis Vuitton enters the world of watchmaking with the acquisition of Geneva manufacture La Fabrique du Temps and the launch of the Tambour collection.
Louis Vuitton introduces in-house movements, elevating its watchmaking credentials beyond purely fashion-oriented timepieces.
The Tambour Horizon smartwatch is launched, demonstrating Louis Vuitton's ambition to lead connected-watch design in the luxury segment.
Louis Vuitton debuts at Watches & Wonders Geneva, signalling its serious ambitions within the global fine watchmaking calendar.

Unveils the Tambour Forty Five in new ceramic-and-titanium iterations and a Tambour Carpe Diem mechanical table clock. Expands La Fabrique du Temps Geneva manufacture output under creative director Hamdi Chatti.

Unveils nine novelties at LVMH Watch Week 2026 including the $239,000 Escale Worldtime Tourbillon. Collaborates with De Bethune on a GMT limited to 12 pieces. Awards the second Louis Vuitton Watch Prize to Hazemann & Monnin.

faqItems.question: When did Louis Vuitton start making watches?
faqItems.answer: Louis Vuitton entered watchmaking formally in 2002, launching the Tambour collection alongside the acquisition of La Fabrique du Temps, a Geneva-based manufacture.

faqItems.question: Does Louis Vuitton make its own watch movements?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Louis Vuitton develops in-house calibres at La Fabrique du Temps in Geneva, where a team of watchmakers produces movements exclusively for the Maison.

name: Ludovic Ballouard
description: Ludovic Ballouard is an independent French-Swiss watchmaker who worked at F.P. Journe and Breguet before establishing his atelier in Geneva in 2009. He is known for inventing the Upside Down dial, on which all the hours except the current one are inverted, reflecting his philosophy that only the present moment matters.

keyCollections.name: Upside Down
keyCollections.description: Ludovic Ballouard’s debut Upside Down is an eccentric philosophical watch in which every hour numeral is inverted except the one marking the current hour, turning the dial into a reminder to stay focused on the present while showcasing a highly original, hand-finished independent movement.

referenceDetails.name: Upside Down / reference B01
referenceDetails.note: The brand’s manual-winding patented complication calibre B01 powers the original Upside Down concept.

referenceDetails.name: Upside Down collection
referenceDetails.note: Official collection page describing the inverted numerals concept and present-hour logic.

referenceDetails.name: Classic Collection variants
referenceDetails.note: The brand currently groups multiple classic and special-edition variants under this family.

timeline.event: The brand says the Upside Down was born in December 2009.
Ballouard’s later brand materials note his continued independent production and philosophy centered on living in the moment.
Recent brand pages still present Upside Down as a core expression of the maison’s identity and philosophy.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Upside Down is the foundational Ludovic Ballouard watch: it established the brand’s playful but technically serious approach and remains the clearest collector reference for the maison’s worldview.

faqItems.question: Why are the numerals upside down?
faqItems.answer: Ballouard designed the watch so the past and future are literally inverted, leaving only the current hour right side up as a reminder to live in the moment.

faqItems.question: Is the minute display conventional?
faqItems.answer: No. The watch uses a distinctive mechanical presentation rather than a standard easy-read sports layout, which is part of its collector appeal.

keyCollections.name: Half Time
keyCollections.description: Ludovic Ballouard’s Half Time is a philosophical jumping-hour watch that splits every numeral except the current hour, making the present moment the only fully legible one while a retrograde minute display adds mechanical drama and a distinctly independent-watchmaker voice.

referenceDetails.name: Half Time / reference B02
referenceDetails.note: The brand’s manual-winding patented complication calibre B02 is the core reference for Half Time.

referenceDetails.name: Half Time collection
referenceDetails.note: Official collection page describing the split numerals and retrograde minutes.

referenceDetails.name: Half Time / Green Line
referenceDetails.note: Named special-edition variant highlighted by GPHG and the brand.

timeline.event: Ballouard states that Half Time was presented in January 2012.
GPHG identifies Half Time / Green Line as a later iteration of the Half Time concept and notes its launch date as 2018.
Brand materials continue to frame Half Time around the idea that the most important time is the present.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Half Time is one of the clearest expressions of Ludovic Ballouard’s philosophy: it turns time display into a statement piece, while still delivering a serious, in-house mechanical complication with strong collector identity.

faqItems.question: What is the core idea behind Half Time?
faqItems.answer: Only the current hour is shown whole; the other numerals are split in half, reinforcing the brand’s message that the present moment matters most.

faqItems.question: What complication does it use?
faqItems.answer: The watch uses a retrograde minute display in addition to the split-numeral jumping-hour presentation.

timeline.event: Ludovic Ballouard begins his career in fine watchmaking, working alongside master watchmakers at prestigious houses including Breguet and F.P. Journe.
Ballouard founds his own independent atelier and unveils the Upside Down, his debut timepiece, to immediate critical acclaim at Baselworld.
The Half Time watch is introduced, extending Ballouard's philosophical concept of present-moment awareness into a second, even more complex creation.
Ludovic Ballouard cements his reputation as one of independent watchmaking's most original thinkers, with both pieces becoming sought-after collector's items.
Releases a new Half Time model in platinum with a guilloché dial, maintaining extremely limited annual production of around 30 pieces from his Sainte-Croix atelier.

faqItems.question: What is the concept behind Ludovic Ballouard's watches?
faqItems.answer: Ballouard's watches are philosophical objects: by displaying the current time differently from past and future hours, they encourage the wearer to focus on the present moment rather than dwelling on what has passed or what is yet to come.

faqItems.question: How many watches does Ludovic Ballouard produce each year?
faqItems.answer: Production is extremely limited — Ballouard produces only a handful of watches per year, making his pieces rare and highly prized by independent watchmaking collectors.

name: Luminox
description: Luminox is an American watch brand founded in 1989 and based in San Mateo, California, known for pioneering the use of self-powered tritium gas tubes for always-visible luminescence. Adopted by the US Navy SEALs in 1992, Luminox produces tactical, dive, and field watches worn by military and emergency services personnel worldwide.

keyCollections.name: Navy SEAL
keyCollections.description: Luminox’s Navy SEAL collection is its signature tactical watch line, defined by rugged construction, strong night visibility, and long-running association with U.S. Navy SEAL branding across the brand’s catalog.

keyCollections.name: Pacific Diver
keyCollections.description: Luminox’s Pacific Diver collection is a dive-oriented family built for underwater use, combining a rotating bezel, high legibility, and the brand’s signature illumination system in a robust sports-watch package.

keyCollections.name: Leatherback Sea Turtle
keyCollections.description: A lightweight, brightly illuminated sport watch line built around Luminox Light Technology, CARBONOX construction, and an accessible everyday-adventure profile, with a conservation-minded sea turtle identity and a focus on durable daily wear.

keyCollections.name: Atacama Field
keyCollections.description: Luminox’s Atacama Field collection is a rugged field-watch family inspired by harsh desert environments, built for outdoor use with highly legible dials and durable, adventure-ready construction.

timeline.event: Atacama Field models continued to appear in the official Luminox catalog and regional storefronts.
Luminox is founded in San Mateo, California, with a commitment to always-visible illumination using self-powered tritium gas tubes — a technology previously used in military applications.
The U.S. Navy SEALs adopt Luminox as their watch of choice for night missions after being sought out by a Navy RDT&E officer seeking a more dependable timepiece.
Luminox expands internationally, establishing partnerships with adventure athletes and first-responder communities worldwide.
Bear Grylls becomes a Luminox brand partner and ambassador, extending the brand's reach to global outdoor adventure audiences.
Luminox launches the Navy SEAL Foundation partnership collection, directing proceeds to support U.S. Navy SEAL veterans and their families.
Launches the Bear Grylls Survival Master 3780 CARBONOX+ series and new Navy SEAL Foundation editions, continuing its focus on military-grade luminous watches.

faqItems.question: How does Luminox's illumination work?
faqItems.answer: Luminox uses self-powered tritium gas tubes — called Luminox Light Technology — which glow for up to 25 years without any need for light exposure, battery charging or button-pressing.

faqItems.question: Are Luminox watches truly used by the Navy SEALs?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Since 1992, Luminox has been the official watch of the U.S. Navy SEALs. The collaboration began when a Navy officer sought a more dependable timepiece for night missions and selected Luminox for its always-visible illumination.

name: LVMH
description: LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton is the world's largest luxury goods conglomerate, controlling watch brands including TAG Heuer, Hublot, Zenith, and Bulgari through its Watches & Jewellery division. LVMH also owns Bulgari's manufacture and has invested significantly in developing genuine in-house watchmaking across its portfolio.

keyCollections.name: TAG Heuer
keyCollections.description: TAG Heuer is LVMH’s most accessible watch maison, defined by motor-racing heritage, precision chronographs, and sporty everyday luxury. The brand’s collection architecture is led by Carrera, Monaco, and Aquaracer, with a modern range that extends from mechanical chronographs to connected watches.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: TAG Heuer matters because it is one of the clearest entry points into LVMH watchmaking: historically rooted, broad in assortment, and strongly tied to motorsport, which makes it both commercially important and immediately legible to consumers.

timeline.event: TAG Heuer’s official collection pages continue to center Carrera, Monaco, and Aquaracer as the brand’s key families.
LVMH describes TAG Heuer as a core watchmaking maison within the group’s Watches & Jewelry division.
The Carrera page emphasizes the collection’s origin at Sebring and its role as the home for the brand’s most innovative movements.

referenceDetails.name: TAG Heuer Carrera Collection
referenceDetails.note: Current official collection page with racing-origin story and positioning around innovative movements.

referenceDetails.name: TAG Heuer Monaco Collection
referenceDetails.note: Current official collection page for the square chronograph icon launched in 1969.

referenceDetails.name: TAG Heuer Aquaracer Collection
referenceDetails.note: Current official collection page for the dive-oriented sports line.

faqItems.question: What is TAG Heuer best known for?
faqItems.answer: Sports watches, especially chronographs tied to motorsport heritage, plus the Monaco and Carrera icons.

faqItems.question: Is TAG Heuer a luxury brand?
faqItems.answer: Yes, it sits in the accessible luxury segment within LVMH’s watch division.

keyCollections.name: Hublot
keyCollections.description: Hublot is LVMH’s innovation-led Swiss watch maison, built around the Art of Fusion: bold materials, contemporary case design, and sport-forward luxury. Its core identity is anchored by the Big Bang and Classic Fusion families, which balance technical experimentation with wearable, modern design.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Hublot matters because it represents LVMH’s most visibly experimental watchmaking voice, translating the group’s luxury positioning into a distinctive mix of high-tech materials, statement design, and commercially recognizable sports-luxury icons.

timeline.event: Hublot’s ongoing Art of Fusion positioning remains centered on the Big Bang and Classic Fusion families on official brand pages.
LVMH’s Watches & Jewelry division continues to present Hublot as one of its core watchmaking maisons.
Hublot’s official collection pages highlight the Big Bang as the flagship model and Classic Fusion as the brand’s elegant counterpart.

referenceDetails.name: Big Bang Collection
referenceDetails.note: Flagship line and primary brand icon; current official collection page.

referenceDetails.name: Classic Fusion Collection
referenceDetails.note: Current official collection page describing the line as a reinterpretation of classic elegance.

referenceDetails.name: Spirit of Big Bang
referenceDetails.note: Named sub-line within the Big Bang family on current official assortment pages.

faqItems.question: What defines Hublot’s style?
faqItems.answer: A mix of unconventional materials, sporty silhouettes, and a strong contemporary identity centered on the Art of Fusion.

faqItems.question: Which collections are most important?
faqItems.answer: The Big Bang and Classic Fusion are the brand’s principal collections and most recognizable product families.

keyCollections.name: Zenith
keyCollections.description: Zenith is LVMH’s historic manufacture house, known for precision chronographs, technical credibility, and the El Primero legacy. Its current collection structure is anchored by CHRONOMASTER, DEFY, PILOT, and newer brand storytelling that emphasizes innovation, integrated manufacture capability, and avant-garde Swiss watchmaking.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Zenith matters because it gives LVMH deep horological legitimacy: a long-running manufacture with an especially important place in chronograph history, plus a modern collection framework that still leans on technical prestige.

timeline.event: LVMH’s official Zenith page describes the maison as a fully integrated manufacture with the El Primero at the center of its legacy.
The official collection overview highlights CHRONOMASTER, DEFY, and PILOT as Zenith’s current core families.
LVMH positions Zenith within its Watches & Jewelry division as a watchmaking house grounded in centuries of savoir-faire and innovation.

referenceDetails.name: CHRONOMASTER
referenceDetails.note: Current official Zenith collection family emphasizing high-precision chronographs.

referenceDetails.name: DEFY
referenceDetails.note: Current official collection family for Zenith’s technical and avant-garde designs.

referenceDetails.name: PILOT
referenceDetails.note: Current official collection family celebrating Zenith’s aviation heritage.

faqItems.question: What is Zenith’s most famous movement?
faqItems.answer: The El Primero automatic chronograph movement is the house’s signature technical reference.

faqItems.question: What kind of brand is Zenith?
faqItems.answer: A Swiss manufacture focused on precision, chronographs, and technical innovation.

keyCollections.name: Bulgari
keyCollections.description: The Italian jeweller's watchmaking arm, acquired by LVMH in 2011, known for world-record ultra-thin movements and the Octo Finissimo collection.

timeline.event: LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton is created through the merger of Louis Vuitton and Moët Hennessy, with Bernard Arnault establishing control and beginning a luxury consolidation strategy.
LVMH acquires TAG Heuer, Zenith and Ebel in a landmark move that establishes its dedicated watchmaking division — LVMH Watch & Jewellery.
Louis Vuitton launches its own watch collection via Geneva manufacture La Fabrique du Temps, adding a fashion-luxury dimension to the group's watch portfolio.
LVMH acquires Hublot, adding the bold 'Art of Fusion' brand and its fast-growing sports-luxury customer base to the group.
LVMH completes the acquisition of Bulgari, expanding its jewellery and watchmaking credentials with one of Italy's most prestigious luxury names.
Watch division continued to grow with TAG Heuer, Hublot, and Zenith performing well. Launched the inaugural Louis Vuitton Watch Prize for Independent Creatives.
LVMH Watch Week moves to Milan for January 2026 with nine brands. Béatrice Goasglas appointed first female CEO of TAG Heuer (effective May 2026). Julien Tornare takes over as CEO of Hublot.

faqItems.question: Which watch brands does LVMH own?
faqItems.answer: LVMH's watch portfolio includes TAG Heuer, Hublot, Zenith, Bulgari's watch division and Louis Vuitton Watches — covering segments from accessible sport chronographs to ultra-luxury complications.

faqItems.question: Is LVMH a watch brand itself?
faqItems.answer: No. LVMH (Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton) is a luxury conglomerate, the world's largest by revenue. Its watchmaking presence is exercised through the brands it owns rather than under the LVMH name itself.

name: Magellan
description: Acquired in 2024, MAGELLAN embodies Swiss watchmaking audacity. Each three-dimensional watch, inspired by the spirit of exploration, pushes conventional design boundaries — sculpted cases, innovative time display and Swiss movement quality that honours the explorer's legacy in timepieces as bold as the voyages they evoke.

keyCollections.name: 1521 Earth
keyCollections.description: The 1521 Earth is Magellan’s globe-centered signature model, using a hand-painted three-dimensional Earth motif, domed sapphire construction, and an exploration-led aesthetic to turn the passage of time into a miniature planetary scene.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Earth is the clearest expression of the 1521 collection’s identity: planetary imagery, technical domed crystal construction, and a poetic travel narrative that anchors the line.

referenceDetails.name: 1521 Collection Earth
referenceDetails.note: Official product page for the Earth model.

referenceDetails.name: 1521 Collection Northern Hemisphere
referenceDetails.note: Sibling model that confirms the collection’s globe-centric naming scheme.

referenceDetails.name: 1521 Collection Planet
referenceDetails.note: Another official 1521 variant that reinforces the line’s celestial/planetary positioning.

timeline.event: Magellan’s current ownership change provided a fresh backdrop for the brand’s contemporary 1521 positioning.
The 1521 Collection page highlighted the line’s domed sapphire crystal and globe-trotter hand concept.
The Earth model was presented as a poetic view of the planet from orbit, centered on a hand-painted 3D globe.

faqItems.question: What makes the Earth model distinctive?
faqItems.answer: Its centerpiece is a hand-painted 3D Earth motif paired with Magellan’s domed crystal and travel-inspired dial architecture.

faqItems.question: Is Earth part of the 1521 Collection?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The official page labels it as 1521 Collection Earth.

keyCollections.name: 1518 Collection
keyCollections.description: A bold entry into the Magellan line-up, honouring the year Magellan's expedition departed, with innovative three-dimensional dials and Swiss movements.

keyCollections.name: 1520 Collection
keyCollections.description: Mid-collection timepieces blending technical Swiss precision with the exploratory spirit of the brand's namesake navigator.

timeline.event: Magellan Watch SA is established in Switzerland, named after the Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan who led the first circumnavigation of the Earth.
Mario G. Nargi acquires Magellan Watch and takes over as CEO, with a vision to elevate the brand to international renown through bold, sculptural design.
Magellan launches its signature 1521 Earth collection, featuring three-dimensional cases crafted by gifted Swiss artisans in the heart of watch-country.
Magellan Watch undergoes further development under new ownership, reaffirming its commitment to Swiss-made audacity and exploration-inspired design.
Launches the Magellan Odyssey, a 42mm titanium GMT diver, expanding its explorer-themed collection with improved in-house movement finishing.

faqItems.question: Why is the brand called Magellan?
faqItems.answer: The brand is named after Ferdinand Magellan (1479–1521), the Portuguese explorer who led the first expedition to circumnavigate the globe — an act of audacity and precision that mirrors the brand's watchmaking philosophy.

faqItems.question: Where are Magellan watches made?
faqItems.answer: Magellan watches are Swiss-made, produced in the heart of Switzerland's watchmaking region using Swiss precision components and crafted by skilled local artisans.

name: Maison Alcée
description: Maison Alcée allows any curious mind eager to discover the beauty of watchmaking to assemble their own timepiece — part education, part craft, entirely personal. A French atelier that democratises horological knowledge and participation, Maison Alcée makes the art of the watchmaker accessible to enthusiasts at every level.

keyCollections.name: Assembly Workshop Kit
keyCollections.description: Maison Alcée’s Assembly Workshop Kit is a hands-on horological experience that lets an enthusiast build a mechanical timepiece at home from a complete, guided set of components, tools, and instructional materials.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is the brand’s defining proposition: a product that is simultaneously a kit, a learning experience, and a statement about transmitting horological craft to newcomers.

referenceDetails.name: Persée watchmaking set
referenceDetails.note: Official first creation and the core assemble-it-yourself product.

referenceDetails.name: Persée Or
referenceDetails.note: Gold-toned edition and one of the named variants in the lineup.

referenceDetails.name: Persée Azur
referenceDetails.note: Blue-themed edition referenced as part of the launch lineup.

image.alt: Maison Alcée Persée watchmaking kit hero image

timeline.event: Maison Alcée’s site materials note a Persée Or unveiling in October 2024.
The brand describes Persée as its first creation, assembled by the enthusiast at home.
Maison Alcée positions the kit around transmission of watchmaking know-how and a guided assembly experience.

faqItems.question: What comes in the Assembly Workshop Kit?
faqItems.answer: The official materials describe a presentation box with 233 components, 17 watchmaking tools, and a guide for the full assembly process.

faqItems.question: Is the kit a finished watch or a learning product?
faqItems.answer: It is both: the user assembles the timepiece and learns the mechanics through the process.

keyCollections.name: Atelier Collection
keyCollections.description: Finished timepieces produced by the atelier, embodying the house philosophy that beauty is most deeply appreciated when understood from the inside out.

name: Marathon

Marathon Watch Company is founded in Canada with a mandate to supply precision timing instruments to military and government clients.

faqItems.question: Who is William Massena?
faqItems.answer: William Massena is a respected watch consultant, collector and dealer who has spent decades at the intersection of vintage and contemporary Swiss watchmaking. He founded Massena LAB to produce the kind of watches that serious collectors actually want.

faqItems.question: Does Massena LAB manufacture its own watches?
faqItems.answer: No — Massena LAB does not manufacture watches itself. Instead, it collaborates with established Swiss manufacturers to produce limited-edition pieces, directing every detail of design, specification and historical reference.

The Aikon collection launches, giving Maurice Lacroix a contemporary sport-luxury identity to complement its classical Masterpiece and Pontos lines.

faqItems.question: Does Maurice Lacroix make its own movements?

faqItems.question: What is the difference between the Aikon and Masterpiece collections?
faqItems.answer: The Aikon is Maurice Lacroix's contemporary sport-luxury line — modern in design, broadly accessible, and widely distributed. The Masterpiece is the brand's haute horlogerie tier, featuring complex in-house complications aimed at serious watch enthusiasts.
