faqItems.answer: Max Twelve cases are CNC-milled from solid blocks of metal — a process borrowed from the precision engineering industry — giving each watch an architectural, sculptural quality that reflects industrial manufacturing as high design.

faqItems.question: Are Max Twelve watches Swiss-made?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Max Twelve is rooted in Switzerland's mechanical precision industry and produces its watches using Swiss components and manufacturing standards.

name: MB&F
description: MB&F (Maximilian Büsser and Friends) was founded in Geneva in 2005 by former Harry Winston CEO Max Büsser, dedicated to creating what he calls Mechanical Art Devices — three-dimensional, sculptural watches that function as kinetic art. Each limited-edition HM (Horological Machine) is created in collaboration with a community of specialist craftspeople.

keyCollections.name: Horological Machine (HM Series)
keyCollections.description: MB&F's groundbreaking flagship line: three-dimensional kinetic sculptures masquerading as watches. Each HM (Horological Machine) is a radical reimagining of what a watch can be, co-created with specialist craftsmen — 'Friends' — from across the horological world.

keyCollections.name: Legacy Machine (LM Series)
keyCollections.description: A tribute to 19th-century watchmaking — featuring large balance wheels above the dial, flying tourbillons and other classical complications — reinterpreted through MB&F's contemporary artistic lens.

keyCollections.name: Performance Machine (M.A.D. Series)
keyCollections.description: MB&F's more accessible line produced under the M.A.D.1 sub-brand, offering the brand's experimental spirit at a lower entry price through a mechanical wristwatch with unconventional time display.

timeline.event: Maximilian Büsser founds MB&F (Maximilian Büsser and Friends) in Geneva after leaving his role as CEO of Harry Winston Timepieces, with a vision to create horological machines as artistic collaborations.
The first Horological Machine — HM1 — is unveiled, a radical three-dimensional watch unlike anything previously seen, establishing MB&F's unique creative identity.
MB&F introduces the Legacy Machine series, proving the brand can also apply its artistic ambitions to classical complications and historical watchmaking references.
MB&F opens M.A.D. Gallery in Geneva, a concept space for 'Mechanical Art Devices' — kinetic sculptures, automata and watches — cementing the brand's position at the intersection of art and horology.
MB&F celebrates its 15th anniversary with a series of limited-edition pieces, and Max Büsser is widely recognised as one of independent watchmaking's most influential entrepreneurs.

Celebrates 20th anniversary with a year of special releases including the LM Longhorn in steel, HM11, collaboration with Bulgari, and two M.A.D.2 editions with Eric Giroud. Chanel acquires a 25% stake in MB&F.
Presents the LM Perpetual Evo 2 and an HM9 'Road Edition' at Watches & Wonders 2026, continuing to push boundaries in haute horlogerie creativity.

faqItems.question: What does MB&F stand for?
faqItems.answer: MB&F stands for Maximilian Büsser and Friends — reflecting founder Max Büsser's philosophy that the best creative work is done collaboratively, bringing together 'Friends' who are expert craftsmen from across the horological and artistic world.

faqItems.question: Are MB&F watches investments?
faqItems.answer: Many MB&F pieces — particularly the Horological Machine series — have appreciated significantly on the secondary market. Their ultra-limited production, artistic credibility and cult following among collectors make them highly sought-after, though MB&F itself does not market them as investments.

name: MeisterSinger
description: MeisterSinger is a German watch brand founded in 2001 by Manfred Brassler in Münster, Germany, specialising in single-hand watches that display time using an ancient horological tradition. The brand's minimalist dials, typically read to within five minutes, draw on medieval clock aesthetics while using contemporary Swiss movements.

keyCollections.name: No. 01
keyCollections.description: MeisterSinger’s No. 01 is the original single-hand model that established the brand’s minimalist, one-hand reading concept and remains a foundational reference within the line-up.

keyCollections.name: Pangaea
keyCollections.description: A slimmer, more discreet MeisterSinger single-hand collection in 40mm-style proportions, aimed at buyers who want a cleaner and more versatile expression of the brand’s philosophy.

keyCollections.name: Salthora
keyCollections.description: MeisterSinger’s jumping-hours collection, offering a distinctive single-disc hour display that reinterprets the brand’s one-hand concept in a more contemporary, complication-led format.

keyCollections.name: Archao
keyCollections.description: A contemporary addition to the line-up featuring bold, assertive proportions with the signature single-hand, available in DLC finishes for a more modern, darker aesthetic.

timeline.event: Manfred Brassler founds MeisterSinger in Münster, Germany, and introduces the No. 01 — a single-hand watch referencing the reading method of medieval clock towers, representing a radical statement in a two-hand-dominated market.
MeisterSinger expands its collection with the Pangaea and additional colourways, establishing the single-hand concept as a viable, desirable watchmaking category.
The Salthora is introduced, bringing a jumping-hour complication to the MeisterSinger line-up and demonstrating the brand's ability to evolve beyond its founding concept.
MeisterSinger partners with Swiss movement specialists to use quality Swiss-made calibres, reinforcing the brand's commitment to mechanical reliability beneath its distinctly German design identity.
The Archao DLC collection launches, offering a contemporary, darker aesthetic for a new generation of single-hand enthusiasts.
Debuts the Kaenos integrated-bracelet collection and Archao at Watches & Wonders 2025, the brand's first appearance at the fair. Celebrates approaching 25th anniversary.
Marks 25th anniversary with the Panthero Jumping Hour complication (EUR 6,990). Does not return to Watches & Wonders 2026.

faqItems.question: Why does MeisterSinger use only one hand?
faqItems.answer: MeisterSinger's founder, Manfred Brassler, was inspired by medieval public clocks, which displayed the time with a single hand pointing to the relevant hour. With just one hand, the wearer reads time with appropriate imprecision — liberating rather than enslaving by the minute — reflecting a more relaxed, philosophical relationship with time.

faqItems.question: Is MeisterSinger Swiss-made?
faqItems.answer: MeisterSinger is a German brand, founded and designed in Münster. Its watches use Swiss-made movements — typically from ETA or Sellita — ensuring reliable mechanical quality within the brand's distinctly German design ethos.

name: Mühle-Glashütte
description: Mühle-Glashütte is a family-owned German watchmaker founded in 1869 by Robert Mühle, originally producing precision measuring instruments for Glashütte's watch industry. Now in its sixth generation under Thilo Mühle, the company creates robust, functional wristwatches and nautical instruments known for their proprietary woodpecker-neck fine adjustment and Glashütte finishing.

keyCollections.name: Teutonia
keyCollections.description: Teutonia is Mühle-Glashütte’s elegant classic-business watch family: silver-guilloché heritage, refined dial work, and the brand’s precision-oriented Glashütte execution, positioned as the manufactory’s most successful watch line.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Teutonia is the clearest expression of Mühle-Glashütte’s move beyond pure instrument watches into a recognizable dress-oriented family, while still carrying the brand’s technical and finishing identity.

referenceDetails.name: Original Teutonia (2002)
referenceDetails.note: First Teutonia model presented in early 2002; silver guilloché dial and big date defined the family start.

referenceDetails.name: Teutonia II family
referenceDetails.note: Continuation of the line with multiple small-second, GMT, chronograph and medium variants on the official collection page.

image.alt: Teutonia II Medium with guilloché dial

referenceDetails.name: Teutonia IV family
referenceDetails.note: Modern branch of the line; brand notes the Teutonia IV Moonphase launched in 2019 as the first moonphase in the collection.

timeline.event: Mühle-Glashütte presented the original Teutonia with a silver guilloché dial and big date.
The Teutonia IV Moonphase launched as the first moonphase display in the family.
Mühle-Glashütte described Teutonia as its most successful watch family and the unmistakable flagship of the manufactory.

faqItems.question: What kind of watch is Teutonia?
faqItems.answer: It is Mühle-Glashütte’s elegant classic/business line, distinct from the brand’s more overt tool watches.

faqItems.question: What makes Teutonia recognizable?
faqItems.answer: The silver guilloché dial language, applied indexes, and the family’s long-running role as a signature collection.

keyCollections.name: S.A.R. Rescue-Timer
keyCollections.description: Mühle-Glashütte’s S.A.R. Rescue-Timer is the brand’s best-known professional rescue watch, developed with the German Maritime Search and Rescue Service and built for extreme readability, durability, and mission-ready performance in harsh marine conditions.

referenceDetails.name: Tool watches page
referenceDetails.note: Official brand page states the S.A.R. Rescue-Timer began accompanying DGzRS missions in February 2002.

referenceDetails.name: S.A.R. Rescue-Timer LUMEN
referenceDetails.note: Official launch page for the luminous version of the rescue watch family.

referenceDetails.name: Edition 1994 special edition
referenceDetails.note: Official anniversary special edition page connecting the rescue watch to the brand’s 2024 milestone year and production history.

timeline.event: Mühle-Glashütte highlighted the S.A.R. Rescue-Timer again through the Edition 1994 anniversary special edition.
Official materials reiterated that the watch has accompanied DGzRS rescue work since February 2002.
The rescue watch family continued to expand with modern variants such as LUMEN and nautical color editions.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: This is Mühle-Glashütte’s signature professional instrument watch: the model most closely tied to real-world rescue service and the one that best communicates the brand’s functional credibility.

faqItems.question: Who is the S.A.R. Rescue-Timer made with?
faqItems.answer: It was developed with the German Maritime Search and Rescue Service (DGzRS).

faqItems.question: Why is it notable?
faqItems.answer: Because it is a purpose-built rescue watch known for ruggedness, readability, and a real operational association rather than a purely styling-led story.

keyCollections.name: Terranaut
keyCollections.description: Field-watch collection designed for land-based expeditions, combining robust construction with clear legibility and GMT complications.

keyCollections.name: ProMare
keyCollections.description: Nautical-themed collection bridging the brand's maritime heritage with modern sport-watch design, featuring regatta timers and sailing complications.

keyCollections.name: 29er
keyCollections.description: Mühle-Glashütte 29er is the brand’s maritime everyday watch family, named after the fast one-design sailing dinghy and positioned as a sporty, accessible entry into Mühle’s Glashütte tool-watch style.

referenceDetails.name: 29er Casual Coastal Blue
referenceDetails.note: Official collection-card reference for the 29er Casual coastal-blue model on a leather strap.

referenceDetails.name: 29er Apricot Leather Strap
referenceDetails.note: Current 29er apricot-dial reference from the official 29er collection page.

referenceDetails.name: 29er White Canvas Strap
referenceDetails.note: White-dial 29er on canvas strap, one of the current color-and-strap configurations on the official collection page.

referenceDetails.name: 29er Mint Canvas Strap
referenceDetails.note: Mint-dial 29er reference showing the line’s current casual maritime color palette.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: 29er matters because it is Mühle-Glashütte’s approachable maritime collection: less specialized than the rescue watches, but still tied directly to sailing, legibility, and the brand’s functional Glashütte identity.

image.alt: Mühle-Glashütte 29er Casual Coastal Blue official image

faqItems.question: What is the Mühle-Glashütte 29er named after?
faqItems.answer: The official collection page explains that 29er refers to a fast one-design sailing boat class.

faqItems.question: What kind of watch is the 29er?
faqItems.answer: It is a sporty maritime everyday family, positioned as a practical and accessible branch of Mühle-Glashütte’s watch lineup.

timeline.event: Robert Mühle founds the company in Glashütte, Saxony, producing precision measuring instruments for the local watchmaking industry.
Robert Mühle receives the Gold Medal of the City of Dresden for the outstanding quality of his measuring instruments.
The Mühle factory is dismantled during Soviet occupation; family loses everything.
Hans-Jürgen Mühle, fifth generation, relaunches the company as a watch manufacturer under Nautische Instrumente Mühle-Glashütte.
Thilo Mühle, fifth-generation family member, takes over company management and expands the wristwatch collection significantly.
Introduction of the proprietary woodpecker-neck fine adjustment regulator across the range.
Thilo Mühle takes over as managing director, becoming the sixth generation to lead the company.
Launches the Teutonia Sport II in 41.5mm with woodgrain dial and updated Mühle rotor, and introduces the 29er Big Date. Celebrates the brand's continued family ownership under Thilo Mühle.

faqItems.question: What is Mühle-Glashütte's woodpecker-neck fine adjustment?
faqItems.answer: It is a proprietary regulating mechanism that uses a spring-loaded lever (shaped like a woodpecker's neck) to fine-tune the rate of the movement. This allows for more precise adjustment than a standard regulator and is a hallmark of Mühle watches.

faqItems.question: Is Mühle-Glashütte related to A. Lange & Söhne or other Glashütte brands?
faqItems.answer: They share the same town and watchmaking heritage — Robert Mühle actually apprenticed under Moritz Grossmann — but Mühle-Glashütte is an independent family business with no corporate ties to other Glashütte manufacturers.

faqItems.question: What does S.A.R. stand for in the S.A.R. Rescue-Timer?
faqItems.answer: S.A.R. stands for Search and Rescue. The collection was developed in partnership with the Deutsche Gesellschaft zur Rettung Schiffbrüchiger (DGzRS), Germany's maritime search and rescue service.

faqItems.question: Does Mühle Glashütte make its own movements?
faqItems.answer: Mühle modifies ETA and Sellita base movements in-house, adding proprietary components including the woodpecker-neck fine adjustment, custom rotors, and Glashütte-finished bridges.

faqItems.question: What makes the S.A.R. Rescue-Timer special?
faqItems.answer: Developed with the German Maritime Search and Rescue Service, it is water-resistant to 1,000 metres and features a proprietary fine-adjustment regulator — a genuine professional rescue tool.

name: MHP Maison Horlogère Palmer
description: The Maison Horlogère Palmer combines exceptional craftsmanship with bold aviation spirit. Balancing tradition and innovation, MHP creates pilot watches of real mechanical conviction — timepieces where the precision demanded by flight is expressed through Swiss technical mastery and understated, functional design.

keyCollections.name: Aéronavale
keyCollections.description: Aviation-inspired pilot watch collection combining oversized crowns, legible dials, and Swiss automatic movements with a military aesthetic.

timeline.event: MHP Maison Horlogère Palmer is established in Switzerland, focusing on aviation-inspired pilot watches with strong mechanical conviction.
Releases a refreshed Aérolite collection with updated finishing, maintaining its niche position as a small-series Swiss atelier brand.

faqItems.question: What does MHP stand for?
faqItems.answer: MHP stands for Maison Horlogère Palmer, combining the family name with the French term for watchmaking house.

faqItems.question: Where are MHP watches made?
faqItems.answer: MHP watches are Swiss-made, developed and assembled in Switzerland with a focus on pilot watch functionality and mechanical movements.

name: Micromilspec
description: Micromilspec is a Swiss-Made watch brand specialising in field-tested timepieces developed in close collaboration with military units and select professional organisations. The brand offers both standard collections and custom projects designed for reliability in demanding operational environments.

keyCollections.name: Professional Series
keyCollections.description: Core collection of Swiss-made military field watches developed in collaboration with active-duty military units, featuring robust construction and operational reliability.

timeline.event: Micromilspec is founded in Oslo, Norway by Henrik Rye and Anders Drage, specialising in custom Swiss-made watches for military units and front-line organisations.

faqItems.question: Can civilians buy Micromilspec watches?
faqItems.answer: Yes. While the brand develops custom watches for military units, it also offers standard collections available to the public through authorised retailers.

faqItems.question: What does Micromilspec mean?
faqItems.answer: The name combines 'micro' (precision) with 'milspec' (military specification), reflecting watches built to military-grade standards.

name: Mido
description: Mido is a Swiss watch brand founded in 1918 by Georges Schaeren in Le Locle, Switzerland. Known for watches inspired by architectural masterpieces — such as the Baroncelli, Commander, and Multifort collections — Mido sits within the Swatch Group and produces accessible automatic watches with a design-led identity.

keyCollections.name: Baroncelli
keyCollections.description: An elegant dress-watch collection from Mido with classical proportions and refined dial layouts, positioned as a polished, versatile expression of the brand’s Swiss-made design language.

keyCollections.name: Multifort
keyCollections.description: Mido’s long-running sports-oriented collection, rooted in the brand’s robust early tool-watch heritage and now spanning contemporary mechanical models with versatile, performance-driven styling.

keyCollections.name: Commander
keyCollections.description: A retro-leaning Mido collection that draws on the brand’s mid-century heritage, typically pairing a clean, vintage-inspired profile with modern Swiss watchmaking and practical daily wearability.

keyCollections.name: Ocean Star
keyCollections.description: Mido’s dive-watch family, built around underwater-ready specifications and straightforward legibility, positioned as a durable sports collection for everyday use and maritime-inspired adventures.

timeline.event: Georges Schaeren founds Mido in Le Locle, Switzerland. The name derives from the Spanish 'Yo mido' meaning 'I measure.'
Launch of the Multifort, one of the first automatic, water-resistant, anti-magnetic watches — a technical milestone for the era.
Introduction of the Ocean Star, establishing Mido's presence in professional dive watches.
Mido joins what would become the Swatch Group, securing its long-term production capabilities.
Mido celebrates its centenary with special editions across the Baroncelli and Multifort lines.
Launches the Ocean Star 600 Chronometer COSC-certified diver and refreshed Multifort TV Big Date models. Strengthens its mid-range Swatch Group position with strong presence in Asian markets.
Presents new Baroncelli Heritage slim-dress models and an Ocean Star Decompression Timer 1961 reissue at Watches & Wonders 2026.

faqItems.question: What does the name Mido mean?
faqItems.answer: Mido comes from the Spanish 'Yo mido,' meaning 'I measure.' Founder Georges Schaeren chose it to reflect precision and universality.

faqItems.question: Where does Mido sit in the Swatch Group hierarchy?
faqItems.answer: Mido occupies the upper range of the mid-tier segment, positioned above Tissot and Hamilton but below Longines, offering genuine Swiss automatic movements at accessible prices.

name: Milus
description: Since 1919, Milus has captured the essence of time with refined watches blending traditional Swiss watchmaking with forward-thinking design innovation. The brand is particularly celebrated for its Tirion Tri-Retrograde display — a signature technical achievement — and continues to produce mechanical timepieces that reward collectors who seek the unconventional.

keyCollections.name: Snow Star
keyCollections.description: Flagship reissue of the mid-century field watch once included in US Navy pilot survival barter kits, combining heritage military provenance with modern construction.

keyCollections.name: Archimèdes
keyCollections.description: Archimèdes by Milus is the brand’s modern dive-watch line, reinterpreting the vintage Super Compressor idea with a dual-crown layout, inner rotating bezel, strong legibility, and contemporary 41 mm tool-watch proportions for everyday exploration.

referenceDetails.name: Orange Coral
referenceDetails.note: Milus states this version was officially nominated for the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève 2021.

image.alt: Milus Archimèdes Orange Coral dive watch

referenceDetails.name: Aqua Steel

image.alt: Milus Archimèdes World Timer Blue Odyssey watch

timeline.event: Milus positioned Archimèdes by Milus as the modern successor to its Super Compressor-inspired dive-watch heritage.
Orange Coral was nominated for the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève in the Diver’s category.
The collection remains active on the current Milus website with multiple colorways and worldtimer variants.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Archimèdes is the clearest modern identity statement in Milus’s catalog, tying the brand’s archive to a commercially relevant dive-watch range.

faqItems.question: What is Archimèdes based on?
faqItems.answer: Milus describes it as the modern successor to its Super Compressor dive-watch heritage and the original 666 model lineage.

faqItems.question: What defines the collection design?
faqItems.answer: Dual crowns, an internal rotating bezel, strong lume, and a robust 41 mm steel case built for dive-watch legibility.

keyCollections.name: LAB 01
keyCollections.description: LAB 01 is Milus’s contemporary, more experimental line, using a fiberglass dial and clean urban styling to present a lighter, more design-led interpretation of the brand’s Swiss-made watchmaking language.

referenceDetails.name: Concrete Grey
referenceDetails.note: One of the current LAB 01 variants listed by Milus.

referenceDetails.name: Street Black
referenceDetails.note: Current black variant in the LAB 01 collection.

referenceDetails.name: Sky Blue
referenceDetails.note: Current blue variant in the LAB 01 collection.

timeline.event: Milus highlighted LAB 01 as a modern, technical design with an exclusive fiberglass dial.
The collection was listed on the current Milus website alongside other active ranges.
LAB 01 remains available in multiple colors on the brand site.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: LAB 01 shows Milus pushing beyond heritage-inspired dive watches into a more contemporary, material-driven design direction.

faqItems.question: What is the standout material on LAB 01?
faqItems.answer: Milus says the collection uses an exclusive fiberglass dial with a distinctive texture.

faqItems.question: How is LAB 01 positioned?
faqItems.answer: It is framed as a modern, technical, and urban design statement within the Milus lineup.

timeline.event: Paul William Junod founds Milus in Biel/Bienne, Switzerland.
The Snow Star watch is selected for inclusion in US Navy pilot survival 'barter kits' — items that could be traded for safe passage if shot down.
Launch of the Archimèdes Super Compressor dive watch, which gains a cult following among collectors.
Introduction of the TriRetrograde Seconds, a signature Milus complication displaying seconds across three retrograde sub-dials.
Milus relaunches the Snow Star as a modern reissue, attracting significant attention from the watch enthusiast community.
Releases the Archimèdes Wild Life series featuring hand-painted enamel dials depicting endangered species, partnering with conservation charities.

faqItems.question: What is the Snow Star's military connection?
faqItems.answer: During the mid-20th century, US Navy pilots carried 'life barter kits' containing tradable valuables. The Milus Snow Star was included as a reliable, desirable timepiece that could be exchanged for safe passage.

faqItems.question: Is Milus still independent?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Milus remains an independent Swiss watch brand based in Biel/Bienne, producing mechanical watches with a strong focus on heritage reissues.

name: Minase
description: Minase is a Japanese watch brand launched in 2005 by Kyowa Co., a precision-tooling manufacturer from Akita Prefecture. The brand produces fewer than 500 watches per year and is known for case-in-case construction, Sallaz finishing, Swiss mechanical movements, and collections such as Divido, Uruga, Horizon, and Windows that emphasize Japanese craft and architectural case design.

keyCollections.name: Divido
keyCollections.description: Minase Divido is the Japanese brand's best-known case-in-case collection, using separated polished surfaces, strong dial colors, and steel or rubber configurations.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Divido is the clearest expression of Minase's case-in-case identity, making the brand's layered Japanese finishing and separated surfaces immediately visible.

faqItems.question: What is Minase Divido?
faqItems.answer: Divido is Minase's case-in-case collection, known for separated polished surfaces and strong Japanese case finishing.

faqItems.answer: Minase shows examples including Divido Grey Steel, Green Rubber, and Blue Steel.

faqItems.question: What is Minase Uruga?
faqItems.answer: Uruga is a sculptural Minase collection with integrated-bracelet architecture and bold Japanese case construction.

faqItems.answer: Minase shows examples including UG03-CDLNBL-SSD, UG03-M01NBL-SSB, and a 42 mm ice-blue rubber-strap Uruga.

faqItems.answer: Uruga is more sculptural and integrated, while Horizon is a cleaner sports-watch expression.

faqItems.question: What is Minase Horizon?
faqItems.answer: Horizon is Minase's clean sports-watch collection, using the brand's faceted Japanese casework in steel, rubber, and leather configurations.

faqItems.question: Which Horizon variants are official examples?
faqItems.answer: Minase's page shows examples such as Horizon Grey Rubber, Horizon Blue Steel, and Horizon Black Leather.

faqItems.question: How does Horizon fit within Minase?
faqItems.answer: It is one of the brand's more straightforward sports-watch expressions, compared with the more sculptural Uruga and Windows families.

faqItems.question: What is Minase Windows?
faqItems.answer: Windows is a Minase collection named for its layered visual openings and faceted case construction.

faqItems.question: Which Windows variants are official examples?
faqItems.answer: Minase shows examples including VM15-M01YIB-SSB, VM15-CDBYGR-SSD, and Windows Midsize Steel Rose.

faqItems.question: Why is Windows important for Minase?
faqItems.answer: It highlights the brand's case-in-case architecture and finishing, making construction a visible part of the design.

The brand launched the Yusai concept around a collaboration with contemporary artist Towa Takaya, with each dial hand-painted using her own color materials and studio techniques.
The initial Yusai lineup debuted across three Minase platforms: DIVIDO, SEVEN WINDOWS, and FIVE WINDOWS Mid.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: This collection area shows how Minase extends Japanese craft beyond case finishing into collectible dial art: Urushi models preserve lacquer tradition, while Yusai reframes the JAPAN ART COLLECTION through contemporary hand-painted dials and named artistic compositions.

image.alt: Minase Japan Art Collection SHIBO-URUSHI DIVIDO Scarlet Illusion bracelet model

faqItems.question: What is the difference between Minase Yusai and Urushi pieces?
faqItems.answer: Both sit in Minase’s JAPAN ART COLLECTION, but Urushi models focus on traditional lacquer craft, while Yusai models are hand-painted contemporary-art dials created in collaboration with Towa Takaya.

faqItems.question: When was the Yusai series introduced?
faqItems.answer: Minase announced the Yusai Dials series in 2025 as a new addition to the JAPAN ART COLLECTION and tied it to the brand’s 20th anniversary messaging.

timeline.event: Kyowa Co. Ltd. is established in Akita Prefecture, Japan, as a precision parts manufacturer.
Kyowa launches the Minase watch brand, applying decades of precision machining expertise to horology. Named after the Minase area of Akita.
Minase gains international recognition for its Sallaz polishing technique — a demanding process producing mirror-perfect facets on every surface.
Minase celebrates 20 years with limited-edition Seven Windows models and expanding international distribution.
Unveils the Horizon Year edition with Urushi lacquer dial crafted by Japanese artisans, and announces increased production capacity at its Minase-machi workshop in Akita prefecture.
Debuts the Divido Tourbillon, the brand's first tourbillon watch, at Watches & Wonders 2026, combining traditional Japanese metalwork finishing with haute horlogerie.

faqItems.question: What is Sallaz polishing?
faqItems.answer: Sallaz polishing (also called Zaratsu) is a Japanese mirror-finishing technique requiring extreme skill. Minase applies it to every visible surface of its cases, creating distortion-free reflections across multiple flat facets.

faqItems.question: Are Minase watches entirely Japanese-made?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Minase is one of very few brands producing entirely Japanese-made watches, from case manufacture and finishing to movement assembly, all done in Akita Prefecture.

seoTitle: Minase Watches - Japanese Craft, Sallaz Finishing & Divido | Watchatlas
seoDescription: Minase is a Japanese watchmaker from Akita known for Divido, Uruga, Horizon, Windows, Sallaz finishing and handmade Japanese craft dials.
whyMatters: Minase matters because it brings Japanese machining and finishing expertise into watchmaking: sharp case architecture, mirror-polished surfaces, handmade dials, and a production scale closer to craft manufacturing than mass luxury.

name: Ming
description: Ming is a Malaysian independent watch brand founded in 2017 by photographer and watch enthusiast Ming Thein, based in Kuala Lumpur. The brand produces limited-edition watches in small numbered batches, known for distinctive dial designs that blend photographic inspiration with high-quality Swiss movements.

keyCollections.name: 17 Series
keyCollections.description: MING 17 Series is the independent brand's compact daily-wear family, built around 38 mm cases, layered sapphire dial architecture, luminous dial details, and accessible mechanical movements.

referenceDetails.name: MING 17.01 Anthracite
referenceDetails.note: MING's official 17.01 page describes a 38 mm grade 5 titanium watch with a composite multi-layer sapphire dial, 100 m water resistance, and a hand-winding Sellita SW210-1 movement.

referenceDetails.name: MING 17.03 GMT Blue
referenceDetails.note: MING's official 17.03 GMT Blue page lists a 38 mm grade 2 titanium case, 24-hour timezone display, metallic blue sapphire dial construction, and automatic Sellita SW330-1 movement.

referenceDetails.name: MING 17.09 Blue
referenceDetails.note: MING's official 17.09 Blue page describes an evolved daily wearer with independently adjustable hour hand, laser-etched lume-filled sapphire indices, and a Cal. 330.M1 movement based on the Sellita SW330-2.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The 17 Series is the most direct expression of MING's accessible design language: compact proportions, luminous sapphire-layered dials, strong daily-wear specifications, and the visual vocabulary that made the brand recognizable.

faqItems.question: What is the MING 17 Series?
faqItems.answer: The 17 Series is MING's compact daily-wear line, represented by 38 mm references such as the 17.01, 17.03 GMT, and 17.09.

faqItems.question: Which official 17 Series examples are shown here?
faqItems.answer: MING's official pages shown here include the 17.01 Anthracite, 17.03 GMT Blue, and 17.09 Blue.

funFacts.title: Sapphire dial signature
funFacts.body: The official 17.01 and 17.03 pages describe composite multi-layer sapphire dials as part of the series identity.

funFacts.title: Travel-ready branch
funFacts.body: The official 17.03 GMT Blue page adds a 24-hour timezone display while retaining the compact 38 mm 17 Series format.

keyCollections.name: 19 Series
keyCollections.description: MING 19 Series is the brand's elevated collector family, using gradient sapphire dials, titanium cases, Schwarz-Etienne movements, world-time architecture, and rare special-project complications.

referenceDetails.name: MING 19.01
referenceDetails.note: MING's official 19.01 page describes a grade 5 titanium watch with a sapphire gradient dial, 50 m water resistance, and a Schwarz-Etienne for MING Cal. MSE100.1 movement with more than 100 hours of power reserve.

referenceDetails.name: MING 19.02 Worldtimer
referenceDetails.note: MING's official 19.02 Worldtimer page adds a 24-hour world-time display and microrotor automatic winding to the 19 Series sapphire-dial architecture.

referenceDetails.name: MING 19.CR Monopusher
referenceDetails.note: MING's official 19.CR Monopusher page says the seven-piece subscription watch was delivered in 2021 and used vintage Venus 140 movements with monopusher chronograph function.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The 19 Series is where MING pushes beyond entry-level daily watches into collector-facing horology, pairing the brand's transparent dial language with bespoke Schwarz-Etienne movements, world-time displays, and rare subscription pieces.

faqItems.question: What is the MING 19 Series?
faqItems.answer: The 19 Series is MING's higher-spec collector family, using titanium cases, gradient sapphire dials, and Schwarz-Etienne-linked movements.

faqItems.question: Which 19 Series references are official examples?
faqItems.answer: MING's official pages shown here include the 19.01, 19.02 Worldtimer, and seven-piece 19.CR Monopusher.

funFacts.title: Long reserve
funFacts.body: MING's official 19.01 specifications list a Schwarz-Etienne for MING movement with more than 100 hours of power reserve.

funFacts.title: Seven-piece chronograph
funFacts.body: The official 19.CR Monopusher page describes total production of seven pieces delivered in 2021.

keyCollections.name: 37 Series
keyCollections.description: MING 37 Series is the brand's modern Swiss-operations family, spanning internally managed minimalist watches, moonphase complications, and the Bluefin dive watch with distinctive luminous sapphire execution.

referenceDetails.name: MING 37.02 Minimalist
referenceDetails.note: MING's official 37.02 Minimalist page says it was the first watch designed, engineered, and production-managed internally at the brand's Swiss operations in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

referenceDetails.name: MING 37.05 Moonphase
referenceDetails.note: MING's official 37.05 Moonphase page describes a manual-wind moonphase and date watch with domed sapphire crystals, HyCeram ceramic Super-LumiNova fill, and a Sellita for MING 288.M1 movement.

referenceDetails.name: MING 37.09 Bluefin
referenceDetails.note: MING's official 37.09 Bluefin page describes a 600 m dive watch with internal 60-click timing scale, dual crowns, Super-LumiNova details, and an automatic Sellita for MING SW300.M1 movement.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The 37 Series shows MING maturing from design-led microbrand into a more vertically managed watch company, with official examples covering in-house Swiss operations, complications, and a technically serious dive watch.

faqItems.question: What is the MING 37 Series?
faqItems.answer: The 37 Series is a modern MING family that includes the 37.02 Minimalist, 37.05 Moonphase, 37.09 Bluefin, and other higher-spec references.

faqItems.question: Why is the 37.02 Minimalist important?
faqItems.answer: MING's official page says the 37.02 Minimalist was the first watch designed, engineered, and production-managed internally at its Swiss operations.

funFacts.title: Swiss operations milestone
funFacts.body: The official 37.02 Minimalist page links the watch to MING's internal Swiss operations in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

funFacts.title: Serious dive spec
funFacts.body: The official 37.09 Bluefin specifications list 600 m water resistance and an internal rotating timing scale.

timeline.event: Ming Thein, a photographer and horological writer from Kuala Lumpur, founds Ming Watch with the 17.01 as the debut model.
The 19.01 launches, establishing Ming's reputation for innovative sapphire dial construction and limited-edition strategy.
Ming introduces the 37.05 with a fully in-house movement developed in collaboration with Schwarz-Etienne, marking a major step for the brand.
Growing demand sees every release sell out within minutes; Ming becomes one of the most sought-after independent brands globally.
The 37.09 Bluefin wins the Sports Watch Prize at the GPHG 2025, Ming's second GPHG award. Launches the 37.11 Odyssey ultralight titanium GMT dive watch with 3D-printed Polymesh strap.
Announces the 20.11 Mosaic, a sapphire-cased art piece, and continues to grow its secondary-market desirability.

faqItems.question: Why are Ming watches so hard to buy?
faqItems.answer: Ming produces in very small numbered batches (often under 200 pieces) and sells direct through its website. Most releases sell out within minutes of going live.

faqItems.question: Who designs Ming dials?
faqItems.answer: Founder Ming Thein designs the dials himself, drawing on his background in photography and optics to create distinctive layered sapphire constructions with unique depth and luminosity.

name: Mondaine
description: Mondaine is a Swiss watch brand founded in 1951 by the Bernheim family, and is the official licensee of the iconic Swiss Federal Railways clock design by Hans Hilfiker. The SBB railway clock, with its distinctive red second hand that pauses at 12 before advancing, has become one of the most recognisable watch designs in the world.

keyCollections.name: Official Swiss Railways
keyCollections.description: Mondaine’s iconic licensed SBB line, translating the Swiss Federal Railways station clock into wristwatch form with the famous red seconds hand and clean, highly legible dial architecture.

keyCollections.name: Helvetica
keyCollections.description: A typography-led Mondaine collection that channels Swiss design clarity into a clean, modern watch aesthetic, pairing restrained layouts with a distinctly graphic identity.

keyCollections.name: Essence
keyCollections.description: Mondaine’s eco-conscious take on its iconic Swiss Railway design, using sustainable materials while preserving the instantly recognizable minimalist dial, bold markers, and red seconds hand that define the brand.

timeline.event: Erwin Bernheim founds Mondaine in Zurich, initially as a watch trading company.
Mondaine secures the licence from the Swiss Federal Railways to produce watches based on Hans Hilfiker's 1944 station clock design.
The SBB railway watch gains MoMA Design Collection recognition, cementing its status as a design icon.
Launch of the Helvetica collection, celebrating Swiss design heritage through typography-inspired timepieces.
Introduction of the Essence line, pioneering sustainable materials in Swiss watchmaking.
Expands the Essence sustainability line with vegan straps and bio-sourced castor-oil cases. Launches 75th-anniversary SBB Official Railway Clock Watch in limited gold edition.

faqItems.question: Why does the Mondaine second hand pause at 12?
faqItems.answer: The distinctive 'stop-to-go' second hand pauses at 12 o'clock for about 1.5 seconds before the minute hand advances — exactly replicating how the original SBB station clocks synchronise across Switzerland's rail network.

faqItems.question: Is Mondaine officially connected to Swiss railways?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Mondaine is the exclusive licensee of the SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) clock design, originally created by engineer Hans Hilfiker in 1944.

name: Monta
description: Monta is an American watch brand founded in 2017 by Adam Cook in Washington DC, known for producing high-quality sports and dress watches at honest prices. The brand's Atlas and Noble models feature Swiss movements and robust construction inspired by classic GMT and dress watch aesthetics.

keyCollections.name: Atlas
keyCollections.description: Monta’s GMT sports watch collection, built around a bidirectional 24-hour bezel, Swiss automatic movement, and sturdy steel construction for travel-ready everyday wear.

keyCollections.name: Noble
keyCollections.description: Monta’s Noble is the brand’s refined dress-oriented collection, built around a slim profile, applied indices, and a date display for a cleaner everyday formal look.

keyCollections.name: Oceanking
keyCollections.description: A professional dive watch collection from MONTA, built around 300-meter water resistance, a unidirectional bezel, and the brand’s tool-watch ethos for serious underwater and everyday use.

keyCollections.name: Triumph
keyCollections.description: A clean, legible MONTA chronograph-oriented collection positioned as a modern Swiss-made sports watch option, balancing everyday wearability with a straightforward, functional layout.

timeline.event: Adam Cook founds Monta in Saint Louis, Missouri, with the goal of creating American-designed watches at honest prices with Swiss movements.
The Atlas GMT becomes Monta's breakout model, gaining strong word-of-mouth in the enthusiast community.
Launch of the Oceanking diver, expanding the brand's sports watch lineup.
Monta introduces the Triumph chronograph, its most complex model to date.
Debuts the Triumph true-GMT with in-house M-22 calibre and launches the Atlas V2 with updated bracelet, continuing to build its reputation as a premium American-designed microbrand.

faqItems.question: Where are Monta watches made?
faqItems.answer: Monta watches are designed in the United States and assembled in Switzerland using Swiss movements and components. The brand emphasises transparent pricing and direct-to-consumer sales.

faqItems.question: What movement does Monta use?
faqItems.answer: Monta primarily uses Sellita SW-series movements, including the SW200 and SW330 (GMT), with custom finishing and regulation to chronometer-grade accuracy.

name: Montblanc
description: Montblanc, the Hamburg-based luxury goods house founded in 1906, operates a genuine watch manufacture in Le Locle acquired from Minerva in 2006. The brand produces a range from entry-level to highly complex movements, with the Minerva heritage being used for its prestige 1858 collection.

keyCollections.description: Heritage sports collection inspired by Minerva's professional military chronographs from the 1930s, featuring bronze cases and vintage-styled dials.

keyCollections.name: Star Legacy
keyCollections.description: Classic dress watch collection with Montblanc's signature star emblem, offering automatic and moonphase complications in traditional proportions.

keyCollections.name: TimeWalker
keyCollections.description: Modern sports collection with a racing-inspired aesthetic, featuring chronographs and UTC complications.

keyCollections.name: Heritage
keyCollections.description: Collection celebrating Minerva's haute horlogerie credentials, with high-complication pieces including monopusher chronographs using in-house Minerva calibres.

timeline.event: The company is founded in Hamburg, Germany, as a fountain pen manufacturer.
Montblanc enters the watch market, initially with outsourced movements.
Montblanc acquires the Minerva manufacture in Villeret, gaining access to one of Switzerland's most storied movement-making traditions dating to 1858.
Launch of the Nicolas Rieussec chronograph, the first major watch to use Minerva-derived complications under the Montblanc name.
The 1858 collection launches, directly referencing Minerva's military chronograph heritage and establishing Montblanc's most critically acclaimed watch line.

Reveals the 1858 Iced Sea Automatic Date 41mm in new glacier-blue and forest-green ceramic dial variants. Debuts the TimeWalker Manufacture Chronograph with MB 25.13 calibre. Announces Laurent Le Deunff as new CEO of Montblanc Watches.

Elevates Minerva into a fully distinct entity with its name returning to the dial. Debuts the Minerva Unveiled Crownless with a bidirectional bezel replacing the crown. Departs Watches & Wonders to focus on direct client engagement.

faqItems.question: Does Montblanc make its own movements?
faqItems.answer: Yes, through its Minerva manufacture in Villeret, acquired in 2006. The Minerva facility produces high-end movements for the 1858 and Heritage lines, while entry-level models use Sellita-based calibres.

faqItems.question: What is the connection between Montblanc and Minerva?
faqItems.answer: Minerva is a historic Swiss movement manufacturer founded in 1858 in Villeret. Montblanc acquired it in 2006, integrating its expertise in chronograph movements into the brand's haute horlogerie offerings.

name: Montres KF
description: Montres KF is a small independent watch brand producing limited-edition timepieces with a focus on refined design and Swiss craftsmanship. The brand operates within the independent watchmaking community.

keyCollections.name: KF Collection
keyCollections.description: Limited-edition Swiss timepieces combining refined case design with carefully selected movements, produced in small batches for the independent watch community.

timeline.event: Montres KF is established as a small independent Swiss watch brand, producing limited-edition timepieces for collectors.
Releases limited editions with hand-guillochéd dials from its small French atelier, maintaining artisanal output of fewer than 50 watches per year.

faqItems.question: Where are Montres KF watches made?
faqItems.answer: Montres KF watches are Swiss-made, designed and assembled in Switzerland with a focus on small-batch production and collector-oriented editions.

name: Moritz Grossmann
description: Moritz Grossmann was a real 19th-century Glashütte watchmaker of the first rank; the brand bearing his name was revived in 2008 by Christine Hutter. The contemporary manufacture produces watches with signature Grossmann-style components including the handmade proprietary hairspring and the beautifully executed three-quarter plate.
defunct_reason: Master Glashütte watchmaker Moritz Grossmann died in 1885, and his workshop closed after his death; no commercial successor continued the name.
revival_attempt: Revived in Glashütte in 2008 by Christine Hutter, producing watches with signature Grossmann components including a proprietary handmade hairspring and beautifully executed three-quarter plate movement.

keyCollections.name: Benu
keyCollections.description: The brand's core collection, named after the mythical phoenix, featuring the signature Grossmann balance and hand-engraved three-quarter plate.

keyCollections.name: Atum
keyCollections.description: Contemporary collection with a sweeping seconds display and the brand's proprietary hairspring, representing modern Glashütte finishing at its finest.

keyCollections.name: Tefnut
keyCollections.description: Elegant dress watch collection with slim proportions, named after the Egyptian goddess and showcasing the manufacture's hand-applied finishing.

timeline.event: The historical Moritz Grossmann establishes his workshop in Glashütte, becoming one of the town's most important 19th-century watchmakers.
Christine Hutter revives the Moritz Grossmann brand in Glashütte, establishing a new manufacture dedicated to artisan watchmaking.
First wristwatch, the Benu, is presented at Baselworld, showcasing the brand's handmade proprietary hairspring.
Moritz Grossmann begins producing its own escapement components, further solidifying its manufacture credentials.
Unveils its most complex watch ever, the Perpetual Calendar, in gold (EUR 83,000) and platinum (EUR 91,800). Releases the Tourbillon Titanium limited to 12 pieces.
Celebrates 200th anniversary of Carl Moritz Grossmann's birth with the Tremblage Gold edition in rose gold and platinum, and the Hamatic Silver-Plated by Friction anniversary edition.

faqItems.question: Who was the original Moritz Grossmann?
faqItems.answer: Moritz Grossmann (1826–1885) was one of the most important watchmakers in Glashütte's history. He founded the German School of Watchmaking and developed key techniques still used in Saxon watchmaking.

faqItems.question: Does Moritz Grossmann make its own hairsprings?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Moritz Grossmann is one of very few watchmakers producing its own hairsprings in-house — a technically demanding process that most brands outsource to Nivarox.

name: Movado
description: Movado is a Swiss watch brand founded in 1881 by Achilles Ditesheim in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland. The brand is internationally recognised for the iconic Museum dial, designed by artist Nathan George Horwitt in 1947, featuring a single gold dot at 12 o'clock representing the sun at high noon.

keyCollections.name: Museum
keyCollections.description: Movado’s Museum collection is the iconic single-dot dial line associated with Nathan George Horwitt’s 1947 design, forming the brand’s most recognizable minimalist watch family.

keyCollections.name: Bold
keyCollections.description: Movado’s BOLD collection is the brand’s contemporary design line, using larger cases, modern materials, and a minimalist aesthetic that still incorporates the signature Museum dot language.

keyCollections.name: Heritage Series
keyCollections.description: Reissues and reinterpretations of significant models from Movado's archive, including vintage chronographs and dress watches.

keyCollections.name: SE
keyCollections.description: Movado’s SE collection is the sport-elegant line, pairing more robust, water-resistant case styling with the brand’s signature Museum dot motif in a sportier layout.

timeline.event: Achilles Ditesheim founds the company in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, aged just 19.
The company adopts the name Movado, meaning 'always in motion' in Esperanto.
Artist Nathan George Horwitt designs the Museum dial, which later becomes the first wristwatch dial in MoMA's permanent collection.
Zenith acquires Movado. The brand changes hands several times in subsequent decades.
Movado Group Inc. is formed, eventually becoming a publicly traded company headquartered in New Jersey.

Launches the Museum Classic Automatic 40mm with Swiss Made mechanical movements, signalling a return to its horological roots alongside the fashion-quartz range. Reports strong fiscal year results under Movado Group with growth in digital sales channels.

faqItems.question: Why is it called the Museum dial?
faqItems.answer: In 1960, the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in New York selected Horwitt's single-dot dial for its permanent collection — the first watch dial to receive this honour. The name stuck.

faqItems.question: Is Movado still Swiss?
faqItems.answer: Movado was founded in Switzerland and still produces some Swiss-made models, but the company is now headquartered in New Jersey, USA, as the Movado Group. Many current models use quartz movements.

name: Murex
description: For over 20 years, MUREX has upheld Swiss watchmaking at Le Locle. Combining tradition and innovation, the brand produces robust dive and sport watches with a cult following among collectors who appreciate their military-grade specifications, vintage-inspired aesthetics and genuine Swiss manufacture heritage.

keyCollections.name: ISA
keyCollections.description: Flagship Swiss automatic collection featuring clean dial designs, robust cases, and the brand's signature build quality at accessible Swiss-made prices.

keyCollections.name: MUA
keyCollections.description: MUA is Murex’s main Swiss automatic family label across multiple sub-collections, combining accessible Swiss-made pricing, everyday sport-luxury styling, and a modular naming system used throughout the brand’s current lineup.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: MUA functions as the brand’s live product backbone: it ties together the current automatic offerings and makes Murex’s catalog structure legible for buyers and retailers.

referenceDetails.name: Ocean Collection
referenceDetails.note: Official Murex Ocean collection product family.

referenceDetails.name: Edge Collection
referenceDetails.note: Official Murex Edge automatic collection product family.

referenceDetails.name: Rivage Collection
referenceDetails.note: Official Murex Rivage automatic collection product family.

timeline.event: Murex expanded its automatic collection presentation with cataloged MUA product families and modern sport-chic styling.
The brand published an automatic catalog consolidating several MUA-labeled models and variants.
Current site pages continued to show MUA family references across multiple automatic collections.

faqItems.question: What does MUA represent?
faqItems.answer: It is the naming prefix used across Murex’s automatic collections and variants.

faqItems.question: Is MUA a single watch model?
faqItems.answer: No. It is a family naming system spanning multiple collections and references.

timeline.event: Murex is established in Le Locle, Switzerland, entering the Swiss watchmaking tradition.
The brand refocuses on producing robust sports and dive watches with Swiss-made movements, building a cult following among collectors.

faqItems.question: Where are Murex watches made?
faqItems.answer: Murex watches are Swiss-made, produced in Le Locle — one of the traditional centres of Swiss watchmaking in the Jura region.

name: MVMT
description: MVMT is an American watch brand founded in 2013 in Los Angeles by Jake Kassan and Kramer LaPlante via crowdfunding, originally targeting the millennial market with affordable minimalist designs. Acquired by the Movado Group in 2018, MVMT has expanded into eyewear and accessories while maintaining its direct-to-consumer model.

keyCollections.name: Classic
keyCollections.description: MVMT’s original minimalist watch family, defined by clean dials, slim cases, and strap-first versatility that helped establish the brand’s early identity.

keyCollections.name: Chrono
keyCollections.description: MVMT’s affordable chronograph collection, built around the brand’s minimalist styling with functional sub-dials and broad colorway variety for an entry-level audience.

keyCollections.name: Revolver
keyCollections.description: Fashion-forward collection with bolder designs, incorporating textured dials and contemporary case shapes aimed at younger consumers.

timeline.event: Jake Kassan and Kramer LaPlante launch MVMT via an Indiegogo crowdfunding campaign in Los Angeles, raising over $300,000.
MVMT expands into sunglasses and accessories, growing rapidly through social media marketing.
The Movado Group acquires MVMT for approximately $100 million, validating the direct-to-consumer model.
MVMT surpasses $100 million in cumulative sales, maintaining its position as a leading affordable watch brand.
Expands its range under Movado Group ownership with the MVMT Arc automatic collection, marking the brand's first Swiss-movement offering aimed at upgrading its fashion-watch customer base.

faqItems.question: Is MVMT a luxury brand?
faqItems.answer: No. MVMT is a fashion-forward accessory brand positioned in the affordable segment ($100–$250), targeting younger consumers who want minimalist design without luxury pricing.

faqItems.question: Who owns MVMT?
faqItems.answer: MVMT was acquired by the Movado Group in 2018. The brand continues to operate semi-independently with its direct-to-consumer model and Los Angeles headquarters.

name: Nalla Neram
description: NALLA NERAM means 'a Good Moment in Time' in Tamil. The brand's KAALAM MINUTES TIMER is a beautifully designed Swiss-made watch celebrating South Indian cultural identity — one of the most distinctive independent voices in the Indian watch market, marrying Tamil heritage with Swiss horological quality.

keyCollections.name: Kaalam
keyCollections.description: Nalla Neram’s Kaalam is the brand’s debut Swiss-made chronograph collection, built around South Indian heritage themes and presented as a professional-grade watch line with multiple dial variants.

timeline.event: Brand story materials say the Kaalam collection debuted at Time to Watches in Geneva in April 2025.
The brand’s site presents Kaalam as the core collection with black, blue, red earth, and dark blue sky variants.
Nalla Neram launches, bridging Swiss horological precision with Indian heritage. The brand's name means 'the auspicious time' in Tamil.
Expands its Tamil-inspired watch line with new models featuring temple-architecture dial motifs, gaining visibility as one of India's emerging independent watch brands.

faqItems.question: What does Nalla Neram mean?
faqItems.answer: In Tamil culture, 'Nalla Neram' means 'the auspicious time' — the belief that every significant moment should begin at the right time. The brand channels this philosophy into watchmaking.

faqItems.question: Are Nalla Neram watches Swiss-made?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Despite the Indian cultural identity, Nalla Neram watches are Swiss-made, combining Swiss horological standards with design elements rooted in Indian tradition.

name: Naoya Hida & Co.
description: Naoya Hida & Co. is a Tokyo independent watch brand founded by Naoya Hida, known for small-production modern-vintage watches made with contemporary precision and traditional handwork. Its Type series includes hand-wound dress watches, moonphase models, a perpetual calendar, and a chronograph, often with hand-engraved numerals, silver or porcelain dials, and annual purchase applications.

keyCollections.name: NH Type 1
keyCollections.description: The original small seconds design, refined over several generations with compact proportions and engraved dial details.

keyCollections.name: NH Type 2
keyCollections.description: A center-seconds expression of Naoya Hida’s modern-vintage language, including porcelain-dial variants.

keyCollections.name: NH Type 3
keyCollections.description: The moonphase family, using engraved Roman numerals and carefully proportioned classic layouts.

keyCollections.name: NH Type 6
keyCollections.description: A perpetual calendar line introduced as the brand moved into more complicated high-end watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: NH Type 7
keyCollections.description: A chronograph line using vintage Valjoux architecture with modern case and dial execution.

timeline.event: Naoya Hida, former sales director of IWC Japan, founds Naoya Hida & Co. in Tokyo, producing small-batch dress watches.
The NH Type 1B launches with a distinctive textured dial, attracting immediate international collector attention.
Production remains deliberately limited to around 50 pieces per year, with demand far exceeding supply across all markets.

Releases the NH Type 1B and Type 3B with refined hand-finishing from his Tokyo workshop. Gains increasing recognition in Western markets, with pieces selling at significant premiums on the secondary market.

faqItems.question: Who is Naoya Hida?
faqItems.answer: Naoya Hida is a Japanese watchmaker and entrepreneur who previously served as sales director for IWC in Japan. He founded his eponymous brand to create watches blending Japanese design restraint with traditional Swiss movement craftsmanship.

faqItems.question: How many watches does Naoya Hida make per year?
faqItems.answer: Approximately 50 pieces per year. Each watch is hand-finished in Tokyo with small-batch production being a deliberate choice to maintain quality and exclusivity.

seoTitle: Naoya Hida & Co. - Modern Vintage Japanese Watches | Watchatlas
seoDescription: Naoya Hida & Co. makes limited modern-vintage Japanese watches with hand-engraved dials, Type series models and annual applications.
whyMatters: Naoya Hida & Co. is one of the clearest modern expressions of Japanese independent classicism: restrained case sizes, hand-engraved dial furniture, limited production, and vintage cues executed with present-day tolerances.
knownFor: Small annual production and application windows
Moonphase, perpetual calendar and chronograph models

name: Nepro
description: Enter the world of NEPRO watches, where tradition meets modernity. The NEPROSOLAR reissue brings back a beloved Swiss classic — a timepiece that captured imaginations in its original era — now rebuilt with contemporary precision while honouring every detail of the original design for modern collectors.

hq.address: Rue de la Serre 106, 2300 La Chaux-de-Fonds

keyCollections.name: Neprosolar
keyCollections.description: Reissue of a beloved vintage Swiss watch, rebuilt with contemporary precision while faithfully honouring every design detail of the original for modern collectors.

timeline.event: The original Nepro brand is established in Switzerland, producing watches during the golden age of Swiss watchmaking.
Nepro is revived with the Neprosolar reissue, bringing back the classic design with modern manufacturing standards.

faqItems.question: Is Nepro a new brand?
faqItems.answer: Nepro is a revived brand. The original Nepro operated during Switzerland's mid-century watchmaking heyday; the modern revival focuses on faithful reissues of classic designs.

faqItems.question: What is the Neprosolar?

name: Nivada Grenchen
description: Nivada Grenchen was founded in Grenchen in 1926 and was a pioneer in professional dive and aviation watches during the 1950s and 60s. Revived in 2020 under new ownership, the brand has attracted significant collector attention through faithful re-issues of its Antarctic and Chronomaster references.
defunct_reason: Nivada Grenchen ceased production around 1983 as the quartz crisis decimated the market for mechanical sports and dive watches from smaller Swiss brands.
revival_attempt: Revived in 2020 under new American and Swiss ownership, relaunching the Antarctic diver and Chronomaster chronograph to strong collector acclaim and commercial success.

keyCollections.name: Chronomaster

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Chronomaster is central to Nivada Grenchen's revival because it turns one of the brand's most recognizable 1960s chronographs into an accessible modern collector favorite.

timeline.event: The original Chronomaster Aviator Sea Diver chronograph appears as a multi-role air, sea and land timing watch.
The revived Nivada Grenchen brings the Chronomaster Aviator Sea Diver back as a faithful modern reissue.
The collection continues with multiple dial, strap and movement options around the CASD format.

faqItems.question: What does CASD mean for Nivada Chronomaster?
faqItems.answer: CASD stands for Chronomaster Aviator Sea Diver, a name that points to the model's combined chronograph, aviation and dive-watch roles.

faqItems.question: Why is the Chronomaster important to Nivada Grenchen?

timeline.event: Max Schneider founds Nivada in Grenchen, Switzerland.
The Antarctic dive watch is launched, gaining a reputation among professional divers and explorers.
The Chronomaster chronograph debuts, later becoming one of the most sought-after vintage chronographs among collectors.
Nivada suffers during the quartz crisis and the brand fragments across different markets.
Nivada Grenchen is revived under new ownership, launching faithful reissues of the Chronomaster and Antarctic to immediate critical and commercial success.
Continues reissuing heritage models including the Chronomaster and Depthmaster; brand gains cult following among vintage-inspired watch collectors.
Expands the Antarctic and Chronomaster lines with new dial variants and bracelet options, maintaining strong D2C sales through limited runs.

faqItems.question: Why is Nivada Grenchen suddenly popular?
faqItems.answer: The 2020 revival has been widely praised for producing faithful, affordable reissues of genuinely desirable vintage references — particularly the Chronomaster chronograph, which commands high prices in its original vintage form.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between Nivada and Nivada Grenchen?
faqItems.answer: The original Swiss brand was based in Grenchen. After fragmenting during the quartz crisis, the name was used by different entities in various markets. The 2020 revival uses 'Nivada Grenchen' to distinguish the authentic Swiss continuation.

timeline.event: Cullen Chen and Wesley Kwok found NODUS in Los Angeles, focused on high-value dive and field watches assembled and regulated in California.
Launches the Sector series, quickly earning a loyal following among online watch enthusiasts.
Introduces the Contrail GMT, expanding beyond dive watches into aviation-inspired timepieces.
Releases the Contrail III aviation watch and updated Retrospect IV diver in new dial colours, continuing its streak of well-received, design-driven microbrands from Los Angeles.

faqItems.question: Where are NODUS watches made?
faqItems.answer: NODUS’s global supply chain ends in Los Angeles, where each watch is assembled, regulated and tested in the brand’s workshop.

faqItems.question: What is NODUS known for?
faqItems.answer: Exceptional value for money — well-finished dive and field watches that punch well above their price point, popular in online enthusiast communities.

name: NOMOS Glashütte
description: NOMOS Glashütte was founded in 1990 following German reunification, reviving watchmaking in the historically significant Saxon town. The brand produces watches with an unmistakably Bauhaus-influenced design aesthetic and develops its own escapement and winding system in-house, offering exceptional value at its price points.

keyCollections.name: Tangente
keyCollections.description: NOMOS Glashutte's Tangente is the brand's purest Bauhaus statement: a slim steel dress family with sharp typography, clean geometry, and variants from hand-wound classics to modern date and automatic models.

pronunciation.note: German pronunciation; the name means tangent.

referenceDetails.name: Tangente 35

referenceDetails.name: Tangente 33 duo
referenceDetails.note: A smaller, gold-accented reading of the line with the same disciplined dial language.

referenceDetails.note: Adds NOMOS’s ring date to the classic case, giving the line a double date display.

referenceDetails.name: Tangente neomatik 41 Update
referenceDetails.note: The larger modern Tangente with NOMOS’s ring-date system and an automatic calibre.

timeline.event: NOMOS launches Tangente, which becomes the brand’s clearest visual signature.
Tangente neomatik 41 Update brings the DUW 6101 automatic and ring-date display to the family.
Tangente 2date adds a two-part date display to the classic case.
Tangente neomatik 38 Update extends the ring-date idea across the family.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Tangente is the watch most people mean when they picture NOMOS. It anchors the brand’s identity, turns Bauhaus restraint into a signature, and stays relevant through quiet technical updates.

newsItems.title: Tangente launches as an early modern NOMOS model

faqItems.question: What is Tangente?
faqItems.answer: Tangente is NOMOS’s signature dress line, built around slim steel cases, Bauhaus numerals, and hand-wound or automatic movements.

faqItems.question: When did Tangente start?
faqItems.answer: Tangente launched in 1992, shortly after NOMOS was founded in Glashutte.

faqItems.question: Which movements define Tangente?
faqItems.answer: The line is anchored by manual calibres such as DUW 4001, while newer references add DUW 4601 or DUW 6101.

timeline.event: Roland Schwertner founds NOMOS Glashütte shortly after German reunification, reviving watchmaking in the historic Glashütte region.
Launches the Tangente, which becomes a Bauhaus design icon and the brand's best-selling model.
Begins developing in-house movements at the NOMOS manufacture in Glashütte.
Introduces the DUW 3001 neomatik automatic calibre — the brand's first fully in-house automatic movement.
Officially recognised as a manufacture (Manufaktur) under German trade law.
Debuts first-ever worldtimer complication with the Club Sport neomatik Worldtimer and new DUW 3202 calibre at Watches & Wonders 2025. Named Germany's Best Sports Watch Brand 2025 by The European.
Presents the Club Sport Neomatik 42 and a refreshed Lambda collection at Watches & Wonders 2026, marking NOMOS's first participation at the fair.

faqItems.question: Does NOMOS make its own movements?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Since 2005 NOMOS has been developing in-house calibres in Glashütte, including the DUW automatic and Alpha hand-wound families.

faqItems.question: Why is NOMOS associated with Bauhaus?
faqItems.answer: The Tangente line draws heavily on Bauhaus design principles — clean geometry, minimal decoration and functional typography — making it one of the most recognisable minimalist watches.

timeline.event: Ben Küffer founds NORQAIN in Nidau, Switzerland, as an independent family-owned watch brand.
Launches first collections — Independence and Freedom — powered by quality third-party Swiss movements.
Partners with Kenissi (Tudor's movement manufacturer) for exclusive calibre supply.
Introduces the Wild ONE with a proprietary NORTEQ carbon composite case, weighing under 60 grams.
Expands global distribution and establishes itself as one of Switzerland's fastest-growing independent brands.

Announces landmark multiyear partnership with the NHL as Official Luxury Sports Watch. Debuts the 8K Manufacture Calibre skeletonised flyback chronograph movement and Wild ONE Skeleton 39mm at Watches & Wonders 2025.
Launches the redesigned Adventure 40mm and the Wild One Skeleton Chrono with flyback at Watches & Wonders 2026.

faqItems.question: Who is behind NORQAIN?
faqItems.answer: Ben Küffer, a third-generation Swiss watch industry professional whose family has deep roots in the industry (his father led Breitling for years).

faqItems.question: What makes the Wild ONE special?
faqItems.answer: It uses NORTEQ, a proprietary carbon-fibre composite developed with a Swiss materials specialist, making it one of the lightest Swiss mechanical watches ever produced.

Vietnam War era marks an all-time sales high; the M65 becomes a favourite among US soldiers.
The Caribbean 1000 appears on British TV series The Professionals, boosting visibility.
Company resumes under the name A.I. Wajs, later returning to the O&W brand with new models.
Brand continues producing robust tool watches including the OW Ocean and Caribbean models, maintaining its reputation for affordable professional-grade dive watches.

faqItems.question: What is Ollech & Wajs known for?
faqItems.answer: Robust military and dive watches from the Cold War era, particularly the Caribbean 1000 diver and M65 field watch, popular with US servicemen.

faqItems.question: Are O&W watches still made?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The brand was revived in the 1990s and continues to produce updated versions of its classic diver and military designs from Zurich.

name: Omega
description: Founded in Biel/Bienne in 1848 by Louis Brandt, Omega is the Swatch Group's flagship brand and one of the most recognisable watch names in the world. It is best known as the watch worn on the Moon during Apollo 11 and as the official timekeeper of the Olympic Games, and produces the iconic Seamaster, Speedmaster, and Constellation collections.

keyCollections.name: Speedmaster
keyCollections.description: The Moonwatch and Omega's defining chronograph family, spanning early Broad Arrow references, NASA flight-qualified Professionals, and modern Master Chronometer Moonwatch generations.

pronunciation.note: Often called the Speedy by collectors.

referenceDetails.name: First-generation Broad Arrow Speedmaster
referenceDetails.note: The first Speedmaster generation, defined by Broad Arrow hands, a metal bezel, and the earliest collector vocabulary around the line.

referenceDetails.name: Speedmaster Professional

referenceDetails.name: Last pre-Moon Speedmaster
referenceDetails.note: The 145.022 transition point: newer 861 movement, pre-Moon caseback language, and the late vintage profile collectors still chase.

referenceDetails.name: Current Moonwatch Hesalite
referenceDetails.note: Modern Master Chronometer Moonwatch generation with the latest mainstream Professional architecture.

timeline.event: Omega introduces the Speedmaster as part of its professional trilogy.
NASA flight-qualifies the Speedmaster for crewed space missions.
A Speedmaster is worn on the lunar surface during Apollo 11.
The Moonwatch Professional receives the calibre 3861 Master Chronometer update.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Speedmaster is where Omega’s performance story becomes cultural shorthand: a tool chronograph that moved from motorsport credentials to NASA qualification and lunar history, then stayed relevant through modern calibrated reissues.

faqItems.question: Why is the Speedmaster called the Moonwatch?
faqItems.answer: Because it became NASA flight qualified in 1965 and went on to accompany the Apollo era, including the first Moon landing.

faqItems.question: Which reference first carried the Professional name?
faqItems.answer: The 105.012 is the vintage reference most closely associated with the first Professional dial signature.

faqItems.question: What makes the first Speedmaster important?
faqItems.answer: The CK 2915-1 set the template: Broad Arrow hands, a tachymeter bezel, and the earliest collector identity for the line.

funFacts.title: Bezel-first chronograph
funFacts.body: The first-generation Speedmaster used a bezel tachymeter rather than a dial scale, giving the earliest watches their tool-like face.

funFacts.title: Still legible
funFacts.body: The modern Moonwatch keeps the Speedmaster’s core idea intact: a highly legible chronograph with deep historical continuity.
