Revolution magazine and media platform continues as a major voice in watch journalism, with editor Wei Koh leading collector-focused content and brand collaborations.

faqItems.question: Is Revolution a watch brand or a magazine?
faqItems.answer: Primarily a magazine and media platform, but Revolution also produces limited-edition watch collaborations with brands like Artisan de Genève and Bulgari. It is the most influential independent watch publication in Asia.

faqItems.question: Who is Wei Koh?
faqItems.answer: Wei Koh is the founder and editor-in-chief of Revolution magazine. He is one of the most respected voices in watch journalism, known for his deep knowledge of independent and vintage horology.

name: Rexhep Rexhepi
description: Rexhep Rexhepi is a Kosovan-Swiss master watchmaker who trained at Patek Philippe and Rolex before founding Akrivia in Geneva at the age of 24. His personal reputation as a movement finisher is considered by many experts to be peerless among the current generation of independent watchmakers.

keyCollections.name: Chronomètre Contemporain
keyCollections.description: A time-only watch with extraordinary hand-finishing — the signature piece that established Rexhepi's reputation for peerless movement decoration.

keyCollections.name: Chronomètre Contemporain II
keyCollections.description: The evolution of the original, featuring a redesigned movement with even more elaborate finishing, considered among the finest hand-finished calibres of the modern era.

keyCollections.name: Tourbillon
keyCollections.description: An ultra-refined tourbillon showcasing Rexhepi's supreme finishing skills, produced in extremely limited numbers for the most discerning collectors.

timeline.event: Rexhep Rexhepi founds Akrivia in Geneva at the age of 24, after training at Patek Philippe's restoration workshop.
Wins the GPHG Men's Watch prize for the Chronomètre Contemporain, catapulting him to international recognition.
The Chronomètre Contemporain II is unveiled, widely praised as one of the most beautifully finished watches ever produced by an independent maker.
Continues as one of the most celebrated young independent watchmakers; Akrivia pieces remain extremely sought-after with multi-year waiting lists and auction results that rival established maisons.

faqItems.question: What is Akrivia?
faqItems.answer: Akrivia is the brand name under which Rexhep Rexhepi produces his watches. The name derives from the Greek word 'akriveia,' meaning precision or exactitude.

faqItems.question: Why is Rexhep Rexhepi so highly regarded?
faqItems.answer: His hand-finishing is considered peerless among the current generation — trained at Patek Philippe, he applies finishing techniques that rival the greatest historical makers, yet he was self-taught in watchmaking before his formal training.

name: RGM
description: RGM is an American watch brand founded in 1992 by Roland G. Murphy in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. One of the few truly American watch manufacturers, RGM designs and produces watches with movements finished and decorated in-house, holding the distinction of being one of the last surviving American horological manufacturers.

keyCollections.name: Model 801
keyCollections.description: RGM’s Model 801 line showcases the brand’s Pennsylvania-made, hand-finished approach and is associated with the in-house Caliber 801 family, making it one of the clearest expressions of RGM’s domestic watchmaking identity.

keyCollections.name: Pennsylvania Series
keyCollections.description: RGM’s Pennsylvania Series groups the brand’s American-made cases and in-house or Pennsylvania-made movements under a distinctly regional identity tied to Lancaster County watchmaking heritage and traditional finishing.

keyCollections.name: Model 250
keyCollections.description: RGM’s Model 250 is a classic dress-oriented line built around a larger stainless-steel case and a Swiss automatic movement, positioned as a polished example of the brand’s American-made watchmaking range.

timeline.event: Roland G. Murphy founds RGM Watch Company in Lancaster, Pennsylvania — historically America's watchmaking capital.
RGM produces its first fully in-house movement, the Calibre 801, establishing itself as one of the only true American watch manufacturers.
Continues small-batch American production, with movements finished and decorated in-house using techniques inherited from the golden age of American horology.

faqItems.question: Why is RGM based in Lancaster, Pennsylvania?
faqItems.answer: Lancaster was the historic centre of American watchmaking — home to Hamilton Watch Company. Roland G. Murphy deliberately established RGM there to continue that legacy.

faqItems.question: Are RGM watches made in America?
faqItems.answer: Yes — RGM is one of the very few brands that designs, manufactures, finishes, and decorates movements in the United States, making them genuinely American-made.

name: Richard Mille
description: Richard Mille was founded in Les Breuleux in 2001 by the French businessman and watch enthusiast of the same name, and rapidly became one of the most commercially successful independent brands in horology. The brand is known for its extreme use of exotic materials — carbon TPT, titanium, NTPT carbon — in tonneau-shaped cases that can cost over $1 million.

keyCollections.name: RM 035
keyCollections.description: The Richard Mille RM 035 is the original non-tourbillon 'baby Nadal' watch, launched in 2011 as an ultra-light, shock-resistant sports model created for Rafael Nadal. It translated the radical engineering spirit of the RM 027 tennis watches into a time-only platform and became the first Richard Mille to earn Chronofiable certification for durability under demanding conditions.

referenceDetails.description: The inaugural RM 035 established the collection as a lightweight, manually wound Nadal sports watch. Richard Mille states it was launched in 2011, used the RMUL1 calibre, and became the brand's first Chronofiable-certified timepiece.

image.alt: Richard Mille RM 035 Rafael Nadal official model page image

referenceDetails.description: The RM 35-01 updated the concept with a Carbon TPT case and the RMUL3 manual-wind movement. Richard Mille positions it as a more impact-resistant, ultra-light evolution of the original baby Nadal formula.

referenceDetails.description: The RM 35-02 introduced automatic winding to the Nadal line with calibre RMAL1 and Richard Mille's variable-geometry rotor. Official brand history describes it as the answer to client demand for a self-winding Nadal watch.

image.alt: Richard Mille RM 35-02 Automatic Rafael Nadal official model page image

referenceDetails.description: The RM 35-03 is the current collection expression and the fourth watch in the RM 035 family. It introduced the patented butterfly rotor, letting the wearer switch between winding and non-winding modes during activity.

image.alt: Richard Mille RM 35-03 Automatic Rafael Nadal official model page image

timeline.event: Richard Mille launches the RM 035 Rafael Nadal, the first watch in the collection and the brand's first Chronofiable-certified timepiece.
The RM 35-01 Rafael Nadal debuts with a Carbon TPT case and the lightweight RMUL3 manual-wind movement.
The RM 35-02 Automatic Rafael Nadal adds self-winding capability through calibre RMAL1 and a variable-geometry rotor.
The RM 35-03 Automatic Rafael Nadal arrives as the fourth watch in the RM 035 collection, introducing the patented butterfly rotor after three years of development.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The RM 035 matters because it distilled Richard Mille's Rafael Nadal performance-watch philosophy into a more approachable, time-only family that still pushed materials, weight reduction, shock resistance, and wearability to extremes. It also became a long-running platform for the brand's sports-watch experimentation, evolving from Chronofiable-certified manual-wind engineering into advanced automatic systems like the variable-geometry rotor and butterfly rotor.

faqItems.question: What is the RM 035?
faqItems.answer: It is Richard Mille's original time-only Rafael Nadal watch, introduced in 2011 as a lighter, simpler counterpart in spirit to the more extreme RM 027 tourbillon tennis watches.

faqItems.question: Why is the RM 035 associated with Rafael Nadal?
faqItems.answer: Richard Mille developed the family within its long partnership with Nadal, designing watches intended for extreme lightness, shock resistance, and real sports use.

faqItems.question: What makes the original RM 035 historically important?
faqItems.answer: Richard Mille says it was the first Richard Mille to receive Chronofiable certification, making it a landmark durability-focused model in the brand's history.

faqItems.question: How did the collection evolve after the RM 035?
faqItems.answer: The line progressed to the Carbon TPT manual-wind RM 35-01 in 2014, the automatic RM 35-02 in 2016, and the butterfly-rotor RM 35-03 in 2022.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: Richard Mille describes the RM 35-03 as the fourth watch in the RM 035 collection, confirming that the family grew from one model into a multi-generation Nadal line.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2
funFacts.body: The original RM 035's movement was stated by Richard Mille to weigh only 4.3 grams, showing how aggressively the brand pursued lightness even in a non-tourbillon sports watch.

funFacts.title: Collector note 3

timeline.event: Richard Mille launches his first watch, the RM 001 Tourbillon, featuring a tonneau case and movement architecture inspired by Formula 1 engineering.
Partners with Rafael Nadal, creating the RM 027 — a tourbillon weighing just 20 grams — which Nadal wears during Grand Slam matches.
Production reaches approximately 4,500 pieces per year, with average retail prices exceeding $150,000, making it one of the highest-revenue independent brands.
Revenue exceeds €1 billion, cementing Richard Mille's position as the most commercially successful ultra-luxury independent watch brand in history.
Releases RM 16-02 Automatic Extraflat as a fashion-forward play, RM 74-02 Automatic Tourbillon in Gold Quartz TPT, and RM 30-01 Le Mans Classic edition. Brand continues record revenue growth.

faqItems.question: Why are Richard Mille watches so expensive?
faqItems.answer: The combination of exotic materials (carbon TPT, NTPT, titanium, graphene), extreme mechanical engineering, very limited production (~5,000/year), and association with elite athletes creates scarcity and demand that commands six- and seven-figure prices.

faqItems.question: What does 'TPT' mean in Richard Mille watches?
faqItems.answer: TPT stands for 'Thin Ply Technology' — layers of carbon or quartz fibre just 30 microns thick are stacked and cured at specific angles, creating the distinctive marbled pattern visible on cases and bezels.

pronunciation.note: A French name; English speakers often say RICH-ard MILL, but the French pronunciation is softer.

funFacts.title: Racing-machine language
funFacts.body: Richard Mille frames many watches around motorsport, aerospace materials, and visible engineering.

funFacts.title: Extreme athletes
funFacts.body: The brand built fame through watches worn by athletes during competition, including tennis and Formula 1.

funFacts.title: Reference-first culture
funFacts.body: Collectors often discuss Richard Mille primarily through RM reference numbers rather than collection names.

whyMatters: Richard Mille frames many watches around motorsport, aerospace materials, and visible engineering.

name: Richelieu
description: Since 1966, Richelieu has delivered authentic Swiss watchmaking — handcrafted in the Jura with movements assembled by skilled artisans. A quiet pillar of Swiss horological tradition, Richelieu produces elegant, classically finished timepieces for collectors who value genuine Swiss craft over fashion or celebrity.

keyCollections.name: Classic
keyCollections.description: The brand's core collection of elegant, traditionally finished Swiss watches with clean dials, Roman numerals, and understated Jura craftsmanship.

keyCollections.name: Heritage
keyCollections.description: A refined line drawing on mid-century Swiss design codes, featuring slim cases and vintage-inspired details.

timeline.event: Richelieu is established in the Swiss Jura, producing classically styled watches with an emphasis on traditional Swiss craftsmanship.
Continues steady production of affordable Swiss-made watches, building a loyal following among collectors who value genuine Swiss assembly over fashion branding.
Maintains its position as a quiet Jura-based manufacture, offering authenticated Swiss-made timepieces at accessible price points.
Swiss heritage brand continues producing affordable Swiss-made watches, primarily for the European market through traditional retail channels.

faqItems.question: What makes Richelieu different from fashion watches?
faqItems.answer: Richelieu is a genuine Swiss manufacture based in the Jura — movements are assembled by Swiss artisans, not branded fashion accessories. The brand has quietly produced authentic Swiss watches since 1966.

faqItems.question: Where can I buy Richelieu watches?
faqItems.answer: Richelieu distributes through authorised Swiss retailers and select international dealers. The brand maintains a traditional distribution model rather than pursuing mass-market fashion channels.

keyCollections.name: Online Distribution
keyCollections.description: YOOX Net-a-Porter and Watchfinder — Richemont's digital distribution and certified pre-owned platforms, acquired to control the full luxury value chain.

timeline.event: Johann Rupert spins off Compagnie Financière Richemont from Rembrandt Group (South Africa), creating a dedicated luxury goods conglomerate headquartered in Geneva.
Richemont acquires Jaeger-LeCoultre, IWC, and A. Lange & Söhne, dramatically expanding its haute horlogerie portfolio.
Acquires YOOX Net-a-Porter to control online luxury distribution, signalling Richemont's commitment to owning the full digital value chain.
Richemont's jewellery division (led by Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels) drives record revenues, with the group's market capitalisation exceeding €80 billion.

Luxury conglomerate continues managing its watch portfolio (Cartier, IWC, Jaeger-LeCoultre, Panerai, Piaget, Vacheron Constantin, A. Lange & Söhne, Roger Dubuis). Watches & Wonders 2025 in Geneva draws record attendance. Audemars Piguet announces return for W&W 2026. Completes sale of YNAP to Mytheresa in April, receiving 33% stake in newly renamed LuxExperience.

Signs agreement to sell Baume & Mercier to Italy's Damiani Group, reflecting strategic refocusing on top-tier luxury. Closing expected summer 2026. Watches & Wonders 2026 becomes the largest edition ever with 65 exhibitors.

faqItems.question: What watch brands does Richemont own?
faqItems.answer: Cartier, IWC, Jaeger-LeCoultre, Vacheron Constantin, A. Lange & Söhne, Panerai, Piaget, Baume & Mercier, Roger Dubuis, and formerly Montblanc watches.

faqItems.question: Is Richemont a watch brand?
faqItems.answer: No — Richemont is a luxury conglomerate (holding company) that owns multiple watch and jewellery brands. It does not produce watches under its own name.

name: RMS Zeitmeister Watches
description: RMS Zeitmeister represents German craftsmanship since 1964, blending tradition with modern innovation to create timepieces of lasting relevance. The 'Zeitmeister' — time master — name captures the brand's ambition: watches that achieve genuine mastery of time measurement through precision engineering and considered design.

keyCollections.name: Zeitmeister Classic
keyCollections.description: The brand's core collection embodying traditional German watchmaking values — precision, legibility, and restrained design with in-house quality standards.

keyCollections.name: Zeitmeister Sport
keyCollections.description: A sportier interpretation of the Zeitmeister philosophy, featuring robust cases and functional complications for active wear.

timeline.event: RMS Zeitmeister is established in Germany, beginning production of precision timepieces rooted in German engineering tradition.
Continues refining its range of traditionally crafted German watches, maintaining a focus on precision and understated design.
Modernises its collection while preserving the brand's core identity of German precision engineering and timeless design.
Remains a small German independent brand producing classically styled timepieces in limited quantities.

faqItems.question: What does 'Zeitmeister' mean?
faqItems.answer: 'Zeitmeister' is German for 'time master' — reflecting the brand's ambition to achieve mastery of time measurement through precision engineering.

faqItems.question: Where are RMS Zeitmeister watches made?
faqItems.answer: RMS Zeitmeister watches are designed and produced in Germany, drawing on the country's long tradition of precision instrument-making.

name: Roger Dubuis
description: Roger Dubuis was founded in Geneva in 1995 and quickly established itself through complex skeleton movements and the distinctive Poinçon de Genève hallmark applied to all its calibres. Now part of the Richemont Group, the brand produces highly theatrical watches targeting a young, flamboyant luxury consumer.

hq.address: Chemin du Champ des Filles 32, 1228 Plan-les-Ouates

keyCollections.name: Excalibur
keyCollections.description: Flagship collection featuring bold skeleton dials, flying tourbillons, and the signature star-shaped case architecture inspired by the Knights of the Round Table.

keyCollections.name: Velvet
keyCollections.description: Feminine haute horlogerie line combining gem-setting with complex mechanical movements in elegant, fashion-forward cases.

keyCollections.name: Excalibur Spider
keyCollections.description: Extreme skeletonised versions of the Excalibur with carbon and titanium cases, designed for maximum visual drama and lightness.

timeline.event: Roger Dubuis and Carlos Dias co-found the brand in Geneva, dedicated to haute horlogerie with the Poinçon de Genève hallmark.
Launch of the Excalibur collection, which becomes the brand's defining line.
Richemont Group acquires a majority stake, integrating Roger Dubuis into its luxury portfolio.
Richemont takes full ownership; the brand moves into a new manufacture in Meyrin, Geneva.
Partners with Lamborghini for co-branded Excalibur timepieces combining automotive and horological engineering.

Celebrates 30th anniversary at Watches & Wonders with a perpetual calendar, minute repeater and flying tourbillon masterpiece limited to 8 pieces. Launches the Hommage La Placide bi-retrograde perpetual calendar (28 pieces), honouring founder Roger Dubuis's childhood nickname.

faqItems.question: What is the Poinçon de Genève?
faqItems.answer: The Geneva Seal (Poinçon de Genève) is one of the highest certifications in Swiss watchmaking, guaranteeing craftsmanship, finishing, and accuracy. Roger Dubuis applies it to every movement it produces.

faqItems.question: Who owns Roger Dubuis?
faqItems.answer: Roger Dubuis has been fully owned by the Richemont Group since 2012, alongside brands like Cartier, IWC, and Jaeger-LeCoultre.

name: Roger W. Smith Ltd.

hq.address: PO Box 67, Ramsey, Isle of Man IM99 4LN

description: Roger W. Smith Ltd. is a British independent watchmaking firm founded by Roger Smith in 2006 on the Isle of Man. Trained by legendary watchmaker George Daniels and using Daniels' co-axial escapement, Smith handcrafts a small number of entirely in-house timepieces each year, making them among the most exclusive and collectible watches in the world.

keyCollections.name: Series 2
keyCollections.description: Roger W. Smith’s core hand-made wristwatch series, built on the Isle of Man using the Daniels Method and often treated as the clearest expression of Smith’s independent watchmaking.
keyCollections.whyItMatters: Series 2 deserves mid rather than fallback treatment because it is central to Roger W. Smith’s output and to modern British independent watchmaking.

referenceDetails.note: The core production wristwatch designed around the Daniels Method.

The Series 2 prototype is completed.
Series 2 becomes a defining expression of Smith’s mature independent production.

newsItems.title: Series 2 is described on the official watches page
newsItems.summary: The official page states that the Series Two idea came in 2004 and the prototype was finished in February 2006.

faqItems.question: Why is Roger W. Smith Series 2 important?
faqItems.answer: It is the core wristwatch series most closely associated with Smith’s mature use of the Daniels Method.

faqItems.question: Where is Series 2 made?
faqItems.answer: Roger W. Smith watches are made on the Isle of Man.

keyCollections.name: Great Britain
keyCollections.description: A special commission featuring a unique hand-engraved dial depicting the British Isles, showcasing Smith's artisanal engraving skills alongside his watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: Open Dial
keyCollections.description: Skeleton or semi-skeleton pieces revealing the hand-finished movement architecture and co-axial escapement.

timeline.event: Roger Smith begins studying under George Daniels on the Isle of Man after writing to him as a young watchmaking student.
Completes his first fully hand-made watch, establishing himself as Daniels' successor in independent British watchmaking.
Formally establishes Roger W. Smith Ltd. on the Isle of Man.
George Daniels passes away; Smith continues as the sole practitioner of the Daniels method and co-axial escapement tradition.
A Roger W. Smith Series 2 sells for over £400,000 at auction, confirming the brand's collector status.
Isle of Man-based master watchmaker continues producing approximately 10 watches per year, carrying on the legacy of his mentor George Daniels with hand-made movements.

faqItems.question: What is the co-axial escapement?
faqItems.answer: Invented by George Daniels, the co-axial escapement reduces friction compared to the Swiss lever escapement, theoretically requiring less frequent servicing. Roger W. Smith is the only watchmaker who continues to hand-make it.

faqItems.question: How many watches does Roger W. Smith produce per year?
faqItems.answer: Roughly 8 to 12 watches annually, all hand-made by Smith and a very small team on the Isle of Man, making them among the rarest modern timepieces.

name: Rolex
description: Rolex was founded in London in 1905 by Hans Wilsdorf and Alfred Davis before relocating to Geneva, and is today the world's largest luxury watch brand by revenue. The manufacture holds the world's first waterproof wristwatch patent (the Oyster, 1926), invented the date display (Datejust, 1945), and the GMT function (1954), and remains privately held by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation.

keyCollections.name: Submariner
keyCollections.description: Iconic diving watch introduced in 1953, water-resistant to 300 metres, and one of the most recognised watch designs in the world.

pronunciation.note: Collectors usually stress the third syllable: Submariner, not “submarine-er”.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Submariner is the template for the modern luxury dive watch: rotating bezel, luminous dial, Oyster case, and enough design continuity to make old and new references immediately recognizable.

faqItems.question: What is the most classic modern Rolex Submariner reference?
faqItems.answer: The 124060 is the cleanest modern expression: a no-date Oystersteel Submariner with calibre 3230 and a symmetrical dial.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between the Submariner and Submariner Date?
faqItems.answer: The Submariner is time-only, while Submariner Date references add a date window and Cyclops lens. Modern Date references use calibre 3235.

faqItems.question: Why do collectors care about the 5513 and 1680?
faqItems.answer: The 5513 is one of the great long-running vintage no-date Submariners, while the 1680 introduced the date display to the family.

funFacts.title: A design that barely needs a logo
funFacts.body: The rotating bezel, Mercedes hands, round markers, and Oyster bracelet have become a visual shorthand for the entire dive-watch category.

funFacts.title: Green became a collector signal
funFacts.body: Rolex green-bezel Submariner Date references turned a small color change into one of the easiest modern Submariner variants to recognize.

keyCollections.name: Daytona
keyCollections.description: Chronograph originally designed for racing drivers, named after the Daytona International Speedway. Among the most sought-after watches on the secondary market.

pronunciation.note: Named after Daytona, Florida, and its motorsport association.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Daytona is Rolex’s motorsport chronograph and one of the strongest examples of how vintage racing culture, celebrity ownership, and modern scarcity can transform a model family.

faqItems.question: Why is the Rolex Daytona so famous?
faqItems.answer: It combines motorsport design, Rolex scarcity, vintage Paul Newman lore, and a strong modern waitlist culture into one collection.

faqItems.question: What is the Zenith Daytona?
faqItems.answer: The 16520 generation used Rolex calibre 4030, based on a heavily modified Zenith El Primero movement, before Rolex introduced its own calibre 4130 in 2000.

faqItems.question: What changed with the 126500 generation?
faqItems.answer: The 2023 generation introduced calibre 4131 and subtle visual updates around the case, dial furniture, and bezel framing.

funFacts.title: The name is a place
funFacts.body: Daytona refers to Daytona, Florida, and the speedway culture that shaped the model’s racing identity.

funFacts.title: The dial made the myth
funFacts.body: The once-slow-selling exotic dials now nicknamed Paul Newman dials became central to vintage Daytona mythology.

keyCollections.name: Datejust
keyCollections.description: Introduced in 1945, the Rolex Datejust is the brand’s foundational date-display dress-sport watch: a self-winding Oyster Perpetual that helped define the modern everyday luxury wristwatch through its date window, Cyclops lens, Jubilee bracelet and enduringly versatile design.

timeline.event: Rolex launches the Datejust for the company’s 40th anniversary as the first self-winding wrist chronometer with the date shown in a dial window at 3 o’clock; the Jubilee bracelet is created for it.
The Datejust becomes the first watch fitted with Rolex’s Cyclops lens, magnifying the date for easier reading.
Rolesor Datejust variants combining gold and stainless steel begin appearing in the Rolex catalogue during the 1950s, broadening the model’s appeal.
Rolex presents a new Datejust 31 and reintroduces ombré dial styling to the brand’s catalogue in a modern form.
Rolex unveils Datejust 31 models with floral-motif dials, adding an explicitly decorative contemporary expression to the collection.
Rolex introduces a new Datejust 41 with a green lacquer ombré dial in white Rolesor, showing the collection’s continued evolution in dial design.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Datejust matters because it distilled Rolex’s core innovations—Oyster waterproofness, Perpetual self-winding, chronometer precision and an instantly legible date—into one highly wearable template. More than perhaps any other Rolex, it became the archetype of the versatile luxury wristwatch, equally credible as a daily wearer, formal watch, milestone gift or multigenerational heirloom.

faqItems.question: When was the Rolex Datejust introduced?
faqItems.answer: Rolex introduced the Datejust in 1945 to mark the company’s 40th anniversary.

faqItems.question: Why is the Datejust historically important?
faqItems.answer: It is widely recognized as the first self-winding waterproof chronometer wristwatch to display the date in a window on the dial at 3 o’clock.

faqItems.question: What sizes does the modern Datejust come in?
faqItems.answer: Current Datejust models are offered in multiple sizes, notably Datejust 31, Datejust 36 and Datejust 41.

faqItems.question: What movements power modern Datejust models?
faqItems.answer: According to Rolex, Datejust 31 models use calibre 2236, while Datejust 36 and Datejust 41 models use calibre 3235.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: The Jubilee bracelet was created specifically for the Datejust at the model’s 1945 launch.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2
funFacts.body: Sir Winston Churchill and Dwight D. Eisenhower are among the notable historical figures associated with early Datejust watches.

keyCollections.name: Day-Date
keyCollections.description: Introduced in 1956, the Rolex Day-Date was the first wristwatch to display both the date and the day of the week spelled out in full on the dial. Made only in precious metals and closely tied to the President bracelet, it has become Rolex’s flagship dress watch and one of the brand’s most recognizable status pieces.

referenceDetails.name: Day-Date 36

referenceDetails.description: A cornerstone vintage Day-Date reference from the four-digit era, widely seen in classic fluted-bezel, President-bracelet form and strongly associated with the model’s mid-century image.

referenceDetails.description: Important five-digit Day-Date generation introduced in 1988, notable for its double quick-set functionality and wide range of dial variations.

timeline.event: Rolex launches the Day-Date as the first wristwatch to show both the date and the day of the week spelled out in full.
Rolex expands the Day-Date’s day disc offering to 26 languages, reinforcing the model’s international identity.
Reference 18238 is introduced, bringing the five-digit Day-Date generation and calibre 3155 with double quick-set functionality.
Rolex introduces the Day-Date 40 and applies its redefined Superlative Chronometer standards to the fully assembled watch.
Rolex updates the Day-Date 36 with calibre 3255 and launches new ombré, stone and gem-set dial executions.
Rolex adds new Day-Date 36 and Day-Date 40 variations, including ombré dials on Day-Date 40 for the first time.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Day-Date matters because it crystallizes many of Rolex’s core ideas in one model: waterproof Oyster architecture, automatic winding, calendar innovation, precious-metal exclusivity and the President bracelet. It is also one of the few watches whose cultural reputation reaches beyond watch collecting, giving it a rare mix of horological importance and broad public recognition.

faqItems.question: What is special about the Rolex Day-Date?
faqItems.answer: It was the first wristwatch to display both the date and the day of the week written out in full, and Rolex has kept it exclusive to precious metals.

faqItems.question: Why is the Day-Date called the President watch?
faqItems.answer: The nickname comes from the model’s long association with prominent political and cultural figures and from the President bracelet created for the Day-Date at launch in 1956.

faqItems.question: Is the Rolex Day-Date always made in precious metal?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Rolex states that the Day-Date has only ever been made in precious metals, including yellow, white and Everose gold, as well as platinum.

faqItems.question: What sizes does the modern Day-Date come in?
faqItems.answer: The current collection is offered in 36 mm and 40 mm sizes.

keyCollections.name: GMT-Master II
keyCollections.description: Rolex’s GMT-Master II is the brand’s modern dual-time travel watch, descended from the original GMT-Master created for long-haul aviation. Introduced in 1982, it added independently adjustable local-hour functionality, making it especially practical for frequent travelers crossing time zones.

timeline.event: Rolex launched the GMT-Master II, adding an independently adjustable local-hour hand to the GMT formula.
Rolex introduced calibre 3285 to the GMT-Master II line, bringing the Chronergy escapement and about 70 hours of power reserve.
Rolex released new yellow Rolesor and 18 ct yellow gold GMT-Master II models with a new grey-and-black Cerachrom bezel combination.
Rolex added two Oystersteel GMT-Master II references with the grey-and-black bezel, available on Oyster or Jubilee bracelets.
Rolex introduced its first-ever ceramic dial on a white-gold GMT-Master II, reference 126729VTNR.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The GMT-Master II matters because it is one of the defining modern travel watches: a Rolex professional model with genuine aviation roots, a highly intuitive independently jumping local-hour hand, and some of the most recognizable two-colour bezels in watchmaking. It bridges pure tool-watch utility, luxury status, and decades of continuous evolution.

newsItems.title: The new GMT-Master II: Connecting us to the world
newsItems.summary: Rolex introduced yellow Rolesor and 18 ct yellow gold GMT-Master II models with a new grey-and-black Cerachrom bezel combination.

newsItems.title: The new GMT-Master II: Echoing emotions

newsItems.title: The new GMT-Master II: The perfect match

faqItems.question: When was the Rolex GMT-Master II introduced?
faqItems.answer: Rolex introduced the GMT-Master II in 1982 as the evolution of the original GMT-Master, adding an independently adjustable local-hour hand.

faqItems.question: What does GMT-Master II do?
faqItems.answer: It displays local time plus a second time zone using a dedicated 24-hour hand and a 24-hour graduated rotating bezel; it can also be used to track a third time zone in some setups.

faqItems.question: What movement is used in modern GMT-Master II models?
faqItems.answer: Current references such as 126710BLNR, 126713GRNR, and 126729VTNR use Rolex calibre 3285.

faqItems.question: Why is the GMT-Master II bezel two colours?
faqItems.answer: Rolex uses contrasting day-night bezel colours to make the 24-hour scale easier to read and to emphasize the second-time-zone function.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: Rolex says the GMT-Master was adopted by Pan Am flight crews, helping cement its association with global air travel.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2
funFacts.body: In 2025, the GMT-Master II became the first Rolex collection to receive the brand’s first-ever ceramic dial on a production watch.

timeline.event: Hans Wilsdorf and Alfred Davis found Wilsdorf & Davis in London, importing Swiss movements into quality watch cases.
The trademark 'Rolex' is registered — short, memorable, and easy to pronounce in any language.
Introduction of the Oyster, the world's first waterproof wristwatch, proven by Mercedes Gleitze's English Channel swim in 1927.
Patent of the Perpetual rotor, the first reliable self-winding mechanism, which becomes the foundation of modern automatic watches.
Launch of the Datejust, the first wristwatch with an automatically changing date display.
Introduction of the Submariner (diving) and Explorer (mountaineering) collections.
Launch of the Cosmograph Daytona chronograph for motorsport.
Rolex acquires Bucherer, the world's largest watch retailer, marking its first major retail integration.

At Watches & Wonders, debuts the Land-Dweller — a new model generating significant discussion — and updates the GMT-Master II (ref. 126729VTNR). Brand continues to dominate the Swiss watch market by revenue.
Files patent for coloured sapphire crystals in September, fuelling speculation about a Milgauss revival for the model's 70th anniversary in 2026.

Watches & Wonders 2026 expected to bring GMT-Master II 'Coke' bezel (red-and-black ceramic), possible Milgauss return for 70th anniversary, and Land-Dweller collection expansion. Reports indicate 'Pepsi' GMT-Master II discontinued.

faqItems.question: Is Rolex publicly traded?
faqItems.answer: No. Rolex SA is owned by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation, a private charitable trust established in 1945. It has no shareholders and does not publish financial results.

faqItems.question: Where are Rolex watches made?
faqItems.answer: All Rolex watches are manufactured in four sites in Switzerland: the headquarters in Geneva, and facilities in Bienne, Chêne-Bourg, and Plan-les-Ouates.

faqItems.question: Why are Rolex watches so hard to buy at retail?
faqItems.answer: Rolex deliberately limits production to maintain quality control, creating excess demand over supply for popular models. Authorised dealers allocate based on client relationships.

pronunciation.note: Usually pronounced with a long first syllable: ROH-leks.
pronunciation.nameMeaning: A short invented name registered by Hans Wilsdorf for clarity across languages.

funFacts.title: Foundation owned
funFacts.body: Rolex is privately owned by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation rather than public shareholders.

funFacts.title: Four Swiss sites
funFacts.body: Modern Rolex production is split across Geneva, Bienne, Chene-Bourg, and Plan-les-Ouates.

funFacts.title: Tool-watch vocabulary
funFacts.body: Many everyday watch terms for bezels, bracelets, and water resistance are now shaped by Rolex model families.

whyMatters: Rolex is privately owned by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation rather than public shareholders.

name: Romain Gauthier
description: Romain Gauthier founded his atelier in Le Chenit, Switzerland in 2005 after training as a precision mechanical engineer, bringing an exceptional level of finishing rigour to his small-batch production. He is best known for his Logical One wristwatch, which features a uniquely ingenious chain-and-fusée constant-force mechanism.

hq.address: Route du Canal 20, 1347 Le Sentier, Switzerland

keyCollections.name: Insight Micro-Rotor
keyCollections.description: Romain Gauthier Insight Micro-Rotor is the independent watchmaker's automatic micro-rotor collection, spanning closed-dial and Squelette references with prominent hand-finishing.

faqItems.question: What is Romain Gauthier Insight Micro-Rotor?
faqItems.answer: Insight Micro-Rotor is Romain Gauthier's automatic micro-rotor collection, available in closed-dial and Squelette executions.

faqItems.question: What is Romain Gauthier Logical One?
faqItems.answer: Logical One is Romain Gauthier's constant-force collection built around a chain-and-fusee calibre.

faqItems.question: Which Logical One references are current official examples?
faqItems.answer: The official Logical page lists examples including natural-titanium MON00930 and MON00920 plus white-gold MON00910.

timeline.event: Romain Gauthier founds his independent atelier in Le Chenit, Vallée de Joux, Switzerland.
Debut of the Prestige HM, the brand's first timepiece, featuring a hand-wound movement with exceptional finishing.
Launch of the Logical One with its patented chain-and-snail constant-force system.
Introduction of the Insight Micro-Rotor, which becomes the brand's signature collection.
Launch of the Continuum, representing a new design direction with integrated bracelet.

faqItems.question: What makes Romain Gauthier special?
faqItems.answer: Every component is designed, machined, and finished in-house at the Vallée de Joux atelier, with a level of hand-finishing that rivals — and often surpasses — much larger manufactures.

faqItems.question: How many watches does Romain Gauthier produce?
faqItems.answer: Approximately 60 to 80 pieces per year, making it one of the most exclusive independent watchmakers in Switzerland.

name: RSW
description: RSW — Rama Swiss Watch — has been redefining Swiss watchmaking for over a century. Combining boldness, precision and contemporary design, RSW produces avant-garde Swiss timepieces with unconventional case shapes and striking dial compositions, appealing to collectors who want something genuinely different from the Swiss tradition.

keyCollections.name: La Neuveville
keyCollections.description: Classic dress watch collection named after the Swiss lakeside town, featuring clean dial designs with Swiss automatic movements.

keyCollections.name: Le Locle
keyCollections.description: Sport-elegant collection named after the UNESCO-listed watchmaking town, with robust cases and contemporary styling.

keyCollections.name: Romeo
keyCollections.description: Bold contemporary collection with distinctive cushion-shaped cases and expressive dial designs.

timeline.event: RSW (Rama Swiss Watch) is established by the Rama family in Switzerland, building on their jewellery heritage.
Expands international distribution across Europe and Asia with avant-garde Swiss-made collections.
Refreshes the brand identity with a focus on contemporary Swiss design and accessible luxury positioning.

faqItems.question: What does RSW stand for?
faqItems.answer: RSW stands for Rama Swiss Watch, named after the founding Rama family who also have roots in the jewellery industry.

faqItems.question: Where are RSW watches made?
faqItems.answer: RSW watches are designed and assembled in Switzerland, using Swiss-made movements and components.

name: Rudis Sylva
description: Rudis Sylva is a Swiss independent watchmaker from the Jura region with heritage tracing to 1384, crafting exceptional modern timepieces built around the innovative Harmonious Oscillator regulation system. Produced in minute quantities by master artisans, each Rudis Sylva watch is a testament to the extraordinary watchmaking culture of the Swiss Jura.

keyCollections.name: Harmonious Oscillator
keyCollections.description: The brand's signature complication featuring a proprietary twin-balance regulation system that improves rate stability without a traditional escapement.

keyCollections.name: RS12 Grand Art Horloger
keyCollections.description: Flagship piece combining the Harmonious Oscillator with tourbillon and artistic finishing, representing the pinnacle of the brand's technical ambition.

timeline.event: Jacky Epitaux founds Rudis Sylva in the Jura region of Switzerland, drawing on local horological heritage dating to 1384.
Unveils the Harmonious Oscillator, a patented twin-balance system that attracted attention for its novel approach to regulation.
Presents the RS12 Grand Art Horloger, combining the Harmonious Oscillator with a tourbillon complication.
Niche independent brand continues producing its signature harmonious oscillator complications in extremely limited numbers from its Swiss workshop.

faqItems.question: What is the Harmonious Oscillator?
faqItems.answer: A patented Rudis Sylva invention using two coupled balance wheels that beat in harmony to improve timekeeping stability — a fundamentally different approach from a traditional single-balance escapement.

faqItems.question: What does 'Rudis Sylva' mean?
faqItems.answer: The name derives from Latin and old French references to the wild forests of the Jura region, where the brand's roots and workshop are located.

faqItems.question: How many watches does Rudis Sylva produce per year?
faqItems.answer: Rudis Sylva produces very limited quantities, typically fewer than 20 pieces per year, reflecting its status as a niche independent manufacture focused on hand-finishing and technical innovation.

name: Ruhla 1929
description: The family-owned company POINTtec from Munich-Ismaning is one of the largest German watch manufacturers, producing the Ruhla 1929 and Bauhaus brands. Ruhla 1929 honours the legacy of Thuringia's storied watchmaking town — bringing authentic German horological heritage into a contemporary format for modern collectors.

keyCollections.name: Classic
keyCollections.description: Heritage-inspired dress watches drawing on Thuringian watchmaking tradition with Bauhaus-influenced clean dial designs.

keyCollections.name: Garde
keyCollections.description: Robust everyday collection combining German design principles with reliable quartz and automatic movements at accessible prices.

keyCollections.name: Space Control
keyCollections.description: Retro-inspired collection paying tribute to the original Ruhla Space watches worn by Soviet cosmonauts.

timeline.event: The Ruhla watch factory is founded in the town of Ruhla, Thuringia, quickly becoming one of Germany's largest watch producers.
Under East German state ownership, Ruhla becomes the official watch supplier for the GDR, producing millions of affordable mechanical watches.
German reunification disrupts production; the original factory eventually closes.
POINTtec, a Munich-based watch company, revives the Ruhla name as 'Ruhla 1929,' honouring the brand's Thuringian heritage.
Revived German brand from Thuringia continues producing affordable mechanical and quartz watches, trading on its GDR-era heritage and original factory history.

faqItems.question: Is Ruhla 1929 the same as the original Ruhla?
faqItems.answer: Not directly. The original Ruhla factory closed after reunification. POINTtec in Munich revived the brand name as Ruhla 1929, producing watches inspired by the original's heritage.

faqItems.question: Where are Ruhla 1929 watches made?
faqItems.answer: Designed in Germany by POINTtec (Munich-Ismaning), which also produces the Bauhaus brand. Movements are typically Japanese or Swiss.

name: Sandoz
description: Since 1870, SANDOZ has been a watchmaking house rooted in craft, precision and uncompromising integrity. One of Switzerland's most enduring independent names, Sandoz produces refined mechanical and quartz timepieces that honour over 150 years of Swiss horological tradition with elegant, understated design.

keyCollections.name: Dominator
keyCollections.description: Sport-luxury collection with robust cases, automatic Swiss movements, and a versatile design suitable for everyday wear.

keyCollections.name: Heritage
keyCollections.description: Classic collection celebrating the brand's 150+ year history with traditional Swiss dial designs and mechanical movements.

timeline.event: Henri Sandoz founds a watchmaking workshop in Tavannes, in the Swiss Jura, beginning a long tradition of Swiss-made timepieces.
Sandoz establishes itself as a respected mid-range Swiss brand with wide international distribution.
The brand navigates the quartz crisis and continues production, maintaining its identity as an accessible Swiss watchmaker.
Relaunches with renewed focus on heritage and direct-to-consumer sales under the Sandoz 1870 banner.
Heritage Swiss brand continues producing affordable Swiss-made watches, primarily for Asian and Latin American markets through traditional distribution.

faqItems.question: Is Sandoz watches related to the pharmaceutical company?
faqItems.answer: No. Sandoz watches (founded 1870 by Henri Sandoz) and Sandoz pharmaceuticals (now part of Novartis) are completely unrelated companies that happen to share a common Swiss surname.

faqItems.question: What is Sandoz 1870?
faqItems.answer: Sandoz 1870 is the modern relaunch of the historic Sandoz watch brand, emphasising its founding year and Swiss watchmaking heritage.

name: Sartory Billard
description: Sartory Billard is a French independent watch brand producing accessible vintage-inspired timepieces with Swiss movements. The brand has grown a strong community of enthusiasts through transparent communication and quality-focused collector-oriented releases.

keyCollections.name: SB04
keyCollections.description: The brand's signature piece with a distinctive porthole-style case, vintage-inspired dial with sector markings, and a Swiss automatic movement.

keyCollections.name: SB02
keyCollections.description: A dressier interpretation with a thinner profile and refined dial layout, maintaining the brand's accessible vintage aesthetic.

timeline.event: William Sartory founds Sartory Billard in France, debuting the SB04 — a vintage-inspired watch that quickly gains a following among enthusiasts.
Community growth accelerates through watch forums and social media, with limited-edition drops selling out rapidly.
Expands the range with new dial variations and the SB02, while maintaining small-batch production and direct sales.
French independent watchmaker continues producing the SB04 and other models with in-house movements, gaining recognition in the growing French haute horlogerie scene alongside Yema and SERICA.

faqItems.question: Where are Sartory Billard watches made?
faqItems.answer: Designed in France with Swiss-made movements (typically Sellita). Assembly and quality control are handled by the brand with a focus on small-batch production.

faqItems.question: Why is Sartory Billard popular among collectors?
faqItems.answer: The brand offers exceptional vintage-inspired design and Swiss movements at a fraction of luxury prices, combined with limited production runs that create genuine scarcity.

name: Schwartz Etienne
description: Schwartz-Etienne is a La Chaux-de-Fonds-based manufacture specialising in the development of unique escapements and complications for independent watchmakers and brands. The company also produces watches under its own name, often showcasing the proprietary horological innovations developed in its workshops.

hq.address: Rue de la Serre 40, La Chaux-de-Fonds

keyCollections.name: Kala
keyCollections.description: Contemporary collection featuring the in-house ASE 200.00 automatic movement with distinctive micro-rotor, visible through an open-worked dial.

keyCollections.name: Roma Synergy
keyCollections.description: Collaborative collection developed with retailer partners, showcasing custom dial designs atop the brand's in-house manufacture movements.

keyCollections.name: Sirena
keyCollections.description: Diver-inspired collection combining robust water resistance with the brand's in-house movement expertise and distinctive case design.

timeline.event: Paul Schwartz-Etienne establishes a watchmaking workshop in La Chaux-de-Fonds, initially producing movements for other brands.
Launches its own branded collection, transitioning from pure movement manufacture to a full watch brand.
Develops the in-house ASE 200.00 micro-rotor automatic calibre, establishing true manufacture status.
Expands collaborations with independent retailers for exclusive dial editions on its manufacture base.

faqItems.question: Does Schwartz Etienne make its own movements?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Since 2015, the brand produces the in-house ASE 200.00 automatic movement with micro-rotor, making it a true manufacture. It also develops movements for other independent brands.

faqItems.question: Where is Schwartz Etienne based?
faqItems.answer: La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland — one of the two UNESCO-listed watchmaking cities in the Jura mountains.

name: Seagull
description: Seagull is a Chinese state-owned watch manufacturer founded in 1955 in Tianjin, producing mechanical movements sold to brands worldwide including the ST16 used by many independents. The brand offers its own line of affordable mechanical watches and is known for producing China's first self-made wristwatch movement.

keyCollections.description: Seagull’s 1963 collection revives the famous Chinese Air Force chronograph lineage, pairing vintage military provenance with the brand’s hand-wound mechanical chronograph heritage and enthusiast appeal.

keyCollections.name: Tourbillon
keyCollections.description: Sea-Gull complication-focused collection centered on mechanical tourbillon watches, reflecting the brand’s in-house movement heritage and its positioning of elaborate complications at comparatively accessible price points.

timeline.event: Sea-Gull’s official collections navigation lists Tourbillon as a current category.

keyCollections.name: Ocean Star
keyCollections.description: Sea-Gull dive-oriented collection name suggesting robust underwater tool-watch design, aligned with the brand’s broader Ocean Series emphasis on water resistance, professional styling, and accessible mechanical performance.

timeline.event: Sea-Gull’s official site highlights Ocean Series among its current collection navigation, alongside other named series.
The Tianjin Watch Factory is established as China's first watchmaking facility, producing the country's inaugural domestically made wristwatch.
Develops the hand-wound column-wheel chronograph movement for the Chinese Air Force, later known as the iconic '1963' watch.
Becomes the world's largest producer of mechanical watch movements by volume, supplying brands globally with the ST16, ST19, and ST25 series.
Expands its own-brand retail presence internationally, offering tourbillons and chronographs at unprecedented price points.

faqItems.question: How many movements does Seagull produce?
faqItems.answer: Seagull produces roughly 25% of the world's mechanical watch movements annually — over 6 million units — supplying both its own brand and hundreds of other watch companies.

faqItems.question: Is the Seagull 1963 an authentic military watch?
faqItems.answer: The modern 1963 is a faithful reissue. The original was produced in 1963 for Chinese Air Force pilots using the ST19 column-wheel chronograph movement, which Seagull still manufactures today.

name: Seconde Seconde
description: Seconde/Seconde/ is a French independent watchmaker known for its concept of repurposing second hands from vintage watches to create unique, one-of-a-kind timepieces. The project-based brand challenges conventional notions of production and originality in watchmaking.

keyCollections.name: WNRS (Winners)
keyCollections.description: Playful reinterpretation of vintage watches with custom second hands shaped like everyday objects — scissors, flowers, dinosaurs — challenging horological conventions.

keyCollections.name: Official Collaborations
keyCollections.description: Limited-edition partnerships with brands and artists, applying the signature concept of transformative second hands to collaborative designs.

timeline.event: Romaric André founds Seconde/Seconde/ in Paris, launching a concept of repurposing vintage watches with custom-designed second hands.
Gains cult following through Instagram, with drops selling out in minutes and attracting attention from mainstream fashion and design press.
Collaborates with major brands including Fendi and labels in the art world, establishing the concept as a recognised form of horological art.
Launches new-production watches alongside the vintage reworks, expanding access while maintaining the playful design language.

faqItems.question: Are Seconde/Seconde/ watches new or vintage?
faqItems.answer: Both. The brand originally reworked vintage watches with custom second hands, but has since introduced new-production pieces. The signature concept of playful, sculptural second hands remains the unifying thread.

faqItems.question: What does 'WNRS' mean?
faqItems.answer: WNRS stands for 'Winners' — the brand's main collection name, reflecting the irreverent, optimistic spirit of the designs.

name: Seiko
description: Seiko was founded in Tokyo in 1881 by Kintaro Hattori and has produced some of the most significant technological milestones in watchmaking, including the world's first quartz watch (the Astron, 1969) and the Spring Drive movement, which combines mechanical power with electronic precision. The group encompasses Grand Seiko, Credor, and numerous other sub-brands.

keyCollections.name: Prospex
keyCollections.description: Prospex is Seiko's professional sports line: born from the 1965 Japanese diver, built to move across sea, sky, and land, and kept practical, purposeful, and broad enough for divers, chronographs, and Marinemaster references.

pronunciation.note: Short for Professional Specifications.

referenceDetails.name: Marinemaster Professional 60th Anniversary Limited Edition
referenceDetails.note: Marinemaster expression of the line’s deeper professional dive identity.

timeline.event: Seiko introduces Japan’s first diver’s watch, the historical anchor for Prospex.
Seiko’s sports-timing lineage feeds the modern Speedtimer branch.
Prospex continues to refresh its current lineup across diver and special-edition references.
Seiko anniversary Speedtimer and Marinemaster specials keep Prospex tied to brand milestones.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Prospex is Seiko's clearest expression of tool-watch legitimacy: the most historically anchored, category-spanning sports family in the brand.

newsItems.title: 1968 Heritage Diver’s GMT
newsItems.summary: The GMT diver expands the heritage-diver branch beyond pure dive timing.

newsItems.title: 145th Anniversary Speedtimer Mechanical Chronograph
newsItems.summary: An anniversary chronograph keeps Prospex connected to Seiko’s sports-timing history.

faqItems.question: What does Prospex mean?
faqItems.answer: Prospex is short for Professional Specifications, reflecting Seiko’s professional sports-watch positioning.

faqItems.question: Is Prospex only for divers?
faqItems.answer: No. The collection spans sea, sky, and land, including divers, chronographs, field-style watches, and special editions.

faqItems.question: Where does the line begin?
faqItems.answer: Its historical anchor is Seiko’s first Japanese diver’s watch from 1965.

funFacts.title: Name logic
funFacts.body: Seiko spells Prospex as Professional Specifications, a direct signal that the line is tool-watch first.

funFacts.title: Beyond divers
funFacts.body: Although dive watches dominate the image, Prospex also includes Speedtimer and Marinemaster branches.

keyCollections.name: Presage

pronunciation.note: English approximation; Seiko does not publish a single official English pronunciation guide.

keyCollections.description: Seiko Presage is the brand's mechanical dress-watch family, blending Japanese aesthetics, traditional craft dials, and approachable formal watchmaking.

image.source: Seiko official Presage Sharp Edged page

timeline.event: Presage is introduced as Seiko's dress-watch collection for Japanese design and mechanical watchmaking.
A Presage creation marks the 100th anniversary of the first wristwatch to bear the Seiko name.
The Classic Series gives Presage a fresh formal branch.
Presage expands its craft story with an unglazed Arita porcelain release.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Presage is Seiko's clearest bridge between everyday mechanical watchmaking and Japanese craft, giving the brand a recognizable dress-watch identity below Grand Seiko.

image.source: Seiko official Presage Classic Series page

newsItems.summary: Presage release honoring the first wristwatch to bear the Seiko name.

newsItems.title: Unglazed Arita porcelain Presage release

faqItems.question: What is Presage?
faqItems.answer: Presage is Seiko's dress-watch collection, combining Japanese aesthetics with mechanical watchmaking and craft-led dials.

faqItems.question: Which Presage series matter most?
faqItems.answer: Classic Series, Cocktail Time, Style60s, and Sharp Edged Series form the clearest current map.

faqItems.question: What makes Craftsmanship important?
faqItems.answer: It is where Seiko leans into enamel, urushi lacquer, Shippo enamel, and Arita porcelain dial craft.

faqItems.question: Are Presage watches only formal?
faqItems.answer: Mostly, but Cocktail Time and Style60s add more playful and retro interpretations.

funFacts.title: Yo no bi
funFacts.body: The Classic Series leans into the Japanese idea of beauty in everyday utility.

funFacts.title: Enamel lineage
funFacts.body: Seiko connects Presage craft dials to its early wristwatch heritage.

funFacts.title: Urushi depth
funFacts.body: The urushi side of Presage emphasizes lacquer depth and hand-finished surface character.

funFacts.title: Arita gets matte
funFacts.body: In 2025, Seiko used unglazed Arita porcelain for a more subdued Presage dial texture.

faqItems.question: What is the Seiko Astron collection?
faqItems.answer: It is Seiko's GPS Solar collection, officially described as using GPS to adjust to time zones and light as its energy source.

faqItems.question: Which Astron references are represented?

faqItems.question: Why does Astron matter?
faqItems.answer: Astron captures Seiko's technology-led watchmaking identity and has a dedicated official collection page with current image-backed products.

faqItems.question: What is the Seiko 5 Sports collection?
faqItems.answer: It is Seiko's accessible mechanical sport-watch family, officially presented with SKX, Field, and SNXS series branches.

faqItems.question: Which official 5 Sports examples are represented?
faqItems.answer: This page uses official Seiko product pages and images for SSK023, SRPL83, SSK001, and SRPG35.

faqItems.question: Why is 5 Sports important on Watchatlas?
faqItems.answer: It is one of Seiko's broadest modern mechanical collections and a common entry point into the brand.

keyCollections.name: King Seiko
keyCollections.description: King Seiko is Seiko's revived high-grade mechanical collection, officially rooted in the 1961 King Seiko story and organized into KSK, VANAC, and KS1969 series.
