name: Taos
description: Combining the pure vision and exceptional talents of renowned Genevan dial maker 'Atelier Olivier Vaucher' with bold, innovative case design, TAOS creates timepieces where dial artistry is the protagonist. Each watch is a showcase for the highest standards of Swiss dial-making, housed in architecturally ambitious cases.

keyCollections.name: Métiers d'Art
keyCollections.description: Haute horlogerie pieces featuring exceptional artisanal dial work — engraving, enamelling, and gem-setting — produced in collaboration with master craftsmen from the Vaucher atelier.

keyCollections.name: TAOS I
keyCollections.description: The brand's debut collection showcasing Vaucher's extraordinary engraving expertise applied to wristwatch dials and movements.

timeline.event: TAOS is founded by Olivier Vaucher (master engraver), Dominique Vaucher, and Olivier Gaud, realising a long-held dream of creating watches that showcase artisanal excellence.
First pieces are unveiled, featuring exceptional hand-engraved dials produced in the Vaucher atelier, known for supplying engraving to top Swiss brands.
Exhibits at major watchmaking events, establishing TAOS as a niche brand at the intersection of horological art and haute horlogerie.

faqItems.question: What is the Vaucher connection?
faqItems.answer: Olivier Vaucher is one of Switzerland's most respected master engravers, whose atelier has produced dial and movement engraving for Patek Philippe, Cartier, and others. TAOS brings this artisanship directly to the brand's own watches.

faqItems.question: What does TAOS mean?
faqItems.answer: TAOS carries multiple meanings for its founders — symbolising excellence, humility, and creativity. The brand motto is 'L'Art avant l'Heure' (Art before Time).

name: Tiffany & Co.
description: Tiffany & Co. is an American luxury jeweller and watchmaker founded in 1837 by Charles Lewis Tiffany in New York City. While primarily celebrated for fine jewellery, Tiffany has co-branded timepieces with notable Swiss manufacturers including Patek Philippe, and offers its own watch collections known for elegant simplicity.

keyCollections.name: Atlas
keyCollections.description: Collection inspired by the Roman numeral clock on the Tiffany & Co. flagship's Fifth Avenue façade, featuring bold numerals and distinctive design.

keyCollections.name: CT60
keyCollections.description: Named after Charles Tiffany's personal watch from the 1940s, this premium collection includes Swiss-made automatic and chronograph pieces.

keyCollections.name: East West
keyCollections.description: Unconventional collection with the dial rotated 90 degrees, reading from left to right rather than top to bottom — a signature Tiffany design twist.

timeline.event: Charles Lewis Tiffany and John B. Young open 'Tiffany & Young' in New York City, initially selling stationery and accessories.
Tiffany installs the Atlas Clock on its Fifth Avenue store façade, establishing a connection to timekeeping that persists today.
Tiffany begins producing its own watches and movements in Geneva, establishing early Swiss watchmaking credentials.
LVMH acquires Tiffany & Co. for $15.8 billion, expanding the brand's potential in high-end watchmaking alongside LVMH's existing watch portfolio.
Tiffany-branded Patek Philippe Nautilus pieces and collaborations continue to command extreme premiums, cementing the brand's horological cachet.
Debuts high jewelry timepieces at LVMH Watch Week. Opens flagships in Milan and Tokyo.
Unveils the Tiffany Timer at LVMH Watch Week — 40mm platinum chronograph limited to 60 pieces, powered by Zenith El Primero.

faqItems.question: Does Tiffany make its own watches?
faqItems.answer: Tiffany & Co. has produced watches since the 19th century but now primarily partners with Swiss manufacturers. The 'Tiffany Blue' dial on Patek Philippe and Rolex pieces is among the most valuable branding in horology.

faqItems.question: What is a Tiffany dial?
faqItems.answer: A 'Tiffany dial' refers to any watch dial co-signed with the Tiffany & Co. name, typically in the brand's signature robin's egg blue or with the Tiffany stamp. These command significant premiums at auction.

name: Timex
description: Timex is an American watch brand with roots tracing back to 1854, when the Waterbury Clock Company was established in Connecticut. Known for introducing some of the world's first affordable, mass-produced mechanical watches, Timex popularised the 'Timex Indiglo' backlighting and remains one of the world's best-selling watch brands.

keyCollections.name: Marlin
keyCollections.description: Marlin is Timex’s retro reissue collection, reviving the brand’s compact mid-century hand-wound silhouette with a classic dressy profile and enduring collector appeal.

keyCollections.name: Weekender
keyCollections.description: Timex Weekender is the brand’s affordable, casual quartz collection built for everyday wear, defined by simple styling, interchangeable straps, and the kind of versatile layout that made it a gateway Timex for many watch buyers.

keyCollections.name: Expedition
keyCollections.description: Expedition is Timex’s outdoor-focused collection, built around rugged construction, utility-forward features, and a broad field-watch identity that has remained central to the brand’s accessible adventure category.

keyCollections.name: Q Timex
keyCollections.description: Timex’s Q Timex is the brand’s retro quartz reissue line, inspired by late-1970s styling and built around the cult-favorite look of the original Q with its rotating bezel and easy-wearing everyday format.

keyCollections.name: American Documents
keyCollections.description: American Documents is Timex’s premium-minded collection built around American manufacturing messaging and higher-end materials, signaling the brand’s more ambitious design and positioning efforts.

timeline.event: The Waterbury Clock Company is founded in Waterbury, Connecticut — the predecessor to Timex.
The company rebrands as Timex, launching affordable, durable watches with the legendary 'Takes a licking and keeps on ticking' campaign.
Introduces Indiglo, an electroluminescent backlight technology that becomes a defining Timex feature.
Begins the heritage reissue programme with the Marlin and Q Timex, tapping into the vintage watch revival market.
Launches the American Documents line and collaborations with Todd Snyder, signalling a move upmarket while maintaining accessibility.

faqItems.question: Where are Timex watches made?
faqItems.answer: Timex watches are manufactured across multiple countries including the Philippines, China, and India. The American Documents line uses some American-sourced materials but is not fully US-made.

faqItems.question: What is Indiglo?
faqItems.answer: Indiglo is Timex's proprietary electroluminescent backlight technology, introduced in 1992. It illuminates the entire watch dial evenly with a distinctive blue-green glow at the press of a button.

name: Tissot
description: Founded in Le Locle in 1853, Tissot is the Swatch Group's entry-to-mid-range brand and one of the most widely recognised Swiss watch names globally. It is the official timekeeper of numerous major sports organisations including MotoGP and basketball, and is celebrated for bringing Swiss Made quality to accessible price points.

image.alt: Tissot Le Locle Open Heart T006-207-22-096-01

referenceDetails.name: Tissot Le Locle 39.3mm
referenceDetails.note: Official core 39.3mm Le Locle reference from Tissot's current product-card set.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Le Locle is a recognizable Tissot dress-watch name with a dedicated official page and enough current references to explain the family through anniversary, open-heart, and core automatic models.

faqItems.question: What is the Tissot Le Locle collection?
faqItems.answer: It is Tissot's classical dress-watch family, named after the Swiss watchmaking town Le Locle.

faqItems.question: Which Le Locle references are represented?
Why is Le Locle useful on Watchatlas?
faqItems.answer: It has a dedicated official collection page and a clear dress-watch identity with multiple current image-backed variants.

timeline.event: Charles-Félicien Tissot and his son Charles-Émile found the Comptoir d'Horlogerie Tissot in Le Locle, Switzerland.
Tissot produces the first non-magnetic wristwatch, demonstrating early commitment to technological innovation.
Merges with Omega to form SSIH, which later becomes part of the Swatch Group.
Launches the T-Touch, the world's first tactile watch with a touch-sensitive crystal.
The PRX reissue becomes a cultural phenomenon, driving unprecedented demand and attracting a younger audience to mechanical watches.
PRX collection expands to 60 references including Damascus steel and full titanium 38mm variants. Gains significant market share in North America for the Swatch Group.

faqItems.question: Who owns Tissot?
faqItems.answer: Tissot is owned by the Swatch Group and positioned as the group's key brand in the accessible Swiss-made segment, competing with Seiko, Hamilton, and Mido.

faqItems.question: What is the Powermatic 80?
faqItems.answer: The Powermatic 80 is an ETA-developed automatic movement with an 80-hour power reserve — nearly double the industry standard. It's used across many Tissot collections and represents exceptional value for the price.

name: Titan
description: Titan Company Limited is India's largest watch manufacturer, founded in 1984 as a joint venture between the Tata Group and the Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation. With brands including Titan, Fastrack, and Sonata, it produces over 15 million watches annually and operates India's largest watch retail chain.

keyCollections.name: Edge
keyCollections.description: Titan Edge is the brand’s slim-profile design collection, positioned around streamlined cases and modern styling that emphasize a refined, minimal look within Titan’s entry-level watch range.

keyCollections.name: Raga
keyCollections.description: Titan Raga is the brand’s signature women’s collection, inspired by Indian art, culture, and feminine design, and widely positioned as one of Titan’s most recognisable lifestyle watch families.

keyCollections.name: Octane
keyCollections.description: Titan Octane is a men’s sport chronograph collection with bold, automotive-inspired styling and a straightforward performance-first design language, currently presented on Titan World as a live collection page.

keyCollections.name: Bandhan
keyCollections.description: Titan Bandhan is the brand’s couple-watch collection for gifting and shared occasions, centered on coordinated designs that make it a distinctly Indian relationship-focused line within Titan’s everyday entry offering.

timeline.event: Titan Industries is founded as a joint venture between the Tata Group and the Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO).
Launches its first watches, quickly disrupting the Indian market dominated by HMT with modern designs and quartz movements.
Introduces the Edge, one of the world's thinnest watches, demonstrating engineering ambition beyond affordable mass-market pieces.
Becomes India's largest watch company and the fifth-largest watch manufacturer in the world by volume.
Continues to dominate the Indian watch market with a ~60% market share, with growing presence in smart wearables.

faqItems.question: Who owns Titan?
faqItems.answer: Titan Company Limited is part of the Tata Group, India's largest conglomerate. It is publicly listed on the BSE and NSE stock exchanges.

faqItems.question: Is Titan only sold in India?
faqItems.answer: While the majority of sales are domestic, Titan exports to over 30 countries and has retail presence across Asia, the Middle East, and parts of Europe and North America.

name: Toledano & Chan
description: Toledano & Chan is an independent watch brand founded by Jonathan Toledano and Adrian Chan, producing conversation-starting limited editions that attract a design-aware collector audience. The brand combines Swiss and Asian design perspectives.

keyCollections.name: b/1
keyCollections.description: The brand's debut piece featuring a Grade 5 titanium case, solid 18k gold dial, and asymmetrical sapphire crystal — handcrafted with an emphasis on materials and finishing.

keyCollections.name: b/1.3r
keyCollections.description: Evolution of the original b/1 with a ripple-textured 18k gold dial, titanium case and bracelet, and Swiss Sellita movement — the brand's first Swiss-made piece.

timeline.event: David Toledano and Kenneth Chan found Toledano & Chan, launching with a focus on luxury materials (titanium, 18k gold) and distinctive design.
The b/1 debuts, attracting attention for its solid gold dial, asymmetrical crystal, and unconventional case design.
Introduces the b/1.3r, the brand's first Swiss-made piece with Grade 5 titanium bracelet and refined finishing.

faqItems.question: What makes Toledano & Chan unique?
faqItems.answer: The brand emphasises material richness — solid 18k gold dials, Grade 5 titanium cases — combined with unconventional case geometry and asymmetrical crystals that challenge traditional watch design.

faqItems.question: Where are Toledano & Chan watches made?
faqItems.answer: Initially produced with international components, the brand has moved to Swiss manufacturing for its latest pieces, using Sellita movements and Swiss-finished cases.

name: Torsti
description: Torsti is an independent Finnish watch brand producing timepieces with a strong Nordic design identity, using Swiss movements. The brand represents the small but growing Finnish independent watch scene.

keyCollections.name: Field
keyCollections.description: Finnish-designed field watch with a clean, Nordic-minimalist dial and robust construction, powered by a Swiss or Japanese automatic movement.

keyCollections.name: Diver
keyCollections.description: Dive-rated collection combining Scandinavian design restraint with professional water resistance and legible dial layouts.

timeline.event: Torsti is founded in Finland, bringing a Nordic design sensibility to the microbrand watch space.
Launches the first field watch collection, gaining attention for its clean Scandinavian aesthetic and solid build quality.
Expands with a diver collection, establishing a small but loyal following among enthusiasts who appreciate Nordic minimalism.

faqItems.question: Where is Torsti from?
faqItems.answer: Torsti is a Finnish watch brand, designed in Finland with manufacturing using Swiss or Japanese movements. It brings a distinctly Nordic aesthetic to the independent watch space.

faqItems.question: What style defines Torsti?
faqItems.answer: Clean, functional Scandinavian minimalism — legible dials, understated proportions, and quality materials without unnecessary decoration.

name: Traska
description: Traska is an American independent watch brand founded in 2018, known for the Freediver, Summiteer and Commuter. Its tool-oriented watches pair restrained design with iterative case, crystal and bracelet engineering.

keyCollections.name: Freediver
keyCollections.description: The TRASKA Freediver is the brand's inaugural dive-watch family. Its reference history runs from the 1181 launch model to the current sixth-generation 1186, with 200 m water resistance and continuous incremental refinements.

referenceDetails.name: First Generation
referenceDetails.note: The original Freediver that launched TRASKA.

referenceDetails.name: Fourth Generation
referenceDetails.note: Introduced maxi-style applied markers, a redesigned handset and a fully graduated bezel scale.

referenceDetails.name: Sixth Generation
referenceDetails.note: Current generation, with a revised ceramic bezel insert and further bezel-mechanism refinements.

timeline.event: The first-generation Freediver, Ref. 1181, launches TRASKA.
A new boxed sapphire crystal helps reduce overall case thickness in the core collection.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Freediver is TRASKA's founding model and its clearest record of the brand's iterative approach: the visible design remains restrained while each generation revises the wearing and operational details.

keyCollections.name: Summiteer
keyCollections.description: The TRASKA Summiteer is a field-watch family introduced in 2019. It has evolved from the 2191 through current 36 mm and 38 mm forms, combining vintage field-watch cues with a boxed sapphire crystal and applied luminous markers.

referenceDetails.name: First Generation
referenceDetails.note: TRASKA's second release and the starting point for the Summiteer family.

referenceDetails.name: Third Generation 36 mm
referenceDetails.note: The 36 mm version became a permanent part of the line after its special-edition debut.

referenceDetails.name: Fourth Generation
referenceDetails.note: Fourth-generation models use a slimmer 10.55 mm case including the raised crystal and applied Super-LumiNova markers.

timeline.event: TRASKA introduces the Summiteer as its second release.
The 36 mm Summiteer moves from a special edition into the core line.
The fourth generation adopts a slimmer case, boxed sapphire crystal and applied luminous markers.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Summiteer gives TRASKA a field-watch vocabulary of its own, proving that the brand's case and bracelet engineering can work beyond a conventional dive-watch format.

keyCollections.name: Commuter
keyCollections.description: The TRASKA Commuter is an understated everyday sport-watch family that blurs formal and casual use. Its reference history moves from the 3201 through the slimmer third-generation 3203 and current 8231/7231 executions.

referenceDetails.name: First Generation
referenceDetails.note: The original Commuter established the line's vintage proportions and all-occasion brief.

referenceDetails.name: Second Generation
referenceDetails.note: Second generation added a true no-date variant and legibility-oriented dial revisions.

referenceDetails.name: Third Generation
referenceDetails.note: Third generation used TRASKA's boxed sapphire crystal to reduce case thickness to 10.55 mm including crystal.

timeline.event: The third generation adopts the slimmer boxed-sapphire architecture.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Commuter is the most versatile expression of TRASKA's design system: a compact, restrained daily watch carrying the same attention to case architecture as the brand's more overtly tool-oriented models.

timeline.event: The TRASKA story begins in 2018 with the Freediver.

faqItems.question: What movements does Traska use?
faqItems.answer: Primarily Miyota 9-series automatic movements, selected for their slim profile, reliability, and hacking/hand-winding capability.

seoTitle: Traska Watches: Freediver, Summiteer & Commuter | Watchatlas
seoDescription: Traska watches: Freediver dive watches, Summiteer field watches and Commuter everyday watches from an independent American brand.
whyMatters: Traska combines practical specifications and restrained design with iterative case, crystal and bracelet development.

name: Trilobe
description: Trilobe is a French independent watchmaker founded in 2018, known for the Une Folle Journée — a watch that displays time through rotating discs without any hands, inspired by the works of writer Jean-François Thurot. The brand's watches are produced in extremely limited numbers and have quickly found favour among collectors of avant-garde displays.

keyCollections.name: Les Matinaux
keyCollections.description: Trilobe Les Matinaux is the brand's signature poetic time-display collection, using three rotating indicators instead of traditional hands and drawing its name from Rene Char.

referenceDetails.name: Les Matinaux Grey
referenceDetails.note: A grey-dial expression of Trilobe's original no-hands display, with hours, minutes, and seconds shown by rotating elements rather than central hands.

referenceDetails.name: Les Matinaux Blue
referenceDetails.note: The blue Les Matinaux variant keeps the collection's poetic asymmetric display while adding a more vivid everyday colourway.

referenceDetails.name: Les Matinaux Green
referenceDetails.note: The green model is one of the official colour expressions of Les Matinaux, keeping the collection's disc-based reading of time.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Les Matinaux matters because it defines Trilobe's identity: a French poetic approach to time display, with hours, minutes, and seconds arranged as rotating indications rather than conventional hands.

faqItems.question: What is distinctive about Trilobe Les Matinaux?
faqItems.answer: Les Matinaux uses rotating indications for time instead of traditional hands, making it the clearest expression of Trilobe's display concept.

faqItems.question: Where does the name Les Matinaux come from?
faqItems.answer: Trilobe's official page frames the name as a tribute to Rene Char's poetry collection Les Matinaux.

keyCollections.name: Nuit Fantastique
keyCollections.description: Trilobe Nuit Fantastique is the brand's minimal, nocturnal collection, refining the three-indication Trilobe display through grained dials and rotating time discs.

referenceDetails.name: Nuit Fantastique Dune
referenceDetails.note: The Dune model gives the Nuit Fantastique collection a warm, sandy dial tone while keeping the four-part dial architecture described by Trilobe.

referenceDetails.name: Nuit Fantastique Brume
referenceDetails.note: The Brume execution shows the collection's quieter and more atmospheric side, matching the official nocturnal and minimalist positioning.

referenceDetails.name: Nuit Fantastique Silver
referenceDetails.note: The silver model highlights the collection's minimal dial grammar and the rotating hours, minutes, and seconds presentation.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Nuit Fantastique is important because it turns Trilobe's eccentric display into a cleaner, more architectural design, making the brand's unusual reading of time feel calmer and more contemporary.

faqItems.question: How does Nuit Fantastique display time?
faqItems.answer: Trilobe describes the dial as using rotating elements for hours, minutes, and seconds rather than traditional hands.

faqItems.question: What is the character of Nuit Fantastique?
faqItems.answer: It is Trilobe's more minimal and nocturnal collection, with grained dials and restrained colourways.

keyCollections.name: Secret
keyCollections.description: Trilobe Secret is the brand's personalised star-map watch concept, turning a chosen place, date, and time into a custom sky displayed within the Trilobe universe.

referenceDetails.name: Trente-Deux Secret Rose Gold
referenceDetails.note: The rose-gold Trente-Deux Secret maps a chosen location, date, and time into a personalised sky, according to Trilobe's official Secret page.

image.alt: Trilobe Trente-Deux Secret Rose Gold watch

referenceDetails.name: Trente-Deux Secret Steel
referenceDetails.note: The steel Trente-Deux Secret brings the same custom star-map idea to a bracelet model within the current official Secret offering.

referenceDetails.name: Nuit Fantastique Secret
referenceDetails.note: The Nuit Fantastique Secret variant applies the personalised sky concept to Trilobe's minimal Nuit Fantastique design language.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Secret adds emotional personalisation to Trilobe's technical display idea: the watch becomes a custom celestial record of a chosen moment rather than only a novel way to read time.

faqItems.question: What is Trilobe Secret?
faqItems.answer: Secret is Trilobe's personalised watch concept, mapping a chosen location, date, and time into a starry sky on the watch.

faqItems.question: Which Secret variants are current examples?
faqItems.answer: The official page shows Secret interpretations across Trente-Deux and Nuit Fantastique designs, including rose-gold and steel Trente-Deux Secret pieces.

timeline.event: Gautier Massonneau founds Trilobe in Paris, driven by a vision to reinvent how time is displayed on the wrist.
Debuts Les Matinaux at SIHH/Watches & Wonders, introducing the signature three-disc display to critical acclaim.
Launches the Nuit Fantastique and expands the range, establishing Trilobe as one of France's most interesting new independent watchmakers.
Continues to grow internationally, with strong presence in Asian and European markets and recognition at major watch awards.

faqItems.question: How does a Trilobe watch display time?
faqItems.answer: Instead of traditional hands, Trilobe uses three rotating discs: one for hours, one for minutes, and one for seconds. The discs rotate concentrically with markers that align at the reading point, creating an entirely new way to read time.

faqItems.question: Where are Trilobe watches made?
faqItems.answer: Designed in Paris by Gautier Massonneau and manufactured in Switzerland using Swiss movements (L'Epée and La Joux-Perret calibres), combining French design with Swiss watchmaking.

name: Tudor
description: Tudor was created by Rolex founder Hans Wilsdorf in 1926 as a more affordable alternative to Rolex, sharing the same Oyster case construction. Relaunched in 2011 with a much stronger identity and, eventually, in-house Manufacture movements, Tudor has become one of the most sought-after brands in the mid-range segment.

keyCollections.name: Black Bay
keyCollections.description: Tudor's flagship dive family turns the brand's vintage Submariner language into a modern platform, pairing domed dials, snowflake hands, METAS-certified variants, and a broad spread of sizes and materials.

referenceDetails.name: Black Bay 54
referenceDetails.note: Closest Black Bay to the original compact Tudor dive-watch proportions.

referenceDetails.name: Black Bay 58 Burgundy
referenceDetails.note: Burgundy-leaning Black Bay 58 variant that carries the line's modern METAS-era direction.

referenceDetails.name: Black Bay GMT
referenceDetails.note: The travel-focused Black Bay with the burgundy-and-blue 24-hour bezel.

referenceDetails.name: Black Bay 68
referenceDetails.note: Larger-format Black Bay that rounds out the modern size spread and leans into the latest Master Chronometer era.

timeline.event: The original Black Bay launches with a burgundy bezel and becomes Tudor's modern dive-watch statement.
The Black Bay line receives Manufacture Calibre treatment, marking a shift into Tudor's in-house movement era.
Black Bay 54 arrives, bringing the family closer to the compact proportions of Tudor's early diver references.
Black Bay 58 expands with the GMT and METAS-era updates, pushing the line further into modern daily-wear territory.
Black Bay 68 debuts as a larger Black Bay with Master Chronometer certification.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Black Bay is the collection that rebuilt Tudor's modern collector identity: it is instantly recognizable, easy to understand, and flexible enough to hold everything from faithful vintage proportions to the brand's newest Master Chronometer releases.

image.alt: Tudor Black Bay family hero image

newsItems.title: Black Bay 68 - New watches 2025
newsItems.summary: Tudor adds a larger 43 mm Black Bay that broadens the family's size range and brings the line fully into the Master Chronometer era.

newsItems.title: Black Bay - New watches 2024
newsItems.summary: Tudor refreshes the core Black Bay line with a monochrome direction and a stronger METAS identity.

newsItems.title: Black Bay 58 - New watches 2024
newsItems.summary: The 58 family gains new releases, reinforcing it as the most collector-friendly branch of the Black Bay platform.

newsItems.title: Black Bay 54 - New watches 2023
newsItems.summary: Tudor revives the smallest, most vintage-leaning Black Bay silhouette and re-centers the family on early dive-watch proportions.

faqItems.question: What is Black Bay?
faqItems.answer: Black Bay is Tudor's flagship dive family, built to translate the brand's vintage underwater watches into a modern, widely recognizable platform.

faqItems.question: Which Black Bay models feel closest to the vintage originals?
faqItems.answer: Black Bay 54 and Black Bay 58 are the clearest nods to Tudor's smaller historical dive-watch proportions, while the broader line adds larger and more contemporary variations.

faqItems.question: Do Black Bay watches use Tudor manufacture calibres?
faqItems.answer: Many modern Black Bay references do, and the exact movement depends on the model. The family now includes METAS-certified examples alongside earlier in-house generations.

funFacts.title: Burgundy origin
funFacts.body: The original Black Bay launched in 2012 with a burgundy bezel, which became a defining cue for the line.

funFacts.title: Wide size spread
funFacts.body: The family now spans everything from compact 54-style proportions to the larger Black Bay 68.

keyCollections.name: Pelagos
keyCollections.description: Tudor's professional dive family is the more technical sister to Black Bay, built around titanium, fixed strap bars, serious water resistance, and Navy-linked variants that push the line toward uncompromising tool-watch territory.

referenceDetails.name: Pelagos 39
referenceDetails.note: Reduced-size titanium Pelagos that bridges land and sea without losing the family brief.

referenceDetails.name: Pelagos FXD
referenceDetails.note: Fixed-bar military-leaning Pelagos built for serious underwater use and strap security.

referenceDetails.name: Pelagos FXD GMT
referenceDetails.note: French Naval Aviation-inspired FXD that adds a GMT function and keeps the fixed-bar architecture.

referenceDetails.name: Pelagos Ultra
referenceDetails.note: The deepest and most technically ambitious Pelagos, built around 1,000 metres of water resistance.

timeline.event: Pelagos joins Tudor's lineup alongside Black Bay and establishes the brand's titanium-first diver identity.
Pelagos FXD launches with fixed strap bars and a French Navy-centered brief.
Pelagos 39 broadens the family with a more wearable format that still keeps the technical dive-watch brief intact.
Pelagos 39 wins the GPHG Best Sports Watch prize, confirming the line's wider collector appeal.
Pelagos FXD GMT and Pelagos FXD Chrono expand the platform into travel and chronograph territory.
Pelagos Ultra arrives with 1,000 metres of water resistance and becomes the line's deepest diver.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Pelagos matters because it shows Tudor at its purest tool-watch extreme: lighter materials, real underwater credentials, and military-derived thinking that gives the brand credibility well beyond style alone.

newsItems.title: Pelagos Ultra
newsItems.summary: Tudor pushes the Pelagos line to 1,000 metres of water resistance with a redesigned titanium case and bracelet system.

newsItems.title: Pelagos FXD GMT - New watches 2024
newsItems.summary: A French Naval Aviation-inspired GMT joins the FXD family, keeping the fixed-bar architecture and military utility intact.

newsItems.title: Pelagos FXD Chrono "Cycling Edition" - New watches 2024
newsItems.summary: The FXD platform expands into a chronograph, showing how far Tudor can push the tool-watch brief without losing the family identity.

newsItems.title: TUDOR Takes Home the Best Sports Watch Prize at the GPHG
newsItems.summary: Pelagos 39 wins Best Sports Watch, confirming that the line now resonates far beyond pure dive-watch specialists.

faqItems.question: What makes Pelagos different from Black Bay?
faqItems.answer: Pelagos is Tudor's more technical diver line: titanium-first, more purpose-built, and more directly rooted in professional underwater use.

faqItems.question: How much water resistance does Pelagos offer?
faqItems.answer: It depends on the reference. The family spans 200-metre and 500-metre models, while Pelagos Ultra extends the line to 1,000 metres.

faqItems.question: Why do some Pelagos models use fixed strap bars?
faqItems.answer: The fixed-bar design is part of the line's tool-watch identity and helps keep the watch secure in demanding conditions.

funFacts.title: Land and sea bridge
funFacts.body: Pelagos 39 was positioned as a watch that could move comfortably between dive-watch duty and everyday wear.

funFacts.title: Deep-water apex
funFacts.body: Pelagos Ultra pushed the line to 1,000 metres, making it the deepest Pelagos Tudor has built so far.

keyCollections.name: Royal
keyCollections.description: The Tudor Royal is the brand’s sport-chic integrated-bracelet collection, combining a notched bezel, automatic movements, 100m water resistance, and a broad mix of sizes and dial executions. Reintroduced as a modern family in 2020 and substantially refreshed in 2026, it sits at the intersection of classic dress styling and everyday steel sports-watch practicality.

referenceDetails.functions: Hours, minutes, seconds, day at 12, date at 3

image.alt: Tudor Royal 41 Day-Date ref. M28600-0009 with salmon dial
Tudor Royal 38 ref. M28500-0007 with salmon dial
Tudor Royal 36 ref. M2836C1A0-0101 with black dial

referenceDetails.functions: Hours, minutes, seconds, day at 12, date at 3

image.alt: Tudor Royal 40 ref. M2840D1A0-0001 with black dial

timeline.event: Tudor reintroduced Royal as a modern integrated-bracelet collection, initially in select Asian markets before global rollout, with 41mm, 38mm, 34mm and 28mm sizes.
Tudor expanded the Royal line with new radial-brushed light salmon and chocolate brown dial variants across multiple references.
Tudor thoroughly refreshed the Royal with new 30mm, 36mm and 40mm sizes, redesigned bezel, revised end links and lugs, T-fit clasp, and COSC-certified manufacture calibres.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The Royal matters because it represents Tudor’s most explicit take on the affordable integrated-bracelet sport-chic watch: a category usually dominated by much costlier rivals. It also shows Tudor’s willingness to mix classic Roman-numeral elegance with practical specs like 100m water resistance, while the 2026 update elevated the line with manufacture movements and a more sophisticated bracelet-and-case execution.

gallery.alt: Tudor Royal 38 salmon dial product image

newsItems.title: Introducing The Tudor Royal Collection
newsItems.summary: Hodinkee covered the global launch of the modern Tudor Royal after its initial Asia-market debut, highlighting its integrated bracelet, day-date flagship, and accessible positioning.

newsItems.title: TUDOR Royal - 2023 new watches
newsItems.summary: Tudor announced expanded Royal dial options in light salmon and chocolate brown, extending the range’s color palette and appeal.

newsItems.title: Tudor Royal - New watches 2026
newsItems.summary: The brand unveiled a major Royal refresh with new 30mm, 36mm, and 40mm cases, revamped bracelet integration, T-fit clasp, and updated styling.

newsItems.title: Introducing: Tudor Revitalizes The Royal In 40, 36, And 30mm
newsItems.summary: Hodinkee reported on the 2026 Royal update, noting the redesigned case/bracelet details, manufacture calibres, and refreshed color offerings.

faqItems.question: When was the modern Tudor Royal introduced?
faqItems.answer: The modern Tudor Royal collection first appeared in 2020, initially in select Asian markets before a broader global launch later that year.

faqItems.question: What defines the Tudor Royal design?
faqItems.answer: Key traits include its integrated five-link bracelet, alternating polished-and-notched bezel treatment, Roman-numeral or stick-marker dials, and a sporty-chic overall profile.

faqItems.question: Which Royal models have a day display?
faqItems.answer: In the 2020-2025 generation, the 41mm model carried the day-date layout. In the 2026 refresh, the day complication moved to the 40mm version.

faqItems.question: Are Tudor Royal watches water resistant?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Tudor specifies 100 metres of water resistance for the Royal collection.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: The name Royal is historical for Tudor: the brand says it was first used in the 1950s to emphasize superior quality.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2
funFacts.body: The 2026 refresh changed more than dial colors: Tudor also revised the end links and lugs so bracelet links would not touch the case, helping prevent abrasion.

keyCollections.description: Named for the year the Tudor name was first registered, the Tudor 1926 is the brand’s classic everyday dress-watch family, defined by domed embossed dials, alternating Arabic numerals and markers, automatic movements, and a broad size range spanning compact to full-size references.

referenceDetails.description: 36 mm steel 1926 with white embossed dial, date display, five-diamond hour markers, and seven-row steel bracelet.
39 mm steel 1926 with white domed embossed dial, gold-tone hands and markers, date at 3 o’clock, and seven-row steel bracelet.
41 mm steel 1926 with white embossed dial, date display, polished smooth bezel, and seven-row steel bracelet.

timeline.event: Tudor introduced the 1926 collection as a new classic mechanical line, naming it after the year the Tudor name was registered.
Tudor issued a 1926 new-watches press kit, indicating a refresh/continuation of the line within the brand’s annual novelties cycle.
Tudor expanded the family with the 1926 Luna moon-phase models, adding a more complicated dress-oriented variant to the collection.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: The 1926 matters because it anchors Tudor’s non-sporty side: a more affordable, classically styled automatic collection that connects the brand’s early history to modern buyers who want Swiss-made quality, versatile sizing, and restrained design outside the Black Bay universe.

newsItems.title: TUDOR 1926 launch press material published
newsItems.summary: Official launch material described the 1926 as a new line paying tribute to Tudor’s origins and positioned it as a classic mechanical collection.

newsItems.title: 1926 included in Tudor New Watches 2021 press kit
newsItems.summary: Tudor published an updated 1926 press kit in its 2021 new-watches materials, showing the line remained an active part of the catalog.

newsItems.title: Tudor 1926 Luna announced
newsItems.summary: Tudor added the 1926 Luna, introducing a moon-phase execution and expanding the classical 1926 family with a more decorative complication.

newsItems.title: The Tudor 1926 Luna Adds A Moonphase Complication To The Lineup
newsItems.summary: Hodinkee covered the 1926 Luna as an expansion of Tudor’s dress-watch offering, highlighting its refined styling and moon-phase display.

faqItems.question: When was the Tudor 1926 introduced?
faqItems.answer: The Tudor 1926 was introduced in 2018, with official launch material tied to that year’s release cycle.

faqItems.question: Why is it called 1926?
faqItems.answer: The collection is named after 1926, the year the Tudor name was first registered, making the line a direct nod to the brand’s origins.

faqItems.question: What sizes does the Tudor 1926 come in?
faqItems.answer: The current collection page shows 28 mm, 36 mm, 39 mm, and 41 mm case sizes, depending on reference and configuration.

faqItems.question: What movement does the Tudor 1926 use?
faqItems.answer: The standard date models documented here use the automatic Tudor Calibre T601 with an approximately 38-hour power reserve.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: The 1926 collection takes its name from the year the Tudor trademark was registered rather than from a historic single model.

funFacts.title: Collector note 2
funFacts.body: In 2025 Tudor broadened the line with the 1926 Luna, adding a moon-phase complication to one of the brand’s most traditional collections.

timeline.event: Hans Wilsdorf registers the Tudor brand in Geneva as a more affordable alternative to Rolex.
Montres Tudor SA is officially incorporated on 6 March, formalising the brand's structure.
Tudor supplies dive watches to the French Navy, beginning a long association with military and professional diving.
Tudor introduces its first in-house movement, the MT5621, in the Pelagos, marking a major step towards manufacture independence.
The Tudor Royal is launched, establishing the brand firmly in the integrated sports watch segment.
Launches Black Bay 68 (43mm, METAS-certified), Pelagos Ultra (1000m titanium), first moonphase complication, and Black Bay 58 Burgundy — all with Master Chronometer certification.
Celebrates 100th anniversary — the Tudor name was registered by Hans Wilsdorf on 17 February 1926. Centenary collection expected at Watches & Wonders 2026.

faqItems.question: What is the relationship between Tudor and Rolex?
faqItems.answer: Tudor was founded by Hans Wilsdorf, the same entrepreneur who founded Rolex, as a way to offer watches with Rolex-quality cases and bracelets but at a lower price point. Montres Tudor SA is a wholly owned subsidiary of Rolex SA, though Tudor operates as an independent brand with its own design language, collections, and in-house movements.

faqItems.question: Does Tudor make its own movements?
faqItems.answer: Yes, since 2015 Tudor has developed and produced in-house calibres for its core collections, including the Black Bay and Pelagos. Earlier models used movements from ETA SA and other suppliers. Tudor's in-house calibres carry COSC chronometer certification and feature silicon hairsprings.

faqItems.question: Is Tudor considered a luxury watch brand?
faqItems.answer: Tudor occupies the premium segment of the watch market, offering Swiss-made mechanical watches with high production standards. While it sits below Rolex in terms of price and prestige, it is generally considered a genuine luxury brand with strong collector appeal, particularly for its vintage-inspired Black Bay models.

timeline.event: The Urofa watch factory is established in Glashütte, Saxony, forming the foundation of what becomes Tutima.
Tutima begins producing the Fliegerchronograph for the German Luftwaffe, establishing its reputation for precision aviation timekeeping.
The Glashütte factory is destroyed at the end of the Second World War, forcing operations to restart from scratch.
The Tutima brand name is officially registered, consolidating the company's identity.
Tutima relocates production fully back to Glashütte, reaffirming its roots in the historic German watchmaking village.

faqItems.question: Is Tutima a genuine Glashütte watchmaker?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Tutima Uhrenfabrik is based in Glashütte, Saxony, and assembles its watches there using movements that meet the Glashütte origin requirements. The brand traces its roots to the Urofa factory founded in 1927, making it one of the historic watchmaking names from this German watchmaking centre.

faqItems.question: What makes Tutima famous in the aviation watch world?
faqItems.answer: Tutima's reputation in aviation stems from its production of the Fliegerchronograph for the German Luftwaffe during the Second World War, and its subsequent supply of pilot's chronographs to NATO forces. The M2 model continues to serve as official equipment for NATO and Bundeswehr pilots today.

name: U-BOAT

hq.address: Via per San Gennaro 13, 55012 Gragnano, Capannori (Lucca)

description: U-BOAT is an Italian luxury watch brand founded in 2000 by Italo Fontana in Florence, inspired by a 1942 commission for Italian naval officers. The brand is renowned for its oversized, asymmetrical cases with crowns positioned at the 9 o'clock position and bold military-influenced aesthetics.

keyCollections.name: Classico
keyCollections.description: U-Boat’s Classico is the brand’s core oversized watch family and the style that most clearly defines its left-crown, bold-numeral aesthetic, presented across multiple case sizes and materials including steel, titanium, bronze, and PVD variants.

keyCollections.name: Flightdeck
keyCollections.description: U-BOAT’s Flightdeck is an aviation-inspired collection built around oversized, highly legible dials and instrument-panel styling, while preserving the brand’s signature left-side crown and bold Tuscan tool-watch character.

keyCollections.name: Sommerso
keyCollections.description: U-BOAT’s Sommerso is the brand’s dive-led line, defined by layered dial construction, oversized proportions, and professional-diving orientation, with current official pages describing the range as highly water resistant and technically bold.

timeline.event: Italian Navy Commander Gino Sorgini commissions a specification for a large, rugged watch for submarine crews — an idea that inspires U-Boat's design philosophy decades later.
Italo Fontana founds U-Boat in Florence, Italy, reviving the original 1942 naval watch concept.
The first U-Boat Classico watches are introduced at Basel World, featuring the distinctive left-hand crown placement.
U-Boat expands its range with new materials and case sizes, growing its presence in international markets.
The brand launches the Sommerso collection, broadening U-Boat's appeal beyond its military and diving heritage.

faqItems.question: Why is the crown on the left side of U-Boat watches?
faqItems.answer: The left-side crown placement is the brand's most distinctive design feature, derived from the original 1942 Italian Navy specification that inspired Italo Fontana. The positioning was practical for naval use, preventing the crown from digging into the wearer's wrist during physical activity, and it has become the defining trademark of every U-Boat timepiece.

faqItems.question: Where are U-Boat watches made?
faqItems.answer: U-Boat watches are designed and assembled in Italy, where the brand is headquartered. The movements used are Swiss-sourced, primarily from ETA and Sellita, while the cases and overall design work are Italian in origin, blending Swiss mechanical quality with Italian craftsmanship and aesthetic sensibility.

timeline.event: Ulysse Nardin founds his watchmaking company in Le Locle, Switzerland, at the age of 23.
The company receives its first series of precision certificates from the Neuchâtel Observatory for its marine chronometers.
Rolf W. Schnyder acquires the company and, working with watchmaker Ludwig Oechslin, begins its revival and transformation.
The Freak is launched at Basel World, pioneering the use of silicon in mechanical watch movements and rotating the movement itself as a time indicator.
Ulysse Nardin and Girard-Perregaux complete a management buyout from Kering, forming the independent Sowind Group.
Launches the Diver [AIR] at Watches & Wonders — the world's lightest mechanical dive watch at 52 grams. Collaborates with Urwerk on the UR-Freak, a 100-piece limited edition.

faqItems.question: What is Ulysse Nardin famous for historically?
faqItems.answer: Ulysse Nardin earned global fame for its exceptionally precise marine chronometers, which were supplied to over 50 navies and shipping fleets from the late 19th century until the 1950s. Between 1846 and 1975, the company received 4,324 precision certificates from the Neuchâtel Observatory — a record unmatched by any other watchmaker.

faqItems.question: Who owns Ulysse Nardin today?
faqItems.answer: Ulysse Nardin is owned by the Sowind Group, an independent holding company formed through a management buyout from the French luxury group Kering in 2022. The Sowind Group also owns Girard-Perregaux, with both brands sharing leadership under CEO Patrick Pruniaux.

faqItems.question: What is the Freak collection?
faqItems.answer: The Freak, introduced in 2001, is one of the most revolutionary watch designs of the 21st century. It has no crown, no dial, and no hands in the traditional sense. Instead, the entire movement rotates to indicate the time. It was also the first watch to use silicon components in its escapement, pioneering a material now used across the industry.

name: UNDONE
description: UNDONE is a Hong Kong-based watch brand founded in 2014, offering customisable watches at accessible price points with a wide range of dial and strap options. The brand has built a large following through collaborations with popular culture properties and its transparent online customisation platform.

keyCollections.name: Urban
keyCollections.description: Undone's core collection offering extensive customisation across case shape, dial, colour, and strap, aimed at watch enthusiasts who want a personalised timepiece. The Urban draws on vintage watch archetypes — field watches, dress watches, and classics — and allows buyers to configure their watch through an online tool. It is fitted with Japanese automatic or quartz movements.

keyCollections.name: Aqua
keyCollections.description: A dive-inspired collection featuring 200-metre water resistance, rotating bezels, and robust construction, while retaining Undone's signature customisation options. The Aqua appeals to fans of vintage-style diving watches who want personal expression in a tool watch format. Colourful dials and varied bezel inserts make it one of the brand's most visually playful lines.

keyCollections.name: Basecamp
keyCollections.description: Undone's adventure-focused collection inspired by mid-century exploration and field watches, featuring bold numerals, canvas or leather straps, and vintage colour palettes. The Basecamp is designed for outdoor enthusiasts and collectors drawn to the aesthetic of classic military and expedition timepieces.

timeline.event: Undone is founded in Hong Kong, positioning itself as a customisable watch brand targeting online-native consumers.
The brand launches its first Kickstarter campaign, quickly surpassing its funding goal and gaining international attention.
Undone opens its first physical retail experience, expanding beyond pure e-commerce while retaining its direct-to-consumer model.
The brand releases a series of licensed collaborations with cultural and entertainment properties, broadening its audience beyond traditional watch collectors.
Undone expands its customisation platform, offering a wider range of case materials and dial options for greater personalisation.

faqItems.question: How does Undone's customisation process work?
faqItems.answer: Undone allows customers to configure their watch through an online builder, choosing from various case shapes, dial designs, colour combinations, case materials, and strap options. The personalised watch is then assembled and shipped directly to the customer. Lead times vary depending on the complexity of the configuration.

faqItems.question: What movements does Undone use?
faqItems.answer: Undone primarily uses Japanese movements from Miyota (automatic) and Seiko NH-series (automatic) for its mechanical watches, as well as Ronda quartz movements. The brand focuses on design and customisation rather than movement manufacture, keeping costs accessible while ensuring reliability.

timeline.event: Simone Nunziato and Costantino Cugini found Unimatic in Milan, launching the U1 dive watch through their website in limited numbers.
The brand gains rapid international attention from the watch collecting community, selling out its first production runs within hours.
Unimatic introduces the U2 and U3 models, expanding the range while maintaining strict limited-edition production discipline.
The brand begins producing collaborative limited editions with select partners and retailers, further fuelling collector interest.
Unimatic releases the Modello Tre in new configurations, consolidating its position as one of the most sought-after independent Italian microbrands.

faqItems.question: Why are Unimatic watches so hard to buy?
faqItems.answer: Unimatic intentionally produces very small batches — often just a few hundred pieces per release — and sells them exclusively through its own website. This limited distribution model creates high demand relative to supply, meaning new releases routinely sell out within minutes and command significant premiums on the secondary market.

faqItems.question: What movements does Unimatic use?
faqItems.answer: Unimatic uses Swiss and Japanese movements from established suppliers, including ETA and Seiko NH-series automatics. The brand's focus is on design and finishing rather than movement manufacture, ensuring reliability while keeping the watches competitively priced for collectors.

whyMatters: Unimatic is a defining modern Italian microbrand: its minimal, instantly recognisable cases make a coherent platform for divers, field watches, chronographs and limited collaborations.

name: Union Glashütte
description: Union Glashütte is a German watch brand originally founded in 1893 in the watchmaking town of Glashütte, Saxony. Acquired by the Swatch Group in 1995, it produces elegant mechanical timepieces in the classic German tradition, with movement parts bearing the coveted Glashütte hallmark.

keyCollections.name: Noramis
keyCollections.description: Noramis is Union Glashütte’s classic-minded collection, blending 1960s and 1970s elegance with modern automatic movements, curved crystals, domed dials, and a more timeless, refined design language.

keyCollections.name: Belisar
keyCollections.description: Belisar is Union Glashütte’s sporty, versatile collection, spanning chronographs and date models with a strong character and distinctive screw-down flanks, positioned for wearers who want mechanical watchmaking with a more dynamic everyday personality.

keyCollections.name: Seris
keyCollections.description: Seris is Union Glashütte’s elegant, feminine collection, centered on refined dial layouts, automatic movements, and a dressier profile that aims for understated daily wear with clear Glashütte watchmaking cues.

timeline.event: Union Glashütte is founded in Glashütte, Saxony, as part of the flourishing German watchmaking industry of the late 19th century.
The brand produces pocket watches and wristwatches for both civilian and export markets during the interwar period.
Following East German nationalisation, Union Glashütte becomes part of the combined VEB Glashütter Uhrenbetriebe state enterprise.
After German reunification, Union Glashütte re-establishes itself as an independent brand in the reviving Glashütte watchmaking scene.
The Swatch Group acquires Union Glashütte, securing its position and enabling investment in its product range and manufacture facilities.

faqItems.question: Is Union Glashütte a genuine Glashütte watchmaker?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Union Glashütte has been based in Glashütte, Saxony since its founding in 1893, and its watches are assembled in that town using movements that comply with the Glashütte origin requirements. The brand forms part of the Swatch Group's portfolio of Glashütte-based watchmakers, alongside the more prominent Glashütte Original.

faqItems.question: Who owns Union Glashütte?
faqItems.answer: Union Glashütte is owned by the Swatch Group, the world's largest watch manufacturer, which acquired the brand in 2000. Despite being part of this large corporate structure, the brand continues to position itself as an authentic Glashütte watchmaker with roots going back to 1893.

name: Universal Geneve
description: Universal Genève was founded in 1894 in Geneva and was considered in the mid-20th century to be among the finest chronograph manufacturers in Switzerland, competing with Patek Philippe and Vacheron Constantin. The brand has been revived by new ownership focused on restoring its heritage chronograph models for contemporary collectors.

keyCollections.name: Polerouter
keyCollections.description: Universal Genève's most celebrated model, originally introduced in 1954 and designed by Gérald Genta for Scandinavian Airlines' polar routes. The Polerouter featured a pioneering microtor (miniature rotor) automatic movement that kept the watch slim, and became the preferred choice of airline pilots flying over the Arctic. Its elegant cushion-shaped case and understated dial have made it one of the most coveted vintage watches of the post-war era.

keyCollections.name: Compax
keyCollections.description: A chronograph collection first produced in 1933 and developed throughout the 1930s and 1940s, earning Universal Genève the reputation as a 'watch couturier'. The Compax was worn by world leaders including Harry S. Truman and Juan Perón, and by celebrities such as Eric Clapton, who wore a panda-dial variant now known as the 'Nina Rindt' watch. It remains one of the most collected vintage chronograph families.

keyCollections.name: Aero Compax
keyCollections.description: An aviator's compact chronograph introduced in 1936, designed specifically for pilots and military use in the years leading up to the Second World War. The Aero Compax featured a tachymeter and telemeter scale alongside its stopwatch function, making it a genuinely functional aviation instrument. It was produced in various configurations including versions made for the Royal Italian Air Force.

timeline.event: Universal Watch is co-founded in Le Locle by Numa-Emile Descombes and Ulysse Georges Perret as a manufacturer of cases, movements, and complications.
Universal Genève claims the creation of the first-ever wristwatch chronograph, a milestone that cements its reputation for complication expertise.
The Polerouter is introduced, designed by Gérald Genta and featuring a revolutionary microtor movement for Scandinavian Airlines' polar routes.
Hong Kong-based investment firm Stelux Holdings acquires Universal Genève, moving control of the brand to Asia.
Stelux sells the Universal Genève intellectual property to Partners Group, majority owner of Breitling, signalling a major relaunch of the brand.

Official relaunch under Partners Group with Georges Kern. Debuts four collections at Watches & Wonders: Polerouter, Compax, Cabriolet and Disco Mini, all featuring the new proprietary UG-200 micro-rotor movement. First deliveries expected autumn 2026.

faqItems.question: Why is the Universal Genève Polerouter so collectible?
faqItems.answer: The Polerouter combines several highly desirable attributes: it was one of the first watches designed by Gérald Genta (who later created the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak and Patek Philippe Nautilus), it featured a pioneering microtor movement, and it was worn by Scandinavian Airlines pilots on arctic crossings. This combination of horological significance and design pedigree makes it one of the most sought-after vintage watches.

faqItems.question: Is Universal Genève being relaunched?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Following the acquisition of the brand's intellectual property by Partners Group (owner of Breitling) in 2023, Universal Genève is being revived as an active watchmaking brand. Breitling CEO Georges Kern has indicated that new watches are planned, balancing the brand's heritage with contemporary relevance.

name: Urwerk
description: Urwerk was founded in Geneva in 1997 by watchmaker Felix Baumgartner and artist Martin Frei, and produces watches in which satellite-mounted hour numerals orbit around a dial to indicate the time. The brand's wandering-hour complication is an entirely original approach to displaying time and has become one of the defining concepts of contemporary independent horology.

faqItems.question: What is URWERK UR-100V?
faqItems.answer: UR-100V is a satellite-hours collection that combines URWERK's wandering-hour display with space-time themed indications.

faqItems.question: Which UR-100V variations are current official examples?
faqItems.answer: URWERK's official page lists examples including Lightspeed Ceramic, Magic T Hunter Green, and Ultraviolet.

keyCollections.name: UR-111C
keyCollections.description: URWERK UR-111C is a Special Projects collection built around non-traditional time display, using linear, digital, and jumping indications instead of the brand's usual satellite layout.

referenceDetails.name: UR-111C G
referenceDetails.note: A gunmetal UR-111C variation from URWERK's official Special Projects page.

referenceDetails.name: UR-111C I

referenceDetails.name: UR-111C B

keyCollections.whyItMatters: UR-111C shows URWERK experimenting outside its signature satellite-hour system, making it a useful Special Projects page for explaining the brand's more radical display architecture.

faqItems.question: What is URWERK UR-111C?
faqItems.answer: UR-111C is a Special Projects collection that uses linear, digital, and jumping indications rather than URWERK's usual satellite-hour display.

faqItems.question: Which UR-111C variations are official examples?
faqItems.answer: URWERK's official page shows variations including UR-111C G, UR-111C I, UR-111C B, and UR-111C TT.

keyCollections.name: AMC (Atomic Master Clock)
keyCollections.description: A unique collaboration project between URWERK and F.P. Journe in which a mechanical master clock is paired with a satellite wristwatch, allowing the mechanical watch to be automatically regulated by the master clock. The AMC explores the relationship between mechanical timekeeping and atomic precision, and exists as a single unique piece — a philosophical and technical statement about the nature of time.

timeline.event: Felix Baumgartner and Martin Frei found URWERK in Zürich, naming the brand after the Sumerian city of Ur, believed to be the origin of the earliest timekeeping.
URWERK presents its first watch, the UR-101, featuring the signature wandering-hours satellite complication.
The UR-202 is released, introducing a regulator system that allows the winding efficiency of the automatic rotor to be adjusted.
The EMC (Electro Mechanical Control) is unveiled, a watch that can measure its own accuracy and allow the owner to adjust its rate without specialist tools.
URWERK unveils the AMC, a mechanical master clock paired with an adjustable wristwatch — a unique collaboration with F.P. Journe.

Collaborates with Ulysse Nardin on the UR-Freak (100 pieces), combining wandering satellite hours with the Freak rotating movement via new UN-241/UR-241 calibre. Completes the UR-230 trilogy with the Black Star.

faqItems.question: What makes URWERK's satellite complication unique?
faqItems.answer: URWERK's signature satellite complication uses revolving carousel arms, each carrying three rotating cubes or cylinders engraved with hour numerals. As time passes, the correct numeral sweeps across the dial and pauses over a retrograde minutes scale, before the next hour arm takes over. This mechanism has no equivalent in conventional watchmaking and is entirely URWERK's own invention.

faqItems.question: Are URWERK watches considered luxury watches?
faqItems.answer: URWERK occupies the highest tier of independent watchmaking — sometimes called 'haute horlogerie indépendante' — with prices typically ranging from CHF 50,000 to well over CHF 200,000. The brand produces only a few hundred watches per year and each piece requires months of hand assembly, placing URWERK firmly in the category of the world's most exclusive timepieces.

name: Vacheron Constantin
description: Vacheron Constantin was founded in Geneva in 1755 and has been in continuous production ever since, making it the world's oldest continuously operating watch manufacture. As part of the Richemont Group, it produces watches of the highest finishing standards and has registered some of the most complicated wristwatches ever made, including the 57260 pocket watch with 57 complications.

keyCollections.name: Patrimony
keyCollections.description: Vacheron Constantin’s Patrimony is the maison’s purest expression of the modern dress watch: a round, ultra-refined collection launched in 2004 and styled after the brand’s minimalist 1950s references. Its identity is built around slender cases, a slim bezel, short lugs, gently cambered dials, and the signature pearl minute track, while the line also serves as a platform for elegant high complications.

referenceDetails.name: Patrimony Manual-Winding
referenceDetails.description: A closed-back, extra-thin time-only Patrimony that distills the collection to its essentials, pairing a silver-toned opaline dial with baton markers, a pearl minute track, and a slim hand-wound movement.

referenceDetails.name: Patrimony Self-Winding 270th Anniversary
referenceDetails.description: A 2025 limited edition of 370 pieces celebrating Vacheron Constantin’s 270th anniversary, with a dial motif inspired by the Maltese cross and a specially finished anniversary movement.

referenceDetails.name: Patrimony Moon Phase Retrograde Date 270th Anniversary
referenceDetails.description: A 2025 limited edition of 270 pieces that combines one of Vacheron Constantin’s most graceful calendar displays with the Patrimony’s restrained mid-century-inspired design language.

image.alt: Vacheron Constantin Patrimony moon phase retrograde date 4010U/000R-H117

timeline.event: Vacheron Constantin launches the Patrimony collection as a deliberately minimalist dress-watch family inspired by the maison’s 1950s designs.
The Patrimony line becomes a showcase for ultra-thin high complication watchmaking with the debut of the Patrimony Contemporaine Ultra-Thin Calibre 1731 minute repeater.
For the collection’s 20th anniversary, Vacheron Constantin introduces new Patrimony manual-winding and moon-phase models and unveils the 100-piece Patrimony x Ora Ïto limited edition.
Patrimony joins the maison’s 270th-anniversary celebrations with limited self-winding and moon phase retrograde date editions featuring commemorative dial and movement decoration.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Patrimony matters because it defines Vacheron Constantin’s modern idea of the classic dress watch: restrained rather than flashy, historically grounded yet contemporary in scale, and capable of housing everything from elegantly simple hand-wound calibres to record-setting chiming complications. Within high-end Swiss watchmaking, it is one of the clearest bridges between mid-century Geneva design codes and present-day haute horlogerie.

newsItems.title: Vacheron Constantin Revamps A Classic With Three New Patrimony Models
newsItems.summary: For Patrimony’s 20th anniversary, Vacheron Constantin refreshed the line with two new 39 mm manual-winding models and a new moon phase retrograde date model, underscoring the collection’s continuing relevance as the brand’s core dress watch family.

newsItems.title: Celebrating the 20th Anniversary of the Vacheron Constantin Patrimony with a Design by Ora Ïto
newsItems.summary: Monochrome covered the 100-piece yellow-gold Patrimony x Ora Ïto, a special edition with concentric dial decoration created to mark the collection’s 20th birthday.

newsItems.summary: As part of Vacheron Constantin’s 270th-anniversary program, Patrimony received new limited self-winding and moon phase retrograde date editions with anniversary dials and special movement finishing.

faqItems.question: When was the Vacheron Constantin Patrimony collection introduced?
faqItems.answer: The Patrimony collection was launched in 2004 as Vacheron Constantin’s modern, minimalist dress-watch family.

faqItems.question: What defines the Patrimony design?
faqItems.answer: Its hallmarks are a pure round case, slender profile, slim bezel, short lugs, gently curved dial, baton markers, and the signature pearl minute track inspired by Vacheron Constantin watches of the 1950s.

faqItems.question: Is Patrimony only a simple dress-watch collection?
faqItems.answer: No. Although it is best known for time-only and date-free dress watches, Patrimony also includes moon phase, retrograde date, perpetual calendar, and minute repeater executions.

faqItems.question: Why is the Patrimony important within Vacheron Constantin?
faqItems.answer: It is the maison’s clearest modern expression of classical Geneva elegance and one of the main collections through which Vacheron Constantin presents both minimalist design and refined high complications.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1

funFacts.title: Collector note 2

keyCollections.name: Overseas
keyCollections.description: Vacheron Constantin's Overseas is the maison's modern luxury sports watch: travel-ready, integrated-bracelet, and quietly technical, with a lineage that reaches back to the 1977 222 and a current identity built around interchangeable straps and refined everyday utility.

The Overseas line launches as Vacheron Constantin's modern luxury sports watch.

faqItems.question: Why do collectors care about the Overseas?

keyCollections.description: Vacheron Constantin's showcase for haute horlogerie complications, including perpetual calendars, tourbillons, minute repeaters, and the brand's most elaborate grand complications. The Traditionnelle collection uses traditional pocket-watch-inspired case shapes and dial layouts, with movements finished to the strictest Geneva Seal standards. It represents the full depth of the maison's 270-year technical heritage.

keyCollections.name: Métiers d'Art
keyCollections.description: Vacheron Constantin’s Métiers d'Art collection is the Maison’s dedicated stage for decorative watchmaking, where engraving, enamelling, guillochage, gem-setting, miniature sculpture and other artisanal crafts become central to the watch’s identity. Rather than being defined by one case design, the collection is united by the idea of turning horology into a cultural and artistic medium inspired by history, mythology, astronomy and world civilizations.
keyReferences: The legend of the Chinese zodiac
Tribute to The Quest of Time

referenceDetails.description: A landmark early Métiers d'Art series inspired by masks from the Barbier-Mueller Museum; Christie’s notes the project ran as annual sets from 2007 to 2009, helping establish the modern identity of the collection as wearable art rooted in world cultures.

Métiers d'Art Tribute to great civilisations debuted as a Louvre collaboration, with the first four-watch series unveiled in 2022.
For the Maison’s 270th anniversary, Métiers d'Art expanded with Tribute to The Quest of Time and the 12-piece-per-sign Tribute to The Celestial zodiac series.
Tribute to great civilisations received a new chapter at Watches and Wonders 2026, adding four more antiquity-inspired limited editions.

keyCollections.whyItMatters: Métiers d'Art matters because it is where Vacheron Constantin most explicitly fuses fine watchmaking with the decorative arts, using the dial, case and movement as vehicles for cultural storytelling. It also serves as a showcase for the Maison’s in-house artisanal capabilities, proving that haute horlogerie can be about historical transmission, rare handcraft and mechanical ingenuity all at once.

faqItems.question: What is the Métiers d'Art collection at Vacheron Constantin?
faqItems.answer: It is Vacheron Constantin’s art-focused watch collection, centered on decorative crafts such as engraving, enamelling, guillochage and gem-setting rather than a single recurring case design.

faqItems.question: When was the modern Métiers d'Art collection introduced?
faqItems.answer: The best-supported first appearance for the modern collection identity is 2007, when Vacheron Constantin launched the Les Masques series.

faqItems.question: What kinds of themes define Métiers d'Art watches?
faqItems.answer: They often draw from art, history, astronomy, world cultures and symbolic storytelling, with decorative technique playing as large a role as the movement itself.

faqItems.question: Is Métiers d'Art the same as Les Cabinotiers?
faqItems.answer: No. Métiers d'Art is a collection focused on artistic series and decorative crafts, while Les Cabinotiers is Vacheron Constantin’s department for unique pieces and highly bespoke creations.

funFacts.title: Collector note 1
funFacts.body: The Les Masques project was released as annual sets of four watches from 2007 to 2009, making early Métiers d'Art references especially distinctive in how they were conceived as grouped cultural series.

timeline.event: Jean-Marc Vacheron establishes his watchmaking workshop in Geneva — the founding date of the world's oldest continuously operating watch manufacturer.
François Constantin becomes a business partner; the company becomes Vacheron & Constantin, and its famous motto — 'Do better if possible, and that is always possible' — is coined.
Vacheron Constantin receives the first-ever Geneva Seal certification, the highest mark of Genevan watchmaking quality.
Richemont Group acquires Vacheron Constantin, providing the financial stability for the brand to invest in new manufacture facilities and complicated movements.
Vacheron Constantin unveils the Reference 57260, a bespoke pocket watch with 57 complications — the most complex mechanical watch ever made at the time.

Celebrates 270th anniversary at Watches & Wonders with the Les Cabinotiers Solaria Ultra Complication (43 complications), the world's most complicated wristwatch, and the Traditionnelle Tourbillon Perpetual Calendar limited to 127 pieces.
Launches the inaugural Concours d'Elegance Horlogere in partnership with Phillips, the first competition of its kind in watchmaking.

faqItems.question: What is the Holy Trinity of watchmaking and where does Vacheron Constantin fit?
faqItems.answer: The Holy Trinity refers to the three Swiss watchmakers considered the absolute pinnacle of the craft: Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet, and Vacheron Constantin. Vacheron Constantin's place in this group is justified by its status as the world's oldest continuously operating watch manufacturer (since 1755), its unwavering commitment to in-house complications, and its long practice of receiving the prestigious Geneva Seal hallmark.

faqItems.question: Has Vacheron Constantin ever missed a year of production?
faqItems.answer: Vacheron Constantin proudly claims an uninterrupted history of watchmaking since 1755, making it the oldest continuously operating watch manufacturer in the world. Even during periods of economic crisis — including the Great Depression and the quartz crisis of the 1970s — the company continued to produce watches, a record unmatched by any other brand.

pronunciation.nameMeaning: Named for founder Jean-Marc Vacheron and partner Francois Constantin.

name: Vaer
description: Vaer is an American direct-to-consumer watch brand founded in 2017 by Chris Ramsey in Los Angeles, California. The brand specialises in field and diver watches assembled in the USA using Swiss and American-made components, with a focus on honest value and transparency.

keyCollections.name: A-Series (Anchor)
keyCollections.description: Vaer’s A-Series (Anchor) is a compact, field-inspired collection built around clean no-date styling and American-assembly values, reflecting the brand’s rugged, affordable outdoor-watch positioning.

keyCollections.name: C-Series (Cascade)
keyCollections.description: Vaer’s C-Series (Cascade) is a more versatile everyday line, described by the brand as a premium quartz field platform with solar-powered movement and U.S. assembly, aimed at practical daily wear.

keyCollections.name: D-Series (Delta)
keyCollections.description: Vaer’s D-Series (Delta) is the brand’s dive-watch family, associated with tool-watch styling and outdoor utility, and positioned within Vaer’s broader collections hub alongside its other core series.

timeline.event: Cameron Weiss and Ryan Torres found Vaer in Los Angeles, California, with a mission to produce honest, quality watches at fair prices.
Vaer launches its first collection via crowdfunding, quickly gaining a following among consumers frustrated by inflated luxury watch prices.
The brand introduces its American-assembled A-Series, becoming one of the few watch companies to offer watches with American assembly at accessible price points.
Vaer expands its line to include diving watches and solar-powered quartz options, broadening its appeal to different watch enthusiasts.
The brand continues to grow its direct-to-consumer model, partnering with select retailers while maintaining competitive pricing through its website.

faqItems.question: Are Vaer watches truly made in the USA?
faqItems.answer: Vaer's A-Series watches are assembled in the United States, which is the core of its American-made claim. However, like virtually all American watch brands, Vaer sources components internationally — movements from Switzerland or Japan, cases and dials from Swiss suppliers — as the infrastructure for full domestic production no longer exists in the US.

faqItems.question: How does Vaer keep its prices competitive?
faqItems.answer: Vaer sells primarily direct-to-consumer through its website, eliminating retailer mark-ups that can add 30–50% to traditional watch retail prices. The brand also focuses on functional, no-frills designs without extensive marketing budgets, passing the savings on to customers.
